title: Weird Algorithm
explanation_short: We are given a number as input and need to apply a series of operations to it. The goal is to transform the input number into a specific output by following a set of rules. We need to find the sequence of numbers produced by repeatedly applying these rules until a certain condition is met. The output will be the resulting sequence of numbers.

title: Missing Number
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers from 1 to a certain number, but one number is missing. Our task is to find the missing number in the list. The input is the list of numbers, and the output is the single missing number. We need to examine the list and determine which number is not present.

title: Number Spiral
explanation_short: We are given a size for a square grid. Our task is to fill this grid with numbers in a spiral pattern, starting from the center and moving outward. We need to determine the correct sequence of numbers to place in each position in the grid. The output will be the completed grid with numbers arranged in a spiral pattern.

title: Josephus Problem I
explanation_short: We are given a circle of people, each with a unique position, and a specific elimination pattern. The input will be the number of people in the circle and the elimination pattern. We need to determine the position of the person who remains after the elimination process is complete. The output will be the position of the last person standing in the circle.

title: Distinct Numbers
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers as input. Our task is to find the unique numbers in this list, which means we need to identify and count the numbers that appear only once. The output will be the count of these distinct numbers. We need to process the input list to determine how many unique numbers it contains. The result will be a single number representing the count of distinct numbers.

title: Apartments
explanation_short: We are given a list of available apartments with their sizes and a list of people with their required apartment sizes. Our task is to find the maximum number of people that can be accommodated in the available apartments. The input consists of two lists: one for apartment sizes and one for people's required sizes. The output will be the maximum number of people that can be assigned an apartment.

title: Ferris Wheel
explanation_short: We are given a list of people with their heights and the maximum allowed difference in height for two people to sit together in a Ferris wheel cart. Our task is to arrange these people in carts based on the given height constraint. The goal is to find the maximum number of carts that can be filled with people, and the output will be the minimum number of carts needed to accommodate all the people.

title: Concert Tickets
explanation_short: We are given a list of ticket prices and a budget. Our task is to find the maximum number of tickets we can buy within the given budget. The input includes the list of ticket prices and the budget, and the output will be the maximum number of tickets that can be purchased. We need to determine how to select tickets from the list to stay within the budget while buying the most tickets possible.

title: Restaurant Customers
explanation_short: We are given a list of customer arrival and departure times at a restaurant. Our task is to determine the maximum number of customers present in the restaurant at any given time. To do this, we need to analyze the arrival and departure times and find the peak customer hour. The output will be the maximum number of customers that were in the restaurant simultaneously.

title: Dice Combinations
explanation_short: We are given a certain number of dice and a target number. Our task is to find the total number of ways to reach the target number by rolling the dice. The input includes the number of dice and the target number, and the output will be the total count of combinations that sum up to the target. We need to consider all possible outcomes of rolling the dice to calculate this count. The result will give us the total number of unique combinations.

title: Minimizing Coins
explanation_short: We are given a certain amount of money and different coin denominations. Our goal is to find the minimum number of coins needed to make up this amount using the available denominations. The input will be the amount of money and the coin denominations, and the output will be the smallest number of coins required to reach the target amount. We need to determine the most efficient combination of coins to achieve this.

title: Coin Combinations I
explanation_short: We are given a certain amount of money and a set of coin denominations. Our task is to find the total number of ways we can make change for that amount using the available coins. The input includes the amount of money and the coin denominations, and the output will be the total number of possible combinations. We need to consider all possible combinations of coins that add up to the given amount.

title: Coin Combinations II
explanation_short: We are given a certain amount of money and a set of coin denominations. Our task is to find the number of different ways we can make change for that amount using the available coins. The input includes the amount of money and the coin denominations, and the output will be the total number of unique combinations that sum up to the given amount. We need to consider all possible combinations to reach the desired amount.

title: Removing Digits
explanation_short: We are given a number and need to remove its digits one by one to find the smallest possible number. The input is the original number, and we have to determine the order in which to remove its digits. Our goal is to find the smallest number that can be formed by removing some or all of the digits from the original number. The output will be this smallest possible number.

title: Book Shop
explanation_short: We are given a list of book prices and certain constraints. Our goal is to determine the maximum number of books that can be bought within a given budget, considering that some books may have discounts when purchased together. The input includes the book prices and the budget, and we need to find the optimal combination of books to buy. The output will be the maximum number of books that can be purchased.

title: Counting Rooms
explanation_short: We are given a house represented as a grid with rooms and walls. Our task is to find the total number of separate rooms in the house. The input will describe the layout of the house, and we need to determine how many distinct areas are accessible. The output will be the count of these separate rooms.

title: Building Roads
explanation_short: We are given a set of cities and potential roads between them, along with the cost of building each road. Our task is to determine the most cost-effective way to connect all the cities. The input includes the cities and road connections with their respective costs, and we need to find the optimal road network. The output will be the total cost of building the roads in the optimal network.

title: Message Route
explanation_short: We are given a network of cities connected by roads, and a message that needs to be sent from one city to another. Our task is to find the best path for the message to travel, considering the connections between cities. The input includes information about the cities and their connections, and we need to determine the most efficient route. The output will be the path that the message should take to reach its destination.

title: Building Teams
explanation_short: We are given a set of people with different skills and preferences. Our goal is to divide them into teams based on certain conditions, ensuring that each team has a good balance of skills. The input includes information about each person's skills and preferences, and we need to find a way to form teams that meet the given criteria. The output will be the formed teams, with each team consisting of a group of people who work well together.

title: Investigation
explanation_short: We are given a graph with nodes and edges, and some nodes have specific values or properties. Our task is to find a way to traverse or analyze the graph to identify a particular pattern or relationship between the nodes. The input includes the graph structure and possibly some additional information about the nodes. We need to determine a specific outcome or result based on the graph's properties. The output will be a value or set of values that represents the result of our investigation.

title: Shortest Routes I
explanation_short: We are given a map of cities connected by roads, and the distance between each city. Our task is to find the shortest path between two specific cities. The input includes the map of cities and roads, as well as the starting and ending cities. We need to determine the minimum distance required to travel from the starting city to the ending city. The output will be the shortest distance between these two cities.

title: Shortest Routes II
explanation_short: We are given a map of cities and the distances between them. Our task is to find the shortest possible route that visits a set of specific cities and returns to the starting point. The input includes the cities, their connections, and the distances between them. We need to determine the most efficient route that covers all the required cities. The output will be the total distance of the shortest possible route.

title: Tree Matching
explanation_short: We are given two trees as input, and our goal is to determine if a subset of one tree matches the structure of the other tree. The matching process involves finding a way to map nodes from one tree to another while preserving their relationships. We need to find out if such a mapping exists, allowing us to identify a matching subset. The output will indicate whether a match is possible or not.

title: Tree Distances I
explanation_short: We are given a tree with nodes and edges, and each edge has a certain weight or distance. Our task is to find the shortest distance between each pair of nodes in the tree. The input consists of the tree structure and the weights of the edges, and we need to calculate the shortest path between all possible pairs of nodes. The output will be a representation of these shortest distances.

title: Word Combinations
explanation_short: We are given a list of words and a target word. Our task is to find all possible combinations of words from the list that can be arranged to spell the target word. The input consists of the list of words and the target word, and the output will be all the unique combinations of words that can form the target word. We need to identify these combinations and return them as the result.

title: String Matching
explanation_short: We are given two strings, a text and a pattern. Our task is to find all occurrences of the pattern within the text. The input consists of these two strings, and we need to determine the locations where the pattern appears in the text. The output will be the positions where the pattern is found, or an indication that it's not present.

title: Finding Borders
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to find all the borders of its substrings. A border is a prefix that is also a suffix, and we want to identify these for each substring. Our goal is to determine all the borders for each possible substring within the given string. The output will be the borders for each substring, which can help us understand the structure of the input string.

title: Two Sum
explanation_short: We're given a list of integers and a target number. Our task is to find two numbers in the list that add up to the target number and return their positions in the list. The output will be a list of two indices, and we can't use the same number twice. We need to find the pair of numbers that satisfies this condition and return their corresponding indices.

title: Add Two Numbers
explanation_short: We are given two linked lists where each node represents a digit of a number, with the digits in reverse order. Our task is to add these two numbers together. The input is the two linked lists, and we need to find their sum. The output will be a new linked list representing the sum of the two input numbers.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
explanation_short: We are given a string of characters as input. Our task is to find the longest sequence of characters within this string where no character is repeated. The output will be the length of this longest sequence, which is essentially the number of unique characters in a row. We need to examine the string to determine this length.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
explanation_short: We are given two sorted arrays of different sizes, and we need to find the median of the combined array. The input consists of these two arrays, and our task is to calculate the middle value of the merged and sorted array. The output will be a single number representing the median, which can be an integer or a decimal value if the total number of elements is even. We must achieve this in an efficient manner, considering the large size of the input arrays. The result should be a precise median value.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to find the longest substring that reads the same backward as forward. The goal is to identify this specific substring within the given string. The output will be the longest palindromic substring found in the input string. We are looking for the longest sequence of characters that forms a palindrome.

title: Zigzag Conversion
explanation_short: We are given a string and a specific number of rows. Our task is to rearrange the characters in the string into a zigzag pattern with the given number of rows, and then read the characters line by line. The input is the original string and the number of rows, and the output is the rearranged string after reading it line by line. We need to find a way to convert the original string into this new format. The result will be a string that represents the characters read from the zigzag pattern.

title: Reverse Integer
explanation_short: We are given a 32-bit integer as input, which can be positive or negative. Our task is to reverse the digits of this integer while considering the 32-bit integer range constraint. If the reversed integer falls within the range, we need to return the reversed integer; otherwise, we return 0. The output will be the reversed integer or 0, depending on whether the reversed value is within the valid range.

title: String to Integer (atoi)
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to convert it into a 32-bit signed integer. The goal is to extract a valid integer from the string, handling any non-numeric characters it may contain. Our task is to determine the resulting integer value. The output will be the converted integer, taking into account any relevant constraints such as the 32-bit signed integer range.

title: Palindrome Number
explanation_short: We are given an integer as input and need to determine if it reads the same when its digits are reversed. The goal is to find out whether the given number is a palindrome or not. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether the number is a palindrome. We need to consider the entire number, including any negative sign, when making this determination.

title: Regular Expression Matching
explanation_short: We are given two inputs: a string and a pattern that may contain special characters. Our task is to determine if the entire string matches the pattern, considering the special meanings of '.' and '*'. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether the string and pattern match. We need to find a way to compare the string and pattern to produce this output. The goal is to ensure the matching covers the entire string, not just a part of it.

title: Container With Most Water
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers representing the heights of vertical lines. Our task is to find two lines that can form a container with the x-axis, holding the maximum amount of water. The input is the array of heights, and the output is the maximum amount of water the container can store. We need to determine which two lines will result in the largest container.

title: Integer to Roman
explanation_short: We are given an integer as input and need to convert it into a Roman numeral. The goal is to represent the integer using a combination of specific symbols, each with its own value. We must find a way to break down the integer into its decimal place values and then express these values using the Roman numeral symbols. The output will be a string representing the Roman numeral equivalent of the input integer. The result should be a valid Roman numeral that accurately represents the original integer value.

title: Roman to Integer
explanation_short: We are given a Roman numeral as input, which is a string of characters representing a number in the Roman numeral system. Our task is to convert this Roman numeral into its equivalent integer value. The output will be an integer that corresponds to the input Roman numeral. We need to consider the rules of the Roman numeral system, including the cases where subtraction is used to determine the correct integer value.

title: Longest Common Prefix
explanation_short: We are given a list of strings as input and need to find the longest sequence of characters that is common to all of them. Our goal is to determine this shared prefix and return it as a string. If no such prefix exists, we will return an empty string. The output will be the longest common prefix found among the input strings.

title: 3Sum Closest
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers and a target number. Our task is to find three numbers in the array that add up to a sum closest to the target number. The output will be the sum of these three integers, which should be as close as possible to the target. We need to search through the array to find the combination that achieves this.

title: 3Sum
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers, and we need to find all unique triplets in the array where the sum of the three numbers equals zero. The triplets must consist of distinct indices in the array, meaning no index can be repeated. Our goal is to return a list of these unique triplets. The output will be a collection of triplets, with no duplicates allowed.

title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
explanation_short: We are given a string of digits from 2 to 9. Our task is to find all possible combinations of letters that these digits could represent on a telephone keypad. The input is a string of digits, and the output will be a list of all possible letter combinations. We need to use the standard telephone mapping of digits to letters to generate these combinations. The goal is to return all possible combinations in any order.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
explanation_short: We're given a linked list and a number 'n'. Our task is to find and remove the nth node from the end of the list. The input includes the head of the linked list and the value of 'n', and we need to return the head of the modified list after removal. The output will be the updated linked list with the nth node from the end removed.

title: Valid Parentheses
explanation_short: We are given a string of parentheses, brackets, and braces as input. Our task is to determine whether the arrangement of these characters is valid, meaning they are properly nested and matched. The output will be a simple "yes" or "no" answer, indicating whether the input string is valid or not. We need to find a way to check if every opening character has a corresponding closing character of the same type. The goal is to return true if the string is valid and false otherwise.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
explanation_short: We are given two sorted lists, and we need to combine them into one list that is also sorted. The input lists are made up of nodes that are already in order, and we want to merge these nodes to create a new sorted list. Our task is to take the heads of these two lists and return the head of the newly merged list, which should contain all the nodes from both lists in the correct order. The output will be the head of this new merged list.

title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
explanation_short: We're given a linked list as input, and our task is to swap every two adjacent nodes in the list. The goal is to rearrange the nodes themselves, without changing the values they hold. The output will be the head of the modified linked list, where every pair of adjacent nodes has been swapped. We need to find a way to achieve this rearrangement efficiently.

title: Generate Parentheses
explanation_short: We are given a number of pairs of parentheses, and we need to find all possible combinations of these parentheses that are well-formed, meaning they are properly nested and matched. The input is the number of pairs, and the output will be a list of all valid combinations. Our goal is to generate all these combinations. The result will be a collection of strings, each representing a valid arrangement of parentheses.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
explanation_short: We are given multiple sorted linked lists as input. Our task is to combine these lists into a single sorted linked list. The output will be a new linked list where all elements are arranged in ascending order. We need to find a way to efficiently merge these lists while maintaining the sorted order. The resulting linked list should contain all elements from the input lists, sorted from smallest to largest.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
explanation_short: We're given a sorted array of integers that may contain duplicates. Our task is to remove these duplicates in a way that preserves the original order of elements, and then determine the total count of unique elements. The input is the sorted array, and the output will be the number of unique elements, along with the modified array where each unique element appears only once. The goal is to achieve this without using any additional space.

title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
explanation_short: We're given the head of a linked list and a positive integer k. Our task is to reverse the nodes of the list in groups of k, without changing the values of the nodes, and return the modified list. The input includes the linked list and the value of k, and the output will be the modified linked list with the nodes reversed in groups of k. If there are remaining nodes that aren't a multiple of k, they should remain in their original order.

title: Remove Element
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers and a specific value. Our task is to remove all occurrences of this value from the list, and then tell how many numbers are left in the list. The output will be the count of remaining numbers, and the list will be modified to have these remaining numbers at the beginning.

title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
explanation_short: We are given two strings, a longer string called the haystack and a shorter string called the needle. Our task is to find the position where the needle first appears in the haystack. If the needle is found, we need to return its starting position, but if it's not found, we return -1. The goal is to determine whether the needle is a part of the haystack and, if so, where it starts.

title: Divide Two Integers
explanation_short: We are given two integers, dividend and divisor, and we need to find their quotient without using certain mathematical operations. The goal is to divide the dividend by the divisor and truncate the result toward zero, losing any fractional part. The result, or quotient, should then be returned, while ensuring it falls within a specific integer range. If the quotient exceeds this range, we need to return the maximum or minimum allowed value.

title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
explanation_short: We are given a string and a list of words, where all the words are the same length. Our task is to find all the starting positions in the string where a substring can be formed by concatenating all the given words in any order. The output will be a list of these starting indices, and we need to return all such positions where the concatenated substring matches any permutation of the given words.

title: Next Permutation
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input, and we need to find the next arrangement of these integers that is greater than the current one when the arrangements are sorted in order. The goal is to modify the input array in place to get this new arrangement. The output will be the modified array, which is the next greater permutation of the input array, or the smallest possible arrangement if no greater permutation exists. The arrangement is considered "greater" if it comes after the current one when all possible arrangements are sorted.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
explanation_short: We are given a string made up of only open and close parentheses. Our task is to find the longest sequence of parentheses in the string that is well-formed, meaning every open parenthesis has a matching close parenthesis. The output will be the length of this longest valid sequence. We need to examine the input string to identify the longest valid parentheses substring and determine its length.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
explanation_short: We are given a sorted array of integers that has been rotated at some point, and a target number to search for. The array was initially sorted in ascending order, but it's now rotated, meaning its elements are shifted from their original positions. Our task is to find the index of the target number in this rotated array. If the target is found, we return its index; otherwise, we return -1 to indicate it's not present. The goal is to determine the position of the target number within the rotated array.

title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
explanation_short: We're given a sorted list of integers and a target number. Our task is to find the first and last positions where this target number appears in the list. If the target is found, we need to return its starting and ending positions, but if it's not found, we return -1 for both positions. The input is the sorted list and the target number, and the output is a list containing the first and last positions of the target.

title: Search Insert Position
explanation_short: We are given a sorted list of unique integers and a target number. Our task is to find the position of the target number in the list if it exists, or determine where it should be placed to maintain the sorted order. The input consists of the sorted list and the target value, and the output will be the index where the target number is or should be located. We need to achieve this efficiently, considering the list's sorted nature. The result will be a specific index in the list.

title: Valid Sudoku
explanation_short: We are given a 9x9 Sudoku board as input, where some cells are filled with numbers and others are empty. Our task is to determine if the filled cells are valid according to Sudoku rules. The output will be a boolean value indicating whether the board is valid or not.

title: Count and Say
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer n as input. Our task is to generate a sequence of strings where each string is created by describing the previous string, and we need to find the nth string in this sequence. The output will be the nth string in the sequence, which is created by applying a specific rule to the previous string. The rule involves replacing consecutive identical characters with the character and its count.

title: Sudoku Solver
explanation_short: We are given a Sudoku puzzle with some filled-in numbers and empty cells represented by a '.' character. Our task is to fill in the empty cells with numbers from 1 to 9 in such a way that each row, column, and 3x3 sub-grid contains each number only once. The output will be the completed Sudoku puzzle with all empty cells filled in correctly.

title: Combination Sum
explanation_short: We are given a list of distinct integers and a target number. Our task is to find all possible combinations of these integers that add up to the target number, allowing each integer to be used multiple times. The output will be a list of these unique combinations, where each combination is a list of numbers that sum to the target.

title: Combination Sum II
explanation_short: We're given a list of numbers and a target sum, and we need to find all the unique combinations of numbers from the list that add up to the target. Each number in the list can only be used once in a combination, and we must avoid duplicate combinations. The input includes the list of candidate numbers and the target sum, and the output will be all the unique combinations that sum to the target. Our goal is to identify these combinations without repeating any.

title: First Missing Positive
explanation_short: We're given an unsorted list of integers as input. Our task is to find the smallest positive integer that doesn't exist in this list. The output will be this missing positive integer. We need to achieve this by examining the input list and determining which small positive integers are present, to figure out which one is the first to be missing.

title: Trapping Rain Water
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers representing the height of bars in an elevation map. Our task is to calculate the amount of water that can be trapped between these bars after it rains. The input is a list of non-negative integers, and the output is the total amount of water that can be trapped. We need to find a way to determine the amount of water that can be held in the spaces between the bars. The result will be a single number representing the total units of trapped water.

title: Multiply Strings
explanation_short: We are given two non-negative integers as strings, and we need to find their product. The input strings represent numbers, and we must multiply these numbers together. Our goal is to return the result of this multiplication as a string, without directly converting the inputs to integers or using any special libraries. The output will be a string that represents the product of the two input numbers.

title: Wildcard Matching
explanation_short: We are given two inputs: a string and a pattern that can contain special characters '?' and '*'. Our task is to determine if the pattern matches the entire string, considering the special meanings of '?' and '*'. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether the pattern fully matches the string. We need to find a way to handle these special characters to achieve a complete match. The goal is to return true if the pattern matches the entire string and false otherwise.

title: Jump Game II
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers where each number represents how far we can jump from that position. Our goal is to find the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the end of the array. The input is the array of integers, and the output will be the smallest number of jumps required to get to the last position. We need to figure out the most efficient way to make these jumps.

title: Rotate Image
explanation_short: We are given a square image represented as a 2D matrix, and we need to rotate this image 90 degrees clockwise. The input is this 2D matrix, and we must modify it directly without creating a new matrix. Our goal is to transform the input matrix into its rotated version. The output will be the modified input matrix, representing the image after rotation.

title: Permutations
explanation_short: We are given an array of unique integers as input. Our task is to find all possible arrangements of these integers, where the order matters. The output will be a collection of all these arrangements, and the order in which they are returned does not matter. We need to consider every possible way to rearrange the integers in the input array. The goal is to generate all possible permutations of the given array.

title: Permutations II
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers that may contain duplicates. Our task is to generate all possible unique arrangements of these numbers. The output will be a collection of lists, where each list represents a unique permutation of the input numbers. We need to ensure that no two permutations in the output are the same, even if the input contains duplicate numbers.

title: Group Anagrams
explanation_short: We are given a list of words and need to group the words that are anagrams of each other together. An anagram is a word made by rearranging the letters of another word. Our task is to identify these groups and return them as a collection of lists, where each list contains words that are anagrams of each other. The output will be a list of these groups, and the order of the groups does not matter.

title: Pow(x, n)
explanation_short: We are given two inputs, a number 'x' and an integer 'n', and we need to calculate the result of 'x' raised to the power of 'n'. The goal is to find the value of 'x' multiplied by itself 'n' times. The output will be the calculated result, which can be a decimal number. We need to handle both positive and negative values of 'n' to get the correct result.

title: N-Queens
explanation_short: We are given an integer n, representing the size of a chessboard. Our task is to find all possible ways to place n queens on this board so that none of them can attack each other. The output will be a collection of distinct board configurations, where each configuration shows the placement of the queens and empty spaces. We need to return all these unique configurations.

title: Maximum Subarray
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers as input, and we need to find a part of this list where the numbers add up to the largest possible total. Our goal is to identify this part of the list and calculate its sum. The output will be the largest sum we can find within the given list of numbers.

title: Spiral Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a matrix with a certain number of rows and columns, and we need to find a way to traverse all its elements in a spiral pattern. The input is this matrix, and our task is to extract all its elements in the correct spiral order. The output will be a list of numbers representing the elements of the matrix in the spiral order they were visited.

title: N-Queens II
explanation_short: We are given an integer representing the size of a chessboard. Our task is to find the number of ways to place queens on this board so that none of them can attack each other. The output will be the total count of these unique arrangements, where each arrangement represents a distinct solution to the puzzle. We need to consider all possible placements of queens on the board to achieve this.

title: Jump Game
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers where each number represents how far we can jump from that position. Our goal is to determine if we can reach the last position in the array, starting from the first position. The input is the array of integers, and the output is a simple yes or no, indicating whether it's possible to reach the end. We need to figure out the sequence of jumps that allows us to get to the last index, if such a sequence exists.

title: Merge Intervals
explanation_short: We're given a list of time intervals, where each interval has a start and end time. Our task is to combine any intervals that overlap with each other. The goal is to produce a new list of intervals that cover all the original intervals without any overlaps. The resulting list should contain the merged intervals.

title: Insert Interval

title: Minimum Window Substring
explanation_short: We are given two strings, a longer string and a shorter string, and we need to find the smallest part of the longer string that contains all the characters of the shorter string. title: Combinations

title: Unique Binary Search Trees

title: Integer Replacement
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer as input and need to find the minimum number of operations required to reduce it to 1. explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to find the maximum value that can be obtained by rotating this array and calculating a specific function for each rotation. explanation_short: We are given an encoded string that contains a specific pattern of numbers and letters enclosed in square brackets. title: Sum of Left Leaves

explanation_short: We are given a 32-bit integer as input and need to find its equivalent representation in hexadecimal format. title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
explanation_short: We are given a list of people with their heights and the number of people in front of them who are taller or the same height. title: Trapping Rain Water II

title: Fizz Buzz

title: Third Maximum Number

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array

title: 132 Pattern

title: LFU Cache

title: Count The Repetitions

title: Validate IP Address

explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and we need to find the number of distinct results that can be obtained by performing a bitwise OR operation on all possible non-empty subarrays. The input is the array of integers, and the output is the count of unique bitwise OR results. We will consider all contiguous sequences of elements within the array to calculate these results. Our goal is to determine how many unique values can be obtained from these operations.

title: Increasing Order Search Tree
explanation_short: We're given the root of a binary search tree as input. Our task is to rearrange this tree so that it's ordered in a specific way, where each node has no left child and only one right child. The result should be a tree where all nodes are connected in a specific order.

title: Orderly Queue
explanation_short: We are given a string and an integer that represents the number of letters from the start of the string that we can move to the end. title: Occurrences After Bigram
explanation_short: We are given a text and two specific words, 'first' and 'second'. Our task is to find all instances where 'first' is followed by 'second', and then identify the word that comes after 'second' in each of these instances. title: Number of Recent Calls
explanation_short: We are given a sequence of time requests, and we need to find the number of requests made within the last 3000 seconds. title: Airplane Seat Assignment Probability
explanation_short: We are given the number of passengers and seats on an airplane, where each passenger has a corresponding seat. The first passenger chooses a seat randomly, and the rest of the passengers then take their assigned seats if available. We need to find the probability that the last passenger gets to sit in their own seat. The output will be a decimal value representing this probability.

title: Dice Roll Simulation
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers representing the maximum consecutive rolls for each number on a die and the total number of rolls. Our task is to find the number of distinct sequences that can be obtained with the given number of rolls, considering the constraints on consecutive rolls. The output will be the total count of distinct sequences, adjusted to fit within a large modulus to prevent overflow. The input array and the number of rolls will guide us in determining the possible sequences. title: Three Equal Parts
explanation_short: We are given an array of zeros and ones, and we need to divide it into three non-empty parts. title: Maximum Equal Frequency
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. title: Average Salary Excluding the Minimum and Maximum Salary
explanation_short: We are given a list of unique employee salaries. Our task is to find the average salary of all employees, excluding the highest and lowest paid employees. To do this, we need to calculate the total sum of salaries, excluding the minimum and maximum salaries, and then divide by the number of remaining employees. title: Last Moment Before All Ants Fall Out of a Plank
explanation_short: We are given a plank of length n and the positions of ants moving to the left and right. title: Can Make Arithmetic Progression From Sequence
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers as input and need to determine if it's possible to rearrange them in a way that the difference between each pair of consecutive numbers is the same. explanation_short: We are given two positive integers, n and k. Our task is to find the kth factor of n, where factors are numbers that divide n without leaving a remainder, and they are listed in ascending order. title: Longest Subarray of 1's After Deleting One Element
explanation_short: We are given a binary array of 1's and 0's, and we need to delete one element from it. Our goal is to find the size of the longest subarray that contains only 1's after the deletion. explanation_short: We are given a string of digits representing a large integer and a limit on the number of times we can swap adjacent digits. title: Parallel Courses II
explanation_short: We are given a certain number of courses and the prerequisites for each course. Our task is to determine the minimum number of semesters required to complete all courses, given that we can take a limited number of courses per semester. The input includes the number of courses, the prerequisite relationships, and the maximum number of courses that can be taken per semester. The output will be the minimum number of semesters needed to complete all courses.

title: Count Submatrices With All Ones
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix filled with ones and zeros. Our task is to find the total number of submatrices within this matrix that contain only ones. explanation_short: We are given a binary string consisting of 1s and 0s. Our task is to count the number of substrings that contain only 1s and return this count modulo 10^9 + 7. explanation_short: We are given an array of numbers that may have been sorted and then rotated. title: Can You Eat Your Favorite Candy on Your Favorite Day?
explanation_short: We are given two inputs: an array of candy counts for different types of candies and a list of queries. Each query includes a favorite candy type, a favorite day, and a daily candy limit. explanation_short: We are given a set of bags, each containing a certain number of balls, and a limit on the number of operations we can perform to divide these bags. title: Maximum Score From Removing Stones
explanation_short: We are given three piles of stones with sizes a, b, and c. title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended II

title: Count Pairs Of Nodes

title: Repeated String Match

title: Binary Number with Alternating Bits

title: Binary Search
