The output will be a collection of numbers between the given left and right boundaries that meet this specific divisibility condition.

title: My Calendar I
explanation_short: We are given a series of events, each with a start and end time. Our task is to determine whether we can add a new event to the calendar without causing a double booking, where a double booking occurs when two events overlap. The input is a list of existing events and a new event to be added. We need to find out whether the new event can be added without overlapping with any existing events. The output will be a boolean value indicating whether the new event can be added to the calendar.

title: Count Different Palindromic Subsequences
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to find the number of unique non-empty subsequences that are palindromes. A palindrome is a sequence that reads the same forwards and backwards. Our task is to count these unique palindromic subsequences and return the result modulo 10^9 + 7. The output will be the total count of such subsequences.

title: My Calendar II
explanation_short: We're given a calendar and a stream of new events, each with a start and end time. Our task is to determine whether adding a new event would cause a triple booking, where three events overlap at some point. We need to find a way to track existing events and check for overlaps when a new event is added. The goal is to decide whether to add the new event or not, based on the presence of triple bookings. The output will be a decision on whether the new event can be added to the calendar.

title: My Calendar III
explanation_short: We are given a series of events, each with a start and end time. Our task is to find the maximum number of events that overlap at any given time after each new event is added. The input is a stream of events, and the output is the maximum number of overlapping events, also known as the maximum k-booking, after each event is processed. We need to design a system that can efficiently track and update the maximum k-booking as new events are added.

title: Flood Fill
explanation_short: We are given an image represented as a grid of integers and three integers: the starting row, starting column, and a new color. Our task is to change the color of the starting pixel and all connected pixels of the same color to the new color. The input includes the image grid and the three integers, and the output will be the modified image grid after the color change. We need to find a way to identify and change the color of all connected pixels.

title: Asteroid Collision
explanation_short: We are given a list of asteroids with their sizes and directions. Our task is to determine the final state of these asteroids after they have all potentially collided with each other. The output will be a list representing the remaining asteroids after all collisions have occurred, considering that smaller asteroids explode when colliding with larger ones and asteroids moving in the same direction do not collide. We need to find this final list based on the given asteroid sizes and directions. The result will show which asteroids are left after all possible collisions.

title: Parse Lisp Expression
explanation_short: We are given a string representing a Lisp-like expression, which contains variables, values, and operations. Our task is to evaluate this expression and find its integer value, considering the scope and order of variable assignments. The input string can include nested expressions and variable declarations, and we need to parse it correctly to determine the final output value. The output will be an integer that represents the result of the evaluated expression.

title: Monotone Increasing Digits
explanation_short: We are given an integer as input and need to find the largest integer less than or equal to the input that has monotone increasing digits. This means each digit from left to right is either increasing or staying the same. Our goal is to determine this largest integer. The output will be the largest integer with monotone increasing digits that meets the condition.

title: Daily Temperatures
explanation_short: We are given a list of daily temperatures, and we need to find out how many days it will take for the temperature to rise after each day. Our task is to create a new list where each entry corresponds to the number of days until a warmer temperature is reached. The output will be a list of the same length as the input, with each value representing the number of days to wait for a warmer temperature, or 0 if no warmer temperature is found.

title: Delete and Earn
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers and we need to find the maximum number of points that can be earned by deleting numbers from the list. When a number is deleted, it earns points equal to its value, but all other numbers that are one less or one more than the deleted number are also deleted. Our goal is to determine the total maximum points that can be earned. The output will be the maximum total points.

title: Cherry Pickup
explanation_short: We are given a grid representing a field of cherries where each cell has one of three possible values. Our goal is to find the maximum number of cherries that can be collected by moving through the grid and following certain rules. The output will be the total number of cherries collected. We need to determine the best path to take in order to maximize the cherry collection. The grid's values and movement rules will guide us in finding the optimal solution.

title: Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target
explanation_short: We are given a sorted list of characters and a target character. Our task is to find the smallest character in the list that comes after the target character in alphabetical order. If no such character exists, we need to return the first character in the list. The output will be a single character that meets this condition.

title: Network Delay Time
explanation_short: We're given a network with nodes and directed edges representing travel times between them. Our task is to find the minimum time it takes for a signal sent from a specific node to reach all other nodes in the network. The input includes the network's nodes, travel times, and the starting node, and the output will be the minimum time required for all nodes to receive the signal, or -1 if it's impossible. We need to determine the shortest path to all nodes from the given starting point.

title: Prefix and Suffix Search
explanation_short: We are given a list of words and need to design a system that can efficiently search for words based on a given prefix and suffix. The input will be a word to be added to the system and then queries with a prefix and suffix to search for matching words. Our goal is to find all words in the system that match the given prefix and suffix. The output will be the total number of words that match the search query. We need to design a system that can handle these add and search operations efficiently.

title: Largest Number At Least Twice of Others
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers where the largest number appears only once. Our task is to check if this largest number is at least twice as big as every other number in the list. If it is, we need to find the position of the largest number in the list, and if not, we indicate that it doesn't meet the condition. The result will be the position of the largest number if it's at least twice as big as the others, or a special value to show it's not.

title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
explanation_short: We are given a list of costs for each step on a staircase, and we can climb either one or two steps at a time. Our goal is to find the minimum total cost to reach the top of the staircase, considering that we can start from either the first or second step. The input is the list of costs, and the output is the minimum total cost to reach the top. We need to determine the most cost-effective path to the top, taking into account the costs of each step and the flexibility to climb one or two steps at a time.

title: Open the Lock
explanation_short: We are given a lock with 4 wheels, each having 10 slots, and a list of deadend codes that will stop the lock from turning. The lock starts at '0000' and we need to find the minimum number of turns required to reach a target code, while avoiding the deadend codes. The output will be the minimum total number of turns or -1 if it's impossible to open the lock. We have to consider all possible moves, which involve turning one wheel one slot at a time.

title: Cracking the Safe
explanation_short: We are given a safe with a password of n digits, where each digit can be one of k possible values. Our goal is to find the shortest sequence of digits that will unlock the safe at some point, considering that the safe checks the most recent n digits after each new digit is entered. The input consists of the number of digits in the password (n) and the number of possible digit values (k). The output will be a string of digits that guarantees the safe will be unlocked.

title: Contain Virus
explanation_short: We are given a grid representing a world with infected and uninfected cells. Our task is to determine the minimum number of walls needed to quarantine the infected areas by installing walls between adjacent cells. The goal is to contain the spread of the virus, and we need to find the total number of walls used to achieve this. The output will be the total number of walls installed to quarantine the infected regions.

title: Valid Palindrome II
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to determine if it can be made into a palindrome by removing at most one character. A palindrome is a string that reads the same forwards and backwards. Our goal is to find out if such a modification is possible, and if so, we return true; otherwise, we return false. The output will be a boolean value indicating whether the string can be made into a palindrome.

title: Trim a Binary Search Tree
explanation_short: We are given a binary search tree and two boundaries, a low value and a high value. Our task is to remove all nodes from the tree that have values outside of this range, while preserving the structure of the remaining nodes. The input includes the tree's root and the low and high boundaries, and we need to find the root of the resulting trimmed tree. The output will be the root of this trimmed binary search tree, which may be different from the original root.

title: Binary Tree Tilt
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree as input. Our task is to calculate the sum of the tilt of every node in the tree, where the tilt of a node is the absolute difference between the sum of its left subtree and right subtree. The output will be the total sum of these tilts. We need to consider the values of all nodes in the tree to find this sum.

title: Second Minimum Node In a Binary Tree
explanation_short: We are given a special binary tree where each node has a non-negative value and exactly two or zero sub-nodes. Our task is to find the second minimum value among all the nodes in the tree. The input is the binary tree itself, and we need to output the second smallest value if it exists, or -1 if it doesn't. The tree has a unique property where a node's value is the smaller of its two sub-nodes, which might help us in finding the solution. We will search for a value that is greater than the smallest value in the tree.

title: Baseball Game
explanation_short: We are given a list of operations for a baseball game, where each operation is either a score or a special command. We need to apply these operations to a record and find the total sum of all scores on the record after all operations have been applied. The output will be the total sum of the scores, which is calculated by applying the given operations in order. The operations can add a score, remove the previous score, double the previous score, or add the sum of the last two scores.

title: Bulb Switcher II
explanation_short: We are given a room with a certain number of bulbs and a limited number of button presses. The goal is to determine the number of unique possible states of the bulbs after using all the allowed presses. Each press can be one of four different buttons, each with its own effect on the bulbs. The input consists of the number of bulbs and the number of presses, and the output is the count of distinct possible bulb statuses.

title: Kth Smallest Number in Multiplication Table
explanation_short: We are given the dimensions of a multiplication table, represented by the integers m and n, and a target position k. Our task is to find the number that appears at the kth smallest position in this table. The input consists of these three integers, and the output will be the kth smallest number in the multiplication table. We need to determine this number without necessarily generating the entire table.

title: 24 Game
explanation_short: We are given four numbers, each between 1 and 9, and we need to use these numbers along with basic math operators like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division to create an expression that equals 24. The expression can also include parentheses to group operations. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to create such an expression using the given numbers. The output will be true if we can create an expression that equals 24, and false otherwise.

title: Reach a Number
explanation_short: We are given a target position on a number line and we need to find the minimum number of moves to reach that position from position 0. The input is the target position, and we want to determine the fewest moves required to get there. The output will be the minimum number of moves needed to reach the target. We can move in a way that allows us to change direction and step size. The goal is to find the shortest sequence of moves to reach the target.

title: Find the Closest Palindrome
explanation_short: We are given a string that represents an integer, and we need to find the closest integer that is a palindrome, excluding the input itself. The closest integer is the one with the smallest absolute difference from the input. Our task is to determine this closest palindrome integer. The output will be a string representing the closest palindrome integer, and if there are multiple closest palindromes, we should return the smaller one.

title: Shortest Completing Word
explanation_short: We are given a string representing a license plate and a list of words. Our task is to find the shortest word in the list that contains all the letters in the license plate, ignoring numbers and spaces, and considering letters as case insensitive. The output will be the shortest word that meets this condition, and if there are multiple shortest words, we return the first one that appears in the list.

title: Prime Number of Set Bits in Binary Representation
explanation_short: We are given two integers, left and right, that define a range of numbers. Our task is to count how many numbers in this range have a binary representation with a prime number of 1's. The output will be the total count of such numbers within the specified range. We need to consider each number in the range, convert it to binary, and determine if the number of 1's is a prime number.

title: Set Intersection Size At Least Two
explanation_short: We are given a collection of integer ranges, where each range includes all integers from a start value to an end value. Our task is to find the smallest set of integers that includes at least two integers from each of these ranges. The output will be the minimum number of integers required in this set. We need to determine the smallest possible size of this set.

title: Toeplitz Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a matrix with a certain number of rows and columns as input. Our task is to determine if this matrix meets a specific condition, where all elements in each diagonal from top-left to bottom-right are the same. We need to examine each diagonal in the matrix to check for consistency in the elements. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether the matrix satisfies this condition or not.

title: Partition Labels
explanation_short: We are given a string and need to divide it into parts such that each letter appears in only one part. The goal is to create as many parts as possible while still following this rule. The input is the string, and the output will be a list of integers representing the size of each part. We want to find the optimal way to split the string into these parts. The resulting parts should be able to be concatenated to form the original string.

title: Couples Holding Hands
explanation_short: We are given a row of seats with people sitting in them, where each person has a unique ID. Our goal is to find the minimum number of swaps needed so that each couple, identified by consecutive IDs, can sit side by side. The input is the arrangement of people in the seats, and the output is the minimum number of swaps required to achieve the desired seating arrangement. We need to determine the fewest number of seat exchanges to get all couples together.

title: Largest Plus Sign
explanation_short: We are given a binary grid of size n x n with some cells marked as 0, representing mines. Our task is to find the largest axis-aligned plus sign of 1's that can be formed within this grid. The input includes the size of the grid and the locations of the mines, and we need to determine the order of the largest plus sign that can be formed. The output will be the order of the largest plus sign, or 0 if no such plus sign exists.

title: Special Binary String
explanation_short: We are given a binary string as input, which is a string consisting only of 1s and 0s. Our goal is to find the lexicographically largest string that can be obtained by swapping consecutive special substrings of the input string. The output will be the largest possible binary string after applying these swap operations. We need to determine the sequence of swaps that will result in the largest string.

title: Reorganize String
explanation_short: We are given a string of characters, and our task is to rearrange these characters so that no two adjacent characters are the same. We need to find a way to reorder the characters to meet this condition. The output will be a rearranged string if it's possible to do so, or an empty string if it's not possible. Our goal is to determine if a valid rearrangement exists and provide it if so.

title: Pyramid Transition Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a string representing the bottom row of blocks and a list of allowed triangular patterns. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to build a pyramid from the bottom row, using the allowed patterns, all the way to the top. The output will be true if the pyramid can be built and false otherwise, indicating whether every triangular pattern in the pyramid matches one in the allowed list.

title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers that represents a mixed-up version of the numbers from 0 to the array length minus 1. Our goal is to divide this array into smaller groups, or chunks, and sort each chunk individually, then combine them to get the fully sorted array. The output will be the largest number of chunks we can create to achieve this sorted result. We need to find the optimal way to split the array to maximize the number of chunks.

title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted II
explanation_short: We are given an integer array as input, and we need to divide it into chunks, sort each chunk individually, and then combine them to get the overall sorted array. Our goal is to find the maximum number of chunks that can be created to achieve this. The output will be the largest possible number of chunks. We want to split the array in a way that results in the most chunks while still producing a sorted array when they are concatenated.

title: Jewels and Stones
explanation_short: We are given two strings, one representing the types of jewels and the other representing the stones we have. Our task is to find out how many of the stones are also jewels. The input consists of these two strings, and the output will be the count of stones that are jewels, considering that letters are case sensitive. We need to compare each stone with the types of jewels to determine the count.

title: K-th Symbol in Grammar
explanation_short: We are given two integers, n and k, which represent the row number and the position of the symbol we need to find in that row. The input is used to generate a table of n rows, where each row is constructed based on the previous row by replacing 0 with 01 and 1 with 10. We need to determine the symbol at the kth position in the nth row. The output will be either 0 or 1, depending on the symbol found at that position.

title: Basic Calculator IV
explanation_short: We are given an algebraic expression and a set of variables with their corresponding values. Our task is to simplify the expression by substituting the given variable values and combining like terms. The input includes the expression and the variable values, and we need to produce a list of simplified terms as output. The goal is to represent the simplified expression in a list format, with each term separated and combined according to the usual order of operations.

title: Reaching Points
explanation_short: We are given two points, a starting point (sx, sy) and a target point (tx, ty), and we need to determine if it's possible to transform the starting point into the target point. The transformation involves changing the point's coordinates using specific rules. Our goal is to find out if this transformation is possible, and if so, we return true; otherwise, we return false. The output will be a simple true or false value indicating whether the transformation is possible.

title: Swim in Rising Water
explanation_short: We are given a grid with elevation values at each point, and water is rising over time. Our goal is to find the minimum time it takes to be able to swim from the top left corner to the bottom right corner of the grid. The water level at time t means any cell with elevation less than or equal to t is reachable. We need to determine the minimum time until a path is available to reach the bottom right square from the top left square.

title: Swap Adjacent in LR String
explanation_short: We are given two strings, a starting string and an ending string, both composed of 'L', 'R', and 'X' characters. Our task is to determine if it's possible to transform the starting string into the ending string by swapping adjacent 'L' and 'X' characters or 'R' and 'X' characters. The output will be a boolean value indicating whether such a transformation is possible. We need to find out if there exists a sequence of these swaps to change the starting string into the ending string.

title: Global and Local Inversions
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers that represents a permutation of numbers from 0 to the array length minus 1. Our task is to compare the number of global inversions, which are pairs of elements in the wrong order, with the number of local inversions, which occur when two adjacent elements are in the wrong order. We need to determine if these two counts are equal. The output will be a boolean value indicating whether the counts match.

title: Sliding Puzzle
explanation_short: We are given a 2x3 puzzle board with tiles labeled 1 to 5 and an empty square represented by 0. Our goal is to find the minimum number of moves required to rearrange the tiles into a specific solved state, where the board looks like [[1,2,3],[4,5,0]]. We need to determine the least number of swaps between the empty square and adjacent tiles to achieve this solved state, or conclude that it's impossible to solve. The output will be the minimum number of moves required, or -1 if it's impossible to solve.

title: Minimum Distance Between BST Nodes
explanation_short: We're given the root of a special tree called a Binary Search Tree, where the input is the tree itself. Our task is to find the smallest difference in values between any two distinct nodes in this tree. The output will be the minimum difference found. We need to examine the tree's nodes and their values to determine this minimum difference. The result will be a single number representing the smallest gap between any two node values.

title: Rabbits in Forest
explanation_short: We are given an array of answers from rabbits, where each answer represents the number of rabbits that have the same color as the one being asked. We need to find the minimum number of rabbits that could be in the forest based on these answers. The output will be the smallest possible total number of rabbits in the forest, considering the given answers. The input array provides clues about the distribution of rabbit colors, and we must use this information to determine the minimum number of rabbits.

title: Transform to Chessboard
explanation_short: We are given a square grid of 0s and 1s. Our goal is to find the minimum number of row or column swaps needed to rearrange the grid so that no two adjacent cells have the same value. The output will be the minimum number of swaps required to achieve this, or -1 if it's impossible. The resulting grid should resemble a chessboard pattern.

title: Letter Case Permutation
explanation_short: We're given a string that contains letters and possibly other characters. Our task is to generate all possible versions of this string where each letter can be either lowercase or uppercase. The output will be a list of all these possible strings, and the order of the strings in the list doesn't matter. We need to consider every possible combination of uppercase and lowercase letters to create these new strings.

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
explanation_short: We are given an undirected graph with a certain number of nodes, and each node is connected to other nodes. Our task is to determine if it's possible to divide the nodes into two groups such that no nodes within the same group are connected to each other. The input is a description of the graph, and the output is a simple "yes" or "no" answer indicating whether the graph can be divided in this way.

title: Rotate String
explanation_short: We are given two strings, s and goal. Our task is to determine if it's possible to transform string s into string goal by shifting characters from the left end of s to the right end. The output will be true if such a transformation is possible and false otherwise. We need to figure out if any number of shifts can make string s identical to string goal.

title: Custom Sort String
explanation_short: We are given two strings, one that represents a custom order and another string that needs to be rearranged. Our goal is to rearrange the characters in the second string so that they follow the same order as the first string. The output will be a rearranged version of the second string, where characters that appear earlier in the custom order string come before characters that appear later. Characters not present in the custom order can appear anywhere in the output string.

title: K-th Smallest Prime Fraction
explanation_short: We are given a sorted array of unique integers, including 1 and prime numbers, along with an integer k. Our task is to find the k-th smallest fraction that can be formed by dividing any two numbers in the array. The output will be an array containing the numerator and denominator of this k-th smallest fraction. We need to consider all possible fractions that can be formed from the given array and determine the one at the k-th position when arranged in ascending order.

title: Escape The Ghosts
explanation_short: We are given a starting point, a destination point, and the positions of several ghosts on a 2-D grid. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to reach the destination before any of the ghosts can catch up to us, considering that both we and the ghosts can move in any of the four cardinal directions or stay still each turn. The input includes the destination point and the ghosts' positions, and the output is a boolean value indicating whether an escape is possible. We need to find out if there's a way to evade the ghosts and reach the target safely.

title: Number of Subarrays with Bounded Maximum
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and two boundary values, left and right. Our task is to find the number of subarrays within the given array where the maximum value falls within the range of left to right. The input includes the array and the two boundary values, and the output will be the count of such subarrays. We need to consider all possible contiguous non-empty subarrays to determine the total count.

title: Number of Matching Subsequences
explanation_short: We are given a string and a list of words. Our task is to find out how many of these words can be formed by removing some characters from the given string, while keeping the remaining characters in the same order. The input is the string and the list of words, and the output is the count of words that can be formed in this way. We need to determine which words are subsequences of the given string.

title: Domino and Tromino Tiling
explanation_short: We are given an integer n, representing the length of a 2 x n board. Our task is to find the number of ways to cover this board using 2 x 1 dominoes and trominoes, allowing rotations. The goal is to count all possible unique tilings, where every square on the board is covered by a tile. The result should be returned as the number of ways to tile the board, adjusted to fit within a large modulus to handle very large answers.

title: Preimage Size of Factorial Zeroes Function
explanation_short: We are given an integer k, which represents the number of zeroes at the end of a factorial. Our task is to find the number of non-negative integers x that have exactly k zeroes at the end of their factorial. The output will be the count of such integers x. We need to determine how many values of x satisfy this condition for a given k.

title: Valid Tic-Tac-Toe State
explanation_short: We are given a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe board as input, represented as a string array with ' ', 'X', and 'O' characters. Our task is to determine if the given board position can be reached during a valid game of Tic-Tac-Toe, following the standard rules of the game. The output will be a boolean value indicating whether the board state is valid or not. We need to consider the rules of Tic-Tac-Toe, such as turn order and possible moves, to make this determination.

title: Rotated Digits
explanation_short: We are given a range of numbers from 1 to a certain number n. Our task is to find how many numbers in this range are considered "good", meaning they change into a valid and different number when each digit is rotated 180 degrees. The output will be the count of these good numbers within the given range. We need to consider which digits remain valid after rotation and which numbers meet the criteria.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
explanation_short: We are given a list of flights between cities, each with a specific cost, and we need to find the cheapest way to travel from one city to another with a limited number of stops. The input includes the list of flights, the starting city, the destination city, and the maximum number of stops allowed. Our goal is to determine the lowest cost to travel from the starting city to the destination city within the given stop limit. The output will be the cheapest price if such a route exists, or -1 if it's not possible.

title: All Paths From Source to Target
explanation_short: We are given a directed graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1, where each node has a list of nodes it can connect to. Our task is to find all possible paths that start at node 0 and end at node n - 1. The output will be a list of all these paths, in any order, where each path is a sequence of node numbers. We need to explore the graph to identify all valid paths from the starting node to the target node.

title: Smallest Rotation with Highest Score
explanation_short: We are given an array of numbers and the ability to rotate it by any non-negative integer. Our goal is to find the rotation that results in the highest score, where a score is calculated by counting the number of entries that are less than or equal to their index after rotation. The output will be the smallest rotation index that achieves this highest score.

title: Unique Morse Code Words
explanation_short: We are given an array of words, where each word can be translated into Morse code. Our task is to find out how many unique Morse code translations exist among all the given words. The input is an array of strings, and the output will be the number of different Morse code transformations. We need to determine the count of unique translations by converting each word into its Morse code equivalent.

title: Champagne Tower
explanation_short: We are given a pyramid of glasses and a certain amount of champagne poured into the top glass. The champagne flows down the pyramid, filling each glass and overflowing into the glasses below. We need to find out how full a specific glass is after the champagne has been poured. The input is the amount of champagne poured and the location of the glass we're interested in, and the output is the amount of champagne in that glass.

title: Number of Lines To Write String
explanation_short: We are given a string of lowercase letters and the width of each letter in pixels. We need to write this string across multiple lines, with each line limited to 100 pixels, and determine the total number of lines and the width of the last line. The input includes the string and the widths of the letters, and the output will be an array with two values: the number of lines and the width of the last line.

title: Max Increase to Keep City Skyline
explanation_short: We are given a city layout represented as a grid of building heights. Our goal is to find the maximum total increase in building heights that can be made without changing the city's skyline when viewed from any direction. The input is the grid of building heights, and the output is the maximum total sum that the heights can be increased by. We need to determine how much each building can be increased in height while preserving the city's skyline.

title: Chalkboard XOR Game
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers on a chalkboard, and two players, Alice and Bob, take turns removing one number at a time. The goal is to determine if Alice will win the game, where a player loses if they make the total XOR of the remaining numbers equal to 0, or wins if the total XOR is 0 at the start of their turn. We need to find out if Alice can win the game, assuming both players play perfectly. The input is the list of numbers, and the output is a simple "yes" or "no" indicating whether Alice wins.

title: Split Array With Same Average
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers and need to divide it into two non-empty groups, A and B. Our goal is to make the average of the numbers in A equal to the average of the numbers in B. The input is the array of integers, and the output is a simple yes or no, indicating whether it's possible to achieve this equal average split. We need to determine if such a division is possible based on the given array.

title: Minimum Swaps To Make Sequences Increasing
explanation_short: We are given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, of the same length. Our goal is to find the minimum number of swap operations needed to make both arrays strictly increasing. The input consists of these two arrays, and the output will be the minimum number of swaps required. We need to determine the fewest swaps necessary to ensure that each array is strictly increasing, meaning each element is greater than the previous one.

title: Find Eventual Safe States
explanation_short: We are given a directed graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1, and each node has a list of adjacent nodes it connects to. Our task is to identify the "safe" nodes, which are nodes where every possible path leads to a terminal node (a node with no outgoing edges) or another safe node. We need to return a list of all these safe nodes in ascending order. The input is the graph structure, and the output is a sorted list of safe node indices.

title: Bricks Falling When Hit
explanation_short: We are given a grid representing bricks and empty spaces, along with a sequence of locations to erase bricks. Our task is to determine the number of bricks that will fall after each erasure, considering that a brick is stable if it's connected to the top or adjacent to another stable brick. The output will be an array where each element represents the number of bricks that fall after each erasure. We need to find this output array based on the given grid and sequence of erasures.

title: Soup Servings
explanation_short: We are given two soups, A and B, each with a certain amount of liquid. We need to find the probability that soup A is used up before soup B, considering that there are four possible serving operations that can be chosen at random. The output is the calculated probability, taking into account the scenarios where both soups are used up at the same time. The input is the initial amount of liquid in each soup, represented by the variable n.

title: Subdomain Visit Count
explanation_short: We are given a list of domains with their visit counts. Our task is to find the visit counts for each subdomain within these domains. The input is a list of strings representing the domains and their visit counts, and the output will be a list of strings representing the visit counts for each subdomain. We need to break down the given domains into their subdomains and calculate the total visit count for each subdomain.

title: Expressive Words
explanation_short: We are given a string and a list of query words. Our task is to determine how many of these query words can be transformed into the given string by repeating characters in groups to match the string's pattern. The output will be the count of query words that can be stretched to match the given string.

title: Largest Triangle Area
explanation_short: We are given a set of points on a plane, each with x and y coordinates. Our task is to find the largest possible area of a triangle that can be formed using any three of these points. The input is a list of points, and we need to calculate the maximum area that can be achieved. The output will be the area of the largest triangle.

title: Binary Tree Pruning
explanation_short: We're given the root of a binary tree as input. Our task is to remove every subtree that doesn't contain the value 1, and return the resulting tree. The output will be the modified binary tree with all subtrees not containing a 1 removed. We need to identify which subtrees meet the condition and prune the tree accordingly.

title: Linked List Components
explanation_short: We're given a linked list with unique integers and a subset of those integers in an array. Our task is to find the number of connected components in the array, where two values are connected if they appear one after the other in the linked list. The input consists of the linked list and the array, and the output will be the count of these connected components. We need to analyze the linked list and the array to determine which values are connected and group them accordingly. The result will be the total number of these connected groups.

title: Most Common Word
explanation_short: We are given a string of text and a list of banned words. Our task is to find the most frequently occurring word in the text that is not on the banned list. The input text is case-insensitive and punctuation is ignored. We need to return this most common non-banned word in lowercase as the output.

title: Bus Routes
explanation_short: We are given a list of bus routes and two bus stops, a source and a target. Our task is to find the minimum number of buses we need to take to travel from the source to the target. The input includes the bus routes and the source and target stops, and the output will be the least number of buses required to make the trip, or -1 if it's not possible. We need to determine the most efficient way to use the buses to get from the source to the target.

title: Ambiguous Coordinates
explanation_short: We are given a string of digits that originally represented 2-dimensional coordinates, but had all commas, decimal points, and spaces removed. Our task is to find all possible original coordinate representations that could have produced this string. We need to consider all valid ways to insert commas, decimal points, and spaces back into the string. The output will be a list of strings representing these possible original coordinates, with each coordinate having exactly one space between the numbers.

title: Largest Sum of Averages
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a number k, representing the maximum number of groups we can divide the array into. Our task is to find the best way to divide the array into at most k groups, where each group's score is the average of its numbers, and the total score is the sum of these averages. The goal is to achieve the highest total score possible. The output will be the maximum total score we can get from all possible divisions of the array.

title: Race Car
explanation_short: We are given a target position on an infinite number line and a car that starts at position 0 with a speed of +1. The car can move according to a sequence of instructions to accelerate or reverse. We need to find the shortest sequence of these instructions to reach the target position. The output will be the length of this shortest sequence.

title: Card Flipping Game
explanation_short: We are given two lists of numbers representing the front and back of cards. Our task is to flip some or all of the cards to find the smallest number that appears face down on at least one card and not face up on any card. The output will be this minimum number, or 0 if no such number exists. We need to consider all possible combinations of flipped cards to achieve this.

title: Short Encoding of Words
explanation_short: We are given a list of words as input, and we need to find the shortest possible string that can be used to encode all these words. The encoding involves creating a reference string where each word is represented as a substring followed by a special character. Our goal is to determine the length of this shortest reference string. The output will be the length of the shortest possible encoding string.

title: Goat Latin
explanation_short: We're given a sentence with multiple words, and our task is to convert it into a made-up language called Goat Latin. The input sentence consists of words separated by spaces, containing only lowercase and uppercase letters. We need to apply certain rules to transform each word and then combine them to form the final sentence. The output will be the converted sentence in Goat Latin. Our goal is to determine the correct transformation of the input sentence.

title: Binary Trees With Factors
explanation_short: We are given an array of unique integers, all greater than 1. Our task is to find the number of possible binary trees that can be created using these integers, where each non-leaf node's value is the product of its children's values. We need to count all possible combinations, considering that each number can be used multiple times. The result should be the total count of such binary trees, adjusted to fit within a specific numerical range by taking the result modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Friends Of Appropriate Ages
explanation_short: We are given a list of ages of people on a social media website. Our task is to determine the total number of friend requests made, considering certain conditions that restrict who can send a request to whom. The input is a list of ages, and the output is the total count of friend requests. We need to find a way to calculate this count based on the given conditions. The result will be the total number of friend requests made among all the people.

title: Shortest Distance to a Character
explanation_short: We are given a string and a specific character that appears in the string. Our task is to find the shortest distance from each position in the string to the nearest occurrence of the specified character. The output will be an array of integers, where each integer represents the distance from the corresponding position in the string to the closest occurrence of the character. The distance is calculated as the absolute difference between the two positions.

title: Most Profit Assigning Work
explanation_short: We are given three lists: the difficulty of each job, the profit of each job, and the skills of each worker. Our goal is to assign jobs to workers in a way that maximizes the total profit, considering that each worker can only do one job, but each job can be done multiple times. The input includes these three lists, and the output will be the maximum possible total profit that can be achieved. We need to find the best way to match workers with jobs to get the highest profit. The result will be a single number representing the maximum achievable profit.

title: Count Unique Characters of All Substrings of a Given String
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to find the sum of unique characters in all possible substrings of this string. The output will be the total count of unique characters across all substrings. We need to consider every substring, including repeated ones, and calculate the number of unique characters in each. The result will be a sum of these unique character counts.

title: Consecutive Numbers Sum
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer n as input. Our task is to find the number of different ways we can express n as a sum of consecutive positive integers. The output will be the total count of these different ways. We need to consider all possible combinations of consecutive integers that add up to n. The result will be the total number of valid combinations.

title: Flipping an Image
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix image with the same number of rows and columns. Our task is to perform two operations on this image: first, flip it horizontally by reversing each row, and then invert it by swapping all 0s with 1s and vice versa. The result will be a new binary matrix image after these operations have been applied. The input is the original image, and the output is the resulting image after flipping and inverting.

title: Making A Large Island
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix where each cell is either 0 or 1, representing water or land. Our goal is to find the size of the largest island that can be formed by changing at most one water cell to a land cell. The island is defined as a group of connected land cells, and we need to determine the maximum size of the island after applying this change. The output will be the size of the largest island.

title: Positions of Large Groups
explanation_short: We are given a string of lowercase letters where the same characters appear together in groups. Our task is to identify the groups that have 3 or more characters and find their start and end indices in the string. The output will be a list of these large groups' intervals, sorted by their start index. We need to examine the string to determine which groups meet the size criteria. The result will be a collection of intervals representing the large groups.

title: Find And Replace in String
explanation_short: We are given a string and three parallel arrays representing replacement operations. The input includes the original string, the positions where replacements should occur, the substrings to be replaced, and their corresponding replacements. We need to find the resulting string after applying all these replacement operations simultaneously. The output will be the modified string with all replacements made.

title: Masking Personal Information
explanation_short: We are given a string representing either an email address or a phone number. Our task is to mask this personal information according to specific rules, which involve modifying the input string to hide sensitive details. The output will be the masked version of the input string, with the rules applied to either the email address or phone number. We need to determine whether the input is an email or phone number and apply the corresponding masking rules. The goal is to produce a modified string that protects the personal information.

title: Rectangle Overlap
explanation_short: We are given two rectangles, each defined by the coordinates of its bottom-left and top-right corners. Our task is to determine whether these two rectangles overlap, meaning they have a common area. To do this, we need to analyze the positions and dimensions of the rectangles. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether an overlap exists. We are looking for a way to compare the rectangles' boundaries to make this determination.

title: Push Dominoes
explanation_short: We are given a string representing the initial state of dominoes, where each character shows whether a domino is falling to the right, left, or is upright. Our task is to determine the final state of the dominoes after they have all been pushed and the forces have balanced out. The output will be a string showing the final state of each domino. We need to consider how the forces of falling dominoes interact with each other and with upright dominoes. The goal is to find the resulting state of all dominoes after these interactions.

title: New 21 Game
explanation_short: We are given the maximum number of points Alice can gain in one draw, the target number of points she needs to reach or exceed to stop drawing, and the maximum number of points we want her to have. We need to find the probability that Alice will have a certain number of points or fewer after she stops drawing. The input includes the maximum points per draw, the target points to stop, and the maximum allowed points. The output is the probability of Alice having the specified number of points or fewer.

title: Sum of Distances in Tree
explanation_short: We are given a tree with a certain number of nodes and the connections between them. Our task is to find the total distance from each node to all other nodes in the tree. The input includes the number of nodes and the connections between them, and the output will be an array where each value represents the sum of distances from the corresponding node to all other nodes. The goal is to calculate these sums for all nodes in the tree.

title: Image Overlap
explanation_short: We are given two square images represented as binary matrices of the same size. Our task is to find the largest possible overlap between these two images by sliding one image over the other in any direction. The input consists of two binary matrices, and we need to determine the maximum number of positions where both images have a 1 after sliding one image. The output will be the size of this largest overlap.

title: Similar String Groups
explanation_short: We are given a list of strings where each string is an anagram of every other string. Our task is to find the number of groups that can be formed based on string similarity, where two strings are similar if they are identical or can be made equivalent by swapping at most two letters. The output will be the total count of these groups. We need to determine how many connected groups exist based on the similarity rule. The result will be an integer representing the number of groups.

title: Magic Squares In Grid
explanation_short: We are given a grid of integers with a certain number of rows and columns. Our task is to find the number of 3x3 subgrids within this grid that are "magic squares", meaning each row, column, and diagonal has the same sum. The input grid can contain numbers up to 15, but a magic square can only have distinct numbers from 1 to 9. We need to count how many of these magic square subgrids exist in the given grid. The output will be the total count of such subgrids.

title: Keys and Rooms
explanation_short: We are given a set of rooms, where each room may contain keys to unlock other rooms. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to visit all the rooms, starting from room 0, which is the only unlocked room. We need to find out if we can collect enough keys to unlock all the other rooms. The output will be true if we can visit all the rooms and false otherwise.

title: Split Array into Fibonacci Sequence
explanation_short: We're given a string of digits, and we need to split it into a sequence of numbers where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, similar to a Fibonacci sequence. The input string can be divided into parts, but each part must be a valid number without extra leading zeroes. Our goal is to find such a sequence or determine if it's impossible. The output will be a list of numbers representing the sequence, or an empty list if no valid sequence can be found.

title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
explanation_short: We are given a special kind of array where the numbers first go up and then come back down, with a peak in the middle. Our task is to find the position of this peak in the array. The input is the array itself, and the output is the index of the peak element. We need to find this peak index efficiently, using a method that can handle large arrays quickly.

title: Shifting Letters
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase letters and an array of shift amounts. Our task is to apply these shifts to the string, where each shift amount corresponds to shifting a portion of the string a certain number of times. The goal is to determine the final string after all shifts have been applied. The output will be the resulting string after these shifts.

title: Longest Mountain in Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our task is to find the longest subarray within this array that forms a "mountain" - meaning it increases and then decreases. The output will be the length of this longest mountain subarray, or 0 if no such subarray exists. We need to examine the array to identify the longest sequence that meets the mountain criteria.

title: Loud and Rich
explanation_short: We are given information about a group of people, including how much money they have and their level of quietness, as well as comparisons of who has more money than whom. We need to find the least quiet person among those who have equal to or more money than each individual. The output will be an array where each element corresponds to the least quiet person who has more money than the person at that index. The goal is to determine this quietest person for each individual in the group.

title: Backspace String Compare
explanation_short: We are given two strings, s and t, that contain characters and a special backspace character '#'. Our task is to determine if the strings are equal after processing the backspace characters. The input strings can contain any combination of characters and '#', and we need to find a way to compare them after applying the backspace operations. The output will be true if the processed strings are equal and false otherwise.

title: Rectangle Area II
explanation_short: We are given a collection of rectangles, each defined by the coordinates of its bottom-left and top-right corners. Our task is to calculate the total area covered by all these rectangles, making sure to count any overlapping areas only once. The input is a 2D array of rectangle coordinates, and we need to find the total covered area. The output will be this total area, returned modulo 10^9 + 7 to handle large results.

title: Guess the Word
explanation_short: We are given a list of unique six-letter words and a secret word that is one of them. Our task is to find the secret word by guessing words from the list, with a limited number of guesses allowed. We will get feedback on each guess in the form of the number of matching letters. Our goal is to guess the secret word correctly within the allowed number of guesses.

title: Mirror Reflection
explanation_short: We are given a square room with mirrors on each wall and receptors on three corners, along with the room's size and where a laser beam first hits the east wall. Our goal is to determine which receptor the laser beam meets first after being reflected off the mirrors. The input consists of two integers representing the room's size and the initial laser beam position, and the output is the number of the receptor that the beam meets first.

title: Prime Palindrome
explanation_short: We are given an integer as input and need to find the smallest number that is both prime and a palindrome, and is greater than or equal to the input number. A prime number is one that has only two divisors, 1 and itself, and a palindrome is a number that reads the same forwards and backwards. Our task is to find this special number. The output will be the smallest prime palindrome that meets the condition. We need to search for this number starting from the input number.

title: Advantage Shuffle
explanation_short: We are given two lists of numbers, nums1 and nums2, that are the same length. Our goal is to rearrange the numbers in nums1 to maximize the number of times a number in nums1 is greater than the corresponding number in nums2. The output will be a rearranged version of nums1 that achieves this maximum advantage. We need to find the best way to match up the numbers in nums1 with the numbers in nums2 to get the most advantages. The result will be a new list of numbers that is a permutation of nums1.

title: Leaf-Similar Trees
explanation_short: We are given two binary trees, represented by their root nodes root1 and root2. Our task is to determine if the sequence of leaf node values in both trees is the same when read from left to right. The input consists of the two trees, and the output will be a boolean value indicating whether the trees are leaf-similar or not. We need to compare the leaf value sequences of the two trees to find the answer.

title: Reordered Power of 2
explanation_short: We are given an integer as input and need to determine if its digits can be rearranged to form a power of two. The rearranged number must not start with zero. Our goal is to find out if such a rearrangement is possible. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether the rearranged number can be a power of two.

title: Smallest Subtree with all the Deepest Nodes
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree, and we need to find the smallest subtree that contains all the deepest nodes. The deepest nodes are those with the largest distance from the root. Our goal is to identify this smallest subtree and return its nodes. The output will be the values of the nodes in the smallest subtree that contains all the deepest nodes.

title: Binary Gap
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer as input, and we need to find the longest distance between any two adjacent 1's in its binary representation. The distance is calculated as the absolute difference between the bit positions of the two 1's. Our goal is to determine this longest distance. If no such adjacent 1's exist, the output will be 0. The result will be the maximum distance found between any two adjacent 1's in the binary form of the input number.

title: Length of Longest Fibonacci Subsequence
explanation_short: We are given a strictly increasing array of positive integers. Our task is to find the length of the longest subsequence within this array that follows a Fibonacci-like pattern, where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones. The output will be the length of this longest Fibonacci-like subsequence, or 0 if no such subsequence exists. We need to examine the input array to identify the longest sequence that meets this condition.

title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a target sum, and we need to find the shortest subarray within this array that has a sum of at least the target. The input includes the array and the target sum, and the output will be the length of this shortest subarray. If no such subarray exists, the output will be -1, indicating that it's not possible to find a subarray with the required sum. We are looking for the shortest contiguous part of the array that meets this condition.

title: Buddy Strings
explanation_short: We are given two strings, s and goal. Our task is to determine if it's possible to swap two characters in the string s to make it identical to the string goal. The output will be true if such a swap is possible and false otherwise. We need to find out if there are two characters in s that can be exchanged to match the goal string.

title: Transpose Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a 2D array of integers, known as a matrix, as the input. Our task is to flip this matrix over its main diagonal, effectively swapping its rows and columns. The output will be a new 2D array representing the flipped matrix. We need to find a way to transform the input matrix into this new arrangement. The resulting output matrix will have the original rows as columns and vice versa.

title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
explanation_short: We're given a binary tree, a target node, and a distance k. Our task is to find all nodes in the tree that are exactly k steps away from the target node. The input includes the tree's structure, the target node's value, and the distance k, and we need to output an array of values of the nodes that meet this condition. The output can be in any order, and if no nodes are found at the specified distance, an empty array is returned.

title: Maximize Distance to Closest Person
explanation_short: We are given a row of seats where some seats are occupied by people and some are empty. Our goal is to find the maximum distance Alex can be from the closest person when he sits in one of the empty seats. The input is an array representing the row of seats, and the output is the maximum distance to the closest person. We need to determine where Alex should sit to achieve this maximum distance. The result will be the largest possible distance between Alex and the nearest person.

title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
explanation_short: We are given a car's starting fuel, a target destination, and a list of gas stations with their positions and fuel capacities. Our goal is to determine the minimum number of times the car needs to stop and refuel to reach its destination. The car uses one liter of gas per mile and can refuel at gas stations, and we need to find the minimum number of refueling stops required to reach the target, or return -1 if it's impossible. The output will be the minimum number of refueling stops or -1 if the destination cannot be reached.

title: Score After Flipping Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix with rows and columns that can be flipped, meaning all 0's become 1's and all 1's become 0's. Our goal is to find the highest possible score that can be achieved by flipping any number of rows or columns. The score is calculated by interpreting each row as a binary number and summing them up. We need to determine the optimal flips to maximize this score. The output will be the maximum achievable score.

title: Lemonade Change
explanation_short: We are given a sequence of bills that customers pay with to buy lemonade, which costs $5. Our task is to determine if we can provide the correct change to each customer using the bills we've already collected. The input is a list of bills, and we need to find out if we can make the correct change for each customer. The output will be true if we can provide the correct change to all customers, and false otherwise.

title: Car Fleet
explanation_short: We are given the starting positions and speeds of multiple cars traveling towards a target mile. Our task is to determine how many groups of cars, or "car fleets," will arrive at the destination, considering that a car cannot pass another but can catch up and travel alongside it. The input consists of the target mile, the starting positions, and the speeds of the cars. We need to find the number of car fleets that will arrive at the target mile. The output will be the count of these car fleets.

title: Walking Robot Simulation
explanation_short: We are given an array of commands that a robot needs to execute on an infinite XY-plane, starting from point (0, 0) facing north. The robot's movement is restricted by obstacles on the grid, and if it encounters one, it will stay at its current location and move on to the next command. Our task is to find the maximum squared Euclidean distance the robot reaches from the origin at any point in its path. The input includes the sequence of commands and the locations of obstacles, and the output is the maximum squared distance achieved. We need to determine how the robot's position changes based on the commands and obstacles to calculate this distance.

title: Middle of the Linked List
explanation_short: We are given a singly linked list as input, and we need to find the middle node of this list. If the list has an even number of nodes, we should return the second middle node. Our task is to identify this middle node and return it as the output. The output will be a part of the linked list starting from the middle node to the end.

title: Uncommon Words from Two Sentences
explanation_short: We are given two sentences, each containing words separated by spaces. Our task is to identify the words that appear only once in one of the sentences and not at all in the other sentence. The input consists of these two sentences, and we need to find these unique words. The output will be a list of all such uncommon words from both sentences.

title: Stone Game
explanation_short: We are given a row of piles with different numbers of stones. Our goal is to determine if Alice will win the game, assuming both Alice and Bob play optimally, by taking turns removing piles from either end of the row. The input is the number of stones in each pile, and the output is a boolean indicating whether Alice wins or not. We need to figure out who will end up with the most stones after all piles have been removed.

title: Boats to Save People
explanation_short: We are given a list of people with different weights and a maximum weight limit for each boat. Our goal is to find the minimum number of boats required to transport all the people, with each boat carrying one or two people at a time, as long as the total weight does not exceed the limit. The input consists of the list of people's weights and the weight limit, and the output is the minimum number of boats needed to transport everyone. We need to determine how to pair the people and allocate them to boats efficiently. The result will be the smallest possible number of boats required.

title: Fair Candy Swap
explanation_short: We are given two lists of candy box sizes, one for Alice and one for Bob, and we need to find two boxes, one from each list, to swap so that Alice and Bob have the same total amount of candy. The input is the two lists of candy box sizes, and the output is a list containing the sizes of the two boxes to be swapped. Our goal is to make the total amount of candy Alice has equal to the total amount of candy Bob has after the swap. We need to find the right combination of boxes to achieve this balance.

title: Nth Magical Number
explanation_short: We are given three integers: n, a, and b, where a and b are used to determine if a number is magical. A number is considered magical if it can be divided by either a or b. We need to find the nth number that meets this magical condition. The result should be the nth magical number, and because it could be very large, we'll provide the answer modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Projection Area of 3D Shapes
explanation_short: We are given a grid representing towers of cubes, where each cell's value indicates the number of cubes stacked on it. Our task is to calculate the total area of the projections of these cubes when viewed from the top, front, and side. The input is a 2D grid of cube tower heights, and we need to find the total area of the three projections. The output will be the sum of the areas of these projections.

title: Decoded String at Index
explanation_short: We are given an encoded string and an integer k. Our task is to decode the string by following specific steps and then find the kth letter in the decoded string. The input includes the encoded string and the integer k, and the output will be the kth letter in the decoded string. We need to figure out how to properly decode the string and then locate the desired letter. The goal is to return the correct letter based on the given input and decoding rules.

title: Super Egg Drop
explanation_short: We are given a certain number of identical eggs and a building with a specific number of floors. Our goal is to find the minimum number of moves required to determine the highest floor from which an egg can be dropped without breaking. The input consists of the number of eggs and the number of floors, and the output is the minimum number of moves needed to find this critical floor. We need to consider the optimal strategy for dropping the eggs to achieve this goal.

title: Koko Eating Bananas
explanation_short: We are given several piles of bananas with different quantities and a time limit of h hours. Koko needs to determine her optimal eating speed, measured in bananas per hour, to finish all the bananas within the given time frame. The goal is to find the minimum eating speed that allows her to consume all the bananas before the time runs out. The input includes the number of bananas in each pile and the time limit, and the output is the minimum eating speed required.

title: Profitable Schemes
explanation_short: We are given a group of members and a list of crimes with their respective profits and required participants. Our goal is to find the number of subsets of these crimes that generate a certain minimum profit and do not exceed the total number of members. The input includes the number of members, the minimum required profit, and the details of each crime. We need to calculate the total number of such subsets, known as profitable schemes, and return this count modulo a large number to avoid overflow.

title: Reachable Nodes In Subdivided Graph
explanation_short: We are given an undirected graph with nodes and edges, where each edge can be subdivided into multiple new nodes and edges. Our task is to find the number of nodes that can be reached from node 0 within a certain number of moves, called maxMoves, in the new graph after all edges have been subdivided. The input includes the original graph and the maximum number of moves allowed, and the output is the count of reachable nodes. The graph is modified by replacing each edge with a chain of new nodes and edges based on a specified count for each edge.

title: Spiral Matrix III
explanation_short: We are given a grid with a specific number of rows and columns, and a starting position. Our task is to traverse the grid in a clockwise spiral shape, visiting every position, and keep track of the order in which we visit them. The input includes the grid size and the starting position, and we need to find the sequence of coordinates that represents the order of visited positions. The output will be an array of these coordinates.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Postorder Traversal
explanation_short: We are given two lists of numbers, representing the preorder and postorder traversal of a binary tree. Our task is to use these lists to reconstruct the original binary tree. The input lists contain the values of the nodes in the tree, and the output will be the reconstructed binary tree itself, which can be represented in a specific format. We need to figure out how to use the given lists to determine the structure of the tree. The output tree should have the same values as the input lists, but in the correct hierarchical order.

title: Monotonic Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our task is to determine whether this array is either increasing or decreasing in order. We need to examine the array to find out if it meets either of these conditions. The output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether the array is monotonic or not.

title: Sort Array By Parity
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers as input, and our task is to rearrange them so that all the even numbers come first, followed by all the odd numbers. The order of the even and odd numbers themselves doesn't matter, as long as all the evens are before all the odds. Our goal is to produce an array that meets this condition. The output will be a rearranged version of the input array, with all even integers at the beginning and all odd integers at the end.

title: Fruit Into Baskets
explanation_short: We are given a row of fruit trees, each represented by a type of fruit. Our goal is to collect the maximum amount of fruit possible while following certain rules. The input is an array of fruit types, and we need to determine the largest number of fruits that can be picked. The output will be the maximum number of fruits that can be collected. We must find a way to navigate the array to achieve this maximum amount.

title: Groups of Special-Equivalent Strings
explanation_short: We are given a list of strings, all of the same length. Our task is to group these strings based on whether they can be made identical by swapping certain characters. We need to find the total number of these groups. The output will be the count of unique groups of strings that can be transformed into each other.

title: Valid Permutations for DI Sequence
explanation_short: We are given a string of length n, where each character is either 'D' or 'I'. Our task is to find the number of valid permutations of n + 1 integers, where a permutation is considered valid if it satisfies certain conditions based on the input string. The output will be the count of such valid permutations, and since this count can be large, we need to return it modulo 10^9 + 7. We need to consider all possible permutations and determine which ones meet the specified criteria.

title: Find and Replace Pattern
explanation_short: We are given a list of words and a pattern string. Our task is to find the words that match the given pattern by replacing each letter in the pattern with another letter, ensuring that no two letters map to the same letter. The output will be a list of words that match the pattern. We need to determine which words can be transformed into the pattern by rearranging the letters. The result can be returned in any order.

title: Online Stock Span
explanation_short: We're given a stream of daily stock prices, and for each day, we need to find the maximum number of consecutive days leading up to the current day where the price was less than or equal to the current day's price. Our goal is to design a system that can efficiently process these daily prices and calculate this span. The input is a series of daily stock prices, and the output is the span of the stock's price for each day. We'll use this information to implement a class that can handle these calculations.

title: All Possible Full Binary Trees
explanation_short: We are given an integer representing the number of nodes in a binary tree. Our task is to generate all possible full binary trees with the given number of nodes, where each node has a value of 0 and either 0 or 2 children. The output will be a list of root nodes, each representing a unique full binary tree. We need to find all possible combinations of nodes that satisfy the conditions of a full binary tree. The resulting list of trees can be in any order.

title: Maximum Frequency Stack
explanation_short: We are given a sequence of elements to push onto a stack. Our task is to design a data structure that can push these elements and then pop the most frequent element from the stack. The input will be a series of push and pop operations, and we need to determine the correct order of popped elements. The output will be the elements popped from the stack in the correct order, with the most frequent element popped first in case of a tie.

title: Sum of Subsequence Widths
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our task is to find the sum of the widths of all possible non-empty subsequences that can be formed from this array, where the width is the difference between the maximum and minimum elements in a subsequence. The output will be this sum, but since it can be very large, we need to return it modulo 10^9 + 7. We need to consider all possible subsequences, including those with one or more elements.

title: Super Palindromes
explanation_short: We are given two positive integers as strings, representing a range from left to right. Our task is to find the number of integers within this range that are both palindromes and the square of a palindrome. We need to count these special numbers, known as super-palindromes, and return the total count as the output. The input range is inclusive, meaning we should consider both the left and right boundaries when searching for super-palindromes.

title: Surface Area of 3D Shapes
explanation_short: We are given a grid representing towers of cubes, where each cell's value indicates the number of cubes stacked on it. Our task is to find the total surface area of the 3D shapes formed when adjacent cubes are glued together. The input is a 2D grid of cube tower heights, and the output is the total surface area of the resulting shapes, including the bottom face of each shape. We need to calculate the surface area by considering all exposed faces of the cubes.

title: Numbers At Most N Given Digit Set
explanation_short: We are given a set of digits and a number n. Our task is to find how many positive integers can be formed using these digits, with each digit allowed to be used any number of times, such that the formed integers are less than or equal to n. title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our task is to find the sum of the minimum values of all possible subarrays that can be formed from this array. The output will be the total sum of these minimum values, and since the sum can be large, we need to return it modulo 10^9 + 7. We need to consider every contiguous subarray and find its minimum value to calculate the total sum.

title: Smallest Range I
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers and a number k. Our goal is to find the smallest possible difference between the largest and smallest numbers in the list after potentially changing some of the numbers. The input list and the number k are the starting points, and the output will be the smallest achievable difference. We need to determine how to adjust the numbers to achieve this smallest difference.
