explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to divide it into two parts, left and right, where these parts are next to each other in the array. title: Reverse Only Letters
explanation_short: We are given a string as input, and our task is to reverse the order of the letters in the string. Our goal is to produce the modified string as output, where the letters are in reverse order. The output will be a string with the same characters as the input, but with the letters rearranged.

title: Snakes and Ladders
explanation_short: We are given a square board with numbered cells, some of which have snakes or ladders that lead to other cells. The input is the board layout, and the output is the least number of rolls required to reach the final cell, or -1 if it's impossible. title: Smallest Range II
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers and a number k. Our task is to find the smallest possible difference between the largest and smallest numbers in the list after we've been allowed to modify each number by up to k. The input list and the number k will help us determine the best modifications to make. The output will be the smallest possible difference between the largest and smallest modified numbers.

The output will be a simple "yes" or "no" answer, indicating whether the cards can be partitioned in this way.

title: Sort an Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers, and our task is to arrange these numbers in ascending order. title: Word Subsets
explanation_short: We are given two lists of words, and we need to find the words from the first list that contain all the letters of every word in the second list, considering the frequency of each letter. title: Online Election
explanation_short: We are given two lists: one containing the people who received votes and another containing the times when those votes were cast. Our task is to determine who was leading the election at a given time. We need to consider all votes cast up to that time and, in case of a tie, choose the person who received the most recent vote. The output will be the person leading the election at the specified time.

title: Cat and Mouse
explanation_short: We are given an undirected graph where two players, Mouse and Cat, take turns moving along the edges. title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
explanation_short: We are given a string of parentheses as input, and our goal is to determine the minimum number of parentheses that need to be added to make the string valid. The output will be the count of these additional parentheses.

title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray

title: Complete Binary Tree Inserter

title: Sort Array By Parity II
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers with an equal number of odd and even numbers. title: Flip String to Monotone Increasing
explanation_short: We are given a binary string, which is a string consisting of only 0's and 1's. Our task is to find the minimum number of changes, or "flips", needed to make the string monotone increasing, meaning it starts with some number of 0's followed by some number of 1's. title: Unique Email Addresses
explanation_short: We are given a list of email addresses where each address may contain special characters like '.' or '+'. title: Beautiful Array
explanation_short: We are given an integer n, which represents the length of an array. Our task is to create an array of this length that meets certain conditions, making it a "beautiful array". title: Minimum Falling Path Sum

title: Minimize Malware Spread

We need to find the node that, if removed from the initial infected list, would result in the fewest number of infected nodes after the spread stops. The output will be the index of this node, with the smallest index chosen if multiple nodes could be removed to achieve the minimum.

title: Minimize Malware Spread II
explanation_short: We are given a network of connected nodes, where some nodes are initially infected with malware, and the malware can spread to directly connected nodes. title: Valid Mountain Array

title: Prison Cells After N Days

title: Least Operators to Express Number

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted III

title: Minimum Area Rectangle II

title: Univalued Binary Tree

The result will be true if the points are a boomerang and false otherwise.

title: Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon
explanation_short: We are given a convex polygon with integer values at each vertex, provided in a clockwise order as an array. Our task is to divide this polygon into triangles, where each triangle's weight is the product of its vertex values, and find the minimum total score possible. The total score is the sum of the weights of all triangles formed. The output will be the minimum possible score achievable through some triangulation of the polygon.

title: Moving Stones Until Consecutive II
explanation_short: We are given a set of stone positions on the X-axis as input. Our goal is to determine the minimum and maximum number of moves required to rearrange these stones so that they are in three consecutive positions. The output will be an array of two integers representing the minimum and maximum number of moves needed to achieve this arrangement. We need to consider the rules of the game, where an endpoint stone can be moved to a new position in one move.

title: Escape a Large Maze
explanation_short: We are given a large grid with a source point and a target point, as well as a list of blocked squares. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to move from the source to the target by walking one square at a time in any of the four main directions, without stepping on a blocked square or going outside the grid. The input includes the source coordinates, target coordinates, and the list of blocked squares, and the output is a simple "yes" or "no" indicating whether the target can be reached. We need to find a path that avoids all blocked squares and stays within the grid boundaries.

title: Flower Planting With No Adjacent
explanation_short: We are given a number of gardens and the paths that connect them. Our task is to assign one of four types of flowers to each garden, ensuring that any two gardens connected by a path have different types of flowers. The input includes the number of gardens and the paths between them, and the output will be an array representing the type of flower in each garden. We need to find a valid arrangement of flowers that meets the condition.

title: Robot Bounded In Circle
explanation_short: The input is a string of instructions that a robot follows on an infinite plane, starting at position (0, 0) and facing north. We need to determine if the robot's movements will keep it within a certain circle, given that it repeats the instructions forever. The output is true if the robot stays within a circle and false otherwise. The robot can move forward or turn left and right based on the instructions. We must find a way to analyze the robot's movements and determine if it will remain bounded within a circle.

title: Partition Array for Maximum Sum
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a maximum length, and we need to divide the array into subarrays of that maximum length. Our goal is to find the largest possible sum of the array after changing the values in each subarray to the maximum value in that subarray. The input consists of the array and the maximum length, and the output is the largest sum that can be achieved. We need to determine the optimal way to partition the array to maximize the sum. The result will be the largest possible sum of the modified array.

title: Last Stone Weight
explanation_short: We're given a list of stone weights, and we need to simulate a game where the heaviest two stones are smashed together on each turn. The goal is to find the weight of the last stone remaining after all possible smashings. The input is a list of integers representing stone weights, and the output is the weight of the last stone. We need to determine how to efficiently smash the stones to find the final weight.

title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase English letters as input. Our task is to repeatedly remove pairs of adjacent letters that are the same until no more pairs can be removed. The output will be the resulting string after all these removals have been made. We need to find a way to efficiently process the string to achieve this final output.

title: Last Stone Weight II
explanation_short: We are given a set of stones with different weights. Our goal is to smash these stones together in a way that minimizes the weight of the last stone remaining. We need to find the minimum possible weight of the last stone after smashing all the stones together. The output will be the minimum weight of the last stone.

title: Longest String Chain
explanation_short: We are given a list of words, and we need to find the longest sequence of words where each word can be formed by adding one letter to the previous word. The input is a list of words, and the output is the length of the longest possible sequence of words that meet this condition. Our goal is to determine the maximum number of words that can be linked together in this way.

title: Longest Duplicate Substring
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to find the longest substring that appears at least twice in the string, even if the occurrences overlap. The goal is to identify the longest duplicated substring and return it as the output. If no such substring exists, the output will be an empty string. The input string can contain any characters, and we need to consider all possible substrings to find the longest duplicate. The output will be the longest duplicated substring, or an empty string if none is found.

title: Height Checker
explanation_short: We are given two sets of information: the current heights of students in a line and the expected heights in non-decreasing order. Our task is to compare these two sets of heights and find the number of positions where they do not match. The input is the current order of student heights, and the output is the count of mismatched positions. We need to determine how many students are not standing in the correct position based on their height.

title: Previous Permutation With One Swap
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our goal is to find the lexicographically largest permutation that is smaller than the input array, which can be achieved by swapping exactly two elements. The output will be this new permutation if it exists, or the original array if no such permutation is possible. We need to determine the optimal swap to achieve this.

title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
explanation_short: We are given information about the number of customers entering a store each minute and whether the owner is grumpy at that time. Our task is to find the maximum number of satisfied customers the owner can have throughout the day, considering they can use a technique to remain not grumpy for a certain number of minutes. The input includes the number of customers per minute, the grumpiness status per minute, and the duration of the technique. The output will be the maximum number of satisfied customers.

title: Distant Barcodes
explanation_short: We are given a list of barcodes where some barcodes appear multiple times. Our task is to rearrange these barcodes so that no two identical barcodes are next to each other. The output will be a rearranged list of barcodes that meets this condition, and we are guaranteed that a valid rearrangement exists. The input list contains duplicate barcodes, and we need to find a way to reorder them to satisfy the condition.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Equivalent String
explanation_short: We are given two strings, s1 and s2, and a base string baseStr, where characters at the same position in s1 and s2 are considered equivalent. Our task is to find the lexicographically smallest string that is equivalent to baseStr, using the equivalency information from s1 and s2. The output will be a string where each character is the smallest possible equivalent character from baseStr.

title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
explanation_short: We are given two strings, str1 and str2, as input. Our task is to find the largest string that can be repeated to form both str1 and str2. The output will be the largest string that divides both input strings, meaning it can be concatenated with itself to form both str1 and str2. We need to identify this largest common divisor string.

title: Flip Columns For Maximum Number of Equal Rows
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix with m rows and n columns. Our task is to find the maximum number of rows that can have all equal values by flipping some or all of the columns. The input is the binary matrix, and the output is the maximum number of rows with equal values after flipping columns. We need to determine the optimal columns to flip to achieve this maximum number of rows.

title: Adding Two Negabinary Numbers
explanation_short: We are given two numbers in base -2, represented as arrays of 0s and 1s, and we need to add them together. The input arrays represent numbers in a unique base system where each digit's place value is a power of -2. Our task is to find the sum of these two numbers and return the result in the same array format, with no leading zeros. The output should be an array of 0s and 1s that represents the sum of the input numbers in base -2.

title: Insufficient Nodes in Root to Leaf Paths
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree and a limit value. Our task is to remove nodes from the tree that have a sum less than the limit on every path from the root to a leaf node that passes through them. The output will be the root of the resulting binary tree after removing these insufficient nodes. We need to determine which nodes to remove based on the sum of values on the paths from the root to the leaf nodes.

title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
explanation_short: We are given a matrix of numbers and a target sum as input. Our task is to find the total count of all possible non-empty submatrices within the given matrix that add up to the target sum. The output will be the total number of such submatrices. We need to consider all possible submatrices, regardless of their size or shape, and determine how many of them meet the target sum criteria.

title: Letter Tile Possibilities
explanation_short: We are given a set of letter tiles, each with a single letter printed on it. Our task is to find the total number of unique sequences of letters that can be formed using these tiles, considering all possible combinations. The input is the set of letters on the tiles, and the output is the count of all possible non-empty sequences of letters that can be made. We need to consider how to arrange the letters in different ways to achieve this count.

title: Smallest Subsequence of Distinct Characters
explanation_short: We are given a string as input, and we need to find a subsequence that includes all unique characters from the string, with each character appearing only once. The goal is to find the smallest possible subsequence in alphabetical order. The output will be a string that meets these conditions. We will need to process the input string to determine the correct order and selection of characters to achieve this result.

title: Largest Values From Labels
explanation_short: We are given two lists of integers, one for item values and one for their corresponding labels, along with two additional integers. Our goal is to select a subset of items that maximizes the sum of their values, while ensuring we don't exceed a certain limit on the number of items per label. The output will be the maximum sum of values achievable under these conditions. We need to carefully choose which items to include in our subset to achieve the highest total value.

title: Duplicate Zeros
explanation_short: We're given a fixed-length array of integers as input. Our task is to find all the zeros in the array, duplicate them, and shift the remaining elements to the right to make space for the duplicates. The output will be the modified array with the zeros duplicated and the other elements shifted accordingly, all done within the original array length. The goal is to achieve this modification in place, without creating a new array.

title: Shortest Common Supersequence
explanation_short: We are given two input strings, str1 and str2. Our goal is to find the shortest possible string that contains both str1 and str2 as subsequences, meaning we can delete some characters from this new string to get str1 and str2. The output will be this shortest string that satisfies the condition. We need to determine the characters and their order in this resulting string.

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a square grid filled with 0s and 1s, where 0 represents a clear cell and 1 represents a blocked cell. Our goal is to find the shortest path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, where we can only move through clear cells. The path length is determined by the number of cells we visit. If no such path exists, we need to indicate that by returning a specific value.

title: Statistics from a Large Sample
explanation_short: We are given a large sample of integers in the range 0 to 255, represented by an array where each element is the count of its index in the sample. We need to find and calculate the minimum, maximum, mean, median, and mode of this sample. The output will be an array of these five statistics as floating-point numbers.

title: Car Pooling
explanation_short: We are given a car with a certain capacity and a list of trips, each with a number of passengers and pickup and dropoff locations. Our task is to determine if it's possible to accommodate all the passengers for their respective trips without exceeding the car's capacity at any point. The input includes the car's capacity and the trip details, and we need to return a simple yes or no answer indicating whether all trips can be completed successfully. The output will be true if the car can handle all the trips and false otherwise.

title: Find in Mountain Array
explanation_short: We are given a special kind of array called a mountain array and a target value. Our task is to find the smallest index at which the target value appears in the array. The input is the mountain array and the target value, and the output will be the minimum index where the target is found, or -1 if it's not found. We need to achieve this without directly accessing the array, but instead using a specific interface to get values from it.

title: Brace Expansion II
explanation_short: We are given an expression that represents a set of lowercase words, following specific grammar rules. Our task is to find all the unique words that this expression can represent. The input is the expression itself, and we need to generate all possible words based on the given grammar rules. The output will be a sorted list of these unique words.

title: Distribute Candies to People
explanation_short: We are given a certain number of candies and a row of people. Our task is to distribute these candies among the people in a specific way, following a repeating pattern of increasing candy distribution. The goal is to find the final amount of candies each person receives. The output will be an array showing the total number of candies each person gets, with the total number of candies in the array equal to the initial amount of candies.

title: Path In Zigzag Labelled Binary Tree
explanation_short: We are given a label of a node in a special binary tree where nodes are labelled in a zigzag pattern. Our task is to find the path from the root of the tree to the node with the given label. The input is the label of the target node, and the output will be a list of labels representing the path from the root to the target node. We need to figure out how to navigate through the tree to construct this path.

title: Filling Bookcase Shelves
explanation_short: We are given a list of books with their thickness and height, and a shelf width. Our task is to arrange these books onto shelves in a way that minimizes the total height of the bookcase. The goal is to find the minimum possible height by strategically placing books on each shelf, ensuring the total thickness of books on a shelf does not exceed the given shelf width. The output will be the minimum total height of the bookcase after all books have been placed.

title: Defanging an IP Address
explanation_short: We are given a valid IP address as input, and we need to modify it by replacing every period with "[.]". Our task is to take this IP address and transform it into its defanged version. The output will be the modified IP address with all periods replaced. The goal is to return this new defanged IP address as a string.

title: Corporate Flight Bookings
explanation_short: We are given a list of flight bookings, where each booking includes the first and last flight numbers and the number of seats reserved for each flight in that range. We need to find the total number of seats reserved for each individual flight. The input includes the list of bookings and the total number of flights, and the output should be a list of total seats reserved for each flight. Our goal is to calculate the total seats reserved for each flight based on the given bookings.

title: Parsing A Boolean Expression
explanation_short: We are given a string that represents a boolean expression, which can contain logical operators and true or false values. Our task is to evaluate this expression and determine its final result. The input string follows specific rules and is guaranteed to be valid. We need to find a way to parse the expression and return a boolean value indicating whether it evaluates to true or false. The output will be either true or false, depending on the evaluation of the given expression.

title: Delete Nodes And Return Forest
explanation_short: We are given a binary tree and a list of node values to delete. Our task is to remove all nodes with these values from the tree and find the roots of the remaining trees. The input consists of the tree's root and the list of values to delete, and the output will be a collection of roots of the trees that are left after deletion. We need to identify which nodes will become the new roots after the specified nodes are removed.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of Two Valid Parentheses Strings
explanation_short: We are given a string of parentheses that is valid, meaning it can be split into two separate valid strings of parentheses. Our goal is to divide this string into two parts, A and B, such that both A and B are valid and the maximum nesting depth between them is as small as possible. The input is this string of parentheses, and the output will be an array indicating which part of the string belongs to A and which to B. We need to find a way to split the string to achieve this minimum maximum nesting depth.

title: Relative Sort Array
explanation_short: We are given two arrays, arr1 and arr2, where arr2 contains distinct elements that are also found in arr1. Our task is to rearrange the elements of arr1 so that they follow the same order as in arr2. Elements not present in arr2 should be placed at the end of arr1 in ascending order. The output will be the rearranged arr1 array.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of Deepest Leaves
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree as input. Our goal is to find the lowest common ancestor of the deepest leaves in the tree. The output will be the node that is the lowest common ancestor of these deepest leaves. We need to identify this node based on the tree structure and the depth of its leaves. The result will be the node that satisfies this condition.

title: Longest Well-Performing Interval
explanation_short: We are given a list of hours worked per day by an employee, and we need to find the length of the longest interval where the number of days with more than 8 hours worked is greater than the number of days with 8 hours or less worked. The input is a list of daily hours, and the output is the length of this longest interval. We need to identify the intervals where the employee performed well, based on the number of tiring and non-tiring days. The goal is to determine the maximum length of such an interval.

title: Smallest Sufficient Team
explanation_short: We are given a list of required skills and a list of people, each with their own set of skills. Our task is to find the smallest group of people that together possess all the required skills. The input consists of the required skills and the skills of each person, and the output will be a list of indices representing the people in the smallest sufficient team. We need to determine which combination of people will cover all the required skills with the fewest members.

title: Maximum of Absolute Value Expression
explanation_short: We are given two arrays of integers with the same length. Our task is to find the maximum value that can be obtained by calculating a specific expression involving absolute differences between elements and their indices. The expression involves comparing each pair of elements from the two arrays. The output will be the maximum value of this expression across all possible pairs of elements.

title: Number of Equivalent Domino Pairs
explanation_short: We are given a list of dominoes, where each domino is represented by two numbers. Our task is to count the number of pairs of dominoes that are equivalent, considering that two dominoes are equivalent if one can be rotated to match the other. The output will be the total number of such equivalent pairs. We need to find a way to compare each pair of dominoes and determine if they are equivalent.

title: Minimum Cost Tree From Leaf Values
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers and need to consider all possible binary trees that can be formed from these numbers. Our goal is to find the smallest possible sum of the values of each non-leaf node in these trees. The input array represents the leaf node values, and we need to determine the minimum sum of non-leaf node values that can be achieved. The output will be the smallest possible sum of non-leaf node values.

title: Shortest Path with Alternating Colors
explanation_short: We're given a directed graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and edges that are either red or blue. Our task is to find the shortest path from node 0 to each node in the graph, with the condition that the edge colors must alternate along the path. The input includes the number of nodes and the lists of red and blue edges, and we need to output an array where each element represents the length of the shortest alternating path to the corresponding node, or -1 if no such path exists. The goal is to determine the shortest distance to each node while adhering to the color-alternating constraint.

title: N-th Tribonacci Number
explanation_short: We are given a number 'n' as input and we need to find the 'n-th' number in a special sequence called the Tribonacci sequence. The sequence is defined by a specific rule that relates each number to the previous three numbers. Our task is to calculate the 'n-th' number in this sequence. The output will be the value of the 'n-th' Tribonacci number.

title: Alphabet Board Path
explanation_short: We are given a target string and an alphabet board with letters arranged in a specific pattern. Our goal is to find the shortest sequence of moves to spell out the target string, starting from the top-left corner of the board. The output will be a string representing the sequence of moves, using specific characters to denote different directions. We need to determine the minimum number of moves required to reach each character in the target string. The result will be a sequence of moves that achieves this in the fewest steps.

title: Stone Game II
explanation_short: We are given a row of piles, each containing a certain number of stones. Our goal is to determine the maximum number of stones a player can collect, considering that players take turns removing stones from the piles. The input is the number of stones in each pile, and we need to find the largest possible total number of stones that can be collected. The output will be the maximum number of stones that can be obtained.

title: Decrease Elements To Make Array Zigzag
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our goal is to find the minimum number of moves required to transform this array into a zigzag pattern, where a move consists of decreasing an element by 1. The output will be the minimum number of moves needed to achieve this transformation. We need to determine the optimal way to decrease elements to create a zigzag array. The result will be a count of these moves.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
explanation_short: We are given two strings, text1 and text2, and we need to find the length of the longest sequence of characters that appears in the same order in both strings. The input strings can have different lengths and characters, and we need to identify the common subsequence. Our goal is to determine the length of this longest common subsequence, which will be our output, or return 0 if no common subsequence exists. The output will be an integer representing the length of the longest common subsequence.

title: Longest Chunked Palindrome Decomposition
explanation_short: We are given a string of characters as input. Our goal is to divide this string into the largest possible number of substrings, known as chunks, where each chunk is a palindrome. The output will be the total number of chunks we can create, with the aim of maximizing this count. By splitting the string into these palindromic chunks, we need to find the largest possible value of chunks.

title: Binary Tree Coloring Game
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree and the total number of nodes in the tree, which is an odd number. Each node in the tree has a unique value. The first player chooses a value, and we need to determine if the second player can choose a node that would give them an advantage. The output will be a boolean indicating whether the second player can win or not.

title: Snapshot Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of a certain length and a series of operations to perform on it. Our task is to design a system that can set values in the array, take snapshots of the array at certain points, and then retrieve values from the array at specific snapshot points. The input will be a sequence of these operations, and the output will be the results of the get operations. We need to find a way to efficiently store and retrieve the values at different snapshot points.

title: Number of Dice Rolls With Target Sum
explanation_short: We are given a certain number of dice, each with a specific number of faces, and a target sum. Our task is to find the number of possible ways to roll the dice so that the sum of the face-up numbers equals the target sum. The input consists of the number of dice, the number of faces on each die, and the target sum, and the output is the number of possible ways to achieve the target sum, returned as a modulo value to handle large results.

title: Swap For Longest Repeated Character Substring
explanation_short: We are given a string of characters, and we can make one swap between any two characters in the string. Our goal is to find the longest substring where all characters are the same after making this single swap. The output will be the length of this longest substring with repeated characters.

title: Online Majority Element In Subarray
explanation_short: We are given an array and need to design a system that can efficiently find the majority element within any given subarray of that array. The majority element is the one that appears at least a certain threshold number of times in the subarray. Our task is to create a data structure that can handle these queries and return the majority element for any subarray. The input will include the array and the threshold, and the output will be the majority element for a specific subarray. We need to find a way to do this efficiently for any subarray query.

title: Find Words That Can Be Formed by Characters
explanation_short: We're given a list of words and a set of characters. Our task is to find the words that can be formed using these characters, with each character only used once. We need to calculate the total length of all these "good" words. The output will be the sum of the lengths of the words that can be formed from the given characters.

title: Last Substring in Lexicographical Order
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to find the last substring that comes last in dictionary order. The input string contains a sequence of characters, and we must identify all possible substrings. Our goal is to determine the last substring in lexicographical order among all these substrings. The output will be the last substring that meets this condition.

title: Largest 1-Bordered Square
explanation_short: We are given a 2D grid filled with 0s and 1s. Our task is to find the largest square subgrid within this grid that has all 1s on its border. We need to determine the total number of elements in this largest square subgrid. The output will be the size of this subgrid, or 0 if no such subgrid exists.

title: Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree, where each level of the tree has a certain sum of node values. Our task is to find the level in the tree that has the maximum sum of node values. The input is the binary tree itself, and the output will be the level number that corresponds to the maximum sum. We need to calculate the sum of node values at each level and determine which level has the highest sum.

title: Day of the Year
explanation_short: We are given a date in the format of year, month, and day. Our task is to determine the day number of the year for the given date. The input is a string representing a date, and we need to find the corresponding day of the year. The output will be the day number, which is a numerical value. For example, if the date is January 9th, the output would be 9, indicating it's the 9th day of the year.

title: Compare Strings by Frequency of the Smallest Character
explanation_short: We are given two lists of strings: a list of words and a list of query strings. For each query string, we need to count how many words have a higher frequency of their smallest character compared to the query string's smallest character frequency. The input consists of these two lists, and the output will be a list of counts, one for each query string. We are looking for the number of words that meet this condition for each query.

title: Invalid Transactions
explanation_short: We are given a list of transactions, where each transaction includes information about the person's name, time of transaction, amount, and city. Our task is to identify transactions that may be invalid based on certain conditions, such as transactions occurring within a short time frame, having the same name, and being in different cities. We need to analyze these transactions and return a list of those that are possibly invalid. The output will be a list of transactions that meet these conditions.

title: As Far from Land as Possible
explanation_short: We are given a grid of water and land cells, represented by 0s and 1s. Our goal is to find a water cell that is as far away as possible from any land cell, using the Manhattan distance. We need to calculate the maximum distance from a water cell to the nearest land cell. The output will be this maximum distance, or -1 if the grid doesn't contain any land or water.

title: Can Make Palindrome from Substring
explanation_short: We are given a string and a set of queries, each specifying a substring and a number of characters that can be replaced. We need to determine if it's possible to rearrange the substring and replace up to the given number of characters to form a palindrome. The output will be a boolean array indicating whether each query's substring can be made into a palindrome.

title: Remove Zero Sum Consecutive Nodes from Linked List
explanation_short: We are given a linked list where each node has a value. Our task is to find and remove consecutive nodes that add up to zero. The output will be the head of the resulting linked list after all such sequences have been removed. The goal is to return the modified linked list with no consecutive nodes summing to zero.

title: Prime Arrangements
explanation_short: We are given a number n and need to find the number of ways to arrange the numbers 1 to n. The catch is that prime numbers must be placed at positions that are also prime numbers, considering the positions are numbered from 1. Our task is to calculate this number of arrangements and provide the result after applying a specific mathematical operation to handle large numbers. The result will be the total count of valid arrangements, adjusted to fit within a certain range.

title: Number of Valid Words for Each Puzzle
explanation_short: We are given two lists: a list of words and a list of puzzles. Our task is to find the number of valid words that can be formed from each puzzle, where a valid word is one that can be created using the letters in the puzzle. The output will be a list of counts, where each count represents the number of valid words for the corresponding puzzle.

title: Distance Between Bus Stops
explanation_short: We are given a list of distances between neighboring bus stops that form a circle. Our task is to find the shortest distance between a given start stop and a destination stop, considering that the bus can travel in both clockwise and counterclockwise directions. The input includes the list of distances and the start and destination stop numbers. We need to calculate the minimum distance the bus needs to travel to get from the start to the destination. The output will be the shortest distance between the two stops.

title: Dinner Plate Stacks
explanation_short: We are given a row of stacks with the same maximum capacity, and we need to manage these stacks by adding and removing plates. Our task is to implement a system that can handle two main operations: adding a plate to the first available stack that has space, and removing a plate from a specific stack. The input will include the maximum capacity of each stack and a series of operations to add or remove plates. The output will be the result of these operations, reflecting the state of the stacks after each operation is performed.

title: Day of the Week
explanation_short: We are given a date as three separate integers: the day, month, and year. Our task is to determine the day of the week that corresponds to this date. The goal is to find the correct day of the week, which will be one of the seven days: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, or Saturday. The result will be the name of the day of the week as a string.

title: Maximum Number of Balloons
explanation_short: We are given a string of characters and need to find out how many times we can form the word "balloon" using each character only once. The input is the string of characters, and we want to determine the maximum number of "balloon" instances that can be created. Our goal is to count the characters in the string and figure out how many complete "balloon" words can be formed. The output will be the maximum number of "balloon" instances that can be formed from the given string.

title: Reverse Substrings Between Each Pair of Parentheses
explanation_short: We're given a string with lowercase English letters and brackets. Our task is to reverse the parts of the string that are enclosed within matching pairs of brackets, working from the innermost pairs outwards. The goal is to produce a new string where these reversals have been made, and all brackets have been removed. The input string will contain only lowercase letters and brackets, and the output will be a string with the same letters, but with the specified parts reversed and no brackets.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum with One Deletion
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our goal is to find the maximum possible sum of a subarray, with the option to delete at most one element from it, ensuring the subarray is not empty after deletion. The output will be the maximum sum we can achieve. We need to consider all possible subarrays and determine whether deleting an element would increase the sum.

title: K-Concatenation Maximum Sum
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers and a number k, which we'll use to create a new array by repeating the original array k times. Our task is to find the maximum sum of a sub-array within this new, repeated array. The sub-array can be any length, including 0, in which case its sum is 0. We'll return this maximum sum, adjusted to fit within a specific large number range.

title: Make Array Strictly Increasing
explanation_short: We are given two integer arrays, and our goal is to make the first array strictly increasing. To do this, we can replace elements in the first array with elements from the second array. We need to find the minimum number of replacements needed to achieve a strictly increasing order in the first array. The output will be the minimum number of operations required to make the array strictly increasing.

title: Critical Connections in a Network
explanation_short: We are given a network of servers connected by undirected connections. Our task is to identify the connections that are crucial for the network's connectivity, meaning that if they are removed, some servers will no longer be able to reach others. The input consists of the number of servers and the connections between them, and we need to find all such critical connections. The output will be a list of these critical connections.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference
explanation_short: We are given an array of unique integers and need to find all pairs of numbers that have the smallest possible difference between them. Our goal is to identify these pairs and return them in a list, sorted in ascending order. The input is the array of integers, and the output will be a list of pairs that meet this condition, with each pair containing two numbers. We need to compare the differences between all possible pairs to achieve this.

title: Unique Number of Occurrences
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our task is to determine if the frequency of each number in the array is unique, meaning no two numbers appear the same number of times. The output will be a boolean value, true if the frequencies are unique and false otherwise. We need to analyze the array to find the occurrence of each value and compare these occurrences to determine the result.

title: Get Equal Substrings Within Budget
explanation_short: We are given two strings of the same length and a maximum budget. Our goal is to find the longest substring where we can change one string to match the other, considering the cost of changing each character based on the difference in their ASCII values. The output will be the maximum length of such a substring that can be changed within the given budget. If no such substring exists, the output will be 0.

title: Ugly Number III
explanation_short: We are given four integers: n, a, b, and c, where n represents the position of the ugly number we need to find. An ugly number is defined as a positive integer that is divisible by a, b, or c. Our task is to find the nth ugly number based on these conditions. The output will be the nth ugly number in the sequence of ugly numbers. We need to determine this number using the given values of a, b, c, and n.

title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
explanation_short: We're given a string and an integer, where the integer represents the number of adjacent equal letters that can be removed from the string. Our task is to repeatedly remove these sets of adjacent equal letters until no more removals can be made. The input string and integer will be used to determine the final output string, which is the result after all possible removals have been made. The goal is to find this final string.

title: Smallest String With Swaps
explanation_short: We are given a string and a list of index pairs that can be swapped. Our goal is to find the lexicographically smallest string that can be formed by swapping the characters at these index pairs any number of times. The input includes the original string and the list of swappable index pairs, and the output will be the smallest possible string after all possible swaps. We need to determine the optimal sequence of swaps to achieve this result.

title: Design Skiplist
explanation_short: We are given a set of numbers that will be inserted into a data structure. Our task is to design this data structure, called a Skiplist, which allows us to quickly add, remove, and search for numbers. The input will be a series of numbers to be added, removed, or searched, and the output will be the result of these operations, such as whether a number is found or not. We need to handle duplicate numbers and ensure the data structure operates efficiently. The goal is to achieve fast operation times, similar to other data structures like treap and red-black tree.

title: Sort Items by Groups Respecting Dependencies
explanation_short: We are given a set of items, some of which belong to specific groups, and a list of dependencies between items. Our task is to sort these items in a way that respects their dependencies and group memberships. The input includes the number of items, the number of groups, the group each item belongs to, and the items that must come before each item. The output will be a sorted list of items that satisfies these conditions, or an empty list if no such sorting is possible.

title: Minimum Moves to Reach Target with Rotations
explanation_short: We are given a grid with empty and blocked cells, and a snake that spans two cells, starting from the top left corner. The goal is to find the minimum number of moves for the snake to reach the lower right corner, where a move can be a rotation or a translation. The snake's movements are restricted by the grid's layout and the blocked cells. The output will be the minimum number of moves required to reach the target, or -1 if it's impossible. The grid's layout and the snake's possible movements will determine the solution.

title: Minimum Cost to Move Chips to The Same Position
explanation_short: We are given a list of chip positions and need to find the minimum cost to move all chips to the same position. The input is a list of numbers representing the positions of the chips. Our goal is to determine the lowest total cost required to align all chips at one position. The output will be the minimum cost needed to achieve this.

title: Split a String in Balanced Strings
explanation_short: We are given a string consisting of 'L' and 'R' characters, where the total number of 'L's equals the total number of 'R's. Our task is to divide this string into substrings, ensuring each substring has an equal number of 'L' and 'R' characters. We need to find the maximum number of such balanced substrings that can be created. The output will be the count of these balanced substrings.

title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence of Given Difference
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a specific difference. Our task is to find the longest subsequence within the array where the difference between each pair of adjacent elements is equal to the given difference. The output will be the length of this longest subsequence. We need to examine the array and identify the longest sequence that meets this condition.

title: Count Vowels Permutation
explanation_short: We are given an integer n, representing the length of a string. Our task is to count the number of unique strings of length n that can be formed using the letters "a", "e", "i", "o", and "u" under specific rules. The output will be the total count of such strings, and since the result may be large, we need to return it modulo 10^9 + 7. We need to find a way to calculate this count efficiently.

title: Path with Maximum Gold
explanation_short: We are given a grid representing a gold mine, where each cell contains a certain amount of gold. Our task is to find the maximum amount of gold that can be collected by navigating through the grid. The output will be the maximum total gold that can be collected. We need to determine the optimal path to achieve this maximum amount of gold.

title: Check If It Is a Straight Line
explanation_short: We are given a list of points in the XY plane, where each point has an x and y coordinate. Our task is to determine if all these points lie on the same straight line. To do this, we need to analyze the relationships between the points and figure out if they can be connected by a single line. The result will be a simple "yes" or "no" answer, indicating whether the points form a straight line or not.

title: Circular Permutation in Binary Representation
explanation_short: We are given two integers, n and start, and we need to find a specific order of numbers from 0 to 2^n - 1. The goal is to arrange these numbers in a way that each adjacent pair differs by only one bit in their binary representation. Our task is to return this special arrangement of numbers, starting from the given start value. The output will be a list of numbers in the desired order.

title: Find Positive Integer Solution for a Given Equation
explanation_short: We are given a function with a hidden formula and a target value. Our task is to find all pairs of positive integers that, when input into the function, produce the target value. The function is monotonically increasing, meaning its output increases as the inputs increase. We need to return all such pairs of positive integers. The output will be a list of pairs, and the order of the pairs does not matter.

title: Maximum Length of a Concatenated String with Unique Characters
explanation_short: We are given a list of strings and need to find the maximum length of a new string that can be formed by combining some or all of these strings in a way that the new string has all unique characters. The input is a list of strings, and the output is the maximum possible length of the concatenated string. We need to figure out which strings to combine to achieve the longest string with no repeating characters. The goal is to determine this maximum length.

title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a target number of odd integers. Our task is to find the number of continuous subarrays within the given array that contain exactly the target number of odd integers. The input consists of the array and the target number, and the output will be the count of such subarrays, known as "nice" subarrays. We need to determine how many subarrays meet this specific condition.

title: Replace the Substring for Balanced String
explanation_short: We are given a string containing only four characters: 'Q', 'W', 'E', and 'R'. Our goal is to find the minimum length of a substring that needs to be replaced to make the entire string balanced, meaning each character appears an equal number of times. The output will be the length of this substring, or 0 if the string is already balanced. We need to determine the shortest part of the string that is causing the imbalance.

title: Find Elements in a Contaminated Binary Tree
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree whose node values have all been overwritten with -1. The original values follow a deterministic rule: the root should be 0, a left child equals 2 × parent + 1, and a right child equals 2 × parent + 2. Your task is to “restore” these hidden values and then answer many queries asking whether a specific integer appears in the recovered tree. For each query, return true if the target value exists, otherwise false.

title: Greatest Sum Divisible by Three
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers called nums. From these numbers you may choose any subset (including possibly none) and add them together. Your task is to find the largest possible total that is a multiple of three. The answer you return is that maximum sum; if no subset yields a sum divisible by three, the result is 0.

title: Shift 2D Grid
explanation_short: You are given a rectangular grid of numbers and an integer k. One shift moves every element one step forward in row‑major order, sending the last element to the first cell. Apply this shift operation exactly k times. Return the grid after the shifts, preserving its original dimensions.

title: Count Servers that Communicate
explanation_short: You receive a rectangular grid of 0s and 1s, where each 1 marks a server’s location. A server can talk to another one if they lie in the same row or the same column. Your task is to determine how many servers have at least one partner they can communicate with. Return that number as a single integer.

title: Search Suggestions System
explanation_short: You receive a list of product names and a single search word. After each character of the search word is entered, you must find up to three products that start with the current prefix. The suggested products for each prefix should be the lexicographically smallest ones among all matches. Return a sequence of lists, where the i‑th list contains the suggestions after the first i characters of the search word.

title: Minimum Time Visiting All Points
explanation_short: You are given a list of n points on a 2‑D grid, each written as a pair of integer coordinates \([x_i, y_i]\). Starting at the first point, you must travel to each subsequent point in the given order, moving one unit horizontally, vertically, or diagonally per second. Your task is to compute the smallest total number of seconds required to finish the whole sequence. Return that minimum time as a single integer.

title: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps
explanation_short: You are given two integers `steps` and `arrLen`. A pointer starts at index 0 of an array of length `arrLen`, and for each of the `steps` moves it may go one position left, one position right, or stay where it is, never leaving the array bounds. You must determine how many different sequences of moves bring the pointer back to index 0 after exactly `steps` steps. Return that number modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Minimum Moves to Move a Box to Their Target Location
explanation_short:
You are given an m × n grid where each cell is a wall ('#'), empty floor ('.'), the box ('B'), the target ('T'), or the storekeeper ('S').  
The storekeeper can walk on empty cells and push the box one step at a time, but only if he stands right behind it and the destination cell is not a wall.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of pushes required to place the box on the target cell.  
If the box cannot be moved onto the target under the rules, output -1.

title: Find Winner on a Tic Tac Toe Game
explanation_short: You receive a list of moves, each given as a pair [row, col] that shows where the current player placed their mark on the 3 × 3 board, with player A always moving first. After processing the moves you must decide whether one of the players has formed a complete row, column, or diagonal, whether the board is full with no winner, or whether the game still has empty squares. Return the result as the string `"A"`, `"B"`, `"Draw"`, or `"Pending"`.

title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
explanation_short:
You are given a rectangular grid of 0s and 1s.  
Your task is to count every square region inside the grid whose cells are all 1.  
Each square can be of any size ≥ 1, as long as it fits entirely within the matrix.  
Return the total number of such all‑one squares.

title: Palindrome Partitioning III
explanation_short: You are given a lowercase string s and an integer k. You must cut the string into exactly k contiguous pieces and may change characters so that each piece becomes a palindrome. Return the smallest possible total number of character changes needed.

title: Subtract the Product and Sum of Digits of an Integer
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n. Compute the product of all its decimal digits and also the sum of those digits, then subtract the sum from the product. Output the resulting integer.

title: Number of Burgers with No Waste of Ingredients
explanation_short: You receive two integers: the total number of tomato slices and the total number of cheese slices available. Each jumbo burger uses 4 tomato slices and 1 cheese slice, while each small burger uses 2 tomato slices and 1 cheese slice. Find non‑negative counts of jumbo and small burgers that consume exactly all the given tomato and cheese slices. Return those two counts as a two‑element list, or an empty list if no such combination exists.

title: Group the People Given the Group Size They Belong To
explanation_short:
You receive an array where the value at each index tells you how many people must be together with that person.  
Your task is to partition all indices 0…n‑1 into groups so that every index appears in exactly one group and each group’s size matches the required size for all its members.  
Return the collection of groups as a list of lists of indices; the order of groups and the order inside each group do not matter.  
A solution is guaranteed to exist, and any valid grouping may be returned.

title: Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `threshold`. Choose a positive divisor `d` and replace each element with the smallest integer not less than `nums[i]/d`; then add those values together. Return the smallest `d` for which this summed total does not exceed `threshold`.

title: Iterator for Combination
explanation_short: You are given a string of distinct lowercase letters and an integer k. The task is to create an object that can walk through every possible k‑letter combination formed from the characters, ordered lexicographically. The object must support a method that returns the next combination as a string and another method that tells whether any combinations remain. The output consists of the sequence of strings produced by successive calls to the “next” method until “hasNext” reports false.

title: Element Appearing More Than 25% In Sorted Array
explanation_short: You are given a list of integers that is already sorted in non‑decreasing order. One of the numbers appears in the list more than a quarter of the total length. Your task is to identify which integer that is. Return that integer as the result.

title: Minimum Falling Path Sum II
explanation_short: You receive an n × n integer matrix called grid. From each row you must pick exactly one element, but the column you choose cannot be the same as the column chosen in the row directly above it. The goal is to make the total sum of the selected elements as small as possible. Return that minimum sum as a single integer.

title: Minimum Number of Flips to Convert Binary Matrix to Zero Matrix
explanation_short: You are given an m × n matrix containing only 0s and 1s. In one move you may pick any cell and toggle its value together with the values of its up, down, left, and right neighbors (if they exist). Your task is to determine the smallest number of such moves that turns every entry of the matrix into 0, returning -1 if no sequence of moves can achieve this. The output is that minimum count (or -1).

title: Remove Covered Intervals
explanation_short: You are given a list of intervals, each written as a pair [li, ri) meaning it includes li but excludes ri. An interval is removed if there exists another interval that starts no later and ends no earlier, completely covering it. Your task is to determine how many intervals are left after all such covered intervals are discarded. The answer you return is this count as an integer.

title: Sequential Digits
explanation_short:
You are given two integers low and high that define a closed interval.  
A number is considered “sequential digits” when each digit is exactly one larger than the digit before it (for example, 123 or 4567).  
Your task is to list every integer within the interval [low, high] that satisfies this property.  
Return the resulting numbers in increasing order as a list.

title: Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold
explanation_short:
You are given a rectangular grid of integers `mat` and an integer `threshold`.  
From the grid you may choose any square sub‑matrix (all sides equal) and compute the sum of its elements.  
Your task is to determine the largest possible side length of such a square whose total sum does not exceed `threshold`.  
Return that side length, or 0 if no square satisfies the condition.

title: Convert Binary Number in a Linked List to Integer
explanation_short: The input is a reference to the head of a singly‑linked list whose nodes each contain a 0 or a 1. Traversing the list from head to tail gives the bits of a binary number, with the most‑significant bit first. You need to compute the decimal (base‑10) value represented by those bits. Output that integer.

title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of 0s (empty) and 1s (obstacle) together with an integer k. You must travel from the cell (0, 0) to the cell (m‑1, n‑1), moving only up, down, left or right, and you may turn up to k obstacle cells into empty ones along the way. Return the smallest number of moves required for such a walk, or -1 if reaching the destination is impossible.

title: Find Numbers with Even Number of Digits
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers called `nums`. Your task is to determine how many of those integers are written with an even number of decimal digits. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Divide Array in Sets of K Consecutive Numbers
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`. Your task is to determine whether the entire array can be partitioned into groups of exactly `k` numbers where each group consists of consecutive values. Return `true` if such a division is possible; otherwise return `false`.

title: Maximum Number of Occurrences of a Substring
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` and three integers: `maxLetters`, `minSize`, and `maxSize`. Look at every substring whose length is at least `minSize` and at most `maxSize`, and that uses no more than `maxLetters` different letters. Among those substrings, determine which one occurs most frequently in `s` (overlaps count). Output that highest occurrence count; if no substring satisfies the conditions, output 0.

title: Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `arr` and a single integer `target`. Choose a value `v` so that every element of `arr` larger than `v` is replaced by `v`, and the sum of the resulting array is as close as possible to `target` in absolute difference. If multiple values give the same minimal difference, return the smallest such `v`. The output is that integer `v` (which may or may not appear in the original array).

title: Replace Elements with Greatest Element on Right Side
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers. For every position except the last, replace its value with the greatest number that occurs somewhere to its right. The final element, which has no elements after it, should become -1. Return the resulting array.

title: Number of Paths with Max Score
explanation_short: You are given a square board as an array of equal‑length strings, where each cell contains ‘E’, ‘S’, a digit 1‑9, or an obstacle ‘X’. Starting from the bottom‑right cell marked ‘S’, you must reach the top‑left cell marked ‘E’ by moving only up, left, or diagonally up‑left, never stepping on an ‘X’. Along a valid path you collect the numeric values of the visited cells (excluding ‘S’ and ‘E’) and we need the greatest possible total sum. Output a two‑element list: the maximum sum and the number of distinct paths that achieve it, taken modulo 1 000 000 007 (or [0, 0] if no path exists).

title: Deepest Leaves Sum
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree, where each node holds an integer value. First, determine how deep the tree goes-that is, the greatest distance from the root to any leaf. Then add together the values of all leaf nodes that appear at this deepest level. Return the resulting sum as a single integer.

title: Maximum Candies You Can Get from Boxes
explanation_short: You are given n boxes, each described by four arrays: status (1 means the box is already open, 0 means closed), candies (the amount of candy inside each box), keys (the list of keys found inside each box), and containedBoxes (the list of other boxes found inside each box). A separate list initialBoxes tells which boxes you start with. By opening any box you have a key for, you can collect its candies, obtain new keys, and acquire more boxes to potentially open later. Your task is to determine the greatest total amount of candy you can collect following these rules. The answer is a single integer representing that maximum candy count.

title: All Elements in Two Binary Search Trees
explanation_short:
You are given the roots of two binary search trees.  
Each tree contains integer values that follow the BST ordering property.  
Collect every value that appears in either tree and arrange all of them from smallest to largest.  
Return the resulting ordered list of integers.

title: Decrypt String from Alphabet to Integer Mapping
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s` that consists of digits (`'0'–'9'`) and possibly the character `'#'`. Each digit from `1` to `9` represents the letters `a` through `i`, while any two‑digit number followed by `'#'` (for example `10#`, `11#`, …, `26#`) stands for the letters `j` through `z`. Your task is to translate the entire string according to this rule, preserving the order of the characters. The result should be returned as a new string containing only lowercase English letters. The input guarantees that the decoding is unambiguous.

title: Jump Game III
explanation_short: You receive an array of non‑negative integers and a starting index. From any position i you may jump to i + arr[i] or i − arr[i] provided the destination stays within the array bounds. Decide whether you can ever land on an index whose value is 0, and output true if it’s reachable, otherwise false.

title: Find N Unique Integers Sum up to Zero
explanation_short:
You are given a single integer n.  
Your task is to construct a list that contains exactly n different integers.  
The numbers you choose must add up to zero when summed together.  
Return any such list; the order of the elements does not matter.

title: Verbal Arithmetic Puzzle
explanation_short: You are given an array of words that represent numbers and a single word that represents their sum. Each distinct letter must be replaced by a unique digit (0‑9), and no word may start with zero. Determine whether there exists any assignment of digits to letters that makes the arithmetic addition of the left‑hand words equal the right‑hand word. Return true if such an assignment exists; otherwise return false.

title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
explanation_short: You receive an integer array arr and a list of queries, each query given as a pair [left, right] of indices. For every query you must take all elements from arr[left] through arr[right] and compute their bitwise XOR. The XOR combines the binary representations of those numbers into a single integer result. Return an array whose i‑th entry is the XOR result for the i‑th query.

title: Decompress Run-Length Encoded List
explanation_short: You receive an even‑length integer array `nums`. Treat each consecutive pair `[nums[2*i], nums[2*i+1]]` as a “frequency, value” description: the first number tells how many times the second number should appear. Build a new list by writing each value the specified number of times and joining these pieces in order, and return that decompressed list.

title: Get Watched Videos by Your Friends
explanation_short: You are given a list of video titles each person has watched, a friendship graph, your own person id, and an integer k. First collect all videos watched by people whose shortest‑path distance from you is exactly k, then count how many times each video appears. Return the video titles sorted by increasing frequency, breaking ties by alphabetical order.

title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make a String Palindrome
explanation_short: You are given a single string `s`. You may insert any characters at any positions, and you must determine the smallest number of such insertions needed to turn `s` into a palindrome (a word that reads the same forward and backward). Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Sum of Nodes with Even-Valued Grandparent
explanation_short: You are given the root node of a binary tree, where each node stores an integer value. For every node, look at its grandparent (the parent of its parent) and check whether that grandparent’s value is even. Add together the values of all nodes whose grandparent is even‑valued. Return the total sum, or 0 if no such nodes exist.

title: Distinct Echo Substrings
explanation_short: You receive a single string `text`. From all its non‑empty substrings you must identify those that can be written as some string concatenated with itself (i.e., of the form `a + a`). The task is to count how many distinct substrings satisfy this property and output that number.

title: Matrix Block Sum
explanation_short: You are given a rectangular grid of numbers `mat` and a non‑negative integer `k`. For every position `(i, j)` you must add up all entries whose row index is between `i‑k` and `i+k` and whose column index is between `j‑k` and `j+k`, staying inside the matrix borders. The result of this sum becomes the value of `answer[i][j]`. The output is a new matrix of the same dimensions containing all those summed values.

title: Minimum Flips to Make a OR b Equal to c
explanation_short: You are given three positive integers a, b, and c. You may change any single bit of a or b from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0, and you want to do this the fewest possible times so that after the changes the bitwise OR of the new a and b exactly equals c. Output the minimum number of bit flips required.

title: Convert Integer to the Sum of Two No-Zero Integers
explanation_short: You are given a single positive integer n. Your task is to pick two positive numbers a and b that contain no digit 0 in their decimal forms and add up exactly to n. Return them as a two‑element list [a, b]; any pair that satisfies the conditions is acceptable.

title: Minimum Distance to Type a Word Using Two Fingers
explanation_short: You are given a string `word` made of uppercase English letters. You must assign each character to one of two fingers and sum the Manhattan distances each finger travels between its consecutive letters, with the first placement of each finger costing nothing. Return the smallest possible total distance as an integer.

title: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of pairs connections, where each pair [a, b] represents a cable directly linking computer a to computer b. You may take any existing cable and reconnect its two ends to any two computers that are currently disconnected. Find the smallest number of reconnections needed so that every computer can reach every other one through the network. Return that minimum count, or -1 if the available cables are insufficient to achieve full connectivity.

title: Maximum 69 Number
explanation_short: You receive a positive integer whose every digit is either 6 or 9. You may flip at most one digit-turn a 6 into a 9 or a 9 into a 6. Your task is to determine the greatest value that can be obtained after this optional single change. Output that maximum integer.

title: Print Words Vertically
explanation_short: You are given a string s that contains several words separated by spaces. Imagine writing each word in its own column, top‑to‑bottom, and filling any missing characters with spaces so the columns stay aligned. The task is to produce the rows that result from this vertical layout, trimming any spaces at the end of each row. Return those rows as a list of strings.

title: Reverse Subarray To Maximize Array Value
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums`.  
First, compute the “value” of an array as the sum of the absolute differences between every pair of adjacent elements.  
You may pick any single contiguous subarray, reverse its order, and then recalculate the value; the goal is to make this sum as large as possible.  
Return the greatest value achievable after performing at most one such reversal.

title: Delete Leaves With a Given Value
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree and an integer target. Any leaf whose value equals target must be removed, and after a removal its parent may become a new leaf that also matches target, so the process repeats until no such leaves remain. The task is to return the tree that results after all possible deletions. The output should be the root of this pruned tree (often shown as a level‑order array).

title: Minimum Number of Taps to Open to Water a Garden
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and an array ranges of length n + 1, where the i‑th tap at position i can water the interval from i − ranges[i] to i + ranges[i]. Your task is to select as few taps as possible so that every point between 0 and n (including the ends) is covered by at least one opened tap. If no selection can cover the whole garden, you must report that it is impossible. The output is a single integer: the minimum number of taps needed, or ‑1 if the garden cannot be fully watered.

title: Break a Palindrome
explanation_short: You are given a string consisting only of lowercase letters that is already a palindrome. You must change exactly one character to any other lowercase letter so that the new string is no longer a palindrome. Among all such possible strings, you need to return the one that would appear earliest in dictionary order. If no single‑character change can break the palindrome (for example, a one‑character string), return an empty string.

title: Sort the Matrix Diagonally
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of integers. For every diagonal that runs from the top‑most row or the left‑most column toward the bottom‑right corner, rearrange the numbers on that diagonal so they appear in non‑decreasing order. Return the whole matrix after all diagonals have been sorted.

title: Remove Palindromic Subsequences
explanation_short: You receive a string `s` that contains only the letters ‘a’ and ‘b’. In each move you may delete any subsequence of `s` that reads the same forward and backward. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of moves required to erase the entire string. Output that minimum count as an integer.

title: Filter Restaurants by Vegan-Friendly, Price and Distance
explanation_short: You receive an array where each restaurant is described by its id, rating, vegan‑friendly flag (1 or 0), price, and distance, plus three filter values: veganFriendly, maxPrice and maxDistance. First keep only the restaurants that satisfy the vegan‑friendly requirement (if veganFriendly = 1) and whose price and distance do not exceed the given maxima. Return the ids of the remaining restaurants sorted by rating from highest to lowest, breaking ties by larger id first.

title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
explanation_short: You are given the number of cities n, a list of bidirectional weighted edges connecting pairs of cities, and a distance threshold. For each city, count how many other cities can be reached by some path whose total weight does not exceed the threshold (using the shortest possible paths). Return the index of the city with the fewest such reachable neighbors; if several cities tie, choose the one with the largest index.

title: Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule
explanation_short: You are given an array where each element represents the difficulty of a job, and an integer d that tells how many days you have to finish all jobs in order. Each day you must complete at least one consecutive segment of the remaining jobs, and the difficulty of that day equals the hardest job you did that day. Your task is to choose how to split the jobs into d segments so that the sum of the daily difficulties is as small as possible. If it’s impossible to assign at least one job to each day (for example, when d exceeds the number of jobs), output -1; otherwise output the minimal total difficulty.

title: Rank Transform of an Array
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `arr`.  
For each value you must determine its rank among all distinct numbers in the array, where the smallest number gets rank 1, the next smallest gets rank 2, and so on.  
If several elements have the same value they all receive the same rank.  
Return a new array where each position contains the rank corresponding to the original element.

title: The K Weakest Rows in a Matrix
explanation_short: You are given an m × n matrix containing only 0 and 1, where each row’s 1’s (soldiers) appear before any 0’s (civilians), and an integer k. For each row you must determine how many soldiers it has, rank the rows from fewest to most soldiers (breaking ties by smaller row index), and then select the first k indices in that order. The result is a list of those k row indices, ordered from weakest to strongest.

title: Maximum Product of Splitted Binary Tree
explanation_short: The input is the root of a binary tree, described by its node values and structure. You may remove exactly one edge, which splits the original tree into two separate subtrees. For each possible cut, calculate the sum of values in each subtree and take the product of those two sums. Output the greatest such product, applying the modulo 1 000 000 007 after the maximum has been determined.

title: Reduce Array Size to The Half
explanation_short: You receive an integer array arr. You may select a set of distinct numbers and remove every occurrence of each selected number from the array. Find the smallest possible size of such a set that eliminates at least half of the original elements, and output that minimum size.

title: Jump Game V
explanation_short: You are given an integer array arr and a distance limit d. From any position i you may jump left or right up to d steps, but only to a position j that holds a smaller value than arr[i] and where every element between i and j is also smaller than arr[i]. Starting from any index, you can keep jumping while these conditions hold. The task is to output the greatest number of indices that can be visited in a single sequence of such jumps.

title: Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average Greater than or Equal to Threshold
