explanation_short: You are given an integer array arr, a window size k, and a threshold value. For every consecutive segment of exactly k elements, compute its average and check whether it is at least the threshold. Count how many of these length‑k sub‑arrays satisfy that condition. The answer you return is this count.

title: Check If N and Its Double Exist
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers `arr`.  
Your task is to decide whether there exist two distinct positions `i` and `j` such that the value at one position is exactly twice the value at the other (i.e., `arr[i] = 2 * arr[j]` or vice‑versa).  
If such a pair exists, the answer is `true`; otherwise it is `false`.  
Return the result as a Boolean value.

title: Angle Between Hands of a Clock
explanation_short: You receive two integers: `hour` (1‑12) and `minutes` (0‑59). The task is to determine the acute angle formed where the hour hand and the minute hand meet on an analog clock. Compute the smaller of the two possible angles between the hands and express it in degrees. The answer is considered correct if it is within 10⁻⁵ of the true value.

title: Jump Game IV
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers and start at its first element. In each move you may go to the next or previous position, or to any other position that holds the same value as your current one, but you can never leave the array bounds. Your task is to determine the smallest number of moves required to reach the last element, and output that minimum count.

title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
explanation_short: You are given one integer `num`. Starting from this value, you repeatedly apply the rule “if the current number is even, divide it by 2; otherwise subtract 1”. Keep performing steps until the number reaches 0, and count how many steps were required. Return that count as the answer.

title: Minimum Number of Steps to Make Two Strings Anagram
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s` and `t` that have the same length. In each step you may change any single character of `t` to any other letter. Your task is to determine the smallest number of such changes required so that the multiset of characters in `t` matches the multiset of characters in `s` (i.e., `t` becomes an anagram of `s`). Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Tweet Counts Per Frequency
explanation_short: You receive a sequence of operations on a tweet‑tracking system: one operation records that a tweet occurred at a given timestamp, and another asks for how many tweets happened in each sub‑interval of a larger time range. The query specifies a frequency (“minute”, “hour”, or “day”), a start time, and an end time; the range is divided into consecutive chunks of that size, with the final chunk possibly shorter. Your task is to return, for each chunk, the number of recorded tweets whose timestamps fall inside it. The output of a query is a list of integers, one per chunk, in chronological order.

title: Maximum Students Taking Exam
explanation_short: You are given an m × n matrix where each cell is either ‘#’ (broken seat) or ‘.’ (usable seat). Choose a subset of the usable seats to place students so that no two students sit next to each other horizontally or diagonally upward (left‑up or right‑up), because they could see each other’s answers. The arrangement must respect these visibility restrictions across all rows. Return the largest possible number of students that can be seated without any cheating risk.

title: Product of the Last K Numbers
explanation_short: You receive a sequence of operations on a growing list of integers. Each operation is either “add x”, which appends the integer x to the end of the list, or “product k”, which asks for the product of the last k numbers currently in the list. For every “product k” request you must return the computed product as a 32‑bit integer. The list can be arbitrarily long, and the operations are processed in the order they appear.

title: Construct Target Array With Multiple Sums
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `target`. Starting with an array of the same length that contains only 1’s, you may repeatedly pick an index and replace its value by the sum of all current elements. Your task is to decide whether a sequence of such operations can turn the all‑ones array into the given `target`. Return `true` if it is possible, otherwise return `false`.

title: Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid where each row and each column is sorted from largest to smallest. Your task is to determine how many entries in the matrix are negative numbers. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element is a pair [startDay, endDay] describing an event’s time window. You may attend at most one event on any given day, and you can choose any day inside an event’s interval to attend it. Your task is to schedule attendances so that the total number of different events you attend is as large as possible. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Sort Integers by The Number of 1 Bits
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers. Rearrange the elements so that those with fewer 1‑bits in their binary form come first, and if two numbers have the same number of 1‑bits they should appear in increasing numeric order. Return the array after this sorting.

title: Apply Discount Every n Orders
explanation_short: You are given two lists that map each product ID to its price, and for each purchase you receive a list of product IDs together with the quantities bought. For every call you must compute the subtotal by multiplying each quantity by the corresponding product’s price and summing the results. The cashier applies a percentage discount only on every n‑th customer; on those customers the final amount equals the subtotal multiplied by (100 – discount)/100. The method should return the amount the current customer actually pays.

title: Count All Valid Pickup and Delivery Options
explanation_short: You receive an integer n, the number of orders, where each order has a pickup event Pi and a delivery event Di. You must count how many sequences of the 2n events keep every delivery after its corresponding pickup. The result should be given modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` that contains only the letters a, b, and c.  
Your task is to count how many of its contiguous substrings include at least one a, one b, and one c.  
Each possible substring of `s` should be considered, and only those meeting the three‑character requirement contribute to the total.  
Return that total count as an integer.

title: Validate Binary Tree Nodes
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and two length‑n arrays: leftChild[i] and rightChild[i], where each entry is either the index of a child node or –1 if that child is missing. Using these arrays you must decide whether the n nodes can be arranged into a single, well‑formed binary tree (one root, no cycles, and every node reachable from the root). The answer should be returned as a Boolean: true if the structure is a valid binary tree, otherwise false. No node values are involved-only the indices matter.

title: Number of Days Between Two Dates
explanation_short: You are given two strings that each represent a calendar date in the form YYYY‑MM‑DD. Determine the number of whole days that lie between the earlier date and the later date, counting only full days and ignoring any time‑of‑day details. Output this count as a single integer (zero when the dates are identical).

title: Closest Divisors
explanation_short:
You receive a single integer `num`.  
Consider the two numbers `num + 1` and `num + 2`; for each of them look for a pair of integers whose product equals that number.  
Among all such pairs, choose the one whose two numbers are as close together as possible (i.e., with the smallest absolute difference).  
Return the chosen pair in any order.

title: How Many Numbers Are Smaller Than the Current Number
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. For each position `i` you must determine how many other elements in the array have a value strictly less than `nums[i]`. Return a new array where the i‑th entry holds that count, preserving the original order of `nums`.

title: Largest Multiple of Three
explanation_short: You are given a list of single‑digit numbers. From these digits you may pick any subset and arrange them in any order to build the biggest possible integer that is divisible by 3. Return that integer as a string without extra leading zeros; if no such number can be formed, return an empty string.

title: Linked List in Binary Tree
explanation_short:
You are given the first node of a singly‑linked list and the root of a binary tree.  
Check whether there exists any downward path in the tree-starting at some node and moving only to its left or right child-whose node values appear in the same order as the values in the linked list.  
If such a matching path can be found, the answer is true; otherwise it is false.  
The output is a single Boolean value.

title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid where each cell contains a number (1‑4) that indicates the direction you must move from that cell. By changing the direction in any cell you pay a cost of 1, and you may change each cell at most once. Find the smallest total cost needed so that, starting at the top‑left corner, you can follow the directions (including the changed ones) to eventually reach the bottom‑right corner; output that minimum cost.

title: Rank Teams by Votes
explanation_short: You receive an array of strings, each string showing one voter’s complete ranking of the teams from best to worst. Your task is to order all teams by comparing how many first‑place votes each got, then second‑place votes to break any ties, and so on down the ranks. If teams are still tied after all positions are considered, they are ordered alphabetically. Return a single string that lists the teams in their final ranking order.

title: Increasing Decreasing String
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
You must repeatedly take the smallest remaining character, then the next larger ones up to the largest, and afterwards the largest remaining character back down to the smallest, removing each character you use.  
Continue this process until every character from the original string has been placed in the new order.  
Return the string that results from this reordering.

title: Longest ZigZag Path in a Binary Tree
explanation_short: You receive a binary tree via its root node (often described by a level‑order array). A ZigZag path is a sequence of nodes where each step alternates between going to a left child and then a right child, or vice‑versa. Your task is to determine the maximum number of edges (nodes visited minus one) that can be traversed in such an alternating fashion anywhere in the tree. Return that maximum length as an integer.

title: Find the Longest Substring Containing Vowels in Even Counts
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Your task is to locate a contiguous part of the string such that each of the five vowels (a, e, i, o, u) occurs an even number of times inside that part (zero counts as even).  
Among all substrings that satisfy this condition, determine the maximum possible length.  
Return that length as an integer.

title: Generate a String With Characters That Have Odd Counts
explanation_short:
You are given an integer n.  
Create a string of exactly n characters using only lowercase English letters, making sure that every letter that appears does so an odd number of times.  
Any string that satisfies this condition is acceptable.  
Return the resulting string.

title: Number of Times Binary String Is Prefix-Aligned
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `flips` that tells, in order, which positions of an initially all‑zero binary string are toggled from 0 to 1. After each toggle, consider the current step number `i`; the string is “prefix‑aligned” when the first `i` positions are all 1 and every later position remains 0. Your task is to count how many steps of the process produce a prefix‑aligned string. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Sum BST in Binary Tree
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree, where each node stores an integer value. Among all possible sub‑trees of this tree, consider only those that satisfy the binary search‑tree ordering rules. Your task is to determine which such BST sub‑tree has the largest total of its node values. Return that maximum sum as an integer.

title: Time Needed to Inform All Employees
explanation_short: You are given the number of employees `n`, the ID of the head `headID`, an array `manager` where `manager[i]` tells who directly manages employee `i` (with `manager[headID] = -1`), and an array `informTime` where `informTime[i]` is the minutes employee `i` needs before all of his direct reports start spreading the news. Starting from the head, the news propagates down the management tree, and each manager adds his own delay before his subordinates can continue. Compute the longest total delay from the head to any leaf employee, which is the time required for everyone to be informed. Return that total time as an integer.

title: Frog Position After T Seconds
explanation_short: You are given the number of vertices n, a list of undirected edges that form a tree, a time limit t, and a target vertex. A frog starts at vertex 1 and each second moves to an unvisited neighbor chosen uniformly at random; if no unvisited neighbor exists it stays put forever. You must determine the probability that the frog’s position after exactly t seconds is the target vertex. Return this probability as a floating‑point number (acceptable error ≤ 10⁻⁵).

title: Design a Stack With Increment Operation
explanation_short: You receive a list of commands such as “push x”, “pop”, and “increment k val”, each possibly followed by numbers. The stack must behave normally for push (add to the top) and pop (remove and return the top, or –1 if empty), but the increment command adds val to each of the bottom k elements currently in the stack. Process the commands in order, applying these rules, and output the values returned by every pop operation.

title: Find a Corresponding Node of a Binary Tree in a Clone of That Tree
explanation_short: You are given two identical binary trees – the original and its clone – together with a pointer to a node in the original tree. Your task is to locate the node that occupies the same position in the cloned tree without altering either tree. Return the reference to that node in the cloned tree as the answer.

title: Balance a Binary Search Tree
explanation_short: You are given the root node of a binary search tree, which contains a set of integer values arranged so that every left child is smaller and every right child is larger than its parent. Your task is to rearrange those same values into a new binary search tree where, for every node, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most one. The output should be the root of any such balanced tree; the exact shape may vary as long as the BST property and balance condition hold. The input and output are both represented as standard tree structures (e.g., adjacency lists or node objects).

title: Lucky Numbers in a Matrix
explanation_short: You are given an m × n matrix containing distinct integers. Find every element that is the smallest value in its own row while simultaneously being the largest value in its column. Return those elements as a list, in any order.

title: Maximum Performance of a Team
explanation_short: You are given an integer n, an integer k, and two length‑n arrays: speed[i] and efficiency[i] for each engineer i. You must choose up to k different engineers to form a team. The team’s performance equals the sum of the chosen engineers’ speeds multiplied by the smallest efficiency among them. Return the largest achievable performance, taken modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Cinema Seat Allocation
explanation_short: You are given the number of rows n and a list of already‑reserved seats, each expressed as a row number and a seat label from 1 to 10. A four‑person group must sit in four consecutive seats within the same row; seats on opposite sides of the aisle are not adjacent, except that a group may be split exactly in the middle of the aisle (two people on each side). Your task is to determine how many such groups can be placed without using any reserved seat. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Sort Integers by The Power Value
explanation_short: You are given three integers lo, hi and k, where lo ≤ hi defines a consecutive range of numbers. For every integer x in that range you must determine its “power” – the count of steps required to reach 1 by repeatedly applying the rule x → x/2 if x is even, otherwise x → 3·x + 1. After computing these powers, sort the numbers first by increasing power and break ties by the numeric value itself. The answer is the k‑th element (1‑based) in this sorted list.

title: Find the Distance Value Between Two Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays and an integer d. For each element of the first array, check whether any element of the second array lies within a distance d (i.e., the absolute difference is ≤ d). Count how many elements of the first array have no such close counterpart in the second array. Return that count as the result.

title: Create Target Array in the Given Order
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of equal length: `nums` and `index`. Starting with an empty list, take the elements of `nums` one by one and insert each element at the position specified by the matching entry in `index`. Perform the insertions in the order they appear in the arrays. After all insertions are done, output the resulting target array.

title: Check if There is a Valid Path in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of integers, where each integer encodes a specific street shape that connects certain sides of its cell. Starting from the cell at the top‑left corner, you must move only along those street connections and try to reach the cell at the bottom‑right corner. You cannot modify any street type; you simply follow the existing connections between adjacent cells. Return true if such a path exists, otherwise return false.

title: Pizza With 3n Slices
explanation_short: You are given an array `slices` of length 3 × n, where each element is the size of a pizza slice arranged clockwise. You will take turns picking slices: each time you choose one slice, the two friends immediately take the slices directly to its left and right, so the slices you pick can never be adjacent. Your goal is to select exactly n slices (one out of every three) so that the total size of the slices you collect is as large as possible. Return that maximum possible sum as an integer.

title: Four Divisors
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers called nums. For each element, determine whether it possesses exactly four positive divisors. If it does, sum all of its divisors and add that sum to a running total. Return the final total, or 0 if no number in the array meets the four‑divisor condition.

title: Longest Happy Prefix
explanation_short: The input is a single string s. You need to find a non‑empty prefix of s that also occurs as a suffix, but the entire string itself cannot be used. Return the longest such prefix; if no prefix matches a suffix, return an empty string. The output is that longest happy prefix (or “”).

title: Design Underground System
explanation_short: You receive a series of commands that either record a passenger’s check‑in at a station with a timestamp, record their check‑out at another station with a later timestamp, or ask for the average travel time between two specific stations. For each “average” query you must compute the mean of all recorded trips that started at the given start station and ended at the given end station. The result of each query is a single floating‑point number representing that average. All check‑in and check‑out events are guaranteed to be consistent, so you never need to handle mismatched or missing data.

title: Count Number of Teams
explanation_short: You receive an array of distinct integers that represent the ratings of soldiers arranged in a line. A team is any three positions i < j < k where the three ratings are either strictly increasing or strictly decreasing. Count all such triples; a soldier can appear in many different teams. Return the total number as an integer.

title: Find All Good Strings
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and three strings s1, s2, and evil, all of length n (for s1 and s2) or shorter (for evil). Your task is to count how many length‑n strings are lexicographically between s1 and s2 (including the endpoints) while never containing evil as a contiguous substring. Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Find Lucky Integer in an Array
explanation_short: The input is an array of integers. A lucky integer is a value that appears in the array exactly as many times as the value itself. You must find the largest such lucky integer, or return –1 if none exist. The output is that single integer.

title: Construct K Palindrome Strings
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`.  
Using every character of `s` (reordering is allowed) you must split the characters into exactly `k` non‑empty groups, each of which forms a palindrome.  
A palindrome reads the same forward and backward, so each group must have at most one character with odd frequency.  
Return **true** if such a partition exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: Reducing Dishes
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `satisfaction` where each element represents the satisfaction value of a dish. You may choose any subset of dishes and arrange them in any order, cooking one dish per time unit; the like‑time coefficient of a dish equals its cooking time (starting from 1) multiplied by its satisfaction value. Your task is to select the dishes and ordering that maximize the sum of all like‑time coefficients. Output that maximum possible total as a single integer.

title: Count Largest Group
explanation_short:
You receive a single integer n.  
All numbers from 1 to n are placed into groups where two numbers belong to the same group exactly when the sum of their decimal digits is equal.  
Your task is to find how many of those groups contain the maximum possible number of elements.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Circle and Rectangle Overlapping
explanation_short: You are given a circle defined by its radius and center point (xCenter, yCenter), together with an axis‑aligned rectangle given by its lower‑left corner (x1, y1) and upper‑right corner (x2, y2). Your task is to decide whether there exists at least one point that lies inside the circle and also inside the rectangle. In other words, you must check if the two shapes intersect at any location. Return the Boolean value true if they overlap, otherwise return false.

title: Minimum Subsequence in Non-Increasing Order
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. From it you must choose some elements (keeping their original order is not required) so that the sum of the chosen elements is strictly larger than the sum of the elements left out. Among all such choices, you need the one with the smallest possible number of elements, and if several have that size, you pick the one whose total sum is greatest. Return the selected elements sorted from largest to smallest.

title: Stone Game III
explanation_short: You are given an array stoneValue where each element is the value of a stone in a line. Alice moves first, and on each turn a player may take the first one, two, or three remaining stones, adding their values to their own total score. Assuming both players always choose moves that maximize their final score, determine whether Alice ends with a higher total, Bob ends with a higher total, or they finish with equal totals. Return the string "Alice", "Bob", or "Tie" accordingly.

title: String Matching in an Array
explanation_short: You are given a list of words, each word being a string. Your task is to identify every word that occurs as a contiguous piece inside any other word in the same list. Return those qualifying words as a collection, in any order.

title: Queries on a Permutation With Key
explanation_short:
You are given a list `queries` of integers and a number `m`.  
Start with the permutation `P = [1, 2, …, m]`. For each value in `queries` you must locate its current index in `P`, record that index (0‑based or 1‑based as defined by the problem), then move the queried value to the front of `P`.  
The result you return is the sequence of recorded indices, one for each query.

title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number in Binary Representation to One
explanation_short: You are given a binary string `s` that represents a positive integer. Starting from that number, repeatedly apply the following operations: if the current value is even, halve it; if it is odd, add 1. Count how many operations are required until the value becomes 1. Return that count as an integer.

title: Longest Happy String
explanation_short: You are given three integers a, b, and c that represent how many times the letters ‘a’, ‘b’, and ‘c’ may appear. Using at most those counts, you must construct the longest possible string where no character occurs three times in a row. If several strings achieve the maximum length, any one of them is acceptable; if no such string can be formed, return an empty string. The output is that constructed string (or “”).

title: HTML Entity Parser
explanation_short: You receive a single string that may contain HTML entity codes such as &, <, >, ", and '. Your task is to scan the text and replace every valid entity with the character it represents, leaving any unrecognized sequences unchanged. The result should be a new string where all these substitutions have been applied. Return that transformed string as the output.

title: Find the Minimum Number of Fibonacci Numbers Whose Sum Is K
explanation_short: You are given a single integer k. Your task is to choose some Fibonacci numbers (you may reuse a number) so that their total equals k, and you must use as few numbers as possible. The answer you return is that minimum count of Fibonacci numbers needed to reach the sum k.

title: Restore The Array
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` that contains only digits and an integer `k`. You must determine how many different ways the digits can be partitioned into a sequence of positive integers, each between 1 and `k`, such that no number has a leading zero. Return that count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Number of Ways to Paint N × 3 Grid
explanation_short: You are given an integer n that represents the number of rows in a grid that is n by 3. Each cell must be colored either Red, Yellow, or Green, and any two cells that share a side cannot have the same color. Your task is to count how many different complete colorings of the whole grid satisfy this rule. Return that count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: The k-th Lexicographical String of All Happy Strings of Length n
explanation_short: You are given two integers n and k. A happy string of length n is any sequence of characters where no two adjacent characters are the same. Imagine listing every happy string of length n in alphabetical (lexicographical) order; you must return the k‑th string in that list. If fewer than k happy strings exist, output an empty string.

title: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers `nums`.  
Pick a positive integer `startValue` and form a running total by adding `startValue` to the first element, then adding the second element to that sum, and so on from left to right.  
The running total must never drop below 1 at any step.  
Output the smallest positive `startValue` that satisfies this condition.

title: Reformat The String
explanation_short: You are given a string s that contains only lowercase letters and digits. Your task is to reorder its characters so that no two neighboring characters are both letters or both digits-letters and digits must alternate. If such an arrangement exists, return any one of those reordered strings; otherwise return an empty string.

title: Display Table of Food Orders in a Restaurant
explanation_short: You receive a list of orders, each given as a customer name, a table number, and a food item. From this you must build a “display table” where the first row is a header: the word “Table” followed by every distinct food item sorted alphabetically, and each following row corresponds to one table (sorted by table number) showing how many of each item that table ordered. The result should be returned as a two‑dimensional array of strings, with the header row first and the count rows after it.

title: Minimum Number of Frogs Croaking
explanation_short: The input is a single string that mixes the letters of several “croak” sounds made by frogs. You must check whether the whole string can be partitioned into complete, ordered sequences of the letters c‑r‑o‑a‑k. If it can, find the smallest number of frogs that could be croaking simultaneously to produce those sequences. Return that minimum count, or -1 if the string cannot be formed from valid “croak”s.

title: Build Array Where You Can Find The Maximum Exactly K Comparisons
explanation_short:
You are given three integers n, m and k.  
Construct an array arr of length n where each element is a positive integer between 1 and m.  
Count how many different arrays cause the described maximum‑finding procedure to perform exactly k comparisons.  
Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Maximum Score After Splitting a String
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` consisting only of the characters ‘0’ and ‘1’. Choose a split point that creates a non‑empty left part and a non‑empty right part, then count how many ‘0’s appear in the left part and how many ‘1’s appear in the right part. The task is to find the split that makes the sum of those two counts as large as possible and output that maximum sum.

title: Diagonal Traverse II
explanation_short: You are given a jagged 2D array of integers, where each inner list may have a different length. Imagine drawing diagonals that start from the top‑left element and move down‑right, collecting elements that lie on the same diagonal. Your task is to list all numbers following those diagonals, from the first diagonal to the last. Return the resulting sequence as a one‑dimensional list.

title: Constrained Subsequence Sum
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`.  
Choose a non‑empty subsequence of the array such that any two chosen elements are at most `k` positions apart in the original order.  
Among all subsequences that satisfy this distance constraint, find the one whose elements add up to the largest possible total.  
Return that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers representing the points on cards placed in a line and an integer k. In exactly k moves you may remove a card either from the left end or the right end, adding its points to your score. Your task is to choose which ends to take from so that the total sum of the k selected cards is as large as possible. Return that maximum possible sum.

title: Kids With the Greatest Number of Candies
explanation_short: You are given an integer array where each element tells how many candies a particular kid currently has, plus one extra integer extraCandies. For every kid, imagine giving them all of the extra candies and decide whether their new total would be at least as large as the maximum candy count among all kids. Produce a list of Boolean values, one for each kid, that is true when this condition holds and false otherwise. The result array has the same length as the input array.

title: Check If a String Can Break Another String
explanation_short:
You are given two strings `s1` and `s2` that have the same length.  
We must decide whether we can rearrange the letters of one string so that, after also rearranging the other string, every character in the first string is alphabetically greater than or equal to the character at the same position in the second string.  
The condition may hold in either direction (either `s1` can break `s2` or `s2` can break `s1`).  
Return **true** if such a pair of permutations exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: Max Difference You Can Get From Changing an Integer
explanation_short: You are given a single integer `num`. You may apply the following transformation twice, each time independently: pick one digit that appears in `num` and replace every occurrence of that digit with another digit from 1 to 9, making sure the new number has no leading zeros and is not zero. The two results of the transformations are called `a` and `b`. Return the largest possible value of `a − b`.

title: Number of Ways to Wear Different Hats to Each Other
explanation_short: You are given an array where the i‑th sub‑array lists all hat numbers (1‑40) that person i likes. You must assign each person a hat they like, making sure no two people wear the same hat. The task is to count how many distinct assignments satisfy these conditions. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Find the Kth Smallest Sum of a Matrix With Sorted Rows
explanation_short: You receive an m × n matrix where each row is sorted in non‑decreasing order, and an integer k. From every row you must pick exactly one element, forming a new array, and compute the sum of its entries. Among all possible sums generated by the different choices, you need to determine the k‑th smallest one. The answer to return is that k‑th smallest sum value.

title: Destination City
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element contains two city names, the first being the start of a direct route and the second its destination. Your task is to identify the city that never appears as a start point in any of those routes. Because the routes form a single line, there will be exactly one such city. Return that city’s name as a string.

title: Check If All 1's Are at Least Length K Places Away
explanation_short:
You are given an array that contains only 0s and 1s, together with an integer k.  
Your task is to examine every pair of positions that contain a 1 and see how far apart they are.  
If the distance between any two 1’s is less than k, the condition fails; otherwise it holds for the whole array.  
Return true when all 1’s are at least k places apart, and false if any pair is closer.

title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers and a single integer called limit.  
Your task is to locate the longest contiguous segment of the array such that the absolute difference between the smallest and largest values inside that segment never exceeds limit.  
The segment must contain at least one element, and you must consider every possible contiguous segment.  
Return the length of the longest segment that satisfies the condition.

title: Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array arr.  
Choose three indices i, j, k with 0 ≤ i < j ≤ k < n so that the XOR of the elements from i to j‑1 equals the XOR of the elements from j to k.  
Count how many different triples (i, j, k) satisfy this condition.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Minimum Time to Collect All Apples in a Tree
explanation_short: You are given the number of vertices n, a list of undirected edges connecting those vertices, and a boolean array indicating which vertices contain an apple. Starting from vertex 0, you may walk along any edge (costing one second per edge) and must collect every apple that exists in the tree, then return to vertex 0. Your task is to determine the smallest possible total travel time that allows you to pick up all apples and finish back at the start. The answer should be returned as a single integer representing that minimum number of seconds.

title: Number of Ways of Cutting a Pizza
explanation_short: You receive a rectangular grid of characters, where ‘A’ denotes an apple and ‘.’ denotes an empty cell, together with an integer k. You must perform exactly k − 1 cuts, each cut being either vertical or horizontal, and each cut gives the left or top portion of the current pizza to a person while the remaining part continues to be cut. The task is to count how many different sequences of cuts produce k pieces such that every piece contains at least one apple. Output this count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Build an Array With Stack Operations
explanation_short: You receive an integer array target and a number n. Imagine reading the integers 1 through n one by one, and you may either push the current integer onto an initially empty stack or pop the top element of the stack. Choose a sequence of these operations so that after processing some prefix of the stream, the stack’s contents from bottom to top exactly match target. Return the operations as a list of the strings “Push” and “Pop”.

title: Number of Students Doing Homework at a Given Time
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of the same length: `startTime[i]` marks when the i‑th student begins homework and `endTime[i]` marks when they finish. A single integer `queryTime` is also provided. You must count how many students have a time interval that includes `queryTime`, meaning `startTime[i] ≤ queryTime ≤ endTime[i]`. Return that count as an integer.

title: Rearrange Words in a Sentence
explanation_short:
You receive a single string that contains several words separated by spaces.  
Your job is to reorder those words so that shorter words come before longer ones, while keeping the original relative order for any words that share the same length.  
After rearranging, the first word of the resulting sentence must start with a capital letter and the rest should be in lower‑case.  
Return the newly ordered sentence as a single space‑separated string.

title: Consecutive Characters
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Your task is to look at every contiguous block of characters that are all the same and determine which block is the longest.  
The length of that longest block is called the string’s power.  
Return this length as an integer.

title: Simplified Fractions
explanation_short:
You are given an integer n.  
List every fraction a/b that lies strictly between 0 and 1, where b ≤ n and a and b share no common divisor greater than 1.  
Each fraction should be represented as the string “a/b”.  
Return the collection of these strings in any order.

title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
explanation_short: The input is a binary tree represented by its root node, each node containing an integer value. A node is “good” when its value is not smaller than any value on the path from the root to that node. You must determine how many nodes in the tree are good. The output is a single integer giving that count.

title: Form Largest Integer With Digits That Add up to Target
explanation_short: You are given an array `cost` of nine integers where `cost[i]` is the price to paint digit `i+1`, and a target integer `target`. Using any combination of digits whose total painting cost equals exactly `target`, you must form the numerically largest possible integer. The result can be very long, so it should be returned as a string; if no combination reaches the target, return `"0"`. The output is that maximal integer represented as a string.

title: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
explanation_short: You are given a string s and an integer k. Consider every contiguous segment of s that is exactly k characters long. Among those segments, determine how many vowel letters (a, e, i, o, u) appear in each and keep the largest count you find. Output that maximum number of vowels.

title: People Whose List of Favorite Companies Is Not a Subset of Another List
explanation_short: You are given a list where each element is the collection of favorite company names for one person. For every person, check whether their whole collection appears inside the collection of any other person. Keep the indices of those whose collections are **not** completely contained in any other person’s list. Return those indices sorted in ascending order.

title: Maximum Number of Darts Inside of a Circular Dartboard
explanation_short: You are given a list of n points (xᵢ, yᵢ) representing dart hits and an integer r that is the radius of a circular dartboard. Your task is to choose a center for a circle of radius r so that the circle contains as many of the given points as possible (points on the boundary count). Return the largest number of darts that can be covered by such a circle.

title: Check If a Word Occurs As a Prefix of Any Word in a Sentence
explanation_short: You receive a sentence made of words separated by single spaces and a separate string called searchWord. Your task is to locate the first word in the sentence whose beginning matches searchWord exactly as a prefix. Return the position of that word using 1‑based indexing, or –1 if no word starts with the given prefix.

title: Make Two Arrays Equal by Reversing Subarrays
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays of the same length, `target` and `arr`. You may repeatedly pick any contiguous segment of `arr` and reverse the order of its elements. Determine whether, after any number of such reversals, `arr` can be made exactly equal to `target`, and return `true` if it can or `false` otherwise.

title: Pseudo-Palindromic Paths in a Binary Tree
explanation_short: You are given a binary tree where each node holds a digit from 1 to 9. For every path that starts at the root and ends at a leaf, check whether the digits on that path can be reordered to form a palindrome (i.e., at most one digit appears an odd number of times). Return the total number of such pseudo‑palindromic root‑to‑leaf paths.

title: Course Schedule IV
explanation_short: You are given the total number of courses, a list of prerequisite pairs [a, b] meaning course a must be taken before course b, and a list of query pairs [u, v]. For each query you must decide whether course u is a prerequisite of course v, either directly or through a chain of other courses. The result should be a Boolean array where each element corresponds to a query. An entry is true if u must be completed before v, and false otherwise.

title: Max Dot Product of Two Subsequences
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2. Choose a non‑empty subsequence from each array, preserving the original order, and make sure the two subsequences have equal length. Compute the dot product of the selected elements (sum of each pair’s product). Output the maximum dot product achievable.

title: Maximum Area of a Piece of Cake After Horizontal and Vertical Cuts
explanation_short: You are given the height `h` and width `w` of a rectangular cake together with two lists: `horizontalCuts` and `verticalCuts`, which contain the positions (measured from the top or left edge) where straight cuts are made. After performing all those cuts the cake is divided into many smaller rectangles. Your task is to determine the area of the biggest resulting rectangle. Return that maximum area reduced modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Cherry Pickup II
explanation_short: You are given a rectangular grid where each cell contains a non‑negative number of cherries. Two robots start on the first row-one at the leftmost column and the other at the rightmost column-and at each step they both move down to the next row, each choosing to stay in the same column, move left, or move right (staying within the grid). As they travel, they collect the cherries in the cells they occupy, counting a cell’s cherries only once even if both robots land on it simultaneously. Return the largest possible total number of cherries the two robots can gather by the time they reach the bottom row.

title: Probability of a Two Boxes Having The Same Number of Distinct Balls
explanation_short: You are given an integer array balls where balls[i] is the number of balls of the i‑th color, and the total number of balls equals 2 × n. After shuffling all balls uniformly at random, the first n balls go to box 1 and the remaining n balls go to box 2 (the boxes are distinguishable). You must compute the probability that the two boxes contain the same count of distinct colors. The answer should be returned as a decimal value, accurate to within 10⁻⁵.

title: Check If a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size K
explanation_short: You are given a binary string `s` and an integer `k`. You must determine whether every possible binary pattern of length `k` (there are `2^k` of them) occurs somewhere as a contiguous substring of `s`. Return **true** if all such patterns appear, otherwise return **false**.

title: Maximum Product of Two Elements in an Array
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers called `nums`.  
Pick any two different positions `i` and `j` in the array, subtract 1 from each of the chosen numbers, and multiply the results.  
Your task is to determine the largest possible value that can be obtained this way.  
Return that maximum product as a single integer.

title: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to the City Zero
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of n – 1 pairs, each pair [a, b] meaning there is a one‑way road from city a to city b. Because the roads form a tree, there is exactly one undirected path between any two cities. Your task is to flip the direction of as few roads as possible so that every city can reach city 0 by following the directed roads. Return the smallest number of flips required.

title: Design Browser History
explanation_short: The input consists of a list of operations on a browser‑history object, starting with the homepage URL and followed by commands such as visit(url), back(steps), and forward(steps). For each visit call you move to a new page, discarding any forward history; for back or forward you move the current position up to the requested number of steps but never beyond the available history. The task is to simulate these actions in order, keeping track of the current page after each operation. The output is an array where the result of visit operations is null and the result of back or forward operations is the URL of the page you end up on.

title: Paint House III
explanation_short: You are given an array `houses` of length `m` where each entry is 0 (unpainted) or a fixed color 1…`n`. For every unpainted house you may choose a color, paying the corresponding amount from the `cost` matrix, while already painted houses must keep their color. The goal is to paint the houses so that the total number of contiguous groups of the same color (neighborhoods) equals the given `target`. Return the smallest possible total painting cost, or -1 if achieving exactly `target` neighborhoods is impossible.

title: Shuffle the Array
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` that contains `2 × n` integers arranged as `[x1, x2, …, xn, y1, y2, …, yn]` together with the integer `n`.  
Your task is to reorder the elements so that each `xi` is immediately followed by its corresponding `yi`.  
The resulting sequence should look like `[x1, y1, x2, y2, …, xn, yn]`.  
Return this reordered array as the output.

title: Final Prices With a Special Discount in a Shop
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers where each element is the price of an item in order. For every item you must locate the first later item whose price is not larger than the current one; the current price is reduced by that later price, and if no such item exists the price stays unchanged. Return a new array containing the resulting prices for all items.

title: Subrectangle Queries
explanation_short:
You are given a rectangular grid of integers that is passed to the constructor of a class.  
The class must support an operation that replaces every element inside a specified sub‑rectangle (defined by its top‑left and bottom‑right coordinates) with a new value.  
It also needs to answer queries that return the current value at any single cell identified by its row and column indices.  
The output of each query is the integer stored at the requested position after applying any prior updates.

title: The k Strongest Values in an Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array arr and an integer k. First find the centre, which is the element at index ((n – 1)/2) after sorting the array. Then pick the k values that are strongest: a value is stronger if its absolute distance to the centre is larger, and when distances tie the larger number wins. Return those k chosen values in any order.

title: Least Number of Unique Integers after K Removals
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `arr` and a number `k`. Exactly `k` elements must be deleted from the array, and you want to make the remaining collection contain as few different values as possible. Your task is to determine the smallest possible count of distinct integers that can remain after those deletions. The answer is a single integer representing that minimum.

title: Find Two Non-overlapping Sub-arrays Each With Target Sum
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers arr and an integer target. You must pick two sub‑arrays that do not overlap, each of whose elements add up to target. From all possible pairs, choose the one whose combined length (the total number of elements in both sub‑arrays) is smallest. Return that minimum total length, or -1 if no such pair of sub‑arrays exists.

title: Allocate Mailboxes
explanation_short: You are given a list of integers representing the positions of houses along a line and an integer k. You must choose exactly k locations for mailboxes so that each house’s distance to its nearest mailbox is as small as possible. The goal is to compute the smallest possible sum of those distances. Return that minimum total distance as a single integer.

title: Running Sum of 1d Array
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array named `nums`.  
Create a new array where the element at index `i` equals the sum of `nums[0]` through `nums[i]`.  
This sequence of cumulative totals is called the running sum.  
Output the resulting array.

title: XOR Operation in an Array
explanation_short: You receive two integers n and start. From them you form a length‑n array where the i‑th element equals start + 2·i (for i starting at 0). Your task is to compute the bitwise XOR of every element in this array and output that single integer result.

title: Making File Names Unique
explanation_short: You are given a list of folder names in the order they will be created. When a name appears for the first time it stays unchanged, but if it has already been used the system must append “(k)” with the smallest positive k that makes the whole string new. You must determine what name the system will actually assign at each step. Return an array containing those final names in the same order as the input.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
explanation_short: You receive an array where each position tells the day a flower will bloom, plus two numbers m and k. You must wait until you can select m separate groups of k adjacent flowers that have all bloomed, using each flower only once. The task is to determine the smallest day on which this is possible, or return -1 if the garden never contains enough suitable groups.

title: Path Crossing
explanation_short: You receive a string made of the letters N, S, E, W, each meaning a one‑unit move north, south, east, or west from the starting point (0, 0). As you follow the moves in order, you need to check whether you ever step onto a coordinate that you have already been on. Return true if any location is visited twice (including the start), and false if every position is unique.

title: Kth Ancestor of a Tree Node
explanation_short: You are given a tree of n nodes labeled 0 to n‑1, described by an array where each entry tells the parent of that node (the root 0 has no parent). Afterwards a series of queries each provide a node v and an integer k. For each query you must determine the node that lies k steps upward on the path from v to the root, or report that such a node does not exist. The output is the answer for every query, one per line.

title: Number of Subsequences That Satisfy the Given Sum Condition
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`.  
Consider every non‑empty subsequence you can form from `nums`; for each one look at its smallest and largest values.  
Count how many of those subsequences have the sum of their minimum and maximum elements less than or equal to `target`.  
Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Avoid Flood in The City
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array rains where each positive value i means rain fills lake i on that day, and a value 0 means the day can be used to dry one lake.  
Your task is to pick, for every dry day, which lake to empty so that no lake ever receives rain while it is already full.  
Return an array of the same length: put -1 for rain days, and for each dry day put the index of the lake you chose to dry (any lake can be chosen if it’s already empty).  
If it’s impossible to avoid a flood, return an empty array.

title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
explanation_short:
You are given an integer n and an array edges where each entry describes an undirected edge by its two endpoints and its weight.  
First, consider all possible minimum‑spanning trees of the graph.  
Identify edges that must appear in every MST (their removal makes the best possible total weight larger) as critical, and edges that can belong to some MSTs but are not required as pseudo‑critical.  
Return two lists of the original edge indices: the first containing all critical edges, the second containing all pseudo‑critical edges (order is irrelevant).

title: Reformat Date
explanation_short: You receive a single text line that contains a day, a month name, and a year (for example, “20th Oct 2052”). The day includes a numeric value followed by “st”, “nd”, “rd”, or “th”, and the month is given as a three‑letter abbreviation. Your task is to rearrange these parts so the result follows the ISO style “year‑month‑day”, using two digits for month and day and four digits for year. The program should output the reformatted date as a string like “2052-10-20”.

title: Check If Array Pairs Are Divisible by k
explanation_short: You are given an array arr with an even number of integers and a divisor k. You must decide whether the elements can be grouped into exactly n / 2 pairs, using each element once, so that the sum of every pair is a multiple of k. The answer is a single Boolean value: return true if such a pairing is possible, otherwise return false.

title: Max Value of Equation
explanation_short: You receive a list of points `[xi, yi]` sorted by their x‑coordinates and an integer `k`. For every pair of points whose x‑difference does not exceed `k`, compute the value `yi + yj + |xi – xj|`. Return the largest such value among all valid pairs.

title: Stone Game IV
explanation_short: You are given a single positive integer n that represents the number of stones in a pile. Alice moves first, and on each turn a player may remove any positive perfect‑square number of stones (1, 4, 9, …). If a player has no legal move they lose. Assuming both players always choose the best possible moves, decide whether Alice can force a win. Return true if Alice can guarantee a win, otherwise return false.

title: Minimum Difference Between Largest and Smallest Value in Three Moves
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. You may pick at most three positions in the array and replace each chosen element with any value you like. After performing those replacements, consider the maximum and minimum numbers that remain in the array and compute their difference. Return the smallest possible difference achievable with up to three moves.

title: Range Sum of Sorted Subarray Sums
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers `nums` and two positions `left` and `right`. First form the sums of every non‑empty contiguous subarray, sort those sums in non‑decreasing order, and then add together the values that lie between the `left`‑th and `right`‑th positions (using 1‑based indexing). Return this total modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Water Bottles
explanation_short: You are given two integers: `numBottles`, the number of full bottles you start with, and `numExchange`, the number of empty bottles required to trade for one new full bottle. You may repeatedly drink a full bottle (turning it into an empty one) and then exchange groups of empty bottles for more full bottles, continuing as long as enough empties are available. Return the total count of bottles you can drink before no further exchanges are possible.

title: Count Odd Numbers in an Interval Range
explanation_short:
You receive two non‑negative integers called low and high.  
Consider every integer from low through high, including the endpoints.  
Your task is to determine how many of those numbers are odd.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Number of Nodes in the Sub-Tree With the Same Label
explanation_short: You are given an integer n, a list of n − 1 undirected edges that form a tree rooted at node 0, and a string labels where labels[i] is the character label of node i. For each node, consider its subtree-the node itself together with all of its descendants in the rooted tree. You must determine how many nodes inside that subtree have the same label as the node itself. Return an array of length n where the i‑th element is this count for node i.

title: Best Position for a Service Centre
explanation_short:
You are given a list of customer coordinates, each expressed as a pair \([x_i, y_i]\).  
Choose a single point \([x_{\text{center}}, y_{\text{center}}]\) on the plane so that the total Euclidean distance from this point to every customer is as small as possible.  
The task is to compute that smallest possible sum of distances.  
Return the minimal sum, accepting answers that are accurate within \(10^{-5}\).

title: Maximum Number of Non-Overlapping Substrings
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` consisting of lowercase letters. From `s` you must pick a collection of non‑empty substrings that do not overlap, and each chosen substring must contain every occurrence of any character that appears inside it. The objective is to obtain as many such substrings as possible, and if several collections achieve that maximum count, you should return the one whose total length is smallest. Output the selected substrings in any order.

title: Number of Sub-arrays With Odd Sum
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `arr`. Your task is to count how many contiguous sub‑arrays have a sum that is an odd number, and because the total can be huge you must return the count modulo \(10^9+7\). The output is a single integer representing that modulo‑adjusted count.

title: Shuffle String
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` and an integer array `indices` that are both the same length. For each position `i`, the character at `s[i]` must be placed at position `indices[i]` in a new string. Return the string that results after all characters have been moved to their specified positions.

title: Number of Good Ways to Split a String
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s`. A split is made by cutting the string into two non‑empty parts, `sleft` and `sright`, whose concatenation equals the original string. A split is considered good when the number of distinct letters appearing in `sleft` is exactly the same as the number of distinct letters appearing in `sright`. Return the total number of good splits possible for the given string.

title: Minimum Suffix Flips
explanation_short: You receive a binary string target of length n. Starting with another string s of the same length that is all zeros, you may repeatedly choose an index i and flip every bit from i to the end of s. The task is to determine the smallest number of such operations required to transform s into target. Output that minimum count as an integer.

title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `target`. Starting from an array of the same length filled with zeros, you may repeatedly pick any contiguous segment and add 1 to every element in that segment. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of such operations that will turn the zero‑array exactly into `target`. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Minimum Swaps to Arrange a Binary Grid
explanation_short: You are given an n × n matrix containing only 0’s and 1’s. By repeatedly swapping two rows that are next to each other, you must arrange the rows so that every cell strictly above the main diagonal becomes 0. Return the smallest number of such swaps required, or -1 if no sequence of swaps can achieve the condition.

title: Number of Good Leaf Nodes Pairs
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree and an integer distance. A leaf node is a node with no children, and the shortest path between two nodes is the number of edges you must traverse to go from one to the other. Count how many unordered pairs of different leaf nodes have a path length that is at most distance. Return that count as the answer.

title: String Compression II
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`. You may delete at most `k` characters from `s`. After deletions, the remaining characters are encoded by run‑length encoding: single letters stay as they are, while a consecutive block of the same letter of length ≥ 2 becomes the letter followed by the block size. Output the minimum possible length of this encoded string.

title: Count Good Triplets
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array arr and three integers a, b, c.  
Consider every ordered triple of indices i < j < k; the corresponding values (arr[i], arr[j], arr[k]) form a “good” triplet when the absolute differences satisfy |arr[i]‑arr[j]| ≤ a, |arr[j]‑arr[k]| ≤ b, and |arr[i]‑arr[k]| ≤ c.  
Your task is to count how many such good triplets exist in the array.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Can Convert String in K Moves
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s` and `t` of the same length and an integer `k`. In each move you may increase a single character of `s` by one step in the alphabet (wrapping from `z` to `a`). You must decide whether it is possible to turn `s` into `t` using at most `k` such moves. Output “true” if the conversion can be done within the limit, otherwise output “false”.

title: Find the Winner of an Array Game
explanation_short: You are given a list of distinct numbers and a positive integer k. The game repeatedly compares the first two elements; the larger one stays at the front while the smaller one is moved to the back of the list. Play continues until some element wins k times in a row. Return that element, which is guaranteed to exist.

title: Minimum Insertions to Balance a Parentheses String
explanation_short: You are given a string s that contains only the characters ‘(’ and ‘)’. A balanced string requires every ‘(’ to be paired with a consecutive pair of ‘)’ characters, and any extra ‘)’ must also belong to such a pair. You may insert additional ‘(’ or ‘)’ characters anywhere in the string. Return the smallest number of insertions needed to turn s into a balanced string.

title: Get the Maximum Score
explanation_short:
You are given two increasing lists of distinct integers, nums1 and nums2.  
You may start at the beginning of either list and move forward, switching from one list to the other only at numbers that appear in both lists; the score of a path is the sum of all distinct numbers visited.  
Return the largest possible score among all such paths, taken modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Kth Missing Positive Number
explanation_short:
You are given a strictly increasing list of positive integers `arr` and a positive integer `k`.  
From the infinite sequence of positive numbers, consider only those that do **not** appear in `arr`; you must identify the `k`‑th one in that missing set.  
Return that `k`‑th missing positive integer as a single number.

title: Make The String Great
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` consisting of lower‑case and upper‑case English letters.  
Whenever two neighboring characters are the same letter but opposite in case (for example `aA` or `Bb`), you may delete that pair.  
You keep removing such adjacent pairs until no more deletions are possible, at which point the string is considered “good.”  
Return the final string after all possible deletions; it may be empty.

title: Find Longest Awesome Substring
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
A substring of `s` is called “awesome” if its characters can be reordered (by swapping any number of times) to form a palindrome.  
Your task is to determine the greatest possible length among all awesome substrings of `s`.  
Return that maximum length as an integer.

title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
explanation_short: You are given the length n of a stick (marked from 0 to n) and an array cuts containing positions where the stick must be cut. You may perform the cuts in any order, but each time you cut a piece its cost equals the current length of that piece. The goal is to choose an ordering of the cuts that makes the sum of all those costs as small as possible. Return that minimum total cost as a single integer.

title: Find Kth Bit in Nth Binary String
explanation_short: You are given two positive integers n and k. A binary string Sn is defined recursively: start with “0”, then for each i > 1 build Si = Si‑1 + “0” + reverse(invert(Si‑1)). The task is to determine which bit (0 or 1) appears at position k in the final string Sn. Output that single character as a string.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n, which defines an array of length n where the i‑th element equals 2·i + 1 (so the array starts [1, 3, 5,…]). In one operation you may pick two positions, add 1 to one element and subtract 1 from the other. Your task is to determine the smallest number of such operations required to make every element of the array have the same value. Output that minimum count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Number of Non-Overlapping Subarrays With Sum Equals Target
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a single integer `target`. Your task is to select as many non‑empty subarrays as possible so that each chosen subarray’s elements add up exactly to `target` and no two chosen subarrays share any index. Only the count of such non‑overlapping subarrays matters. Return that maximum possible count.

title: Three Consecutive Odds
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers.  
Check whether the array contains any three odd numbers that appear next to each other without any even numbers in between.  
If such a triple exists, the answer is true; otherwise it is false.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Eat N Oranges
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n representing the number of oranges. Each day you may either eat exactly one orange, or, if the current count is divisible by 2, eat half of them, or if it is divisible by 3, eat two‑thirds of them. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of days required to reduce the count to zero using those choices. Return that minimum number of days as an integer.

title: Magnetic Force Between Two Balls
explanation_short: You are given an array of basket positions and an integer m representing how many balls must be placed. You may choose any m different positions from the array, and the magnetic force between two balls equals the absolute distance between their positions. Your task is to arrange the balls so that the smallest distance among all chosen pairs is as large as possible. Return that largest achievable minimum distance as an integer.

title: Minimum Numbers of Function Calls to Make Target Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array nums. Starting from another array of the same length initialized with zeros, you may repeatedly call a function that either increments a single element by 1 or doubles all elements at once. Your task is to compute the smallest possible number of these function calls needed to turn the zero array into nums. Return that minimum count as an integer; it is guaranteed to fit in a 32‑bit signed integer.

title: Thousand Separator
explanation_short:
You receive a single integer `n`.  
Your task is to produce a textual version of that number where a dot (`.`) separates each group of three digits, counting from the rightmost side.  
If the number has fewer than four digits, the output is just the number itself.  
Return the result as a string.

title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
explanation_short: You are given a directed acyclic graph with n vertices labeled 0 to n‑1 and an array of directed edges. Your goal is to pick the smallest possible collection of vertices so that every node in the graph can be reached by following edges from at least one chosen vertex. The answer is guaranteed to be unique, and the vertices can be listed in any order. Return the selected vertices as a list of their indices.

title: Maximum Number of Coins You Can Get
explanation_short: You are given an array whose length is a multiple of three, where each element represents the number of coins in a pile. The piles will be divided into groups of three; in each group the friend with the highest‑valued pile takes it, you receive the second‑highest pile, and the remaining pile goes to the third player. Your task is to choose how to form the groups so that the sum of the piles you collect is as large as possible. Return that maximum possible sum.

title: Stone Game V
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers stoneValue that represents the values of stones placed in a line. Alice repeatedly splits the current segment into two non‑empty parts; Bob discards the part with the larger sum (or Alice decides when the sums are equal), and Alice adds the sum of the remaining part to her score. The game continues until only a single stone remains. Return the maximum total score Alice can obtain by choosing her splits wisely.

title: Detect Cycles in 2D Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of characters. You must check whether you can start from some cell, move only up, down, left, or right to neighboring cells that contain the same character, and eventually return to the starting cell after at least four moves without ever stepping back to the cell you just came from. A valid closed path of this kind is called a cycle. Return true if any such cycle exists in the grid; otherwise return false.

title: Most Visited Sector in  a Circular Track
explanation_short: You are given the number of sectors n and an array rounds that lists the start and end sector of each consecutive lap. While moving from each start to the next end you travel forward through the sector numbers, counting every sector you pass (including the start and end). Your task is to identify which sector(s) appear the most times during the whole sequence of laps. Output those sector numbers in increasing order.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Disconnect Island
explanation_short: You receive an m × n binary grid where 1 means land and 0 means water. An island is a set of land cells that are connected horizontally or vertically, and the grid is “connected” only when there is exactly one island. Each day you may change a single land cell to water, and you must find the fewest days needed so that the grid becomes disconnected (i.e., it has zero or more than one islands). Output that minimum number of days as an integer.

title: Find Latest Group of Size M
explanation_short: You are given a permutation arr of the numbers 1 to n and an integer m. Imagine a binary string of length n that starts with all zeros; at step i you set the bit at position arr[i] to 1. After each step you examine the contiguous groups of 1’s and check whether any group has exactly length m. Output the greatest step number at which such a group appears, or -1 if it never does.

title: Number of Ways to Reorder Array to Get Same BST
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` that contains each integer from 1 to n exactly once. Inserting the elements of `nums` one by one into an empty binary search tree creates a specific BST shape. Your task is to determine how many other permutations of the same numbers would generate a BST identical to the one produced by the original order. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Detect Pattern of Length M Repeated K or More Times
explanation_short:
You are given an array of positive integers `arr` together with two integers `m` and `k`.  
A pattern is a consecutive block of exactly `m` elements that can be repeated back‑to‑back without overlapping.  
Your task is to check whether any such block occurs at least `k` times in a row somewhere in the array.  
Return **true** if such a repeated pattern exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: Maximum Length of Subarray With Positive Product
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. Your task is to locate a contiguous portion of the array whose elements multiply to a positive value and to determine how many elements that portion contains. The answer you return is the maximum possible length among all such subarrays. Zeroes break a subarray because they make the product zero, which is not positive.

title: Count All Possible Routes
explanation_short: You are given a list of distinct city positions, plus three integers: the index of the starting city, the index of the destination city, and the amount of fuel available. Moving from city i to city j consumes fuel equal to the absolute distance between their positions, and you may travel to any other city as long as you have enough fuel left. Every time you reach the destination city (including the start if it equals the finish) you count one valid route, and you can continue moving until the fuel runs out. Return the total number of different routes that can be formed under these rules.

title: Replace All ?'s to Avoid Consecutive Repeating Characters
explanation_short: You are given a string that consists of lowercase letters and the character ‘?’. Every ‘?’ must be changed into some lowercase letter while keeping all original letters unchanged, and the final string may not have two identical characters next to each other. Return any resulting string that satisfies this condition.

title: Matrix Diagonal Sum
explanation_short: You are given a square matrix `mat` containing integers. You need to add together all numbers that lie on the two diagonals of the matrix: the primary diagonal (top‑left to bottom‑right) and the secondary diagonal (top‑right to bottom‑left), but any element that appears on both diagonals should be counted only once. The result is a single integer representing that total sum. The output should be this integer.

title: Number of Ways to Split a String
explanation_short: You are given a binary string s. You must count how many ways you can cut it into three non‑empty consecutive parts s₁, s₂, s₃ such that each part contains the same number of ‘1’ characters. The answer should be returned modulo 10⁹ + 7. The output is a single integer representing that count.

title: Shortest Subarray to be Removed to Make Array Sorted
explanation_short: You receive an integer array arr. You may delete one contiguous segment (or nothing) so that the elements left behind are in non‑decreasing order. Return the smallest possible length of the deleted segment.

title: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of edges, each described by a type (1, 2, or 3) and two node indices. Alice can travel using type 1 and type 3 edges, while Bob can travel using type 2 and type 3 edges, and each must be able to reach every node from any starting node. Your task is to find the greatest number of edges that can be removed while still allowing both Alice and Bob to keep the graph fully connected. Return that maximum count, or –1 if no such removal can keep both traversals possible.

title: Special Positions in a Binary Matrix
explanation_short: You receive an m × n matrix containing only 0s and 1s. A position is “special” when it holds a 1 and every other element in its row and its column is 0. Return the total number of such special positions.

title: Minimum Time to Make Rope Colorful
explanation_short: You are given a string colors where each character denotes the color of a balloon on a rope, and an integer array neededTime of the same length where neededTime[i] is the time required to delete the i‑th balloon. The goal is to delete some balloons so that no two neighboring balloons share the same color. Among all possible ways to achieve this, you must find the smallest total time spent deleting balloons. Return that minimum total time as an integer.

title: Number of Ways Where Square of Number Is Equal to Product of Two Numbers
explanation_short:
You are given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2.  
A “type 1” triplet consists of an index i in nums1 and two different indices j and k in nums2 such that the square of nums1[i] equals nums2[j] × nums2[k]; a “type 2” triplet swaps the roles of the arrays.  
Your task is to count how many such triplets exist across both types.  
Return the total number as a single integer.

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
explanation_short: You are given a list of points on a 2‑dimensional grid, each described by its integer (x, y) coordinates. Connecting any two points costs the Manhattan distance |x₁−x₂| + |y₁−y₂|, and you must select connections so that every point can reach every other point with exactly one simple path between any pair (i.e., the points form a tree). Output the smallest possible total cost of such a set of connections.

title: Count Unhappy Friends
explanation_short: You receive an even integer n, a list preferences where preferences[i] lists all other friends in order of i’s liking, and a list pairs describing the current matching of the friends. A friend x is considered unhappy if there exists another friend u who is paired with v such that x prefers u to its current partner and u also prefers x to its own partner. Your task is to examine all such possible relationships and count how many friends are unhappy. Return that count as a single integer.
