title: Check If String Is Transformable With Substring Sort Operations
explanation_short: You are given two strings s and t of the same length. You may repeatedly pick any contiguous substring of s and sort the characters inside that substring. Your task is to decide whether a series of these operations can turn s into t. Output true if it can be done, otherwise output false.

title: Sum of All Odd Length Subarrays
explanation_short:
You are given an array of positive integers.  
Consider every contiguous subarray whose length is odd, and compute the sum of the elements in each of those subarrays.  
Add together all of those individual sums.  
Return the resulting total as a single integer.

title: Make Sum Divisible by P
explanation_short:
You are given a list of positive integers `nums` and an integer `p`.  
First compute the total sum of the array; if it is already a multiple of `p`, the answer is 0 because no removal is needed.  
Otherwise you must delete a contiguous block of elements (the block may be empty but you cannot delete the entire array) so that the sum of the elements left behind becomes divisible by `p`.  
Return the length of the shortest such block, or `-1` if no block can achieve the required divisibility.

title: Rearrange Spaces Between Words
explanation_short: You receive a single string that contains lowercase words separated by spaces, with at least one word present. Your task is to move the spaces so that every gap between consecutive words gets the same number of spaces, and that number is as large as possible. If the spaces cannot be divided evenly, the remaining spaces should be placed after the final word. Return the resulting string, which must be exactly the same length as the original.

title: Split a String Into the Max Number of Unique Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
You may cut the string into any number of non‑empty contiguous pieces, as long as each piece appears only once in the whole split.  
Your task is to find a way to split the string that uses the largest possible number of distinct pieces.  
Return that maximum number of pieces as an integer.

title: Strange Printer II
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid where each cell contains an integer representing its final color. The printer can print a solid rectangle of a single color, and later rectangles may overwrite earlier ones, but a color can only be printed once. You must decide whether there exists an ordering of such rectangle prints that results exactly in the given grid. Return true if such an ordering is possible, otherwise return false.

title: Maximum Non Negative Product in a Matrix
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of integers. Starting at the top‑left cell, you may move only right or down until you reach the bottom‑right cell, forming a path. Compute the product of the numbers along each possible path and identify the greatest product that is zero or positive. Return that value modulo 10⁹ + 7; if every path’s product is negative, output ‑1.

title: Maximum Sum Obtained of Any Permutation
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a list of request intervals, each defined by a start and end index. By rearranging the elements of `nums` in any order, you want to make the sum of all interval sums as large as possible. For each request you add the values of `nums` that lie inside its range, and you add up these results over all requests. Return the largest achievable total, taken modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Minimum Cost to Connect Two Groups of Points
explanation_short: You are given a matrix `cost` where `cost[i][j]` is the price of connecting the i‑th point of the first group with the j‑th point of the second group. Every point in both groups must be linked to at least one point in the opposite group, and any number of connections may be used. Choose a collection of connections that satisfies these requirements while keeping the total price as low as possible. Return that minimum total cost as a single integer.

title: Crawler Log Folder
explanation_short: You receive an array of strings `logs`, each representing a folder‑change command: a name ending with “/” moves into a subfolder, “../” moves up one level, and “./” leaves you where you are. Starting from the main folder, the commands are applied in order. After all commands have been processed, you must determine how many “../” operations are required to get back to the main folder. The answer is returned as a single integer.

title: Maximum Number of Achievable Transfer Requests
explanation_short: You receive an integer n and a list of requests, each request being a pair [from, to] that indicates an employee wants to move from one building to another. A subset of these requests is feasible only when every building has the same number of employees leaving as arriving, so the net change for each building is zero. Your goal is to select as many requests as possible while keeping the overall transfers feasible. Output the largest possible number of requests that can be satisfied.

title: Maximum Profit of Operating a Centennial Wheel
explanation_short: You are given an array customers where customers[i] is the number of new people arriving just before the i‑th wheel rotation, plus two integers boardingCost and runningCost. Each rotation can board up to four waiting customers, earns boardingCost per boarded person, and costs runningCost for the rotation itself; you may stop rotating at any time, after which remaining customers exit for free. Determine the smallest number of rotations that yields the highest possible total profit, and return that count (or ‑1 if the profit never becomes positive).

title: Throne Inheritance
explanation_short: You are given a king’s name to start the royal family tree. Then a sequence of events occurs: a child can be born to any existing member, or any member can die. After each event you may be asked to list the current line of succession, which includes every living person ordered by the inheritance rules (the king first, then each person’s descendants in birth order, skipping the dead). The output is the ordered list of names of all living heirs at that moment.

title: Design Parking System
explanation_short: You are given three integers that represent how many big, medium, and small parking spots a lot initially has. Then a sequence of car requests arrives, each specifying the car’s size (big = 1, medium = 2, small = 3). For each request you must decide whether the car can be parked in a free spot of the matching size, updating the remaining count if it can. The output is a series of Boolean answers-`true` if the car was parked, `false` otherwise.

title: Find Servers That Handled Most Number of Requests
explanation_short: You are given an integer k and two equal‑length arrays: arrival[i] (the time the i‑th request arrives) and load[i] (the time it needs to finish). Requests are assigned to servers numbered 0 to k‑1 following the rule that request i first tries server i mod k, then the next free server in cyclic order, and is dropped if all are busy at its arrival time. Count how many requests each server successfully handles and identify the maximum count. Return all server IDs whose handled‑request count equals that maximum, in any order.

title: Alert Using Same Key-Card Three or More Times in a One Hour Period
explanation_short: You are given two parallel lists: one containing employee names and the other containing the times (in “HH:MM” 24‑hour format) when each key‑card was used. For each employee, determine whether there is any set of three or more uses that all occur within a one‑hour window. Collect every employee who meets this condition, removing duplicates. Output the collected names sorted in ascending alphabetical order.

title: Find Valid Matrix Given Row and Column Sums
explanation_short: You receive two lists of non‑negative integers: one giving the required sum for each row and the other giving the required sum for each column of an unknown matrix. Your task is to fill a matrix whose dimensions are rowCount × colCount so that every row adds up to its corresponding value in the first list and every column adds up to its matching value in the second list. All entries you place must be non‑negative integers, and at least one such matrix is guaranteed to exist. Return any one matrix that satisfies these row and column sum constraints.

title: Special Array With X Elements Greater Than or Equal X
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` containing non‑negative integers. You must determine whether there exists a number `x` such that exactly `x` elements of the array are greater than or equal to `x` (the value `x` itself need not appear in the array). If such an `x` exists, output that value; otherwise output `-1`. It is guaranteed that at most one such `x` can satisfy the condition.

title: Even Odd Tree
explanation_short:
You are given the root of a binary tree (often supplied as a level‑order array).  
For each depth, the node values must follow a parity rule: nodes on even‑numbered levels must all be odd and strictly increase from left to right, while nodes on odd‑numbered levels must all be even and strictly decrease from left to right.  
Check the whole tree against these rules and return **true** if every level satisfies them, otherwise return **false**.

title: Maximum Number of Visible Points
explanation_short: You are given a list of point coordinates, an integer angle (measured in degrees), and a fixed location [posx, posy]. From that location you can rotate your view any amount, and at any rotation you can see all points whose direction from the location lies within a symmetric angular window of width angle centered on your current facing direction. Points that are exactly at the location are always visible regardless of rotation. Return the largest possible number of points that can be seen simultaneously.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
explanation_short: You receive a string `s` that contains numbers, operators and properly matched parentheses. Your task is to figure out how many parentheses are nested inside each other at the deepest point in the string. The nesting depth is the largest number of open '(' characters that appear before a corresponding ')' is encountered. Return that maximum depth as an integer.

title: Minimum One Bit Operations to Make Integers Zero
explanation_short: You are given a non‑negative integer n. Using the allowed one‑bit operation (which changes certain bits of the binary representation), you must repeatedly apply it until the binary form of n becomes all zeros. Your task is to compute the smallest possible number of such operations needed. Output that minimum count as a single integer.

title: Split Two Strings to Make Palindrome
explanation_short: You are given two strings a and b that have the same length. You may pick any index (including the ends) and split each string at that point into a prefix and a suffix. Then you form the two mixed strings – aprefix + bsuffix or bprefix + asuffix – and see if either one reads the same forward and backward. Return true if a palindrome can be obtained, otherwise return false.

title: Count Subtrees With Max Distance Between Cities
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of n‑1 pairs describing the edges of a tree whose nodes are numbered 1…n. A subtree is any set of nodes that remains connected when only those nodes and the edges between them are kept. For each possible distance d (from 1 to n‑1) you must count how many different subtrees have a diameter-the longest shortest‑path between any two of their nodes-exactly equal to d. Return an array of length n‑1 where the d‑th entry (1‑indexed) holds that count.

title: Mean of Array After Removing Some Elements
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `arr`.  
First, remove the lowest 5 percent of the values and the highest 5 percent of the values from the array.  
Next, calculate the average of the numbers that remain.  
Print that average as a decimal; answers within 10⁻⁵ of the true value are accepted.

title: Maximal Network Rank
explanation_short: You are given the number of cities n and a list of roads, where each road connects two distinct cities bidirectionally. For any two different cities, count all roads that touch at least one of them, but if a road directly links the two cities it is counted only once. Your task is to determine the greatest such count among every possible pair of cities. Output that maximum network rank as a single integer.

title: Coordinate With Maximum Network Quality
explanation_short: You are given a list of towers, each described by its integer x‑coordinate, y‑coordinate, and quality factor, plus an integer radius. For any integer point (x, y), a tower contributes ⌊qi / (1 + d)⌋ where d is the Euclidean distance to that point, but only if d ≤ radius. The total network quality of a point is the sum of these contributions from all reachable towers, and you must find the integer coordinate with the maximum total quality. Return that coordinate as [cx, cy]; if several points tie, output the lexicographically smallest non‑negative one.

title: Largest Substring Between Two Equal Characters
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Find two occurrences of the same character and look at the characters that lie strictly between them.  
Among all such pairs, determine the greatest possible length of that interior substring.  
Output that maximum length, or `-1` if no character appears at least twice.

title: Number of Sets of K Non-Overlapping Line Segments
explanation_short: You are given two integers n and k, where points 0 … n‑1 lie on a line at integer positions. You must count how many distinct collections of exactly k line segments can be drawn so that each segment spans at least two points, segments never overlap (they may share endpoints), and all segment endpoints are at integer coordinates. The answer should be the total number of such collections modulo 1 000 000 007. Return this count as a single integer.

title: Best Team With No Conflicts
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length lists: scores[i] is the skill score of player i and ages[i] is that player’s age. Choose any subset of players so that no younger player in the chosen group has a strictly higher score than an older player (players of the same age never conflict). Return the largest possible sum of scores for a team that satisfies this condition.

title: Fancy Sequence
explanation_short: You receive a list of method calls to a data structure that starts empty. The calls can add a new element to the end, increase every existing element by a given amount, multiply every existing element by a given factor, or ask for the value at a specific position. Each operation must affect the sequence as described, and the value returned by a query should be given modulo 10⁹+7. Your task is to process all calls in order and output the results of the query operations.

title: Slowest Key
explanation_short: You receive two parallel inputs: an integer array `releaseTimes` where each element records when a key was released, and a string `keysPressed` of the same length describing which key was pressed at each step. The first key’s press lasts `releaseTimes[0]` units, and every later key’s press lasts the difference between its release time and the previous one. Your task is to identify the key whose press duration is the greatest, and if several keys share that maximum duration, pick the one that is alphabetically later. Return that single character as the answer.

title: Path With Minimum Effort
explanation_short: You are given a rectangular grid where each cell contains an integer height. Starting from the top‑left corner you may move to any of the four neighboring cells, and the effort of a path is the largest absolute difference in heights between two consecutive cells along that path. Your task is to choose a route that reaches the bottom‑right corner while keeping this maximum difference as small as possible. Return that smallest possible effort value.

title: Graph Connectivity With Threshold
explanation_short: You are given an integer n, a threshold value, and a list of queries where each query contains two city numbers aᵢ and bᵢ. Two different cities are linked by a road exactly when they share a common divisor that is strictly greater than the threshold. For every query you must determine whether aᵢ and bᵢ belong to the same connected component formed by those roads (directly or through other cities). Return an array of booleans, one per query, indicating true for a connected pair and false otherwise.

title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Applying Operations
explanation_short: You are given an even‑length digit string s together with two integers a and b. Two operations may be applied any number of times: add a (mod 10) to every digit in the odd positions, and rotate the whole string to the right by b places. Your task is to determine the lexicographically smallest string that can be reached by repeatedly using these operations in any order. Output that minimal string.

title: Arithmetic Subarrays
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and two equally‑long arrays `l` and `r` that define `m` queries, each query asking about the subarray from index `l[i]` to `r[i]` inclusive.  
For each query you must decide whether the elements of that subarray can be reordered so that they form an arithmetic sequence (a sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is constant).  
Return a Boolean list `answer` where `answer[i]` is true if the corresponding subarray can be rearranged into an arithmetic sequence and false otherwise.  
The length of each subarray is at least two, because a single element cannot be an arithmetic sequence.

title: Rank Transform of a Matrix
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of integers. For each cell you must determine its rank – an integer that reflects how its value compares to other values in the same row and column, following the specified ordering rules that guarantee a unique assignment. Return a new matrix of the same size where each entry is the rank of the corresponding original element.

title: Count Sorted Vowel Strings
explanation_short:
You are given a single integer n.  
Consider all strings of length n that use only the five vowels a, e, i, o, u, and where each character is the same as or comes before the next character in alphabetical order.  
Your task is to determine how many such sorted vowel strings exist.  
Return that number as the output.

title: Sort Array by Increasing Frequency
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers.  
Rearrange its elements so that numbers with a lower occurrence count appear before those with a higher count.  
If two numbers occur equally often, place the larger number earlier in the order.  
Output the array after this reordering.

title: Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary
explanation_short: You are given an array of words, all having the same length, and a separate target string. You must count how many distinct ways you can select characters from the words-moving left to right across columns and possibly using different words for each character-to spell the target in order. Each selection must respect the column index (you cannot jump backward) and you may reuse a word multiple times as long as the column rule holds. Return the total number of ways modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Count Substrings That Differ by One Character
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s` and `t`. Consider every non‑empty substring of `s` and every non‑empty substring of `t` that have the same length; count each pair where the two substrings are identical except for a single character position. The answer is the total number of such pairs.

title: Kth Smallest Instructions
explanation_short:
You are given a two‑element array `destination` where `destination[0]` is the required number of down moves and `destination[1]` is the required number of right moves, plus an integer `k`.  
Each valid instruction is a string of length `destination[0] + destination[1]` consisting of the characters `'V'` (for a down step) and `'H'` (for a right step) that moves Bob from (0, 0) to the target cell.  
All such strings can be ordered lexicographically, and you must determine the k‑th string in this order (1‑indexed).  
Return that instruction string as the answer.

title: Widest Vertical Area Between Two Points Containing No Points
explanation_short:
You are given a list of n points, each described by its x‑coordinate and y‑coordinate.  
Consider vertical strips that extend infinitely up and down; the width of a strip is the distance between its two vertical edges.  
Your task is to determine the maximum possible width of such a strip that contains no given point strictly inside it (points may lie on the edges).  
Return that maximum width as a single integer.

title: Check Array Formation Through Concatenation
explanation_short: You receive a list `arr` of unique integers and a collection `pieces` where each element is a sub‑array of distinct integers. You must decide whether you can place the sub‑arrays side by side, in any order, so that their combined sequence exactly matches `arr` while keeping the internal order of each sub‑array unchanged. Return `true` if such a concatenation exists; otherwise return `false`.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make Character Frequencies Unique
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Each character’s frequency is the number of times it appears in the string.  
You may delete characters, and you want to delete as few as possible so that no two different characters end up with the same frequency.  
Return the smallest number of deletions needed to achieve this condition.

title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
explanation_short: You are given an array `heights` that lists the heights of consecutive buildings, plus two numbers: the total bricks you can spend and the total ladders you can use. Starting at the first building, you may move to the next one; if the next building is taller you must cover the height difference either by spending that many bricks or by using one ladder. Your task is to decide how to allocate bricks and ladders so that you can advance as far as possible. Return the index (0‑based) of the farthest building you can reach.

title: Get Maximum in Generated Array
explanation_short: You receive a single integer n. From it you build a 0‑indexed array nums of size n + 1, where nums[0] = 0, nums[1] = 1, and for each i ≥ 1 you set nums[2·i] = nums[i] and nums[2·i + 1] = nums[i] + nums[i + 1] as long as the indices stay within the array. After the whole array is generated, you must determine the largest value that appears in nums. The program should output that maximum integer.

title: Create Sorted Array through Instructions
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `instructions`. Starting with an empty list, insert the elements one by one in the order they appear, keeping the list sorted after each insertion. For each insertion, add the smaller of “how many existing numbers are less than the new value” and “how many existing numbers are greater than the new value” to a running total, and finally return that total modulo \(10^9+7\). The output is a single integer representing the accumulated insertion cost.

title: Sell Diminishing-Valued Colored Balls
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `inventory` where `inventory[i]` is the initial number of balls of the i‑th color, and an integer `orders` indicating how many balls must be sold. The price of each ball you sell equals the current amount of that color remaining, so each sale reduces the price for the next ball of the same color. You may choose any order of colors to sell exactly `orders` balls. Return the greatest possible total price you can obtain, taken modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Distribute Repeating Integers
explanation_short: You receive an array nums containing n integers, where some values may appear many times, and an array quantity where quantity[i] specifies how many items the i‑th customer wants. You must determine whether the integers in nums can be allocated so that each customer gets exactly the requested number of copies of a single integer value (no customer may receive two different values, and a value cannot be split among customers). Return true if such a distribution is possible; otherwise return false.

title: Defuse the Bomb
explanation_short: You are given a circular array `code` and an integer `k`. For each index you must compute a new number that will replace the original, and all replacements occur simultaneously. If `k` is positive, the new number is the sum of the next `k` elements moving forward around the circle; if `k` is negative, it is the sum of the previous `|k|` elements; if `k` is zero, the new number is 0. Return the resulting array of replaced values in the same order.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
explanation_short: You are given a string s that contains only the letters ‘a’ and ‘b’. You may remove any characters you like, and the goal is to end up with a string where no ‘b’ occurs before an ‘a’ (i.e., all ‘a’s appear before any ‘b’s). Determine the smallest possible number of deletions required to achieve this condition. Output that minimum count as an integer.

title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a target value `x`. In each step you may discard the leftmost or rightmost element of the current array, subtracting its value from `x`. Your task is to determine the smallest number of such discards that makes `x` exactly zero. If no sequence of removals can achieve this, you should output `-1`.

title: Minimum Jumps to Reach Home
explanation_short: You are given an array `forbidden` of positions the bug cannot occupy, and three integers `a`, `b` and `x`. Starting at 0, the bug may jump forward exactly `a` units or backward exactly `b` units (never to a negative coordinate), and it may pass beyond `x` but must finally land exactly on `x`. Return the smallest number of jumps required to reach `x`, or `-1` if no sequence of allowed jumps can do so.

title: Design an Ordered Stream
explanation_short: You receive a series of pairs, each containing an integer ID (from 1 to n) and a string value, arriving in any order. After each insertion you must output a list of the values whose IDs form a consecutive block starting from the smallest ID that has not yet been returned. The overall output, formed by concatenating all these lists, should be the values sorted by their IDs from 1 to n. The task is to implement a data structure that supports these insert‑and‑return operations.

title: Determine if Two Strings Are Close
explanation_short:
You are given two strings, word1 and word2.  
Your task is to decide whether one string can be turned into the other by repeatedly applying the allowed operations (reordering characters and swapping all instances of two existing letters).  
Return true if such a transformation is possible, otherwise return false.  
The output is a single Boolean value indicating whether the two strings are “close.”

title: Ways to Make a Fair Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. For each possible single index you may delete, the remaining elements shift left, so their positions (even‑indexed vs. odd‑indexed) may change. You must count how many deletions result in the sum of the values at even positions equaling the sum of the values at odd positions in the new array. Return that count as an integer.

title: Maximize Grid Happiness
explanation_short: You are given four integers m, n, introvertsCount and extrovertsCount that describe an m × n grid and how many introverts and extroverts are available. Choose any subset of these people and assign each to a distinct cell; each person starts with a fixed happiness value and gains or loses points for every directly adjacent neighbor (north, east, south, west) depending on whether the neighbor is an introvert or an extrovert. Return the largest total happiness achievable across all possible placements.

title: Maximum Repeating Substring
explanation_short: You receive two strings: `sequence` and `word`. Find the greatest integer k so that the string formed by writing `word` k times in a row occurs as a contiguous substring of `sequence`. If `word` does not appear at all, the answer is 0, and you output that integer.

title: Minimum Initial Energy to Finish Tasks
explanation_short: You receive a list of tasks, each given as two integers - the energy you will lose when you finish the task and the minimum energy you must have to begin it. You may perform the tasks in any order you choose. Find the smallest amount of energy you need to start with so that you can complete every task while always meeting its minimum‑energy requirement. Output that minimum initial energy as a single integer.

title: Check If Two String Arrays are Equivalent
explanation_short: You receive two arrays of strings, word1 and word2. Each array represents a single string formed by joining its elements in order. Your task is to decide whether the two resulting strings are exactly the same. Return true if they match and false otherwise.

title: Minimum Number of Removals to Make Mountain Array
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums`.  
Your task is to delete the fewest possible elements so that the remaining elements first increase strictly, then decrease strictly, with at least one element on each side of the peak.  
The answer you must return is the minimum number of deletions required to achieve such a mountain shape.  
If the original array already satisfies the mountain condition, the result is 0.

title: Merge In Between Linked Lists
explanation_short: You receive two singly‑linked lists and two 0‑based indices a and b (with a ≤ b). The task is to cut out the segment of the first list that starts at node a and ends at node b, then insert the entire second list in its place. Return the head node of the newly formed linked list.

title: Smallest String With A Given Numeric Value
explanation_short:
You receive two integers n and k.  
You must construct a string of exactly n lower‑case letters whose total numeric value (a = 1, b = 2, …, z = 26) adds up to k.  
Among all possible strings that meet these conditions, you should return the one that comes first in dictionary order.  
The output is that lexicographically smallest string.

title: Design Front Middle Back Queue
explanation_short: The input is a list of commands that create a queue and then call its six operations: pushFront, pushBack, pushMiddle, popFront, popMiddle, and popBack. Each push command inserts a given integer at the front, back, or the front‑most middle position of the current sequence; each pop command removes and returns the element from the corresponding position, returning –1 if the queue is empty. You must process the commands in order, maintaining the queue’s state after each operation. The output is an array where push calls produce `null` and each pop call yields the removed value (or –1 for an empty queue).

title: Minimize Deviation in Array
explanation_short: You are given a list of positive integers. By repeatedly either doubling an odd number or halving an even number, you may change any element any number of times. Your task is to make the difference between the largest and smallest values in the list as small as possible and output that minimum achievable difference.

title: Richest Customer Wealth
explanation_short: You receive a rectangular grid of integers where each row represents one customer and each column shows how much money that customer has in a particular bank. For every customer you must add up all the amounts in their row to get their total wealth. Then identify which customer’s total is the largest. Return that largest total as a single integer.

title: Find the Most Competitive Subsequence
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums` and a positive integer `k`. From `nums` you may delete any elements, but you must keep the original order of the remaining ones, producing a subsequence of exactly `k` numbers. Among all such subsequences, you need to return the one that is lexicographically smallest – i.e., the first position where two candidates differ should contain the smaller value. The output is that chosen subsequence, listed in the same order it appears in the original array.

title: Max Number of K-Sum Pairs
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a target value `k`.  
Each operation removes two distinct elements whose sum is exactly `k`.  
Your task is to determine how many such operations can be performed before no more qualifying pairs remain.  
Return that maximum count as an integer.

title: Concatenation of Consecutive Binary Numbers
explanation_short: You receive a single integer n. Write down the binary representation of each number from 1 through n, place those strings one after another, and treat the resulting long binary string as a base‑2 number. Compute its decimal value and then take the remainder when divided by 1 000 000 007. Output that remainder.

title: Minimum Moves to Make Array Complementary
explanation_short: You are given an even‑length array nums and an integer limit. A complementary array requires that for every index i, the sum of nums[i] and its mirrored element nums[n‑1‑i] is identical for all pairs. You may change any element to any value between 1 and limit, counting each change as one move. Return the minimum number of moves needed to make the whole array complementary.

title: Goal Parser Interpretation
explanation_short: You are given a single string that consists only of the characters G, ( ), and the substring (al) arranged in any order. Each occurrence of G should become the letter G, each pair of empty parentheses () should become o, and each (al) should become al. Perform these replacements while preserving the original sequence, then join the pieces together. The result of this concatenation is the required output.

title: Sum of Absolute Differences in a Sorted Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array nums that is already sorted in non‑decreasing order. For each index i you must add up the absolute differences between nums[i] and every element of the array, including itself. Collect all these sums into a new array result that has the same length as nums. The output is this result array.

title: Stone Game VI
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of equal length, where the i‑th element of each array tells how many points Alice or Bob would earn if they take stone i. Alice moves first, then the players alternate, each removing one remaining stone and adding the corresponding value to their own score. Assuming both players choose stones optimally and know each other’s values, you must decide whether Alice ends with a higher total, Bob ends with a higher total, or the scores are equal. Return 1 if Alice wins, ‑1 if Bob wins, and 0 for a draw.

title: Delivering Boxes from Storage to Ports
explanation_short: You are given an array boxes where each element is a pair [portᵢ, weightᵢ] describing the destination port and weight of the i‑th box, together with the total number of ports, the ship’s maximum box count maxBoxes, and its maximum total weight maxWeight. The boxes must be loaded and delivered strictly in the given order, and the ship can only carry a batch that does not exceed both maxBoxes and maxWeight. A “trip” is counted each time the ship moves from the storage to a port, from one port to another, or returns from a port to the storage, and the ship must end back at the storage after all deliveries. Return the smallest possible number of trips required to deliver every box.

title: Minimum Incompatibility
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a number `k`.  
You must partition the elements into exactly `k` groups, each containing the same count of numbers and never placing two identical values in the same group.  
For each group compute its incompatibility as the difference between its largest and smallest element, then add these values together.  
Return the smallest possible total incompatibility, or `-1` if such a partition cannot be formed.

title: Maximum Height by Stacking Cuboids
explanation_short: You are given a list of cuboids, each described by three numbers representing its width, length and height. You may rotate any cuboid, then choose some of them and stack them so that for every pair of consecutive cuboids the base dimensions of the upper one do not exceed those of the lower one. The task is to compute the greatest possible total height of such a stack and output that maximum height.

title: Count the Number of Consistent Strings
explanation_short: You receive a string `allowed` that lists distinct letters, and an array `words` containing many lowercase strings. A word is “consistent” when every character it uses appears somewhere in `allowed`. Return the total number of consistent words as an integer.

title: Reformat Phone Number
explanation_short: You receive a single string that may contain digits, spaces, and dashes. First remove every space and dash, leaving only the digits. Then split those digits from left to right into groups of three, but when four or fewer digits remain you must arrange them so that no group has length 1 (the only possibilities are one group of three, or two groups of two). Finally, join the groups with dashes and return the resulting string.

title: Count of Matches in Tournament
explanation_short: You receive a single integer n that tells how many teams start the tournament. In each match one team is eliminated, and the competition continues round by round until only one team remains. Your task is to compute how many matches must be played in total to reach that final winner. Return that number as an integer.

title: Partitioning Into Minimum Number Of Deci-Binary Numbers
explanation_short: You are given a string n that encodes a positive decimal integer. A deci‑binary number is any positive integer whose digits are only 0 or 1 and has no leading zeros. Your task is to determine the smallest possible count of such deci‑binary numbers whose sum equals the integer represented by n. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Stone Game VII
explanation_short: You are given an array stones where each element is the value of a stone placed in a line. Alice and Bob alternately remove either the leftmost or rightmost stone; the player who makes a move scores the sum of the values of all stones that stay on the board after the removal. Assuming both players play optimally-Alice to maximize the final score gap and Bob to minimize it-return the difference between Alice’s total points and Bob’s total points when all stones have been removed.

title: Maximum Erasure Value
explanation_short:
You are given an array of positive integers.  
Pick a contiguous segment of the array that contains no duplicate values.  
The score of the chosen segment equals the sum of its elements.  
Return the highest score achievable by any such segment.

title: Checking Existence of Edge Length Limited Paths
explanation_short:
You are given the number of nodes n, a list of undirected edges (each edge gives its two endpoints and a distance), and a list of queries.  
Each query provides two nodes p and q together with a limit L, and you must decide whether there is any path connecting p and q whose every edge has a distance strictly smaller than L.  
The answer should be an array of booleans, one for each query, where the j‑th entry is true if such a path exists and false otherwise.

title: Maximum Binary String After Change
explanation_short: You are given a binary string consisting only of ‘0’ and ‘1’. By repeatedly applying the allowed operations (which can change the positions of bits), you may transform the string into many different binary strings. Your task is to determine the greatest possible binary string that can be reached, where “greater” means a larger decimal value. Return that maximal string as the output.

title: Jump Game VI
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`. Starting at index 0, you may jump forward to any position up to `k` steps ahead, and you must eventually land on the last index. The score of a path is the sum of the array values at all visited indices, and you need to find the greatest possible score achievable under those jumping rules. Return that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Average Waiting Time
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element contains a customer’s arrival time and the time the chef needs to prepare that order. The chef works on the customers strictly in the order given, starting a new order only when he becomes idle. For each customer you must determine how long they wait-from their arrival until the chef finishes their food-and then compute the mean of all those waiting times. The answer should be returned as a decimal value (acceptable within 10⁻⁵ of the true average).

title: Where Will the Ball Fall
explanation_short: The input is an m × n matrix of 1 and -1, where each value tells whether the diagonal board in that cell redirects a ball to the right (1) or to the left (-1). From the top of each column we drop a ball that moves cell‑by‑cell following those directions. A ball either leaves the grid through the bottom, gets trapped by a “V” formed by opposite boards, or hits a side wall. Return an array of length n where the i‑th entry is the bottom column where ball i exits, or -1 if it gets stuck.

title: Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays: `students`, where each element is a student’s sandwich preference (0 for circular, 1 for square) in the order they stand in line, and `sandwiches`, where each element is the type of sandwich in the cafeteria stack (index 0 is the top). Starting from the front of the queue, each student either takes the top sandwich if it matches their preference or moves to the back of the line; the process repeats until the top sandwich cannot be taken by anyone in the current queue. When this stalemate occurs, the remaining students are unable to eat. Return the count of those students.

title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps for K Consecutive Ones
explanation_short: You are given a binary array `nums` and an integer `k`. You may repeatedly swap two neighboring positions in the array. The task is to determine the smallest number of such swaps that will make at least `k` ones appear consecutively somewhere in the array. Return that minimum swap count as the answer.

title: Determine if String Halves Are Alike
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s` whose length is guaranteed to be even. First split the string into two parts of equal size: the left half `a` and the right half `b`. Count how many vowels (both uppercase and lowercase) appear in each half and check whether the two counts are identical. Return `true` if they match; otherwise return `false`.

title: Maximum Number of Eaten Apples
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length integer arrays: apples[i] tells how many apples appear on day i, and days[i] tells after how many days those apples become rotten. Starting from day 0 you may eat at most one apple each day, and you can continue eating even after the last day of growth as long as some apples are still fresh. Your task is to determine the greatest total number of apples you can consume before they all rot. The answer should be returned as a single integer.

title: Maximum XOR With an Element From Array
explanation_short: You are given a list `nums` of non‑negative integers and a list of queries, each query being a pair `[xi, mi]`. For every query you must look at all numbers in `nums` that are ≤ `mi` and compute the largest possible value of `xi XOR that number`; if no such number exists the answer is -1. Return an array containing the answer for each query in the same order as the queries appear.

title: Count Good Meals
explanation_short:
You are given an array where each element is the deliciousness of a food item.  
Count all pairs of different indices whose sum is exactly a power of two (e.g., 1 + 3 = 4).  
Pairs are considered distinct even when the two items have the same deliciousness value.  
Output the total number of such good meals modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Ways to Split Array Into Three Subarrays
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` of non‑negative integers.  
A “good” split divides the array into three contiguous parts A, B, C such that the sum of A is ≤ the sum of B and the sum of B is ≤ the sum of C.  
Your task is to count how many different positions for the two cuts produce a good split.  
Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Maximum Units on a Truck
explanation_short: You receive a list where each entry tells how many boxes of a certain type exist and how many units each of those boxes contains, plus an integer truckSize that limits how many boxes the truck can hold. Your task is to pick any combination of boxes-without exceeding the truckSize-that yields the greatest possible total number of units. Return that maximum total as a single integer.

title: Maximum Score From Removing Substrings
explanation_short: You receive a string `s` and two integers `x` and `y`. You may repeatedly delete any occurrence of the two‑character substring “ab” (earning `x` points) or “ba” (earning `y` points). The deletions can be performed in any order and as many times as possible. Your task is to determine the greatest total number of points that can be accumulated. Return that maximum score as an integer.

title: Minimum Operations to Make a Subsequence
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays: `target`, which contains only distinct values, and `arr`, which may include repeated numbers. You may insert any integer at any position in `arr` (including the ends) as many times as you like. The goal is to determine the smallest number of such insertions required so that the entire `target` sequence appears in order as a subsequence of the modified `arr`. Return that minimum count as a single integer.

title: Construct the Lexicographically Largest Valid Sequence
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n. You must arrange numbers from 1 to n into a list so that for every value i greater than 1 the two copies of i are placed exactly i positions apart, while the number 1 appears only once. Among all arrangements that satisfy this distance rule, you need to output the one that is lexicographically largest. The output is the resulting sequence written as a list of integers.

title: Minimize Hamming Distance After Swap Operations
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length integer arrays, source and target, plus a list of index pairs that may be swapped any number of times in source. By performing any sequence of those allowed swaps, you can rearrange the elements of source as you wish within each connected group of indices. Your task is to compute the smallest possible number of positions where the final source differs from target (the minimal Hamming distance) and output that integer.

title: Decode XORed Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer first (the first element of a hidden array) and an array encoded where each entry equals the XOR of two consecutive elements of the hidden array. The hidden array arr has length n = encoded.length + 1, and for every i, encoded[i] = arr[i] XOR arr[i+1]. Your task is to rebuild the entire arr using the given first and the encoded values. Return the reconstructed array as a list of integers.

title: Calculate Money in Leetcode Bank
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n representing the number of days that have passed. Each day Hercy deposits an amount that increases by $1 compared to the previous day, and the amount on each new Monday is also $1 higher than the Monday before. Your task is to determine how much money is in the account after the n‑th day. Return that total as an integer.

title: Number Of Rectangles That Can Form The Largest Square
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element gives the length and width of a rectangle. From each rectangle you can cut a square whose side is the smaller of the two dimensions, and you need to determine the greatest square side that any rectangle can yield. Finally, count how many rectangles can produce a square of that maximal side and output that count.

title: Tuple with Same Product
explanation_short:
You are given an array of distinct positive integers.  
You must count how many ordered quadruples (a, b, c, d) can be formed from the array such that a × b equals c × d and all four numbers are different.  
Each quadruple is considered distinct by the order of its elements.  
Return that total count as an integer.

title: Number Of Ways To Reconstruct A Tree
explanation_short: You receive a list of unordered node pairs, each indicating that the two nodes must be in an ancestor‑descendant relationship somewhere in the tree. Your task is to determine how many different rooted trees can be built so that every given pair satisfies that ancestor condition, counting two trees as different if any node has a different parent. The answer is the total number of such rooted trees: 0 if none exist, 1 if the structure is uniquely determined, or 2 if multiple valid trees are possible.

title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List
explanation_short:
You receive a singly‑linked list and an integer k.  
The list is indexed starting at 1, so the kth node from the front and the kth node from the back are identified.  
Your task is to exchange the values stored in those two nodes while leaving the rest of the list unchanged.  
Return the head of the resulting list, which will reflect the swapped values.

title: Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs
explanation_short: You are given an array jobs where each element is the time required for a specific job, and an integer k representing the number of workers available. Each job must be assigned to exactly one worker, and a worker’s workload is the sum of the times of the jobs they receive. Your task is to find the smallest possible value of the largest workload among all workers and output that minimum maximum time.

title: Minimum Number of People to Teach
explanation_short: You are given the total number of languages n, a list describing which languages each user already knows, and a list of friendship pairs. You may pick a single language and teach it to any subset of users so that every pair of friends shares at least one common language. The task is to determine the smallest possible number of users that must be taught this language. Return that minimum count.

title: Decode XORed Permutation
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `encoded` of length *n – 1*, where each element is the XOR of two consecutive numbers in an unknown permutation `perm` of the integers 1 through *n* (and *n* is odd). From this array you must reconstruct the original permutation `perm`. The answer is guaranteed to exist and be unique. Return `perm` as an array of length *n*.

title: Largest Submatrix With Rearrangements
explanation_short: You receive an m × n binary matrix, where each entry is either 0 or 1. You may permute the columns in any order you like. After choosing the best column arrangement, you must determine the largest possible rectangle (contiguous rows and columns) that contains only 1 values. Return the area (number of cells) of that maximal all‑ones submatrix.

title: Cat and Mouse II
explanation_short: You are given a rectangular grid where each cell is a wall (`#`), empty floor (`.`), the cat (`C`), the mouse (`M`), or the food (`F`). The cat and mouse take turns moving; on its turn a player may jump up to its respective limit (catJump or mouseJump) in any of the four directions, stopping early if it hits a wall or the grid edge. The game ends when the mouse reaches the food, the cat catches the mouse, the cat reaches the food first, or after a maximum of 1000 moves without a winner. Return **true** if the mouse can force a win under optimal play, otherwise return **false**.

title: Change Minimum Characters to Satisfy One of Three Conditions
explanation_short: You receive two strings a and b made of lowercase letters. You may change any character in either string to any other lowercase letter, and you need the smallest number of such changes that makes one of three situations true: every letter in a is strictly smaller than every letter in b; every letter in b is strictly smaller than every letter in a; or both strings consist of only one identical letter. Return that minimum number of operations.

title: Find Kth Largest XOR Coordinate Value
explanation_short: You are given an m × n matrix of non‑negative integers and an integer k. For every coordinate (a, b) in the matrix, compute the XOR of all elements in the rectangle from the top‑left corner (0, 0) to (a, b). Collect all these XOR values, sort them in descending order, and pick the k‑th element in that order. The required output is that k‑th largest XOR value.

title: Find the Highest Altitude
explanation_short: You are given an integer array gain, where each element tells how much the biker’s altitude changes when moving from one point to the next, and the trip starts at altitude 0. By adding the gains one after another you can list the altitude at every point visited, including the starting point. From this list you must determine the largest altitude reached. The answer is that maximum altitude, printed as a single integer.

title: Building Boxes
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n, which is both the side length of a cubic room and the total number of unit‑size cubes you must place inside it. The cubes may be stacked in any configuration that fits within the n × n × n space, but you want to arrange them so that as few cubes as possible touch the floor. Determine the smallest possible number of cubes that must be in contact with the floor for a valid placement of all n cubes. Output that minimum count as an integer.

title: Latest Time by Replacing Hidden Digits
explanation_short: You receive a string of the form hh:mm where some characters are ‘?’ instead of digits. Replace each ‘?’ with a decimal digit so that the whole string becomes a valid 24‑hour clock time (00:00 to 23:59). Return the resulting time that is as late as possible.

title: Maximum Number of Balls in a Box
explanation_short: You are given two integers lowLimit and highLimit that define a consecutive range of ball numbers. Each ball is placed into a box whose index equals the sum of the digits of that ball’s number, and you must count how many balls end up in each box. From those counts, determine the largest number of balls that any single box contains. The output is that maximum count as an integer.

title: Count Ways to Make Array With Product
explanation_short: You receive a list of queries, each containing two integers n (the array length) and k (the desired product). For every query you must count how many ordered arrays of n positive integers multiply exactly to k. Different permutations of the same numbers are considered distinct ways. Output an array where the i‑th entry is the count for the i‑th query taken modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Palindrome Partitioning IV
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Your task is to decide whether you can cut `s` into exactly three parts, each of which is non‑empty and reads the same forward and backward.  
If such a three‑piece palindrome partition exists, return `true`; otherwise return `false`.  
The answer depends only on the characters of `s`, not on any external data.

title: Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray
explanation_short:
You receive an array of integers `nums`.  
For every possible contiguous segment of the array (even the empty segment), compute the sum of its elements and then take the absolute value of that sum.  
Among all those absolute values, identify the largest one.  
Return that largest absolute sum as a single integer.

title: Restore the Array From Adjacent Pairs
explanation_short: You are given a list of n ‑ 1 unordered pairs, each pair containing two distinct integers that were next to each other in an unknown array of n unique numbers. Every adjacent relationship from the original array appears exactly once in this list, though the order inside each pair and the order of the pairs themselves are arbitrary. Your task is to piece together the original sequence of numbers that satisfies all those adjacency constraints. Return that reconstructed array; if more than one ordering works, any one of them is acceptable.

title: Sum of Unique Elements
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers. First, determine which numbers appear exactly once in the array. Then add those unique numbers together. The output is the total sum, which is zero if no element occurs only once.

title: Closest Subsequence Sum
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `goal`. From `nums` you may pick any subsequence (removing zero or more elements) and compute the sum of its chosen elements. Your task is to make this sum as close as possible to `goal`, minimizing the absolute difference |sum − goal|. Return the smallest achievable absolute difference.

title: Minimum Length of String After Deleting Similar Ends
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` made only of the letters ‘a’, ‘b’ and ‘c’.  
You may repeatedly choose a non‑empty prefix and a non‑empty suffix that are each made of a single identical character, and delete both of them at the same time.  
Your task is to determine the smallest possible length the string can have after performing any number of such deletions (including none).  
Return that minimum length as an integer.

title: Form Array by Concatenating Subarrays of Another Array
explanation_short:
You receive a list `groups` where each element is an integer subarray, and a single array `nums`.  
You must decide whether you can pick, in order, one non‑overlapping contiguous segment of `nums` for each subarray in `groups` so that each chosen segment exactly matches the corresponding subarray.  
The chosen segments must appear in the same sequence as the subarrays in `groups` and cannot share any indices of `nums`.  
Return **true** if such a selection exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: Minimum Changes To Make Alternating Binary String
explanation_short:
You receive a string s that contains only the characters ‘0’ and ‘1’.  
In one operation you may flip any single character from ‘0’ to ‘1’ or from ‘1’ to ‘0’.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of such flips required so that no two neighboring characters in the resulting string are the same (i.e., the string becomes alternating).  
Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Count Number of Homogenous Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s`.  
Your task is to count every contiguous piece of the string whose characters are all the same.  
Each occurrence is counted separately, even if the same pattern appears in different places.  
Output the total number of such substrings, reduced modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Longest Nice Substring
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s`.  
Your task is to locate the longest contiguous segment of `s` such that every alphabet letter present in the segment appears in both its uppercase and lowercase forms.  
If multiple segments share the maximum length, you must return the one that occurs earliest in the original string.  
The output is that substring, or an empty string when no such segment exists.

title: Largest Merge Of Two Strings
explanation_short: You are given two strings, word1 and word2. By repeatedly removing the first character of either string (while at least one string still has characters) you must create a new string merge that is as large as possible in lexicographic order. The required output is that lexicographically largest possible merge string.

title: Tree of Coprimes
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` where `nums[i]` is the value of node `i`, and a list of `edges` that defines a tree rooted at node 0. For each node you must locate the closest ancestor (a node on the path to the root, excluding the node itself) whose value shares no common divisor greater than 1 with the node’s own value; if none exists, record -1. Return an array `ans` of length `n` where `ans[i]` holds that ancestor’s index or -1.

title: Maximize Palindrome Length From Subsequences
explanation_short: You are given two strings, word1 and word2. From each string you may delete characters (possibly none) to form a subsequence, then place the subsequence from word1 in front of the subsequence from word2. Among all such concatenations, find the greatest possible length of a palindrome that can be formed. Output that length, or 0 if no palindrome can be created.

title: Count Items Matching a Rule
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element contains three strings: the item’s type, its color, and its name. Along with that, you are given a rule consisting of a key (“type”, “color”, or “name”) and a value to match. Count how many items have the attribute specified by the key equal to the given value, and output that count as an integer.

title: Map of Highest Peak
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid where each entry is 0 (land) or 1 (water). Every water cell must be given height 0, and any two cells that share a side may differ in height by at most 1. Your task is to choose heights for all cells so that the largest height in the whole grid is as big as possible while respecting those constraints. Return a matrix of the same dimensions containing the height you assigned to each cell.

title: Check if Number is a Sum of Powers of Three
explanation_short:
You receive a single integer n.  
You must decide whether n can be written as a sum where each term is a different power of three (for example 1, 3, 9, 27, …).  
If such a representation exists, the answer is true; otherwise it is false.  
Return the boolean result.

title: Closest Dessert Cost
explanation_short: You are given a list of ice‑cream base prices, a list of topping prices, and a target amount. You must pick exactly one base and may add each topping zero, one, or two times, forming a total cost. Your task is to find the total cost that is nearest to the target; if two totals are equally close, choose the smaller one. Return that closest cost as the answer.

title: Car Fleet II
explanation_short: You are given a list `cars`, where each element contains a car’s current position and its constant speed. As the cars travel forward, a faster car that catches up to the car directly in front of it merges with it, and the resulting fleet moves at the slower speed. For every car, determine the exact moment it first collides with the next car ahead, or report `-1` if such a collision never occurs. Return an array of these collision times, accepting answers that are accurate within 10⁻⁵.

title: Equal Sum Arrays With Minimum Number of Operations
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, where each element is between 1 and 6. In one operation you may replace any element in either array with any value from 1 to 6. Your task is to determine the smallest number of operations needed so that the total sum of nums1 equals the total sum of nums2, or decide that it cannot be done. Return that minimum count, or -1 if making the sums equal is impossible.

title: Minimum Elements to Add to Form a Given Sum
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`, an integer `limit`, and a target sum `goal`. You may insert any number of additional integers whose absolute value does not exceed `limit` (they can be positive or negative) into the array. The task is to determine the smallest possible count of such numbers that must be added so that the total sum of the original and added elements equals `goal`. Output that minimum count as a single integer.

title: Number of Restricted Paths From First to Last Node
explanation_short: You’re given an undirected weighted graph with nodes labeled 1 to n and a list of edges [ui, vi, weighti]. First determine, for every node, the length of the shortest path to node n. A restricted path is a sequence from node 1 to node n where each next node has a strictly smaller shortest‑to‑n distance than the current one. Count how many such restricted paths exist. Return that count (usually modulo 10⁹ + 7).

title: Find Nearest Point That Has the Same X or Y Coordinate
explanation_short: You are given two integers x and y that describe your current position on a grid, plus an array where each element is a pair [ai, bi] representing another point’s coordinates. Among the points that lie on the same vertical line (same x) or the same horizontal line (same y) as you, you must identify the one whose Manhattan distance |x‑ai| + |y‑bi| is minimal; if several qualify, choose the one with the lowest array index. Return that index, or ‑1 if no point shares either coordinate.

title: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
For every possible contiguous substring of `s`, compute its “beauty”: the difference between the highest and the lowest character frequencies within that substring (ignoring characters that do not appear).  
Add together the beauty values of all substrings.  
Return the resulting sum as an integer.

title: Make the XOR of All Segments Equal to Zero
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`. You may change any element of the array, and each changed element counts as one operation. The goal is to make the XOR of every contiguous segment whose length is `k + 1` equal to zero. You must output the smallest possible number of operations needed to achieve this. If the array already satisfies the condition, the answer is 0.

title: Find Center of Star Graph
explanation_short: You receive a list of pairs, each pair describing an undirected edge between two numbered nodes. Because the graph is a star, one node is connected to every other node while all other nodes have only that single connection. Your task is to determine which node serves as the center and output its label.

title: Maximum Average Pass Ratio
explanation_short: You are given a list where each entry contains two numbers: the current count of passing students and the total number of students in a class. An integer extraStudents tells how many additional perfect‑score students you can place into any classes, one at a time. Your task is to decide how to distribute those extra students so that the overall average of the classes’ pass ratios (passes ÷ total) becomes as large as possible. Return that maximum average value; answers are accepted if they are within 10⁻⁵ of the true result.

title: Check if One String Swap Can Make Strings Equal
explanation_short: You are given two strings of the same length. You may pick any two positions (they may be the same) in exactly one of the strings and swap the characters there, but you can do this at most once. Determine whether after such a single swap the two strings can become identical, and return true if it’s possible and false otherwise.

title: Maximum Score of a Good Subarray
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a position `k`.  
Consider any contiguous segment of the array that includes index `k`; its score is the smallest value inside the segment multiplied by the segment’s length.  
Your task is to determine the greatest possible score among all such segments.  
Return that maximum score as a single integer.

title: Maximize Score After N Operations
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` containing `2 × n` positive integers. In each of the `n` steps you must pick two still‑unused numbers, compute their greatest common divisor, multiply that gcd by the step number (starting from 1), and add the result to your total score. The task is to arrange the pairings so that the final sum is as large as possible, and you should output that maximum achievable score.

title: Maximum Number of Consecutive Values You Can Make
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers where each element represents the value of a coin you own. From these coins you may pick any subset (including none) and add their values together to form a sum. Your task is to determine how many consecutive integer amounts, starting at 0, can be formed using some subset of the coins. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Number of Orders in the Backlog
explanation_short: You receive a list `orders`, each entry giving a price, a quantity, and whether it is a buy (0) or sell (1) order. As the orders arrive one by one, each can be paired with opposite‑type orders that satisfy the price rule (buy price ≥ sell price); matched quantities are removed, and any leftover part stays in the backlog. After all orders are processed, sum the remaining quantities in the backlog and return that sum modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Maximum Value at a Given Index in a Bounded Array
explanation_short:
You are given three positive integers n, index and maxSum.  
You must imagine an array of length n where every element is at least 1, the total of all elements does not exceed maxSum, and any two neighboring values differ by no more than 1.  
Among all such arrays, determine the largest possible value that can appear at position index.  
Return that maximum value as a single integer.

title: Maximum Ascending Subarray Sum
explanation_short:
You are given an array of positive integers `nums`.  
Identify any contiguous segment of the array where each element is strictly larger than the one before it.  
Among all such increasing subarrays, determine the one whose elements add up to the greatest total.  
Return that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Number of Different Integers in a String
explanation_short: You receive a single string that mixes digits with lowercase letters. After turning every letter into a blank space, the remaining substrings of digits represent the integers in the string. Treat each integer by removing any leading zeros, then consider two integers the same only if their cleaned decimal forms match. The answer you must output is the count of distinct integers obtained this way.

title: Count Pairs With XOR in a Range
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and two bounds `low` and `high`. For every pair of indices `i < j`, compute the XOR of `nums[i]` and `nums[j]`; a pair is “nice” if that XOR value falls between `low` and `high` inclusive. Return the total number of nice pairs.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Reinitialize a Permutation
explanation_short: You are given an even integer n, which defines a permutation of the numbers 0 to n‑1 that initially equals the identity (perm[i] = i). One operation builds a new array where each even‑indexed position i takes the element from perm[i/2] and each odd‑indexed position i takes the element from perm[n/2 + (i‑1)/2]; the new array then replaces perm. Your task is to determine the smallest positive number of such operations after which the permutation becomes exactly the original identity again. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Maximize Number of Nice Divisors
explanation_short: You are given a single integer primeFactors representing the maximum allowed total count of prime factors (with multiplicity) for a positive integer n. Your task is to choose such an n so that the number of its “nice divisors” – divisors that are themselves products of at least one of the prime factors of n – is as large as possible. Return that maximal count of nice divisors, taking the result modulo 1 000 000 007. The answer must be computed without actually enumerating all possible n.

title: Sentence Similarity III
explanation_short: You receive two strings, each a sentence made of words separated by single spaces. Your task is to determine whether you can insert any (possibly empty) sequence of whole words at some position in one of the sentences so that the two become exactly the same. The inserted words must be separated from the existing ones by spaces. Output `true` if this is possible; otherwise output `false`.

title: Determine Color of a Chessboard Square
explanation_short: You receive a string such as “a1” that specifies a square on a standard chessboard, with the column letter first and the row number second. Your task is to decide whether that square is white or black. Return the Boolean value true if the square is white, and false if it is black. The input will always be a valid coordinate.

title: Maximum Number of Groups Getting Fresh Donuts
explanation_short: You are given an integer batchSize and an array groups, where each element tells how many customers are in a visiting group. A group is considered happy if the first donut it receives comes from a completely fresh batch, meaning no donuts are left over from the previous group. By rearranging the order in which the groups are served, you must maximize the total number of happy groups. Return that maximum possible count.

title: Truncate Sentence
explanation_short:
You receive a string `s` that contains words separated by single spaces and an integer `k`.  
Your task is to keep only the first `k` words from the sentence and discard the rest.  
The result should be a new string consisting of those words in their original order, with a single space between each and no extra spaces at the ends.

title: Finding the Users Active Minutes
explanation_short: You are given a list of logs, each containing a user ID and the minute when that user performed an action, together with an integer k. For every user you must count how many different minutes they appear in the logs (the user‑active‑minutes). Then create a 1‑indexed array of length k where the j‑th entry tells how many users have exactly j of those unique minutes. Positions for which no user has that count should contain 0.

title: Evaluate the Bracket Pairs of a String
explanation_short: You receive a string `s` that contains substrings enclosed in parentheses, each representing a key, and a list `knowledge` where each element is a pair `[key, value]`. For every parenthesized key in `s`, substitute the whole “(key)” with its corresponding value from `knowledge`; if the key is absent from the list, replace it with a question mark. The answer is the new string after all such replacements have been performed.

title: Minimum Absolute Sum Difference
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays of the same length, nums1 and nums2. For each index i, compute the absolute difference |nums1[i] − nums2[i]| and sum these values. You may change at most one element of nums1 to any other value that already appears in nums1 to make the total sum as small as possible. Return the minimum achievable sum (mod 10⁹ + 7).

title: Count Nice Pairs in an Array
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` of non‑negative integers. A pair of positions `(i, j)` with `i < j` is “nice” when the sum of the element at `i` and the reversed digits of the element at `j` equals the sum of the element at `j` and the reversed digits of the element at `i`. Count all such pairs and return the total modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Minimum Sideway Jumps
explanation_short: You are given an array obstacles of length n + 1 where obstacles[i] is 0 if point i has no obstacle or a value 1‑3 indicating which lane is blocked at that point. A frog starts at point 0 in lane 2 and must reach point n, moving forward on the same lane when possible or side‑jumping to any other free lane at the same point. Your task is to find the smallest possible number of side jumps needed to reach the end (the final lane can be any of the three). Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Number of Different Subsequences GCDs
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` containing positive integers.  
For every non‑empty subsequence you can form from the array, compute the greatest common divisor of the numbers in that subsequence.  
Collect all the GCD values that appear and count how many different numbers there are.  
Return that count as the answer.

title: Sign of the Product of an Array
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums`.  
First, consider the product of every element in the array.  
Then determine the sign of that product: return 1 if it’s positive, ‑1 if it’s negative, and 0 if it equals zero.  
The function should output that sign value as an integer.

title: Find the Winner of the Circular Game
explanation_short: You are given two integers n (the number of friends sitting in a circle) and k (the step count). Starting from friend 1, you repeatedly count k friends clockwise, remove the k‑th friend, and continue counting from the next person still in the circle until only one friend remains. Output the label of that final friend, which is the winner.

title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array Increasing
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly pick any position and add 1 to that element. The task is to make the whole array strictly increasing – each element must be larger than the one before it. Output the minimum total number of increments needed to achieve this.

title: Queries on Number of Points Inside a Circle
explanation_short: You are given a list of points, each described by its x‑ and y‑coordinates, and a list of queries where each query provides the center (x, y) and radius of a circle. For every query you must count how many of the given points lie inside the circle or exactly on its border. A point is counted if its distance to the circle’s center is less than or equal to the radius. Return an array whose j‑th element is the count for the j‑th query.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make String Sorted
explanation_short: You are given a single string `s` consisting of lowercase letters. Repeatedly apply the defined operation-choose positions `i` and `j`, swap the characters at `i‑1` and `j`, then reverse the suffix starting at `i`-until the whole string is in non‑decreasing (sorted) order. Your task is to determine how many such operations are required to reach the sorted state. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Finding MK Average
explanation_short: You are given two integers m and k that define a sliding window of the most recent m numbers in a data stream. For each new number you must be able to insert it into the stream, and at any time compute the “MKAverage”: the average of the numbers that remain after discarding the k smallest and the k largest values among the last m elements. If fewer than m numbers have been seen, the MKAverage is undefined and you should report -1. The required output is the integer part of this average whenever it is requested.

title: Maximum XOR for Each Query
explanation_short: You are given a sorted array `nums` of `n` non‑negative integers and an integer `maximumBit`.
