For each of `n` queries you must choose a number `k` (0 ≤ k < 2^maximumBit) so that the XOR of all current elements of `nums` together with `k` equals the largest possible value (which is 2^maximumBit − 1). After answering a query you remove the last element of `nums` and repeat the process. Return an array containing the chosen `k` for each query in the order they were answered.

title: Check if the Sentence Is Pangram
explanation_short:
You receive a single string that consists only of lowercase English letters.  
Your task is to check whether each of the 26 letters from ‘a’ to ‘z’ appears at least once somewhere in the given string.  
If the string contains every letter, the result should be true; otherwise it should be false.  
Return the appropriate Boolean value as the output.

title: Maximum Ice Cream Bars
explanation_short: You are given an array `costs` where each element is the price of one ice‑cream bar, and an integer `coins` representing the total money available. The task is to determine how many bars can be purchased without exceeding the budget, assuming the bars can be bought in any order. The answer is the largest possible count of items whose summed prices is ≤ `coins`. The result should be returned as a single integer.

title: Find XOR Sum of All Pairs Bitwise AND
explanation_short: You are given two 0‑indexed arrays arr1 and arr2 containing non‑negative integers. For every possible pair (i, j) you compute the bitwise AND of arr1[i] and arr2[j]; then you take the bitwise XOR of all those AND results together. The required output is the single integer that equals this overall XOR sum.

title: Single-Threaded CPU
explanation_short: You receive a list of n tasks, each given as [enqueueTime, processingTime]. Starting from time 0, the CPU can run only one task at a time; whenever it becomes idle it must choose among all tasks whose enqueue time has passed, picking the one with the shortest processing time (breaking ties by the smallest original index). Return an array containing the indices of the tasks in the exact order they are executed.

title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`. You may perform at most `k` operations, each of which adds 1 to any single element of the array. The task is to determine the largest possible count of equal numbers you can obtain after those increments. The answer is a single integer representing that maximum frequency.

title: Maximum Building Height
explanation_short: You are given the total number of buildings `n` and a list of restrictions, each specifying a building index and the highest height allowed for that building. Every building must have a non‑negative integer height, and the height of two neighboring buildings can differ by at most 1. Your task is to assign heights that satisfy all the given restrictions and the adjacency rule while making the tallest building as high as possible. Return that maximum possible height as a single integer.

title: Sum of Digits in Base K
explanation_short: You are given two integers: n, written in decimal, and a base k. First convert n from decimal to its representation in base k. Then add together the individual digits of that base‑k representation, treating each digit as a regular decimal number. Output the resulting sum as a decimal integer.

title: Longest Substring Of All Vowels in Order
explanation_short: You are given a string made up solely of the letters a, e, i, o, and u. A substring is “beautiful” when it consists of one or more a’s, followed by one or more e’s, then i’s, then o’s, and finally u’s, without any other ordering or gaps. Your task is to find the length of the longest contiguous piece of the input that meets this pattern. Return that length, or 0 if no such substring exists.

title: Maximum Element After Decreasing and Rearranging
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers. You may rearrange the elements in any order and repeatedly lower any element’s value (but never increase it) until the array meets the rule that, when viewed from left to right, each element is at most its 1‑based position index. Your task is to determine the greatest value any element can have after the array satisfies this rule. The output is a single integer – that maximum possible element.

title: Seat Reservation Manager
explanation_short: You are given a number n representing seats labeled 1…n that are initially all free. A series of commands will either ask for the smallest currently free seat (which should be returned and marked as taken) or release a previously taken seat back into the pool. Your task is to keep track of which seats are available after each command. For every “reserve” command you must output the seat number that is assigned; “unreserve” commands produce no output. The solution must handle the operations efficiently as they can be many.

title: Minimum Distance to the Target Element
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`, a value `target`, and a starting index `start`. Find an index `i` where `nums[i]` equals `target` and the absolute difference `|i‑start|` is as small as possible. The distance is measured by the absolute difference between the found index and `start`. Output that minimum distance as an integer.

title: Closest Room
explanation_short: You are given a list of rooms, each described by a unique room number and its size, and a list of queries, each containing a preferred room number and a required minimum size. For every query you must pick a room whose size is at least the required minimum and whose room number is as close as possible to the preferred number; if two rooms are equally close, choose the smaller room number. If no room satisfies the size requirement, the answer for that query is -1. Return an array containing the selected room number (or -1) for each query in order.

title: Replace All Digits with Characters
explanation_short: You receive a string where characters at even indices are lowercase letters and characters at odd indices are digits. For each odd position, replace the digit with the letter that lies that many places after the preceding letter in the alphabet (the shift never goes past ‘z’). Return the resulting string after all such replacements.

title: Maximum Population Year
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element gives a person’s birth year and the year they die. For any year x, a person counts toward the population if x is at least their birth year and strictly before their death year. Your task is to determine which year has the largest number of people alive, and if several years tie, pick the earliest one. Return that year as a single integer.

title: Splitting a String Into Descending Consecutive Values
explanation_short:
You receive a string `s` made only of digits.  
You must decide whether the digits can be broken into at least two consecutive pieces so that, when each piece is read as an integer, the numbers strictly decrease and each neighboring pair differs by exactly 1.  
The pieces must be contiguous and non‑empty; leading zeros are allowed because they are part of the substring but do not affect the numeric value.  
Return **true** if such a split exists, otherwise return **false**.

title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Reach the Kth Smallest Number
explanation_short: You are given a string `num` that represents a non‑negative integer and an integer `k`. A “wonderful” integer is any permutation of the digits of `num` that is larger than the original value. Your task is to identify the k‑th smallest wonderful integer and determine how many adjacent digit swaps are required to turn `num` into that target arrangement. Return that minimum swap count as an integer.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
explanation_short: You are given a list of intervals, each defined by its left and right endpoints, and a list of query integers. For every query you must determine the length (right − left + 1) of the smallest interval that includes that query point, or output –1 if no interval covers it. Return an array containing the answer for each query in the order they appear.

title: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph
explanation_short: You are given a string where each character denotes the color of node i, and a list of directed edges connecting the nodes. A path follows the direction of edges, and you must consider every possible path in the graph. Determine the largest count of a single color that appears on any such path; if the graph contains a cycle, the answer is ‑1. Output that maximum count (or ‑1 when a cycle exists).

title: Sorting the Sentence
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s` that consists of several words separated by spaces; each word ends with a digit from 1 to 9 indicating its original place in the sentence. Your task is to reorder the words so that they appear in the order given by those digits and then delete the trailing digits. The result should be the reconstructed sentence as a plain string.

title: Maximum Distance Between a Pair of Values
explanation_short:
You receive two integer arrays that are sorted in non‑increasing order.  
A pair of indices (i, j) is considered valid when i ≤ j and the element from the first array at i is not larger than the element from the second array at j.  
Your task is to locate the valid pair whose indices are farthest apart, i.e., maximize j − i.  
Return that maximum distance (or 0 if no such pair exists).

title: Maximum Subarray Min-Product
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums`. For every non‑empty contiguous subarray, calculate the product of its smallest element and the sum of all its elements, and identify the largest such product among all subarrays. Return that maximum value modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Incremental Memory Leak
explanation_short: You receive two integers memory1 and memory2 that represent the initial free bits on two memory sticks. Starting at second 1, each second i bits must be taken from the stick that currently has more free memory (or the first stick if they are equal); the process stops when neither stick can provide i bits. Return an array [crashTime, memory1Remaining, memory2Remaining] where crashTime is the second at which the allocation fails and the last two values are the bits still available on each stick.

title: Finding Pairs With a Certain Sum
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, and then a sequence of queries. One type of query adds a new integer to nums2; the other type asks how many pairs (one element from nums1 and one from nums2) have a sum equal to a given target value. For each count query you must return that number of qualifying pairs. The overall task is to build a data structure that can process these mixed updates and queries efficiently.

title: Rotating the Box
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid where each cell holds a stone (‘#’), an obstacle (‘*’) or empty space (‘.’). After rotating the whole box 90° clockwise, every stone drops straight down until it meets an obstacle, another stone, or the bottom edge, while obstacles stay fixed. Return the new n × m grid that shows the final positions of all stones and obstacles.

title: Sum of Floored Pairs
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums`. For every possible pair of positions `i` and `j` (including when `i = j`), take the integer division of `nums[i]` by `nums[j]` and round it down, then add all those values together. The required output is a single number representing this total sum.

title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums`. For every possible subset of this array (the empty set counts as a subset), compute the bitwise XOR of the elements in that subset, then add together all of those XOR results. Return the total sum as a single integer.

title: Minimum Number of Swaps to Make the Binary String Alternating
explanation_short:
You are given a binary string `s`.  
You must find the fewest swaps of any two characters that can turn `s` into an alternating string, where no two adjacent bits are the same.  
If no sequence of swaps can achieve an alternating pattern, the answer is `-1`.  
Otherwise, output the minimum number of swaps required.

title: Longer Contiguous Segments of Ones than Zeros
explanation_short: You are given a string s that contains only the characters ‘0’ and ‘1’. You must determine the length of the longest consecutive block of 1’s and the length of the longest consecutive block of 0’s. If the longest 1‑block is strictly longer than the longest 0‑block, the answer is true; otherwise (including when they are equal) it is false. Return this result as a boolean.

title: Number of Ways to Rearrange Sticks With K Sticks Visible
explanation_short: You receive two integers n and k. Consider all possible orderings of the numbers 1 through n; a stick is “visible” when, scanning from the left, it is taller than every stick before it. Your task is to count how many permutations have exactly k visible sticks and output that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Minimum Speed to Arrive on Time
explanation_short: You are given an array dist where dist[i] is the length of the i‑th train ride, and a floating‑point value hour that represents the total time allowed to reach the office. All rides must be taken in order, each at the same integer speed, and after every ride (except the last) you may have to wait until the next whole hour before departing. Your task is to determine the smallest positive integer speed that lets you finish all rides within hour, or return ‑1 if no such speed exists. The output is that minimum speed (or ‑1).

title: Jump Game VII
explanation_short: You are given a binary string s and two integers minJump and maxJump. Starting from index 0 (which is always ‘0’), you may jump forward to any index j where the distance j‑i is at least minJump and at most maxJump, and the target position s[j] must also be ‘0’. Decide whether it is possible to reach the last index of the string, and output true if you can, otherwise false.

title: Substrings of Size Three with Distinct Characters
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Consider every contiguous block of three characters in `s` and check whether the three letters are all different.  
Return the total number of such length‑three blocks, counting each occurrence even if the same substring appears multiple times.

title: Get Biggest Three Rhombus Sums in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of integers. For every possible rhombus whose corners lie on grid cells (including the degenerate case of a single cell), compute the sum of the numbers on its border. Collect all distinct border sums, sort them from largest to smallest, and output the top three values. If fewer than three different sums exist, return whatever you have.

title: Stone Game VIII
explanation_short: You are given an array stones where each element is the value of a stone in a line. Alice and Bob alternately pick a prefix of at least two stones, add the sum of those values to their own score, and replace the removed stones with a single new stone whose value equals that sum; the game stops when only one stone remains. Both players play optimally: Alice tries to make the final (Alice score – Bob score) as large as possible, while Bob tries to make it as small as possible. Return the resulting score difference as an integer.

title: Maximum Value after Insertion
explanation_short: You are given a string n that represents an integer (it may start with a ‘‑’ sign) and a single digit x (1‑9). You may insert the digit x anywhere inside the decimal representation of n, but you cannot place it before a leading negative sign. Choose the insertion position that makes the resulting integer as large as possible. Return the whole number, including any sign, as a string.

title: Minimize Maximum Pair Sum in Array
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` that contains an even number of integers.  
Your task is to split all the elements into `n/2` pairs, using each number exactly once.  
For each pair you calculate its sum, then consider the biggest sum among all pairs.  
Output the minimum possible value of this biggest sum that can be achieved by a suitable pairing.

title: Process Tasks Using Servers
explanation_short: You receive two arrays: `servers`, where each element gives a server’s weight, and `tasks`, where each element tells how many seconds a task needs to run. Starting at second 0, tasks appear one per second and are placed in a queue; whenever a server is free, the front‑most queued task is given to the available server with the smallest weight (breaking ties by smaller index). A server becomes free again after the time it started the task plus the task’s duration. Return an array `ans` where `ans[j]` is the index of the server that processes the j‑th task.

title: Minimum Skips to Arrive at Meeting On Time
explanation_short: You are given an array dist describing the lengths of n roads, a travel speed speed, and a time limit hoursBefore. You travel each road in dist[i]/speed hours, and after every road except the last you must wait until the next integer hour unless you choose to skip that rest. Your task is to determine the fewest rests you must skip so that the total elapsed time does not exceed hoursBefore. Return that minimum number of skips, or -1 if no amount of skipping can meet the deadline.

title: Minimum XOR Sum of Two Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of equal length n. You may reorder the elements of the second array arbitrarily, then pair each position i with the element from the first array and compute the XOR of the two numbers; the goal is to make the total sum of these XOR values as small as possible. Return that minimum achievable sum.

title: Check if Word Equals Summation of Two Words
explanation_short: You receive three lowercase strings - `firstWord`, `secondWord` and `targetWord` - each using only the letters a through j. Convert each string to a number by replacing every letter with its alphabet index (a = 0, b = 1, …, j = 9) and reading the resulting digits as an integer. Return **true** if the integer from `firstWord` plus the integer from `secondWord` equals the integer from `targetWord`; otherwise return **false**.

title: Minimum Number of Flips to Make the Binary String Alternating
explanation_short:
You receive a string consisting only of ‘0’ and ‘1’.  
You may apply two kinds of operations any number of times, but only the second type of operation counts toward the answer.  
Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of those second‑type operations needed to turn the whole string into an alternating pattern, where no two neighboring characters are the same.  
Return that minimum number as an integer.

title: Minimum Space Wasted From Packaging
explanation_short: You are given an integer array packages where each element is the size of a package, and a 2‑D array boxes where each sub‑array lists the box sizes offered by one supplier (each size can be used unlimited times). Choose a single supplier and assign every package to a box from that supplier that is at least as large as the package, then compute the sum of (box size − package size) over all assignments. The task is to find the smallest possible total waste among all suppliers, returning that minimum modulo 1 000 000 007, or -1 if no supplier can accommodate every package.

title: Egg Drop With 2 Eggs and N Floors
explanation_short: You receive a single integer n, the number of floors in a building. Using two identical eggs, you must devise a strategy that always identifies the highest floor from which an egg can be dropped without breaking. The task is to determine the smallest possible number of drops required in the worst case to guarantee finding that floor. Output that minimum number of drops.

title: Determine Whether Matrix Can Be Obtained By Rotation
explanation_short: You receive two square binary matrices of equal dimensions. You may rotate the first matrix clockwise in steps of 90 degrees any number of times. Check whether any of these orientations makes the first matrix exactly match the second one. Output true if a match is possible, otherwise output false.

title: Reduction Operations to Make the Array Elements Equal
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums`. In each operation you look at the current largest value in the array and lower it to the next‑largest distinct value that still appears. You must keep performing such reductions until every element has the same value. Return the total number of operations required.

title: Check if All the Integers in a Range Are Covered
explanation_short: You receive a list of integer intervals, each given as a pair [start, end], and two integers left and right. You must determine whether every integer from left through right (inclusive) lies inside at least one of the given intervals. Return true if the whole range is covered, otherwise return false.

title: Find the Student that Will Replace the Chalk
explanation_short: You are given an array chalk where chalk[i] is the amount of chalk student i needs each time they receive a problem, and an integer k representing the initial pieces of chalk. Starting from student 0, the students take turns in order, each subtracting their required amount from k; when the remaining chalk is less than the amount needed by the current student, that student must replace the chalk. Return the index of this student.

title: Largest Magic Square
explanation_short: You are given a rectangular grid of integers with m rows and n columns. Your task is to locate a square sub‑grid of side length k where the sum of every row, every column, and the two main diagonals are all identical, and to determine the greatest possible k. Return that maximum side length as a single integer.

title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
explanation_short: You are given a list of three‑element arrays (triplets) and a single target triplet [x, y, z]. You may repeatedly pick any two triplets and replace one of them with a new triplet whose each coordinate is the maximum of the corresponding coordinates of the chosen pair. The task is to decide whether, after any number of such operations, the target triplet can appear exactly as one of the triplets in the list. Return true if it is possible, otherwise return false.

title: Redistribute Characters to Make All Strings Equal
explanation_short: You receive a list of strings called words. In each move you may take any single character from one non‑empty string and insert it anywhere in another string. Determine whether, after any number of such moves, all strings can be transformed so that they become identical. Return **true** if it is possible and **false** otherwise.

title: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
explanation_short:
You are given two strings `s` and `p` (where `p` is guaranteed to appear as a subsequence of `s`) and an array `removable` that lists distinct positions in `s`.  
Choose a number `k` and delete the characters at the first `k` indices of `removable` from `s`.  
Your task is to find the largest `k` for which `p` still occurs as a subsequence in the shortened string.  
Return that maximum `k` as an integer.

title: Minimum Cost to Change the Final Value of Expression
explanation_short:
You are given a string that forms a valid Boolean expression using the symbols ‘1’, ‘0’, ‘&’, ‘|’, ‘(’, and ‘)’.  
Each operation may change any single character (for example, flipping a ‘0’ to ‘1’ or swapping ‘&’ with ‘|’) and counts as one unit of cost.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of such operations required so that the overall value of the whole expression flips from its original result.  
Return that minimum cost as an integer.

title: Largest Odd Number in String
explanation_short: You receive a single string `num` that contains the decimal digits of a large integer. From all possible non‑empty contiguous substrings of `num`, you must identify the one that represents an odd integer and has the greatest numeric value. If at least one such substring exists, output it exactly as it appears; otherwise output an empty string `""`.

title: The Number of Full Rounds You Have Played
explanation_short: You receive two strings loginTime and logoutTime in “HH:MM” 24‑hour format. A chess round lasts exactly 15 minutes and starts at every quarter hour (00:00, 00:15, 00:30, … 23:45). You must determine how many of those 15‑minute rounds are completely contained within the period you were logged in, treating a logout earlier than the login as spanning midnight. Return that count as an integer.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference Queries
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a list of queries, each query being a pair `[l, r]` that defines a subarray from index `l` to `r` inclusive. For every query you must determine the smallest absolute difference `|nums[i] - nums[j]|` among any two distinct positions `i` and `j` inside that subarray. If the subarray contains only identical values, the answer for that query is `-1`. Return a list of these answers in the same order as the queries.

title: The Earliest and Latest Rounds Where Players Compete
explanation_short: You are given three integers n, firstPlayer and secondPlayer. Players are paired from the front and back of the line each round, with a middle player advancing automatically when the count is odd, and the winners are reordered by their original numbers. Because the two named players always defeat any opponent, you can decide the results of all other matches to make them meet as early or as late as possible. Return a two‑element list: the smallest round number and the largest round number in which those two players could face each other.

title: Find a Peak Element II
explanation_short: You are given an m × n matrix mat where each cell’s value differs from its immediate left, right, top, and bottom neighbors, and the whole grid is imagined to be bordered by cells of value -1. A “peak” is any element that is strictly larger than all four of those neighboring cells. Your task is to locate any one such peak in the matrix. Return its position as a two‑element array [i, j] representing the row and column indices.

title: Maximum Alternating Subsequence Sum
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. From it you may delete any elements, keeping the remaining ones in their original order, to form a subsequence; then re‑index that subsequence starting at 0 and compute the alternating sum (elements at even positions added, those at odd positions subtracted). Your task is to determine the largest possible alternating sum achievable by any such subsequence. Output that maximum value as a single integer.

title: Count Sub Islands
explanation_short: You receive two m × n binary grids where 1 represents land and 0 represents water. An island is a group of 1 cells connected horizontally or vertically. For each island that appears in the second grid, determine whether every cell of that island is also land in the first grid; those that are become sub‑islands. Output the count of sub‑islands found in the second grid.

title: Maximum Product Difference Between Two Pairs
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. Choose four distinct indices to form two pairs of numbers, say `(nums[w], nums[x])` and `(nums[y], nums[z])`. Compute the product of the first pair minus the product of the second pair, and find the greatest possible result over all valid choices. Output that maximum product difference as a single integer.

title: Remove All Occurrences of a Substring
explanation_short:
You are given two strings `s` and `part`.  
Whenever the exact sequence `part` appears consecutively inside `s`, you delete that segment.  
You keep deleting such occurrences until `s` contains no more copies of `part`.  
The required output is the resulting string after all possible removals.

title: Remove One Element to Make the Array Strictly Increasing
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
You must determine whether removing exactly one element (or none, if it’s already strictly increasing) can make the remaining numbers increase strictly, meaning each element is larger than the one before it.  
If such a removal is possible, the answer is `true`; otherwise it is `false`.  
The output is a single boolean value.

title: Cyclically Rotating a Grid
explanation_short: You receive an m × n integer matrix grid (where both m and n are even) and an integer k. Each concentric “layer” of the matrix must be shifted counter‑clockwise, moving every element to the position of its neighbor, and this shift is performed k times for every layer. Return the matrix after all layers have been rotated the required number of times.

title: Design Movie Rental System
explanation_short: You are given a list of movie copies, each described by a shop ID, a movie ID, and its rental price. The system must handle a sequence of commands: search to list up to five cheapest available shops for a given movie, rent to mark a copy as taken, drop to return a copy, and report to list the five currently rented copies with the lowest price. For each search or report command you must return the requested list of shop‑movie pairs in the correct order; the other commands produce no direct output. The overall output is the collection of all lists produced by the search and report operations.

title: Eliminate Maximum Number of Monsters
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of equal length - `dist[i]` is how far monster i starts from the city and `speed[i]` is how many kilometers it moves toward the city each minute. Starting with a fully‑charged weapon that can kill one monster per minute, you must decide the order in which to eliminate monsters so that no monster reaches the city before you act. The game ends the instant any monster’s distance becomes zero or negative, even if the weapon becomes charged at that same minute. Return the greatest number of monsters you can kill before the loss occurs (or `n` if you can kill them all).

title: Count Ways to Build Rooms in an Ant Colony
explanation_short: You are given an array prevRoom of length n where prevRoom[i] specifies the unique earlier room that must exist before room i can be built (room 0 has prevRoom[0] = –1). Starting from room 0, you may construct rooms one at a time, but a room can only be added after its required predecessor is already built. Your task is to count all possible sequences in which the n rooms can be built while respecting these prerequisite connections. Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Number of Wonderful Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a string `word` made only of the letters a through j.  
A substring is “wonderful” when no more than one of its letters appears an odd number of times.  
Your task is to count every contiguous substring of `word` that meets this condition, counting repeated occurrences separately.  
Return the total number of wonderful substrings as an integer.

title: Build Array from Permutation
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` that contains each integer from 0 to `n‑1` exactly once. For every position `i`, you must place in a new array the element found at index `nums[i]` of the original array. The result is an array of the same length where each entry is `nums[nums[i]]`.

title: Longest Common Subpath
explanation_short: You are given the number of cities n and an array paths where each element is the ordered list of cities visited by one friend. A subpath is any consecutive block of cities inside one of those lists. Your task is to determine the maximum possible length of a block that occurs as a subpath in every friend’s list. Return that length, or 0 if no such common block exists.

title: Count Square Sum Triples
explanation_short:
You are given a single integer n.  
Consider all ordered triples of positive integers (a, b, c) that satisfy the Pythagorean relation a² + b² = c² and have each component not larger than n.  
Your task is to determine how many such triples exist.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Sum Game
explanation_short: You receive an even‑length string that contains digits and ‘?’ placeholders. Alice and Bob alternately replace a ‘?’ with any digit (0‑9), Alice moving first, until no ‘?’ remain. After the string is fully filled, compare the sum of the digits in the first half with the sum in the second half: Alice wins if the sums differ, Bob wins if they are equal. Assuming both players choose their moves optimally, you must decide whether Alice can force a win. Return **true** when Alice can guarantee a win, otherwise return **false**.

title: Count Good Numbers
explanation_short: You are given an integer n. You must count how many length‑n digit strings have an even digit (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) at every even index and a prime digit (2, 3, 5, 7) at every odd index; leading zeros are permitted. The answer should be reported modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Nearest Exit from Entrance in Maze
explanation_short: You receive a rectangular grid where each cell is either empty ('.') or a wall ('+') and a pair of coordinates indicating your starting position. From the start you may move one step up, down, left, or right, never crossing walls or leaving the grid, and you must reach the closest empty cell that lies on the grid’s outer edge (the entrance itself does not count as an exit). Return the minimum number of steps required to reach such a border cell, or –1 if no border cell is reachable.

title: Concatenation of Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. Build a new array `ans` that is exactly twice as long, where the first `n` positions contain the elements of `nums` in order and the next `n` positions repeat the same sequence. The output is this concatenated array `ans`.

title: Merge BSTs to Create Single BST
explanation_short: You receive an array containing the root nodes of n separate binary search trees, each tree having at most three nodes and distinct root values. By repeatedly attaching one tree to a leaf of another (where the leaf’s value equals the other tree’s root) you must perform exactly n − 1 such merges. After all merges you should have a single binary tree that still satisfies the BST ordering property. Return the root of that tree if it exists; otherwise return null.

title: Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time
explanation_short: You are given an integer maxTime, a list of roads where each road connects two cities and has a travel time, and an array passingFees that tells how much you must pay each time you enter a city. Starting at city 0, you must reach city n‑1 within maxTime minutes, and the cost of a journey is the sum of the fees of all cities visited (including the start and destination). Return the smallest possible total fee, or -1 if no route can be completed in the allowed time.

title: Unique Length-3 Palindromic Subsequences
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Consider every way to pick three characters from `s` while keeping their original order; each such pick forms a length‑3 subsequence.  
Count how many of those subsequences are palindromes (the first and third characters are the same) and are distinct from one another.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Painting a Grid With Three Different Colors
explanation_short: You receive two integers m and n, defining an m × n grid whose cells must all be painted. Each cell can be colored red, green, or blue, but any two cells that share a side cannot have the same color. Compute how many distinct colorings satisfy this rule and return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Add Minimum Number of Rungs
explanation_short: You are given a strictly increasing list of rung heights and an integer dist. Starting from height 0, you may step to the next rung only if the gap to it does not exceed dist. You may add new rungs at any positive integer heights that are not already present. Return the smallest number of rungs that must be added so you can reach the last rung.

title: Maximum Number of Points with Cost
explanation_short: You are given an m × n integer matrix points. You must pick exactly one cell in each row, adding the cell’s value to your score. For every pair of consecutive rows, you subtract the absolute difference between the column indices you chose. Output the largest total score achievable after all additions and subtractions.

title: Maximum Number of Words You Can Type
explanation_short:
You receive a single line of text containing several words separated by spaces, and a second string listing the distinct letters whose keys are broken.  
For each word, you must check whether any of its letters appear in the broken‑letter list.  
Count how many words can be typed without using any broken keys.  
The answer is that count, returned as an integer.

title: Maximum Genetic Difference Query
explanation_short:
You are given an array parents that defines a rooted tree (‑1 marks the root) and a list of queries, each containing a node nodeᵢ and an integer valᵢ.  
For every query you must look at every node on the path from nodeᵢ up to the root (including both ends) and consider its genetic value, which is simply its index.  
Take the bitwise‑XOR of valᵢ with each of those values and keep the largest result.  
Return an array where the i‑th element is this maximum XOR for the i‑th query.

title: Check if All Characters Have Equal Number of Occurrences
explanation_short:
You receive a single string `s`.  
You must determine whether every different character that shows up in `s` occurs the same number of times.  
Return `true` if the frequencies are all equal, otherwise return `false`.

title: The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Chair
explanation_short: You receive a list `times` where each entry `[arrival_i, leaving_i]` gives the arrival and departure moments of friend i, and an integer `targetFriend` identifying one of the friends. Friends arrive at distinct times and always choose the smallest‑numbered chair that is currently free; when a friend leaves, their chair becomes free instantly. Your task is to determine which chair number the friend `targetFriend` will occupy during their stay. Return that chair number as the answer.

title: Sum of Digits of String After Convert
explanation_short: You receive a lowercase string `s` and an integer `k`. First each letter is replaced by its position in the alphabet (a = 1, b = 2, …, z = 26) and the resulting numbers are concatenated to form a single integer. Then you repeatedly replace the current number by the sum of its decimal digits exactly `k` times. The answer you must output is the final integer obtained after those `k` transformations.

title: Maximum Compatibility Score Sum
explanation_short: You are given two m × n arrays: one listing each student’s 0/1 answers and the other listing each mentor’s answers. You must assign every student to a distinct mentor so that each pair’s compatibility score-how many answers they share-is summed across all pairs. Return the largest possible total compatibility score.

title: Delete Duplicate Folders in System
explanation_short: You receive a list of folder paths, where each path is an array of names from the root to a specific folder. Two folders are identical if the whole set of their subfolders and the structure beneath them are exactly the same, even if they are located in different parts of the tree. Every folder that belongs to any identical group, together with all of its descendants, is marked for deletion, and the deletion is performed only once. Output the paths of the folders that remain after this deletion, in any order.

title: Describe the Painting
explanation_short: You are given a list of painted intervals, each defined by a start point, an end point (exclusive), and a unique color value. Wherever these intervals overlap, the colors mix, and the mixed color is represented by the sum of the involved color values. Your task is to merge the whole number line into the smallest possible set of non‑overlapping intervals that each carry the correct summed color for that region, ignoring any gaps that were never painted. Return those intervals as a list of triples [start, end, sum] in any order.

title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
explanation_short: You are given an array of distinct integers `heights`, where `heights[i]` is the height of the person standing at position `i` from left to right. For each person you must count how many people to their right are visible, meaning a person `j` (with `j > i`) is visible if every person between `i` and `j` is shorter than both `heights[i]` and `heights[j]`. The result is an array `answer` of the same length, and `answer[i]` stores the number of people that the `i`‑th person can see.

title: Three Divisors
explanation_short: You receive a single integer n. You must decide whether n possesses exactly three positive divisors (including 1 and n itself). Return “true” if it does, otherwise return “false”.

title: Largest Number After Mutating Substring
explanation_short: You receive a numeric string `num` and an array `change` of ten digits, where `change[d]` tells you what digit each original digit `d` can become. You may select one contiguous part of `num` and replace every digit in that part with its mapped value from `change` (or choose to leave the string unchanged). Return the resulting string that represents the greatest possible integer after this single optional mutation.

title: Maximum Number of Weeks for Which You Can Work
explanation_short: You are given an integer array milestones where milestones[i] is the number of weeks of work required for project i. Each week you may choose any project that still has unfinished milestones, but you cannot work on the same project in two consecutive weeks. You keep working week after week until either all milestones are completed or the only remaining milestones would force you to repeat a project back‑to‑back. Return the greatest possible number of weeks you can work under these constraints.

title: Count Number of Special Subsequences
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` that contains only the values 0, 1, and 2. You must count how many different subsequences (chosen by index sets, keeping the original order) consist of at least one 0 followed by at least one 1 and then at least one 2. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Check if Move is Legal
explanation_short: You receive an 8 × 8 board where each cell is “.” (empty), “W” (white) or “B” (black), plus a row index rMove, column index cMove, and the color you are playing (“W” or “B”). After changing the specified empty cell to that color, you must check whether the cell becomes an endpoint of a line (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) of length ≥ 3 whose two ends are the same color and whose interior cells are the opposite color, with no empty cells in the line. Return true if such a line exists and false otherwise.

title: Minimum Garden Perimeter to Collect Enough Apples
explanation_short: You are given a single integer neededApples. Imagine an infinite grid where each point (i, j) holds |i| + |j| apples, and you may choose an axis‑aligned square centered at the origin. Your task is to pick the smallest such square whose interior and border together contain at least neededApples apples. Return the perimeter of that minimal square (four times its side length).

title: Minimum Total Space Wasted With K Resizing Operations
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` where `nums[i]` tells how many elements must fit in the dynamic array at moment `i`, and an integer `k` that limits how many times you may change the array’s capacity.  
Choose a capacity for each moment, starting with an initial size and performing at most `k` resizes, so that the capacity is never smaller than the required `nums[i]`.  
The waste at a moment is the difference between the chosen capacity and `nums[i]`; the goal is to make the sum of these wastes over all moments as small as possible.  
Return that minimum total waste.

title: Remove Stones to Minimize the Total
explanation_short: You are given an array piles where each element tells how many stones are in that pile, and an integer k. Exactly k times you may pick any pile and replace its size with the floor of half its current value (you may pick the same pile repeatedly). Return the smallest possible sum of all pile sizes after performing those k operations.

title: Delete Characters to Make Fancy String
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s`.  
You must remove the smallest possible number of characters so that the remaining string never contains three identical letters in a row.  
Return the string that results after those deletions.  
The correct result is always unique.

title: Minimum Number of Swaps to Make the String Balanced
explanation_short: You are given a string s of even length that contains exactly half opening brackets ‘[’ and half closing brackets ‘]’. You may swap the characters at any two positions any number of times. Your task is to determine the smallest number of swaps required to reorder the brackets so that the string becomes balanced (every prefix has at least as many ‘[’ as ‘]’). Return that minimum swap count as an integer.

title: Find the Longest Valid Obstacle Course at Each Position
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array obstacles.  
For each index i, look at all subsequences that end at i, use only elements from positions 0 to i, and never decrease in height.  
Find the greatest possible length of such a subsequence for every i.  
Return an array ans where ans[i] stores that maximum length.

title: Check If String Is a Prefix of Array
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` and an array `words` of separate strings.  
You must decide whether `s` can be obtained by joining the first k elements of `words` in their given order, for some k ≥ 1.  
If such a prefix concatenation exists, the answer is true; otherwise it is false.  
Return the boolean result.

title: Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Substrings
explanation_short: You are given a string s indexed from 0. Choose two substrings that are both palindromes, have odd length, and do not overlap any character of each other. Among all such pairs, find the one whose lengths multiplied together is as large as possible. Output that maximum product as an integer. If no two qualifying substrings exist, the answer is 0.

title: Minimum Non-Zero Product of the Array Elements
explanation_short: You are given a positive integer p, and you consider the list of all numbers from 1 to 2^p − 1 written in binary. You may repeatedly pick any two numbers and exchange a single bit position between them. Your task is to arrange the bits so that the product of all numbers in the list is as small as possible while staying non‑zero. Return that minimum product, taken modulo 1,000,000,007. The answer must be computed before applying the modulo.

title: Last Day Where You Can Still Cross
explanation_short: You are given the dimensions `row` and `col` of a binary matrix and an array `cells` that lists, day by day, which cell turns from land (0) to water (1). The matrix begins entirely land, and on each successive day the cell indicated by `cells[i]` floods. Your task is to find the greatest day index for which a continuous path of land cells still connects some cell in the top row to some cell in the bottom row, moving only in the four cardinal directions. Output that day number.

title: Array With Elements Not Equal to Average of Neighbors
explanation_short:
You are given a list of distinct integers called nums.  
You must permute the elements so that for every position i with 1 ≤ i < n‑1, the value at i is never exactly the average of the two adjacent values (the elements at i‑1 and i+1).  
The result should be any ordering of the original numbers that satisfies this condition.  
Return the reordered array (or indicate that no such ordering exists, if that case is possible).

title: Number of Strings That Appear as Substrings in Word
explanation_short: You are given a list of strings called patterns and a single string called word. For each string in patterns, check whether it occurs as a contiguous block of characters somewhere inside word. Count how many of those pattern strings are found inside word. Return that count as an integer.

title: Minimum Time to Type Word Using Special Typewriter
explanation_short: You are given a lowercase string `word`. A pointer starts on the letter `a` and each second you may either move the pointer one step clockwise or counter‑clockwise around the 26‑letter circle, or type the character currently under the pointer. Determine the smallest number of seconds required to type the entire string in order. Return that minimum as an integer.

title: Maximum Matrix Sum
explanation_short: You are given an n × n matrix of integers. You may repeatedly choose any whole row or any whole column and flip the sign of every element in that line. Your task is to decide which rows and columns to flip so that the total sum of all matrix entries becomes as large as possible. Output that maximum achievable sum.

title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
explanation_short: You are given the number of vertices n, a list of undirected edges connecting pairs of vertices, and two specific vertices called source and destination. Your task is to decide whether you can travel from source to destination by moving along the edges of the graph. Return true if such a path exists; otherwise return false.

title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
explanation_short: You receive an integer n and a list of roads, each described by two intersection indices and the travel time between them. Your task is to determine how many different routes from intersection 0 to intersection n‑1 take the smallest possible total time. Return that count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Find Greatest Common Divisor of Array
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers called `nums`. First identify the smallest and the largest values in the array, then determine the greatest common divisor of those two numbers. Return that divisor as a single integer.

title: Minimize the Difference Between Target and Chosen Elements
explanation_short: You are given an m × n integer matrix and an integer target. From each row you must pick exactly one element, add the chosen numbers together, and compare that sum to target. Your task is to make the absolute difference |target − sum| as small as possible. Return the smallest achievable difference.

title: Find Array Given Subset Sums
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list sums containing the 2ⁿ numbers that result from adding up every possible subset of an unknown array of length n. Your task is to deduce any array of n integers whose subset‑sum multiset matches the supplied sums. The original array may not be unique, but at least one solution is guaranteed to exist. Return the recovered array (in any order) as the output.

title: Number of Ways to Separate Numbers
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `num` that consists only of digits.  
The string was formed by writing a sequence of positive integers in non‑decreasing order, without any commas, and none of the integers may start with a zero.  
Your task is to count how many different sequences of integers could produce exactly the given string.  
Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Find Unique Binary String
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` that contains `n` different binary strings, each exactly `n` characters long. Your task is to produce any binary string of length `n` that does not occur anywhere in `nums`. Output that new string; any valid choice is accepted.

title: Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the Tasks
explanation_short: You receive an array tasks where each element is the number of hours a particular task takes, and an integer sessionTime that caps the total hours you can work in one continuous session. You may arrange the tasks in any order, but the sum of durations assigned to a single session cannot exceed sessionTime. Compute and return the smallest possible number of sessions needed to finish all tasks.

title: Minimum Difference Between Highest and Lowest of K Scores
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.  
Pick any `k` scores from the array.  
For the chosen scores, compute the difference between the largest and the smallest value.  
Return the minimum such difference that can be achieved by an optimal choice of `k` students.

title: Number of Unique Good Subsequences
explanation_short:
You are given a binary string `binary`.  
A good subsequence is any non‑empty subsequence that either is exactly “0” or does not start with a ‘0’.  
Your task is to determine how many different strings satisfy this condition when taken as subsequences of the given string.  
Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Find the Kth Largest Integer in the Array
explanation_short: You receive a list of strings, each string encoding a non‑negative integer, and an integer k. Treat the strings as numbers and rank them from largest to smallest, counting duplicate values separately. Your task is to identify the value that appears in the k‑th position of this descending order. Return that value as a string.

title: Find the Middle Index in Array
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. You need to locate an index `i` such that the sum of all elements before `i` equals the sum of all elements after `i`; if multiple indices satisfy this, return the smallest one. When `i` is at the start or end of the array, the missing side’s sum is treated as 0. Output the found index, or `-1` if no such index exists.

title: Find All Groups of Farmland
explanation_short: The input is an m × n binary matrix where 1 represents farmland and 0 represents forest. Every isolated rectangular block of 1 cells forms a group, and no two groups touch each other horizontally or vertically. You need to determine the coordinates of the top‑left and bottom‑right cells of each rectangle. Return a list of four‑element arrays [r1, c1, r2, c2] for all groups, or an empty list if there are none; the order of the groups can be arbitrary.

title: Operations on Tree
explanation_short: You are given a tree described by a parent array where parent[i] stores the parent of node i (the root is node 0 with parent -1). After building the tree you will receive a sequence of commands, each asking to lock, unlock, or upgrade a specific node on behalf of a user identified by an integer. For a lock you must succeed only if the node is currently unlocked; for an unlock you must succeed only if the same user previously locked that node; for an upgrade you must succeed only if the node is unlocked, has at least one locked descendant, and none of its ancestors are locked, and then lock the node while unlocking all its locked descendants. For every command you output “true” if the operation succeeds and “false” otherwise.

title: The Number of Good Subsets
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. A subset of the array is considered good when the product of its chosen elements can be written as a product of one or more distinct prime numbers (no prime may repeat). Your task is to count how many different subsets-distinguished by the indices of the elements taken-are good. Output this count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: GCD Sort of an Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly swap any two positions whose values have a greatest common divisor larger than 1. Determine whether, by using only such swaps, the entire array can be rearranged into non‑decreasing order. Return `true` if it is possible and `false` otherwise.

title: The Number of Weak Characters in the Game
explanation_short: You are given a list where each element contains two numbers: the character’s attack value and its defense value. A character is considered weak if there is some other character whose attack **and** defense are both strictly larger than those of the weak character. Return the total number of weak characters as a single integer.

title: Smallest Missing Genetic Value in Each Subtree
explanation_short:
You are given two arrays of equal length n: `parents`, where `parents[i]` is the parent of node i (including -1 for the root), and `nums`, where `nums[i]` is a unique genetic value assigned to node i.  
For each node i, consider the subtree consisting of i and all its descendants, and look at the genetic values that appear in that subtree.  
Your task is to determine the smallest integer in the range [1, 10⁵] that does **not** appear among those values.  
Return an array `ans` of length n where `ans[i]` holds that missing value for the subtree rooted at i.

title: Count Special Quadruplets
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. You must count how many index quadruplets `(a, b, c, d)` exist with `a < b < c < d` such that the sum of the three earlier elements equals the fourth one (`nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] == nums[d]`). Each quadruplet is considered distinct by its indices. Return that total count as an integer.

title: Reverse Prefix of Word
explanation_short: You are given a string `word` and a single character `ch`. Find the first position where `ch` appears in `word`; if it exists, reverse the portion of the string from the start up to and including that position, otherwise keep the string unchanged. Return the string after this possible reversal.

title: First Day Where You Have Been in All the Rooms
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed array `nextVisit` of length `n`, where rooms are labeled `0 … n‑1`. Starting on day 0 in room 0, each day you move to a new room: if the number of times you have already been in the current room is odd you go to `nextVisit[current]`, otherwise you go to `(current+1) mod n`. Your task is to determine the first day on which every room has been visited at least once. Return that day number modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Number of Pairs of Interchangeable Rectangles
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element gives the width and height of a rectangle. Two different rectangles are considered interchangeable when their width‑to‑height ratios are exactly the same. Your task is to count how many unordered pairs of distinct rectangles have this property. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Subsequences
explanation_short: You are given a single string `s`. From this string you must select two subsequences that are each palindromes and that never use the same character position. The quality of a pair is measured by multiplying the lengths of the two palindromes. Your task is to find the largest possible product and output that value as an integer.

title: Count Number of Pairs With Absolute Difference K
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers called nums and another integer k. Your task is to count how many distinct index pairs (i, j) with i ≠ j have an absolute difference |nums[i] − nums[j]| equal to k. The result should be returned as a single integer representing that count.

title: Find Original Array From Doubled Array
explanation_short: You are given an array `changed` that may have been created by taking some original integers, adding each of their doubles, and then shuffling the result. Your task is to determine whether such an original array exists and, if it does, to output any ordering of those original numbers. If no valid original array can produce the given `changed`, you must return an empty array. The output should be a list of the original integers (or an empty list).

title: Maximum Earnings From Taxi
explanation_short: You are given an integer n representing points 1 to n on a road, and a list rides where each entry contains a start point, an end point, and a tip amount. While traveling from point 1 to point n you may take any subset of rides that never overlap (you can drop one passenger and pick up another at the same location), and each taken ride contributes (end − start + tip) dollars to your earnings. Return the greatest total amount of dollars you can earn by choosing rides optimally.

title: Longest Subsequence Repeated k Times
explanation_short: You receive a string `s` and an integer `k`. You must identify the longest string `seq` such that the concatenation of `seq` with itself `k` times appears as a subsequence of `s`; if several have the same maximum length, choose the lexicographically greatest one. Return that subsequence, or an empty string if no such `seq` exists.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Continuous
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. In one operation you may replace any element with any integer you like. The goal is to change as few elements as possible so that, after sorting, the array contains a sequence of consecutive numbers with no gaps (i.e., each value differs from the next by exactly 1). Return the smallest number of replacements required to achieve such a continuous array.

title: Final Value of Variable After Performing Operations
explanation_short: You receive a list of strings, each string being one of the four possible operations on a single variable X (increment or decrement, written as “++X”, “X++”, “--X”, or “X--”). Starting with X equal to 0, you must apply the operations in the given order, updating X each time. After processing the entire list, output the integer value that X ends up with.

title: Sum of Beauty in the Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array and for every position that is not at the ends you must count how many earlier elements are smaller than the current value and how many later elements are larger, then take the smaller of those two counts as the “beauty” of that position; the answer is the sum of all such beauties. A naïve double‑loop would be too slow, so the key is to compute the left‑smaller and right‑larger counts for every index in near‑linear time. This can be done by first compressing the values to a small range and then using a binary indexed (Fenwick) tree to maintain frequencies as you sweep from left to right for the left counts and from right to left for the right counts, finally adding the minima.

title: Detect Squares
explanation_short: You receive a sequence of operations on points in a 2‑D plane: some operations add a new point, and others ask a question about a specific point. For each query point, you must determine how many axis‑aligned squares can be formed where that point serves as one corner and the other three corners are among the points that have been added earlier. The answer to each query is a single integer representing the count of such squares. The input consists of the series of add and query operations, and the output is the list of integers produced by the queries.

title: Grid Game
explanation_short: You are given a 2‑by‑n matrix of non‑negative integers, where each entry tells how many points are at that cell. One robot first travels from the top‑left corner to the bottom‑right corner, moving only right or down, and any points it passes through are removed; then a second robot makes the same kind of trip, trying to collect as many remaining points as possible. Assuming both robots choose optimal routes, return the total points the second robot will collect.

title: Check if Word Can Be Placed In Crossword
explanation_short:
You receive a rectangular grid of characters where each cell is either a lowercase letter, a blank space, or a ‘#’ block, together with a target word string.  
The task is to decide whether the word can occupy a consecutive sequence of empty or matching cells either left‑to‑right, right‑to‑left, top‑to‑bottom, or bottom‑to‑top, without crossing any ‘#’ and without leaving extra letters or blanks adjacent to the placed word.  
All cells that the word covers must either be empty or already contain the same letter in the same position, and the cells immediately before and after the sequence must be either a block or the edge of the board.  
Return **true** if such a placement exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: The Score of Students Solving Math Expression
explanation_short: You are given a string s made of single‑digit numbers, ‘+’, and ‘*’, and an array answers containing the results submitted by n students. First compute the true value of the expression using the normal precedence (multiplication before addition). Then also compute the value obtained if the operators are applied strictly from left to right, ignoring precedence. Each student whose answer matches the true value earns 5 points, each whose answer matches the left‑to‑right value earns 2 points, and all others earn 0; return the total sum of points.

title: Maximum Difference Between Increasing Elements
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
You need to pick two positions `i` and `j` with `i < j` and `nums[i] < nums[j]` and compute the difference `nums[j] – nums[i]`.  
Among all such valid pairs, find the largest possible difference.  
If no pair satisfies the conditions, output `-1`.

title: Maximum Number of Ways to Partition an Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a value `k`. You may optionally replace a single element of `nums` with `k`, or keep the array as it is. After that, you count how many indices can serve as a pivot where the sum of elements on the left side equals the sum on the right side. Return the largest possible count of such pivots.

title: Number of Pairs of Strings With Concatenation Equal to Target
explanation_short:
You are given a list of digit‑only strings `nums` and another digit string `target`.  
Find how many ordered pairs of different positions `(i, j)` satisfy that the string formed by `nums[i]` followed by `nums[j]` is exactly `target`.  
Pairs are counted separately, so `(i, j)` and `(j, i)` are two distinct possibilities when both work.  
Return that total count as an integer.

title: Convert 1D Array Into 2D Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `original` and two integers `m` and `n`. Using all elements of `original` in their original order, you must fill a matrix with exactly `m` rows and `n` columns, where each consecutive block of `n` elements becomes one row. If the total number of elements does not equal `m × n`, the result should be an empty 2‑D array; otherwise, output the constructed `m × n` matrix.

title: Maximize the Confusion of an Exam
explanation_short: You are given a string consisting only of the characters ‘T’ and ‘F’, and an integer k. You may change at most k characters in the string to the opposite answer, and you want to know the longest possible run of identical answers after those changes. Return that maximum length as an integer.

title: Find Missing Observations
explanation_short: You are given a list of the observed dice rolls, an integer mean, and the number n of rolls that went missing. The total of all rolls (the observed ones plus the missing n rolls) must have an average equal to mean. Your task is to determine any set of n values, each between 1 and 6, that makes the overall average exactly mean, or report that it’s impossible. Return those n values as an array, or an empty array if no such set exists.

title: Stone Game IX
explanation_short: You are given an array stones containing the values of n stones. Alice and Bob alternately remove any remaining stone, and after each removal the sum of all taken‑so‑far values is checked; the player who makes this sum divisible by 3 immediately loses. If all stones are removed without the sum ever being a multiple of 3, Bob is declared the winner. Return true if Alice can force a win with optimal play, otherwise return false.

title: Stock Price Fluctuation
explanation_short: You receive a sequence of operations on a stock, each either updating the price at a given timestamp or asking for information about the stock. An update may replace a previous price for the same timestamp, while queries ask for the most recent price, the highest price seen so far, or the lowest price seen so far. Your task is to process these operations in the order they arrive, keeping the data consistent despite out‑of‑order and corrected updates. For each query operation you must return the appropriate price value.

title: Minimum Moves to Convert String
explanation_short:
You receive a string s made only of the characters ‘X’ and ‘O’.  
A move lets you pick any three consecutive positions and turn whatever is there into ‘O’ (already‑‘O’ characters stay unchanged).  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of such moves needed to make every character in the string an ‘O’.  
Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Smallest K-Length Subsequence With Occurrences of a Letter
explanation_short: You are given a string s, an integer k, a specific character letter, and an integer repetition. From s you must select a subsequence that is exactly k characters long and contains the character letter at least repetition times. Among all subsequences satisfying those conditions, you need the one that is lexicographically smallest. Return that subsequence as the answer.

title: Two Out of Three
explanation_short:
You are given three integer arrays.  
Identify every distinct value that occurs in at least two of the three arrays.  
Collect those values into a list (order does not matter).  
Return the list as the output.

title: Minimum Operations to Make a Uni-Value Grid
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of integers and a value x. In each move you may increase or decrease any single cell by exactly x, and you want all cells to end up with the same number. Return the smallest possible number of moves required, or -1 if no common value can be reached.

title: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
explanation_short: You are given two arrays of equal length n: `seats[i]` tells where the i‑th seat is located, and `students[j]` tells where the j‑th student stands. You must pair each student with a different seat so that the sum of the distances each student travels (the number of moves) is as small as possible. Return that minimum total number of moves as a single integer.

title: Remove Colored Pieces if Both Neighbors are the Same Color
explanation_short: You are given a string `colors` containing only ‘A’ and ‘B’, each character representing the color of a piece placed in a line. On a turn a player may delete any piece that is not on an end and whose two adjacent pieces have the same color as the piece itself; the players alternate turns with Alice moving first. Assuming both players choose moves optimally, determine which player will be the first who cannot make a move. Return `true` if Alice can force a win, otherwise return `false`.

title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
explanation_short: You receive an array of 2 × n integers. You must divide the elements into two groups, each containing exactly n numbers. The aim is to make the total of each group as close as possible. Return the minimum achievable absolute difference between the two group sums.

title: Kth Smallest Product of Two Sorted Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays that are already sorted in non‑decreasing order, `nums1` and `nums2`, and an integer `k`. Form every possible product by multiplying one element from `nums1` with one element from `nums2`. Among all these products, identify the one that ranks `k`‑th when they are ordered from smallest to largest. Return that k‑th smallest product as the answer.

title: Simple Bank System
explanation_short: You are given the number of bank accounts and an array containing each account’s initial balance. A list of operations-deposit, withdraw, or transfer between accounts-is then supplied. For each operation you must determine whether it is allowed (for example, a withdrawal or transfer requires sufficient funds) and, if it is, adjust the balances accordingly. After all operations have been processed, output the final balance of every account in order.

title: Second Minimum Time to Reach Destination
explanation_short: You are given the number of vertices n, a list of undirected edges connecting them, the fixed travel time for each edge, and the interval change after which every traffic light switches between green and red. Starting at vertex 1 at time 0, you may enter any vertex at any moment but can only leave when its light is green; you cannot pause at a vertex while the light is green. Your task is to determine the smallest travel time that is strictly larger than the fastest possible time to reach vertex n under these rules. Return that second‑minimum time as a single integer.

title: The Time When the Network Becomes Idle
explanation_short: You are given a list of undirected edges connecting n servers (numbered 0 to n‑1) and an array patience where patience[i] is the resend interval for server i. Server 0 is the master; every other server sends a message to the master at time 0 and, if it hasn’t received a reply by its patience interval, resends the same message repeatedly. All messages travel along the shortest paths, and the master replies instantly along the reverse routes. Return the smallest integer second after which no messages are in transit or arriving at any server.

title: Check if Numbers Are Ascending in a Sentence
explanation_short: You are given a string s that consists of space‑separated tokens, each token being either a positive integer (no leading zeros) or a lowercase word. Scan the tokens from left to right and collect the numbers that appear, then verify that each number is smaller than the one that follows it. Return true if the numbers form a strictly increasing sequence, otherwise return false.

title: Count Number of Maximum Bitwise-OR Subsets
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums`.  
Consider every non‑empty subset of the array (subsets are distinct when they use different indices) and compute the bitwise OR of the elements in each subset.  
First find the greatest possible OR value that any subset can produce.  
Then output the count of subsets whose OR equals that maximum value.

title: Next Greater Numerically Balanced Number
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n. A number is “numerically balanced” when each digit d that appears in it shows up exactly d times in the whole number (for example, 22 has two 2’s). Your task is to locate the smallest such balanced integer that is strictly larger than n. Return that integer as the answer.

title: Count Nodes With the Highest Score
explanation_short: You are given an array parents where parents[i] is the parent of node i in a rooted binary tree (node 0 is the root, so parents[0] = -1). For each node, imagine removing it and all incident edges; the remaining pieces form one or more non‑empty subtrees, and the node’s score is the product of the sizes of those subtrees. Your task is to determine which nodes achieve the maximum possible score and count how many such nodes exist. Return that count as the answer.

title: Parallel Courses III
explanation_short: You are given an integer n for the number of courses, a list of prerequisite pairs relations where each pair [prev, next] means course prev must finish before course next can start, and an array time where time[i] is the months required to complete course i + 1. Courses may be taken simultaneously as long as all their prerequisites are satisfied. Your task is to determine the smallest possible total number of months needed to finish every course while respecting the prerequisite constraints. Return that minimum time as a single integer.

title: Number of Valid Words in a Sentence
explanation_short: You are given a single string that may contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, punctuation marks (!, ., ,) and spaces. The string is split into tokens wherever one or more spaces appear. A token counts as a valid word only if it meets all of the specified character‑placement rules (no digits, at most one hyphen in the middle, punctuation only at the end, etc.). Return the total number of tokens that satisfy those conditions as an integer.

title: Plates Between Candles
explanation_short: You receive a string s made of ‘*’ (plates) and ‘|’ (candles) and an array of queries, each query giving a left and right index that defines a substring of s. Within a query’s substring, a plate counts only if there is at least one candle somewhere to its left and at least one candle somewhere to its right inside that same substring. For every query you must determine how many plates satisfy this condition. Return an array where the i‑th element is the count for the i‑th query.

title: Kth Distinct String in an Array
explanation_short: You are given a list of strings `arr` and an integer `k`. First, consider only those strings that occur exactly once in the list, keeping them in the same order they appear. Return the `k`‑th string from this filtered sequence, or an empty string `""` if fewer than `k` distinct strings exist.

title: Two Best Non-Overlapping Events
explanation_short: You receive a list of events, each described by a start time, an end time, and a value you earn by attending it. You may choose up to two events, but the second one must start strictly after the first one ends (no shared endpoints). Your task is to select the combination that yields the highest total value. Output that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Number of Valid Move Combinations On Chessboard
explanation_short: You are given two arrays of equal length n: `pieces[i]` tells whether the i‑th piece is a rook, queen or bishop, and `positions[i] = [r_i, c_i]` gives its starting square on an 8 × 8 board. For each piece you must pick a destination square (different from its start) and then imagine all pieces moving one step toward their destinations each second, beginning at time 0. A move combination is valid only if at no moment do two or more pieces occupy the same square while they travel. Return the total number of valid combinations of destinations.

title: Check if an Original String Exists Given Two Encoded Strings
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s1` and `s2` that contain lowercase letters and digits 1‑9. Each string may represent a compressed form of some original lowercase word, where any contiguous block of letters can be replaced by the number of characters in that block. Your task is to determine whether there exists at least one original word that could be compressed to match both `s1` and `s2`. Return **true** if such a word exists, otherwise return **false**.

title: Find the Minimum and Maximum Number of Nodes Between Critical Points
explanation_short: You are given the head of a singly‑linked list whose node values are integers. Identify every node that is a local maximum (greater than both its neighbors) or a local minimum (smaller than both neighbors), then measure the number of nodes between each pair of distinct critical points. Return a two‑element array [minimum distance, maximum distance]; if fewer than two critical points exist, return [-1, -1].

title: Vowels of All Substrings
