explanation_short: You are given a string `word`. For each non‑empty contiguous substring of `word`, count how many characters are vowels (a, e, i, o, u). Add up those vowel counts across all possible substrings. Output the resulting sum as an integer (it may exceed 32‑bit range).

title: Maximum Path Quality of a Graph
explanation_short: You are given an array values where values[i] is the score of node i, a list edges describing undirected connections with travel times, and a limit maxTime. A valid route must start and finish at node 0, may revisit nodes, and its total travel time cannot exceed maxTime. The quality of a route is the sum of the scores of the distinct nodes that appear on that route (each node counted at most once). Return the largest possible quality among all valid routes.

title: Smallest Index With Equal Value
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. Your task is to locate the smallest index `i` such that the remainder of `i` divided by 10 equals `nums[i]`. Return that index, or ‑1 if no such position exists.

title: Minimum Operations to Convert Number
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` of distinct integers, a starting value `start`, and a target value `goal`. Beginning with `x = start`, you may repeatedly pick any element `v` from `nums` and replace `x` by `x + v` or `x – v`, but each intermediate value must stay within the range 0 to 1000 (the final step may leave this range). Your task is to determine the smallest number of such operations that makes `x` equal to `goal`. If no sequence of allowed moves can reach `goal`, you should report -1. The output is this minimum count (or -1).

title: Check Whether Two Strings are Almost Equivalent
explanation_short: You are given two strings `word1` and `word2`, each of the same length. For every letter from ‘a’ to ‘z’, compute how many times it appears in each string and compare the two counts. Return **true** if the absolute difference for every letter is at most 3; otherwise return **false**.

title: Count Vowel Substrings of a String
explanation_short:
You are given one string `word`.  
Consider every non‑empty contiguous segment of this string; a segment is a vowel substring if it contains only the letters a, e, i, o, u and each of those five vowels appears at least once.  
Your task is to determine how many such vowel substrings exist in `word`.  
Output the total count as an integer.

title: Maximum Number of Tasks You Can Assign
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays tasks and workers, plus two integers pills and strength. Each task requires a minimum worker strength, and each worker can take at most one pill that adds strength to their ability; you have only pills such boosts available. Choose assignments (and which workers receive pills) so that as many tasks as possible are completed, and output that maximum number.

title: Walking Robot Simulation II
explanation_short: You are given the grid dimensions `width` × `height`, a list of blocked cells (obstacles), and a sequence of commands where a positive number means “move forward that many steps”, `-1` means “turn right 90°”, and `-2` means “turn left 90°”. The robot starts at cell (0, 0) facing East and must obey each command step‑by‑step, never leaving the grid or entering an obstacle cell (such a step is simply ignored). After all commands are processed, report the robot’s final coordinates as a two‑element array [x, y].

title: Most Beautiful Item for Each Query
explanation_short: You receive a list where each entry gives an item’s price and its beauty, plus an array of query values. For every query you must report the highest beauty among all items whose price does not exceed that query (or 0 if none qualify). Return an array containing these maximum beauties in the same order as the queries.

title: Minimized Maximum of Products Distributed to Any Store
explanation_short: You are given the number of stores `n` and an array `quantities` where `quantities[i]` tells how many items of product type `i` exist. All items must be split among the `n` stores, and each store can receive items of only one type (a type may be divided among many stores). Your task is to arrange the distribution so that the largest number of items assigned to any single store is as small as possible. Return that smallest achievable maximum value.

title: Time Needed to Buy Tickets
explanation_short: You are given an array `tickets` where `tickets[i]` tells how many tickets the i‑th person in the line wants, and an index `k` indicating the person of interest. Each second the person at the front buys one ticket, then (if they still need more) moves instantly to the back of the line; anyone who has bought all their tickets leaves the line. You must determine how many seconds pass until the person originally at position `k` has bought all of their tickets. The answer is a single integer representing that total time.

title: Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups
explanation_short: You are given the head of a singly‑linked list. The nodes are divided sequentially into groups whose sizes follow 1, 2, 3, 4, … (the final group may be shorter). For every group that contains an even number of nodes, the nodes inside that group must be reversed, while odd‑length groups stay unchanged. Return the head of the list after all required reversals.

title: Decode the Slanted Ciphertext
explanation_short: You are given a string encodedText that was created by writing an unknown originalText into a matrix with a fixed number of rows, filling the cells along diagonal “slanted” lines, then reading the matrix row‑by‑row. The number of rows rows used for the matrix is also provided. Your task is to reconstruct the originalText that was placed in the matrix before the encoding step. The answer must be the exact original string, without any trailing spaces.

title: Watering Plants
explanation_short: You are given an array plants where plants[i] is the amount of water the i‑th plant needs, and an integer capacity that is the maximum water the can can hold. Starting at the river located at x = –1, you walk along the line of plants, water each one in order, and may have to return to the river to refill whenever the remaining water is insufficient for the next plant. Each unit of movement along the x‑axis counts as one step. Return the total number of steps required to water every plant.

title: Process Restricted Friend Requests
explanation_short: You are given the number of people n, a list of pairs that must never end up in the same friendship group, and a sequence of friend‑request pairs. Initially nobody is connected, and each request is handled one after another. A request is accepted only if linking the two people would not make any forbidden pair become connected through the friendship network (directly or indirectly). Return an array of true/false values showing which requests succeed.

title: Sum of k-Mirror Numbers
explanation_short: You are given two integers k (≥2) and n. A k‑mirror number is a positive integer that reads the same forward and backward when written in base 10 and also when written in base k, without any leading zeros. Your task is to identify the n smallest such numbers and add them together. Return the resulting sum as a single integer.

title: Two Furthest Houses With Different Colors
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array where each element denotes the color of a house on a street. From all pairs of houses that have different colors, consider the distance defined as the absolute difference of their indices. Find the greatest such distance among those pairs. Output that maximum distance as a single integer.

title: Range Frequency Queries
explanation_short: You are given an initial array of integers. Afterwards a series of queries arrives, each specifying three numbers: `left`, `right` (the inclusive bounds of a subarray) and a target value `val`. For every query you must determine how many times `val` appears inside the subarray `arr[left…right]`. The answer for each query is output as a single integer.

title: Minimum Number of Food Buckets to Feed the Hamsters
explanation_short: You are given a string where each character is either a hamster (represented by ‘H’) or an empty spot (represented by ‘.’). You may put food buckets only on empty spots, and a hamster is considered fed if there is at least one bucket directly to its left or right. Your task is to determine the smallest number of buckets needed to feed every hamster, or return -1 if no arrangement can achieve this. The output is a single integer representing that minimum count (or -1 when impossible).

title: Count Fertile Pyramids in a Land
explanation_short: You are given an m × n binary matrix where 1 means a fertile cell and 0 means barren (cells outside the matrix are also barren). A pyramidal plot consists of consecutive rows of fertile cells that form a triangle whose width grows by two cells each lower row, and an inverse pyramidal plot is the same shape upside‑down. You must count every distinct pyramid and inverse pyramid that can be placed entirely within the grid using only fertile cells. Return the total number of such plots as a single integer.

title: K Radius Subarray Averages
explanation_short:
You receive a zero‑indexed integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.  
For each index `i`, look at the segment from `i‑k` to `i+k`; if the segment extends beyond the array bounds, the result for that position is `-1`.  
Otherwise, compute the average of all elements in that segment using integer division (discarding any fractional part).  
Return an array of length `n` where each entry holds the computed average or `-1` as described.

title: Count Common Words With One Occurrence
explanation_short: You are given two arrays of strings, words1 and words2. Find how many different strings show up exactly once in words1 and also exactly once in words2. If a string appears multiple times in either array or is absent from one of them, it is ignored. Output the total count as an integer.

title: Find Target Indices After Sorting Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a single integer `target`. First, imagine the array sorted in non‑decreasing order. Then identify every position `i` where the sorted array’s value equals `target`. Return those positions as a list in increasing order (or an empty list if the target never appears).

title: Finding 3-Digit Even Numbers
explanation_short: You are given an array of single‑digit numbers, which may contain repeats. Using each digit at most as many times as it appears, you must form every possible three‑digit integer that is even and does not start with zero. Collect each distinct integer that meets these rules, then sort them in increasing order. The output is the sorted list of those integers.

title: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
explanation_short:
You are given the head of a singly‑linked list.  
Identify the node whose 0‑based index equals ⌊n / 2⌋, where n is the number of nodes, and remove that node from the list.  
All other nodes must stay linked in their original order.  
Return the head of the list after the removal (or null if the list becomes empty).

title: Removing Minimum and Maximum From Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed array containing distinct integers. Identify the positions of the smallest and the largest values in the array. You may delete elements only from the front or the back, and you need to remove both the minimum and maximum elements using the fewest deletions possible. Return that minimum number of deletions as an integer.

title: Minimum Cost Homecoming of a Robot in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given the size of a grid (implicitly by the lengths of rowCosts and colCosts), a starting cell [startrow, startcol], a target home cell [homerow, homecol], and two arrays that assign a cost to each row and each column. The robot may move one step up, down, left, or right, paying the row cost when it changes rows and the column cost when it changes columns, and it cannot leave the grid. Return the smallest possible total cost needed for the robot to reach its home cell.

title: Find All People With Secret
explanation_short: You are given the number of people n, a list of meetings where each entry contains two participants and the time the meeting occurs, and an index firstPerson. Person 0 starts with the secret and immediately tells firstPerson at time 0. Whenever a meeting happens, any participant who already knows the secret at that exact time will instantly pass it to the other participant, and this can cascade within the same time stamp. Return all person indices that end up knowing the secret after processing every meeting.

title: Find Subsequence of Length K With the Largest Sum
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.  
Your task is to pick exactly `k` elements from the array, keeping their original order, so that the sum of the chosen elements is as large as possible.  
The chosen elements form a subsequence, meaning you may skip any elements you don’t need but cannot rearrange the remaining ones.  
Return the resulting subsequence as an array of length `k`.

title: Find Good Days to Rob the Bank
explanation_short: You are given an array security where each element tells how many guards are on duty on that day, and an integer time. For each day i, you must check whether the time days leading up to i show a never‑increasing sequence of guard counts and the time days after i show a never‑decreasing sequence. All days that satisfy both conditions are considered good days to rob the bank. Return the list of indices of those good days in increasing order.

title: Step-By-Step Directions From a Binary Tree Node to Another
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree where each node has a unique integer label, together with two distinct labels `startValue` and `destValue`. Starting from the node whose label equals `startValue`, you must travel to the node whose label equals `destValue` using the fewest possible moves. Each move is described by a single character: ‘L’ for moving to a left child, ‘R’ for moving to a right child, and ‘U’ for moving up to the parent. Return a string composed of these characters that represents the shortest route from the start node to the destination node.

title: Valid Arrangement of Pairs
explanation_short:
You are given a list of integer pairs, each representing a directed edge from a start value to an end value.  
Your task is to reorder the entire list so that for every consecutive pair in the new order, the end value of the earlier pair equals the start value of the later pair.  
If such an ordering exists, you must return one valid arrangement; otherwise, no output is required.  
The result should be the reordered list of pairs that satisfies the chaining condition.

title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. For each non‑empty contiguous segment of the array, find the difference between its largest and smallest element, which is called the range of that subarray. Add up the ranges of all possible subarrays. The result you return is a single integer representing this total sum. Single‑element subarrays contribute zero because their max and min are equal.

title: Maximum Fruits Harvested After at Most K Steps
explanation_short: You are given a sorted list of positions on a line, each with a certain number of fruits, together with a starting coordinate and a maximum number of steps k. From any point you may move left or right, spending one step per unit distance, but the total distance traveled cannot exceed k. Whenever you arrive at a position you collect all its fruits, which then disappear. The task is to compute the greatest total amount of fruit you can gather within the allowed steps.

title: Detonate the Maximum Bombs
explanation_short: You receive a list where each entry gives a bomb’s x‑coordinate, y‑coordinate, and blast radius. Starting from any single bomb, its explosion triggers every bomb whose center lies inside its circular range, and those newly exploded bombs can trigger others in the same way. Your task is to determine the largest possible count of bombs that can be detonated by choosing the best initial bomb. Return that maximum count as an integer.

title: Sequentially Ordinal Rank Tracker
explanation_short: You receive a series of commands, each either adding a new location (given its unique name and integer attractiveness score) or asking for the name of the location that currently ranks k‑th among all added locations. Rankings are determined first by higher scores, and when scores tie, by the lexicographically smaller name. After each query command you must output the name of the requested k‑th best location. The system starts empty, and the total number of queries never exceeds the number of locations that have been added so far.

title: Rings and Rods
explanation_short: You receive a single string where every two characters form a pair: the first character is the ring’s color (R, G, or B) and the second character is the rod number (0‑9) it sits on. Each pair represents one ring, and many rings can share the same rod. Your task is to determine how many rods contain at least one red, one green, and one blue ring. Return that count as an integer.

title: Adding Spaces to a String
explanation_short: You receive a string `s` and an integer array `spaces` that lists positions in the original string. For each index in `spaces`, a blank space must be placed right before the character that originally occupies that index. After all insertions are performed, the characters keep their original order, just separated by the new spaces. Return the final string with all the added spaces.

title: Watering Plants II
explanation_short: You are given an array plants where plants[i] is the amount of water the i‑th plant needs, and two integers capacityA and capacityB that are the initial amounts of water in Alice’s and Bob’s cans. Starting from the left, Alice waters plants moving rightward, while Bob starts from the right and waters plants moving leftward, each using water from their own can. Whenever a person does not have enough water for the next plant they must refill their can, and you must count how many such refills occur in total. Return that total number of refills as a single integer.

title: Find First Palindromic String in the Array
explanation_short: You receive an array of words as the input. Your task is to locate the earliest element that reads identically from left to right and right to left. Return that word; if no word satisfies the condition, return an empty string.

title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array K-Increasing
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers arr and a positive integer k. An array is K‑increasing when every element is at least as large as the element k positions before it (i.e., for all i ≥ k, arr[i‑k] ≤ arr[i]). You may change any element to any value, and each change counts as one operation. The task is to determine the smallest possible number of operations needed to turn the given array into a K‑increasing one, and output that minimum count.

title: Maximum Number of Words Found in Sentences
explanation_short: You are given an array of strings where each string is a sentence composed of words separated by single spaces and without leading or trailing spaces. For each sentence, count how many words it contains. Identify the greatest word count among all the sentences. Return that maximum count as an integer.

title: Number of Smooth Descent Periods of a Stock
explanation_short: You are given an integer array prices where each element is the stock price on a particular day. A smooth descent period is any contiguous block of days whose prices drop by exactly 1 each day (a single day counts as a valid period). Your task is to determine how many of these periods appear anywhere in the array. Return that total as a single integer.

title: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
explanation_short: You are given three arrays: a list of recipe names, a matching list where each entry contains the ingredients required for that recipe, and a list of supplies you already possess. A recipe can be prepared when every ingredient in its list is either an initial supply or a recipe you have already prepared. Recipes you create may be reused as ingredients for other recipes, and you have unlimited copies of the initial supplies. Output all recipe names that can be made, in any order.

title: Check if a Parentheses String Can Be Valid
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length strings: `s`, made of '(' and ')', and `locked`, made of '0' and '1'. Characters at positions where `locked` is '1' must stay as they are, while those where `locked` is '0' may be changed to either '(' or ')'. Your task is to decide whether it is possible to adjust the changeable characters so that the entire `s` becomes a valid parentheses string. Return **true** if such a transformation exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: Execution of All Suffix Instructions Staying in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given the size n of an n × n grid, a starting cell (startrow, startcol), and a string s of moves (‘L’, ‘R’, ‘U’, ‘D’). For each index i in s, imagine the robot begins executing the suffix s[i…] from the start cell and stops as soon as a move would take it outside the grid. Return an array where the i‑th element is the number of moves the robot can successfully perform for that suffix.

title: Abbreviating the Product of a Range
explanation_short: You receive two positive integers `left` and `right`. First compute the product of every integer from `left` through `right` (inclusive). Then delete all trailing zeros from that product, count how many zeros were removed, and write the remaining digits followed by the letter `e` and the count of removed zeros; if the remaining part has more than ten digits, keep only its first ten digits before the `e`. The result is returned as a string.

title: A Number After a Double Reversal
explanation_short: You receive a single integer `num`. First you reverse the order of its decimal digits, then you reverse the digits of that result again. Return **true** if the final number is exactly the original `num`; otherwise return **false**.

title: Destroying Asteroids
explanation_short: You receive a starting planet mass (an integer) and a list of asteroid masses (an integer array). You may choose any order to let the planet collide with the asteroids; each time the planet’s mass is at least the asteroid’s mass, the asteroid is destroyed and its mass is added to the planet, otherwise the planet is destroyed. Return **true** if there is some ordering that lets the planet eliminate every asteroid, and **false** otherwise.

title: Intervals Between Identical Elements
explanation_short:
You receive a 0‑indexed array `arr` of integers.  
For each index `i`, consider every other index `j` where `arr[j]` equals `arr[i]` and take the absolute difference `|i‑j|`.  
The task is to compute, for every position, the total of those differences.  
Return an array `intervals` where `intervals[i]` holds this sum for index `i`.

title: Recover the Original Array
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` containing `2 n` positive integers, which is the combined multiset of two hidden arrays `lower` and `higher`. Each element of the original array `arr` of length `n` produced a pair `arr[i] - k` and `arr[i] + k` for the same unknown positive integer `k`, one value ending up in `lower` and the other in `higher`. Your task is to determine any possible `arr` that could generate the given `nums` under some positive `k`. Return the recovered `arr` as a list of `n` integers.

title: Check if All A's Appears Before All B's
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` that contains only the letters ‘a’ and ‘b’.  
Your task is to check whether every occurrence of ‘a’ comes earlier in the string than any occurrence of ‘b’.  
If that condition holds, the result should be `true`; otherwise it should be `false`.  
Return the Boolean value that reflects this check.

title: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List
explanation_short: You are given the head of a singly‑linked list that contains an even number of nodes. For each node, its “twin” is the node that is the same distance from the opposite end of the list, and you must compute the sum of each twin pair. Return the largest of those twin sums as a single integer.

title: Capitalize the Title
explanation_short: You receive a single string `title` that contains one or more words separated by spaces. For each word you must adjust its letters: words of length three or more should have their first character in uppercase and the rest in lowercase, while words of length two or less should be entirely lowercase. Return the resulting string after applying these rules to every word.

title: Maximum Employees to Be Invited to a Meeting
explanation_short: You are given an array favorite where favorite[i] is the index of employee i’s favorite colleague (never i itself). You must choose a largest possible subset of employees and arrange them around a circular table so that every chosen employee sits directly next to their favorite person. Return the size of that largest feasible subset.

title: Number of Laser Beams in a Bank
explanation_short: You receive a list of equal‑length strings where each character is ‘0’ (empty) or ‘1’ (a security device) and each string represents one row of the bank’s floor plan. A laser beam can be drawn between two devices that lie in different rows only if there is no row containing a device between those two rows. Your task is to count how many such beams exist across the whole floor plan. Return that count as an integer.

title: Minimum Swaps to Group All 1's Together II
explanation_short: You are given a circular array that contains only 0’s and 1’s. A swap means picking any two different positions and exchanging their values. Your task is to determine the smallest number of such swaps needed so that all the 1’s appear consecutively somewhere in the circle (the block may wrap around the ends). Return that minimum swap count as an integer.

title: Longest Palindrome by Concatenating Two Letter Words
explanation_short: You receive an array where each element is a two‑letter lowercase word. Choose any subset of these words, use each at most once, and order them so that their concatenation reads the same forward and backward. Return the length of the longest such palindrome you can build, or 0 if no palindrome can be formed.

title: Earliest Possible Day of Full Bloom
explanation_short: You are given two arrays of length n: plantTime[i] is the number of days needed to plant seed i, and growTime[i] is the number of days it takes that seed to grow after it has been planted. Starting from day 0 you may plant seeds one per day in any order you like. Choose an ordering that makes the latest bloom happen as early as possible. Return the earliest day on which all seeds have finished growing and are blooming.

title: Stamping the Grid
explanation_short: You receive an m × n binary matrix grid where 1 means occupied and 0 means empty, together with two integers stampHeight and stampWidth. The task is to decide whether you can place any number of rectangular stamps of the given size inside the grid so that every 0 cell is covered by at least one stamp, while no stamp overlaps a 1 cell or extends beyond the matrix borders (stamps may overlap each other). Return true if such a placement exists; otherwise return false.

title: Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers
explanation_short:
You receive an n × n matrix of integers.  
Your task is to verify that every row and every column includes each number from 1 through n.  
If this condition is satisfied for the whole matrix, the answer is true; otherwise it is false.  
The output is a single boolean value indicating whether the matrix is valid.

title: Divide a String Into Groups of Size k
explanation_short: You are given a string `s`, an integer `k`, and a single fill character. Split the string into consecutive pieces each containing exactly `k` characters; if the last piece is shorter, pad it with the fill character until its length reaches `k`. Return the list of all pieces in order as a string array.

title: Solving Questions With Brainpower
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element contains two numbers: the points earned for solving that question and how many subsequent questions you must skip afterward. Starting from the first question, you may either solve it (collect its points and skip the indicated number of next questions) or skip it and consider the following one. Your task is to choose a combination of solves and skips that yields the highest total points possible. Return that maximum total as a single integer.

title: Count Words Obtained After Adding a Letter
explanation_short: You receive two lists of lowercase strings: `startWords` and `targetWords`. For each word in `targetWords` you must determine whether some word in `startWords` can become it after adding exactly one new letter and then permuting the letters arbitrarily. Return the total number of `targetWords` that meet this condition.

title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers where each value is the price of a candy. You may buy any two candies and then pick a third candy for free, as long as the free candy’s price does not exceed the cheaper of the two you paid for. Your task is to choose how to form these groups so that every candy is obtained while spending the least amount of money. Output the minimum total cost required to get all the candies.

title: Minimum Moves to Reach Target Score
explanation_short: You are given two integers `target` and `maxDoubles`. Starting from the value 1, you may add 1 any number of times, but you can apply the “double” operation at most `maxDoubles` times. Your task is to determine the smallest total number of moves (increments plus doubles) required to reach exactly `target`. Return that minimum count as the answer.

title: Count the Hidden Sequences
explanation_short:
You receive an array differences of length n and two integers lower and upper.  
A hidden sequence of length n + 1 must satisfy differences[i] = hidden[i+1] – hidden[i] for every i.  
Count how many possible choices for the first element make the entire sequence stay inside the inclusive range [lower, upper].  
Return that count (or 0 if no such sequence exists).

title: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and an array batteries where each element tells how many minutes that battery can power a computer. You may place at most one battery in each of the n computers at any time, and you can swap batteries instantly at integer minutes. The task is to determine the greatest number of whole minutes during which all n computers can stay powered using any sequence of swaps. Return that maximum duration as a single integer.

title: Number of Ways to Divide a Long Corridor
explanation_short: You are given a string corridor containing only the characters ‘S’ (seat) and ‘P’ (plant). Between any two consecutive positions you may optionally place a room divider, and there are already fixed dividers at the very left and right ends. Your task is to count how many different choices of additional dividers result in every contiguous segment having exactly two ‘S’ characters. Output that count as an integer.

title: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
explanation_short:
You are given an even‑length array that contains the same number of positive and negative integers.  
Your task is to reorder the elements so that every even index holds a positive number and every odd index holds a negative number, while keeping the original relative order of the positives among themselves and of the negatives among themselves.  
Return the resulting array after this rearrangement.

title: Find All Lonely Numbers in the Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. Identify each value that occurs only once **and** whose two neighboring integers (the value minus 1 and the value plus 1) do not appear anywhere in the array. Return a list containing all such “lonely” numbers; the order of the returned elements does not matter.

title: K Highest Ranked Items Within a Price Range
explanation_short: You are given a 2‑D integer grid, a price interval [low, high], a starting cell (row, col) and an integer k. From the start you can move one step at a time to orthogonal neighbours, and you only consider cells whose value lies inside the given price interval. Among all reachable cells in that interval you must pick up to k positions, ordered first by shortest distance from the start, then by lower price, then by smaller row index, and finally by smaller column index. Return the selected coordinates as a list, sorted from the highest‑ranked to the lowest‑ranked item.

title: Count Elements With Strictly Smaller and Greater Elements
explanation_short: The input is an integer array `nums`. You must determine how many elements in the array have at least one other element that is strictly smaller and at least one other element that is strictly larger than them. The output is a single integer giving that count.

title: Find Substring With Given Hash Value
explanation_short: You are given a lowercase string `s` and four integers: `power`, `modulo`, the required length `k`, and a target hash value `hashValue`. For every contiguous substring of `s` that has exactly `k` characters, compute its hash by weighting each character’s alphabet index with successive powers of `power` and taking the result modulo `modulo`. Return the earliest (leftmost) substring whose hash equals `hashValue`.

title: Maximum Good People Based on Statements
explanation_short: You are given an n × n matrix statements where statements[i][j] is 0 if person i claims j is bad, 1 if i claims j is good, and 2 if i makes no claim (the diagonal entries are always 2). A person who is good must tell the truth in all of their statements, while a bad person may either lie or tell the truth. Your task is to decide which assignments of good/bad to the n people are logically possible and return the largest number of people that can be good in any such assignment. The output is a single integer representing that maximum possible count.

title: Groups of Strings
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed array `words` where each element is a lowercase string with no repeated letters. Two strings are considered connected if you can turn the set of letters of one into the other by adding, deleting, or replacing exactly one letter. Your task is to split the array into the smallest possible collection of non‑overlapping groups so that no string in a group is connected to any string in a different group; this partition is guaranteed to be unique. Return a two‑element array where the first value is the total number of groups and the second value is the size of the largest group.

title: Keep Multiplying Found Values by Two
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums` and a starting integer `original`. Starting with `original`, you repeatedly look for the current value in `nums`; each time it is found you double the value and continue the search. The process stops when the current value is not present in the array, and that final value is returned as the answer.

title: All Divisions With the Highest Score of a Binary Array
explanation_short: You are given a binary array `nums` of length `n`. For any division index `i` (0 ≤ i ≤ n) the array is split into a left part containing the first `i` elements and a right part containing the rest. The division’s score equals the count of 0’s in the left part plus the count of 1’s in the right part. Return all indices `i` whose score is maximal; the result should be a list of those indices.

title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` and an integer `pivot`. Rearrange the array so that every element smaller than `pivot` comes before any element larger than `pivot`, while elements equal to `pivot` may appear anywhere in between. The original relative order of the “less‑than” group and the “greater‑than” group must be preserved. Return the array after this rearrangement.

title: Minimum Cost to Set Cooking Time
explanation_short:
You are given four integers: `startAt` (the digit where your finger begins), `moveCost` (fatigue for moving to a different digit), `pushCost` (fatigue for pressing a digit), and `targetSeconds` (the cooking time you need, in seconds).  
You may press at most four digits; the microwave pads the sequence with leading zeros to length four, treats the first two digits as minutes and the last two as seconds, and converts that to total seconds.  
Among all digit sequences that evaluate to exactly `targetSeconds`, you must determine the one that incurs the smallest total fatigue, counting a move cost each time the finger changes digits and a push cost for each pressed digit.  
Return that minimum total cost as an integer.

title: Minimum Difference in Sums After Removal of Elements
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` whose length equals `3 × n` for some integer `n`. You may delete exactly `n` elements, leaving `2 × n` elements that are then divided into two consecutive halves of size `n` each. Compute the difference `sum(first half) - sum(second half)` for the remaining array. Return the minimum possible value of this difference over all ways of removing `n` elements.

title: Minimum Sum of Four Digit Number After Splitting Digits
explanation_short: You are given a positive integer that has exactly four digits. Using each of those digits once, you must form two new integers (they may have leading zeros). Choose the arrangement that makes the sum of the two new integers as small as possible. Output that minimum possible sum.

title: Minimum Time to Remove All Cars Containing Illegal Goods
explanation_short: You are given a binary string s where each character represents a train car, with ‘1’ meaning the car contains illegal goods. You may repeatedly either delete the leftmost car (cost 1), delete the rightmost car (cost 1), or delete a single car that contains illegal goods from anywhere in the train (cost 2). Your task is to choose a sequence of such deletions that eliminates every ‘1’ in the string while minimizing the total cost. Output the smallest possible total cost as an integer.

title: Count Operations to Obtain Zero
explanation_short: You are given two non‑negative integers, num1 and num2. Repeatedly compare them: if num1 ≥ num2 subtract num2 from num1; otherwise subtract num1 from num2. Keep a tally of how many subtractions occur until either number reaches zero. Return that tally as the answer.

title: Sort Even and Odd Indices Independently
explanation_short:
You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
First, the values located at odd indices must be sorted in one order, while the values at even indices are sorted in the opposite order.  
After each group is sorted, the numbers are placed back into their original parity positions.  
The output is the array after this rearrangement.

title: Smallest Value of the Rearranged Number
explanation_short: You receive a single integer `num`, which may be positive, zero, or negative. Rearrange the digits of `num`-keeping the sign unchanged-so that the resulting number is as small as possible while avoiding any leading zeros. Return that minimal rearranged integer.

title: Design Bitset
explanation_short: You are given a sequence of commands, each possibly followed by an integer argument, that operate on a binary array of a fixed size. The commands include setting a specific bit to 1, clearing a bit to 0, flipping all bits, checking whether all or any bits are 1, counting how many bits are 1, and returning the whole array as a string of ‘0’s and ‘1’s. Your task is to process the commands in order, updating the bitset accordingly, and produce the results for the query‑type commands. The output is a list of the returned boolean or integer values and the final string representation, in the same order they were requested.

title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array Alternating
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` of positive integers.  
You may pick any position and replace its value with any positive integer you like, and you want to do this as few times as possible so that every pair of neighboring elements becomes different (i.e., the array is alternating).  
The task is to compute the smallest number of such replacements needed.  
Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Removing Minimum Number of Magic Beans
explanation_short: You are given an array beans where each element tells how many magic beans are in a bag. You may take away any number of beans from each bag (including none), but you cannot add beans back, and after removals every bag that still contains beans must have the same count. Compute and return the smallest total number of beans that must be removed to achieve this condition.

title: Count Equal and Divisible Pairs in an Array
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`.  
Count how many index pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` satisfy two conditions: the two array elements are equal (`nums[i] == nums[j]`) and the product of their indices (`i * j`) is a multiple of `k`.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Find Three Consecutive Integers That Sum to a Given Number
explanation_short:
You are given a single integer `num`.  
Your task is to determine whether `num` can be written as the sum of three consecutive integers, and if so, identify those three numbers in increasing order.  
If such a triple exists, return it as a three‑element array; otherwise return an empty array.  
The output therefore is either the sorted triple that adds up to `num` or `[]` when no such representation is possible.

title: Maximum AND Sum of Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a value `numSlots`. Each slot is numbered from 1 to `numSlots` and may hold at most two numbers; you must place every element of `nums` into some slot. Compute the largest possible total of `(number AND slotNumber)` over all placements and return that maximum sum.

title: Maximum Split of Positive Even Integers
explanation_short: You receive a single integer finalSum. Your task is to break it into a collection of different positive even numbers whose sum equals finalSum, choosing the collection that contains as many numbers as possible. Return those numbers in any order; if no such collection exists, return an empty list.

title: Merge Nodes in Between Zeros
explanation_short: You are given the head of a singly‑linked list whose nodes start and end with a value 0, and every 0 separates a group of positive integers. For each group of nodes that lies between two consecutive zeros, you must replace the whole group with a single node whose value equals the sum of that group, and discard all zero‑valued nodes. Return the head of the resulting list, which contains only the summed values.

title: Construct String With Repeat Limit
explanation_short:
You are given a string s and an integer repeatLimit.  
Using the letters of s (you may leave some unused), build a new string where no character occurs more than repeatLimit times in a row.  
Among all strings that satisfy this rule, choose the one that is lexicographically largest.  
Return that string as the answer.

title: Count Good Triplets in an Array
explanation_short:
You are given two length‑\(n\) arrays, each a permutation of the numbers 0 to \(n-1\).  
For any three different values \(x, y, z\), look at their positions in the first array and require that the index of \(x\) is before \(y\) and the index of \(y\) is before \(z\).  
The same ordering must also hold for their positions in the second array.  
Count how many triples satisfy both ordering conditions and output that count as a single integer.

title: Count Integers With Even Digit Sum
explanation_short:
You are given a single positive integer `num`.  
Consider every positive integer from 1 up to `num` and compute the sum of its digits.  
Count how many of those numbers have an even digit sum.  
Return that count as the answer.

title: Count Array Pairs Divisible by K
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.  
Count how many unordered index pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` have the property that the product `nums[i] × nums[j]` is a multiple of `k`.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Counting Words With a Given Prefix
explanation_short: You receive a list of words and a separate string pref. Your task is to determine how many of the words begin with pref, meaning the prefix matches the first characters of the word. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Minimum Number of Steps to Make Two Strings Anagram II
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s` and `t`. In each step you may append a single character to either string, and each appended character counts as one step. The task is to determine the fewest total steps required so that the two strings end up containing exactly the same multiset of characters (i.e., become anagrams of each other). Output that minimum number of steps.

title: Sort the Jumbled Numbers
explanation_short: You receive a length‑10 array `mapping` that tells how each digit 0‑9 should be changed, and an integer array `nums`. For each number in `nums`, replace every digit d with `mapping[d]`, drop any leading zeros, and treat the result as the number’s “mapped value”. Sort `nums` in non‑decreasing order of these mapped values, keeping the original relative order for numbers that share the same mapped value, and output the reordered list.

title: All Ancestors of a Node in a Directed Acyclic Graph
explanation_short:
You are given the number of vertices n in a directed acyclic graph and a list of edges, each edge written as [from, to].  
For every vertex i you must collect all other vertices that can reach i by following one‑or‑more directed edges.  
The ancestors for each vertex should be placed in ascending order.  
Return a single array where the i‑th entry is the sorted list of ancestors of vertex i.

title: Minimum Time to Complete Trips
explanation_short: You receive an array `time` where each element tells how long a particular bus needs for one trip, and an integer `totalTrips` indicating how many trips must be finished altogether. For any moment `t`, each bus can complete `⌊t / time[i]⌋` trips, and the buses work independently. Your task is to determine the smallest value of `t` for which the sum of these completed trips across all buses reaches at least `totalTrips`. Return that minimum time as a single integer.

title: Minimum Time to Finish the Race
explanation_short: You are given a list of tire types, each described by two numbers \(f_i\) and \(r_i\); using the same tire for its \(x\)‑th consecutive lap costs \(f_i \times r_i^{\,x-1}\) seconds. You also receive the fixed time needed to switch tires, `changeTime`, and the total number of laps, `numLaps`. Starting with any tire and being allowed to change to any tire (including the current type) after each lap, you must decide when to keep a tire running and when to pay the change cost so that the sum of all lap times and change times is as small as possible. Return that smallest achievable total time.

title: Create Binary Tree From Descriptions
explanation_short: You receive a list of triples [parent, child, isLeft] where each entry tells you which node is the parent of which child and whether that child should be attached as a left or right child. All node values are unique, and the triples together describe a single valid binary tree. Your task is to assemble the tree according to these relationships and identify the node that has no parent. The result you return is the root node of the reconstructed binary tree.

title: Replace Non-Coprime Numbers in Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. While there exists a pair of neighboring elements whose greatest common divisor is greater than 1, replace that pair by a single element equal to their least common multiple, keeping the order of the remaining numbers unchanged. Continue this process until no adjacent non‑coprime pair remains. Return the array that results after all possible replacements.

title: Most Frequent Number Following Key In an Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` and an integer `key` that is guaranteed to occur in the array. For every distinct number that appears immediately after an occurrence of `key`, count how many times that adjacency happens. Identify the number with the largest count (the maximum is unique). Output that number.

title: Cells in a Range on an Excel Sheet
explanation_short:
You receive a single string that names the top‑left and bottom‑right cells of a rectangular block on an Excel sheet, written as “C1:R2”.  
Your task is to enumerate every cell that lies inside that rectangle, including the boundary cells.  
The cells must be listed column by column, and within each column from the lower row number to the higher one.  
Return the result as an array of cell strings.

title: Minimum Number of Moves to Make Palindrome
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` made of lowercase letters. In one move you may swap any two neighboring characters, and you may perform as many moves as needed. Your task is to determine the smallest number of such swaps that can reorder the characters so that the whole string reads the same forward and backward (a palindrome), which is always possible for the given inputs. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Append K Integers With Minimal Sum
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`. Choose `k` distinct positive integers that do not already appear in `nums` and add them to the array, aiming to keep the total added sum as small as possible. Only the sum of the `k` newly appended numbers is required. Return that minimal possible sum.

title: Find All K-Distant Indices in an Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` together with two integers `key` and `k`. An index `i` is considered k‑distant if there exists at least one index `j` such that `nums[j]` equals `key` and the absolute difference `|i - j|` is at most `k`. Collect every index that satisfies this condition and output them as a sorted list.

title: Maximize the Topmost Element After K Moves
explanation_short: You are given a list of integers `nums` that represents a pile, where the first element is the current top, and an integer `k` indicating how many moves must be performed. In each move you may either remove the top element or place a previously removed element back on top. After exactly `k` moves you need to determine the largest possible value that could be on the top of the pile. If no sequence of moves leaves the pile non‑empty, output `-1`.

title: Count Artifacts That Can Be Extracted
explanation_short: You are given the size n of a square grid, a list of rectangles that describe where each artifact lies, and a list of cells that will be dug out. Each dig uncovers the cell; an artifact can be taken out only if every cell of its rectangle has been dug. Your task is to determine how many artifacts become completely uncovered after performing all the digs. Return that number as an integer.

title: Minimum Weighted Subgraph With the Required Paths
explanation_short: You are given the number of nodes n, a list of directed weighted edges, and three distinct nodes src1, src2, and dest. You must choose a subset of the edges that forms a subgraph in which both src1 and src2 can each reach dest by following directed paths that lie entirely inside the chosen edges. The cost of a subgraph is the sum of the weights of its selected edges, and you need the smallest possible cost that still satisfies the reachability requirement. Return that minimum cost, or -1 if no such subgraph exists.

title: Minimum Operations to Halve Array Sum
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers. You may repeatedly pick any element and replace it with exactly half of its current value, and you can keep using the reduced numbers in later steps. Find the smallest number of such operations needed to make the total sum drop by at least 50 % of its original amount, and return that count.

title: Maximize Number of Subsequences in a String
explanation_short: You are given a lowercase string `text` and a two‑letter lowercase string `pattern`. You may insert exactly one character-either `pattern[0]` or `pattern[1]`-anywhere in `text`, including at the beginning or end. After the insertion, count how many subsequences of the resulting string equal `pattern`. Return the maximum possible count over the two insertion choices.

title: Minimum White Tiles After Covering With Carpets
explanation_short: You are given a binary string `floor` where each character tells whether a tile is white (0) or black (1). Along with two integers `numCarpets` and `carpetLen`, you may place up to `numCarpets` carpets, each covering exactly `carpetLen` consecutive tiles, and the carpets are allowed to overlap. Your task is to choose the carpet positions so that the number of white tiles that remain uncovered is as small as possible. Return that minimum count of visible white tiles.

title: Divide Array Into Equal Pairs
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` that contains exactly `2 × n` elements.  
Your task is to decide whether the elements can be grouped into `n` pairs so that each pair consists of two identical numbers.  
If such a grouping is possible, the answer is `true`; otherwise it is `false`.  
The output is a single Boolean value indicating whether the required pairing exists.

title: Count Hills and Valleys in an Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For each position that has a different value on both sides, look at the nearest values that differ from it; if both of those neighbors are smaller, the position belongs to a hill, and if both are larger, it belongs to a valley. Consecutive equal elements are considered part of the same hill or valley, so they should be counted only once. Return the total number of distinct hills and valleys found in the array.

title: Maximum Points in an Archery Competition
explanation_short: You are given an integer numArrows and a length‑12 array aliceArrows that tells how many arrows Alice placed in each scoring zone (0 through 11). Choose how many arrows Bob puts in each zone, forming another length‑12 array bobArrows, so that the entries sum to numArrows and Bob’s total score-earned only for zones where his count exceeds Alice’s-is as large as possible. Return any bobArrows array that achieves this maximum score.

title: Count Collisions on a Road
explanation_short: You are given a string `directions` where each character tells whether the car at that position moves left (`L`), right (`R`) or stays still (`S`). All moving cars travel at the same speed, and whenever two cars meet they stop and remain at the collision point, possibly causing further collisions with other cars. Your task is to determine how many individual car‑to‑car contacts occur before no more collisions can happen. Return that total as an integer.

title: Longest Substring of One Repeating Character
explanation_short: You are given a string s and two same‑length arrays: queryCharacters, which holds characters, and queryIndices, which holds positions in s. For each i from 0 to k‑1, replace the character at s[queryIndices[i]] with queryCharacters[i]. After each replacement, find the length of the longest contiguous segment of identical characters in the updated string. Return an array of those lengths, one entry for each query.

title: Find the Difference of Two Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`. You must identify the distinct values that appear in `nums1` but not in `nums2`, and separately the distinct values that appear in `nums2` but not in `nums1`. Return a list containing two sub‑lists: the first with the missing values from `nums1`, the second with the missing values from `nums2`; the order of numbers inside each sub‑list can be arbitrary.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make Array Beautiful
explanation_short: You are given an integer array nums. You may remove any elements (shifting the rest left) and you want the remaining array to be “beautiful”: its length must be even and for every pair of consecutive positions i and i+1 with i even, the element at i must be strictly smaller than the element at i+1. Determine the smallest possible number of deletions that achieve this condition. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Maximum Value of K Coins From Piles
explanation_short: You are given a collection of piles, where each pile is represented by a list of coin values ordered from top to bottom, and an integer k. You may repeatedly take the current top coin from any pile, removing it, until exactly k coins have been taken. The task is to choose those k coins so that their total value is as large as possible. Return that maximum achievable sum.

title: Find Palindrome With Fixed Length
explanation_short: You are given an array queries and a positive integer intLength. For each value k in queries, you must determine the k‑th smallest positive palindrome that has exactly intLength digits (palindromes cannot start with zero), and return -1 if fewer than k such numbers exist. The result is an array where each element corresponds to the answer for the respective query.

title: Number of Ways to Select Buildings
explanation_short: You are given a binary string s that describes the types of buildings along a street. You must count how many triples of distinct indices i < j < k can be chosen so that the characters at those positions never have two equal neighbors – that is, the building types at i and j differ and the types at j and k also differ. The result is the total number of such valid triples. Return this count as an integer.

title: Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
explanation_short: You are given two integers, start and goal. You must determine the smallest number of individual bit changes required to turn the binary representation of start into that of goal. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Find Triangular Sum of an Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed array `nums` where each entry is a single digit (0‑9). Repeatedly, for every adjacent pair you compute the sum of the two digits, keep only its last digit, and form a new shorter array; you continue this process until only one number remains. That remaining number is defined as the triangular sum of the original array. Output this final digit.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Convert Time
explanation_short: You are given two strings `current` and `correct`, each representing a 24‑hour time in the form “HH:MM”. In one move you may increase `current` by exactly 1, 5, 15, or 60 minutes, and you may repeat moves as many times as needed. Your task is to find the smallest possible number of moves that turns `current` into `correct`. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Find Players With Zero or One Losses
explanation_short: You receive an array where each element is a pair [winner, loser] describing the outcome of a match. From all players that appear in the data, you must determine which ones never lost a game and which ones lost exactly one game. The result should be a two‑element list: the first sub‑list contains the zero‑loss players, the second contains the one‑loss players. Both sub‑lists must be sorted in increasing order.

title: Maximum Candies Allocated to K Children
explanation_short: You receive an array whose elements represent the sizes of candy piles and an integer k for the number of children. You may cut any pile into smaller piles, but you cannot merge piles, and each child must be assigned exactly one pile, with all children getting the same number of candies. Your task is to find the largest possible number of candies that each child can receive under these rules. Output that maximum amount (or 0 if no positive amount is feasible).

title: Sum of Scores of Built Strings
explanation_short: You are given a single string s of length n. For each i from 1 to n, look at the i‑character string formed by the last i characters of s (the string you would have after building s step by step) and measure how many characters at the start match the full string s. Add up all those match lengths and output the total as an integer.

title: Encrypt and Decrypt Strings
explanation_short:
You are given three pieces of data: an array `keys` of distinct characters, an array `values` where each entry is a two‑character string paired with the corresponding character in `keys`, and a list `dictionary` of allowed original words.  
Your task is to build a tool that can take a word and either (a) replace each of its characters by the paired two‑character string to produce an encrypted string, or (b) receive an encrypted string and count how many words in `dictionary` could have produced it.  
If a word contains a character not found in `keys`, the encryption operation must return an empty string.  
The output for each operation is either the encrypted string (or empty) or the count of possible original words.

title: Largest Number After Digit Swaps by Parity
explanation_short: You are given a single positive integer `num`. You may repeatedly exchange any two of its digits as long as both digits are either odd or both are even. Your task is to rearrange the digits, using only those parity‑matching swaps, so that the resulting number is as large as possible. Return that maximum attainable integer.

title: Maximum Product After K Increments
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` of non‑negative integers and an integer `k`. You may perform up to `k` operations, each of which adds 1 to any single element of the array. After applying the operations, you must make the product of all elements as large as possible. Return that maximum product taken modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Minimize Result by Adding Parentheses to Expression
explanation_short: You receive a string that contains two positive integers separated by a ‘+’, like “247+38”. Insert one left parenthesis somewhere before the ‘+’ and one right parenthesis somewhere after the ‘+’ so that the new expression is mathematically valid, and choose the placement that makes the evaluated result as small as possible. Return the modified string; any placement that yields the minimum value is acceptable.

title: Maximum Total Beauty of the Gardens
explanation_short: You are given an array flowers (where flowers[i] is the current count in garden i) and four integers: newFlowers (the total extra flowers you may plant), target (the threshold for a garden to be “complete”), full (the beauty contributed by each complete garden), and partial (the beauty contributed per flower of the least‑filled incomplete garden. You may distribute at most newFlowers among the gardens (adding to existing counts but never removing) to maximize the sum full × (number of gardens that reach target) + partial × (minimum flower count among the remaining gardens). Return that maximum possible beauty value.

title: Add Two Integers
explanation_short: You receive two integers, `num1` and `num2`. Your task is to determine the result of adding these two numbers together. Output the resulting sum as a single integer.

title: Root Equals Sum of Children
explanation_short: You receive a binary tree that has only three nodes: a root and its left and right children. Each node stores an integer value. Check whether the root’s value is exactly the sum of the values of its two children. Return true if they match, otherwise return false.

title: Find Closest Number to Zero
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. From this array you must pick the element whose distance to zero (its absolute value) is minimal. When two numbers are equally close to zero, you should return the larger of them. The answer is that single integer.

title: Number of Ways to Buy Pens and Pencils
explanation_short:
You receive three integers: `total` (the money you can spend), `cost1` (price of one pen) and `cost2` (price of one pencil).  
You must consider every possible non‑negative number of pens and pencils whose combined cost does not exceed `total`.  
Count each distinct pair (number of pens, number of pencils) that satisfies this condition.  
Return that count as the answer.

title: Design an ATM Machine
explanation_short:
You receive a series of commands that either add a given amount of cash to the ATM or request a withdrawal of a specific sum.  
The ATM holds unlimited supplies of $20, $50, $100, $200, and $500 bills, and when a withdrawal is requested it must try to give the amount using as many high‑value notes as possible.  
For each deposit command you simply update the internal counts; for each withdrawal command you must determine whether the exact amount can be formed with the available notes and, if so, return the list of notes used (otherwise indicate failure).  
The output is the sequence of results for the withdrawal commands, each either a list of bill denominations or a failure signal.

title: Maximum Score of a Node Sequence
explanation_short: You are given an array scores where scores[i] is the value of node i, and a list edges describing an undirected graph on the nodes 0 … n‑1. A valid node sequence of length 4 is a list of four distinct nodes (a, b, c, d) such that each consecutive pair (a,b), (b,c), and (c,d) appears in edges. The task is to find the greatest possible sum scores[a] + scores[b] + scores[c] + scores[d] among all such sequences. Return that maximum sum, or -1 if no sequence of four nodes satisfies the adjacency condition.

title: Minimum Rounds to Complete All Tasks
explanation_short: You receive an array where each element is the difficulty of a task. In one round you may finish either two or three tasks that all have the same difficulty level. Your goal is to find the smallest possible number of rounds that can complete every task, or return -1 if the tasks cannot be grouped into such rounds. The output is that minimum count (or -1).

title: Calculate Digit Sum of a String
explanation_short: You receive a string s made only of digits and an integer k. While the string’s length is larger than k, you repeatedly cut it into consecutive pieces of length k (the final piece may be shorter) and replace each piece with the decimal representation of the sum of its digits. The process stops when the resulting string’s length is at most k. Return the final string after all such rounds are completed.

title: Maximum Trailing Zeros in a Cornered Path
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of positive integers. For any path that goes straight in one direction, may turn once, and then continues straight without revisiting cells, compute the product of all numbers on the path and count how many zeros appear at the end of that product. Return the largest such count among all possible cornered paths.

title: Intersection of Multiple Arrays
explanation_short: You receive a collection of integer arrays, each representing a separate list of numbers. Your task is to identify every integer that appears in **all** of the given arrays. The result should be a list containing those common integers (order does not matter). If no number is shared by every array, the output is an empty list.

title: Count Number of Rectangles Containing Each Point
explanation_short: You are given a list of rectangles, each described by its length li and height hi, with the lower‑left corner fixed at (0, 0). You also receive a list of points, each given by coordinates (xj, yj). For every point you must determine how many rectangles have both xj ≤ li and yj ≤ hi (i.e., contain the point). Return an array where the j‑th element is that count for the j‑th point.

title: Longest Path With Different Adjacent Characters
explanation_short:
You receive a tree described by an array where each entry gives the parent of a node (the root has parent ‑1) and a string that assigns one character to every node.  
Your task is to consider any simple path in the tree and keep only those paths where every pair of neighboring nodes carries different characters.  
You must determine the maximum possible length of such a path.  
Return that length as an integer.

title: Count Lattice Points Inside a Circle
explanation_short: You receive a list of circles, each given by three integers [xi, yi, ri] that specify the center coordinates and the radius. A lattice point is any point whose x and y coordinates are both integers. Your task is to determine how many different lattice points fall inside (or on the edge of) at least one of the circles. Output that number as a single integer.

title: Number of Flowers in Full Bloom
explanation_short: You are given a list of flower intervals, where each interval [start, end] means that flower is blooming at every integer time from start to end inclusive. You also receive a list of arrival times for several people. For each arrival time you must determine how many of the given intervals contain that time, and output those counts in the same order as the arrivals.

title: Minimum Average Difference
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For each position `i` you compare the integer‑rounded‑down average of the first `i+1` elements with the integer‑rounded‑down average of the remaining elements, take the absolute difference, and keep track of the smallest such difference. Return the index where this minimum difference occurs; if several indices tie, return the smallest one.

title: Count Prefixes of a Given String
explanation_short:
You receive an array `words` of lowercase strings and a single lowercase string `s`.  
Your task is to determine how many entries in `words` match the beginning of `s` exactly.  
A word counts as a prefix when its characters are identical to the first characters of `s`.  
Output the total count as an integer.

title: Count Unguarded Cells in the Grid
explanation_short: You are given two integers m and n that define an m × n grid, plus two lists: one with the coordinates of all guards and another with the coordinates of all walls. A guard can look north, east, south, and west from its position, but its view stops when it hits a wall or another guard. Any empty cell that no guard can see is considered unguarded. Return the number of these unoccupied, unguarded cells.

title: Escape the Spreading Fire
explanation_short: The input is a 0‑indexed m × n integer grid where each cell is grass (0), wall (1), or fire (2). You begin at the top‑left corner (0, 0) and must reach the bottom‑right corner (m − 1, n − 1), moving each minute to an adjacent grass cell while fire spreads after your move to all adjacent non‑wall cells. You may stay in the starting cell for some number of minutes before beginning to move, and we need the greatest number of minutes you can wait while still being able to reach the safehouse safely. Return that maximum waiting time, –1 if reaching the safehouse is impossible, or 10⁹ if you can wait indefinitely.

title: Remove Digit From Number to Maximize Result
explanation_short: You receive a string `number` that encodes a positive integer and a single character `digit` that is guaranteed to appear in the string. Delete exactly one occurrence of `digit` from `number`. From all possible strings that can be formed this way, pick the one whose decimal value is the greatest. Output that resulting string.

title: K Divisible Elements Subarrays
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` together with two integers `k` and `p`. A subarray is any non‑empty contiguous slice of `nums`; we must consider only those subarrays that contain at most `k` elements whose value is divisible by `p`. Among all such subarrays we count each unique sequence of values just once, ignoring how many times it appears in the original array. The answer is the total number of distinct subarrays that satisfy the divisibility condition.

title: Total Appeal of A String
explanation_short: You are given a single string `s`. For every possible contiguous substring of `s`, count how many different letters appear in that substring (its “appeal”). Add together all those appeal values across all substrings. Return the resulting total as an integer.

title: Minimum Consecutive Cards to Pick Up
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers where each element denotes the value of a card in order. You must locate the shortest contiguous segment of the array that contains at least two cards with the same value. The answer is the length of that segment; if no such segment exists, return –1. This length represents the minimum number of consecutive cards you need to pick up to obtain a matching pair.

title: Largest 3-Same-Digit Number in String
explanation_short: You receive a single string `num` that contains the decimal representation of a large integer. From this string you must look for any three‑character segment where all three characters are identical (for example, “777” or “000”). Among all such three‑digit groups, pick the one that represents the greatest numeric value. Return that group as a string, or return an empty string if no three‑same‑digit segment exists.

title: Count Nodes Equal to Average of Subtree
explanation_short: The input is the root of a binary tree, given in the usual array‑style representation. For every node you look at its entire subtree (the node itself plus all its descendants) and compute the average of the values in that subtree, using integer division. You need to count how many nodes have a value that exactly matches this average. The output is a single integer – the total number of such nodes.

title: Count Number of Texts
explanation_short: You are given a string `pressedKeys` that contains only the digits 2‑9, each digit representing a key on a phone keypad and the number of times it appears consecutively indicating how many times that key was pressed. For each group of identical digits, any split of the presses into valid letter groups (according to the keypad mapping) could correspond to a different original message. Your task is to determine how many distinct messages Alice might have typed that would produce exactly the given sequence of key presses. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Check if There Is a Valid Parentheses String Path
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid where each cell contains either '(' or ')'. Starting at the top‑left cell, you may move only right or down until you reach the bottom‑right cell, forming a string from the visited characters. Return true if any such path creates a valid parentheses string, otherwise return false.

title: Find the K-Beauty of a Number
explanation_short: You are given two integers, num and k. View num as a string and look at every contiguous substring that has exactly k characters. For each substring, interpret it as a number and see if it divides num evenly (substrings that become 0 cannot be divisors). Return the total count of substrings that are divisors of num.

title: Number of Ways to Split Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For each possible split point `i` (where the left part is `nums[0…i]` and the right part is `nums[i+1…n‑1]`), you must check whether the sum of the left segment is at least the sum of the right segment. Count how many split indices satisfy this condition. Return that count as the answer.

title: Maximum White Tiles Covered by a Carpet
explanation_short: You receive a list of intervals `tiles`, where each interval `[lᵢ, rᵢ]` denotes every integer position from `lᵢ` to `rᵢ` that is white‑colored. You also get an integer `carpetLen` representing the length of a carpet that can be placed on the number line covering a contiguous segment of that many positions. Your task is to choose where to put the carpet so that the total number of white‑tile positions lying inside the carpet is as large as possible. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Find Resultant Array After Removing Anagrams
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed array of lowercase words. Repeatedly you may pick any position i (> 0) where the word at i is an anagram of the word just before it and delete the word at i. The process stops when no two neighboring strings are anagrams of each other. Return the array that remains after all possible deletions.

title: Substring With Largest Variance
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` made up of lowercase English letters. For any contiguous piece of that string, count how many times each character appears and take the largest difference between the counts of any two characters (the two characters may be the same). Among all possible substrings, find the greatest such difference. Return that maximum value as an integer.

title: Maximum Bags With Full Capacity of Rocks
explanation_short: You receive two equal‑length arrays: `capacity[i]` tells how many rocks bag i can hold, and `rocks[i]` tells how many rocks are already inside it. An integer `additionalRocks` indicates how many extra rocks you may distribute among the bags in any way you choose. Your task is to decide how to place those extra rocks so that the number of bags whose rock count reaches their full capacity is as large as possible. Return that maximum count of completely filled bags.

title: Largest Combination With Bitwise AND Greater Than Zero
explanation_short: You receive an array `candidates` containing positive integers. For any subset of these numbers, compute the bitwise AND of all elements in the subset. Find the maximum possible size of a subset whose AND result is greater than zero. Return that size as the answer.

title: Maximum Consecutive Floors Without Special Floors
explanation_short: You receive two integers bottom and top that define every floor Alice rents from bottom to top (inclusive), plus an array special listing the floors reserved for relaxation. Among the rented floors, consider the gaps that lie between any two special floors as well as the sections before the first special floor and after the last one. Your task is to find the length of the longest such gap that contains no special floor. Return that maximum length (or 0 if every rented floor is special).

title: Count Integers in Intervals
explanation_short: You receive a sequence of commands, each either adding an interval \([L,R]\) to a set, removing an interval \([L,R]\) from the set, or asking for the total number of distinct integers currently covered by all stored intervals. Adding an interval means every integer between \(L\) and \(R\) (inclusive) becomes part of the set; removing an interval means those integers are taken out, even if they were added by previous operations. For every query command you must output a single integer: the size of the union of all intervals after processing all prior commands.
