title: Percentage of Letter in String
explanation_short: You receive a text `s` and a single character `letter`. Your task is to determine what fraction of the characters in `s` are exactly the same as `letter`. Convert that fraction to a percent and round it down to the nearest whole number. Return the resulting integer value.

title: Sum of Total Strength of Wizards
explanation_short: You are given an integer array strength where each entry represents a wizard’s strength. For every non‑empty contiguous subarray, calculate the product of the smallest strength in that subarray and the sum of all strengths in the same subarray. Add up these products for all possible subarrays. Return the total modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Check if Number Has Equal Digit Count and Digit Value
explanation_short: You receive a string `num` that contains only digit characters. For each position `i` (starting from 0), the digit `i` must appear in the whole string exactly the number of times indicated by the character at `num[i]`. Your task is to verify whether this condition holds for every index. Return `true` if it does, otherwise return `false`.

title: Sender With Largest Word Count
explanation_short: You receive two parallel arrays: one containing the text of each chat message and the other containing the name of the sender for that message. For every sender you must total the number of words across all of their messages. Return the name of the sender with the highest total word count, breaking ties by choosing the lexicographically larger name.

title: Minimum Lines to Represent a Line Chart
explanation_short: You receive a list of pairs [day, price] describing the stock’s value on each day. First arrange the points in increasing order of the day coordinate, then imagine drawing straight segments that connect consecutive points in that order. Your task is to determine the smallest number of straight‑line segments that can be combined so that every point lies on at least one of them, preserving the original chart’s shape. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Maximum Total Importance of Roads
explanation_short: You are given the number of cities `n` and a list of bidirectional roads, each described by the two city indices it connects. Assign each city a unique value from 1 to `n`; the importance of a road equals the sum of the values of its two endpoint cities. Compute and return the largest possible total importance, i.e., the sum of the importance of all roads after an optimal assignment.

title: Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid where each cell is either empty (0) or contains an obstacle (1). You may move up, down, left, or right, but can only step on empty cells unless you choose to remove an obstacle. Your task is to determine the smallest number of obstacles that must be removed so that a path exists from the top‑left corner (0, 0) to the bottom‑right corner (m‑1, n‑1). The answer is a single integer representing that minimum removal count.

title: Rearrange Characters to Make Target String
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s` and `target`. From the letters of `s` you may pick any subset and rearrange them however you like. Determine how many whole copies of `target` you can create before you run out of needed characters. Return that maximum count as an integer.

title: Apply Discount to Prices
explanation_short: You receive a sentence (words separated by single spaces) and an integer discount. A word counts as a price only when it starts with ‘$’ followed by digits. For every price word, reduce its numeric value by the given percentage and rewrite it with exactly two decimal places, leaving all other words untouched. Return the entire sentence with the modified price words.

title: Steps to Make Array Non-decreasing
explanation_short: You receive a list of integers `nums`. In one step you delete every element whose immediate left neighbor is larger than it. Keep applying this rule until the remaining sequence never decreases from left to right. Your task is to determine how many steps are required to reach such a non‑decreasing array. Return that step count as an integer.

title: Booking Concert Tickets in Groups
explanation_short: You are given a hall with n rows, each containing m seats, and a sequence of booking requests. Each request either asks for k consecutive seats in a single row not beyond a given maxRow, or for k any seats spread across rows up to maxRow. For every request you must decide whether the hall can satisfy it under those constraints, and if it’s a consecutive‑seat request also return the row and starting seat index. The output is a list of results-booleans for success/failure and, when applicable, the allocated position.

title: Design a Text Editor
explanation_short: You are given a list of commands that modify a single line of text while a cursor moves within it. The commands can insert characters at the cursor position, move the cursor left or right, and delete the character immediately to the left of the cursor (the cursor never leaves the bounds of the current text). Starting from an empty string with the cursor at the beginning, you must process all commands in order. After all operations are applied, output the final contents of the text.

title: Min Max Game
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` whose size is a power of 2. The array is transformed repeatedly by the given procedure, which reduces its length each round until only a single element is left. Your task is to determine which number remains after all the reductions have been performed. The answer you return should be that final remaining integer.

title: Partition Array Such That Maximum Difference Is K
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. You may divide the elements of `nums` into one or more subsequences, using each element exactly once. Each subsequence must satisfy that the difference between its largest and smallest values does not exceed `k`. Return the minimum possible number of such subsequences.

title: Replace Elements in an Array
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed array `nums` of distinct positive integers and a list of `m` replacement operations, each described by a pair `[old, new]`. For each operation, locate the element equal to `old` in the current array and change it to `new`. After performing all operations in order, the array will have been transformed several times. Return the final state of `nums` as the output.

title: Successful Pairs of Spells and Potions
explanation_short: You are given two lists of positive integers-one for spell strengths and one for potion strengths-plus an integer success. For each spell you must determine how many potions, when multiplied by that spell’s strength, reach or exceed the success threshold. Return an array where the i‑th element is the count of such successful potions for the i‑th spell.

title: Strong Password Checker II
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `password`.  
You must verify whether the string satisfies all the strength rules: it is long enough, contains at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, one allowed special character, and never has the same character appearing consecutively.  
If every rule is met, the answer is `true`; otherwise it is `false`.  
Return the boolean result.

title: Match Substring After Replacement
explanation_short: You are given a main string `s`, a target string `sub`, and a list of character pairs `mappings` where each pair `[old, new]` lets you change an occurrence of `old` in `sub` to `new` (each character in `sub` can be changed at most once). Your task is to decide whether, after applying any number of these allowed changes, the resulting version of `sub` can appear as a contiguous block inside `s`. Return **true** if such a replacement makes `sub` a substring of `s`, otherwise return **false**.

title: Calculate Amount Paid in Taxes
explanation_short: You receive a list of tax brackets, each given as [upper limit, percentage] and an integer income. Starting from the lowest bracket, the portion of your income that falls within each bracket is taxed at that bracket’s percentage. Sum the taxes from all applicable brackets to get the total amount you owe. The result should be printed as a decimal number (typically with five digits after the point).

title: Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K
explanation_short:
You are given an array of positive integers `nums` and an integer `k`.  
For every contiguous subarray, compute its score as the sum of its elements multiplied by its length.  
Count how many of these subarrays have a score that is strictly smaller than `k`.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Minimum Path Cost in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of distinct integers and a separate (moveCost) matrix where moveCost[v][j] gives the cost of moving from a cell whose value is v to column j in the next row. Starting from any cell in the first row, you may jump to any cell in the row directly below, paying the corresponding move cost each time, and you also add the values of all visited cells to the total. Your task is to choose a sequence of cells that reaches the last row with the smallest possible sum of cell values plus move costs. Output that minimum total cost as a single integer.

title: Fair Distribution of Cookies
explanation_short: You are given an array where each element tells how many cookies are in a bag, and an integer k that tells how many children must receive the bags. Every bag must be given whole to exactly one child; you cannot split a bag. The unfairness of an assignment is the biggest total number of cookies any single child ends up with. You need to output the minimum possible unfairness among all ways of distributing the bags.

title: Selling Pieces of Wood
explanation_short: You are given the height m and width n of a rectangular board and a list of triples [hi, wi, pricei] describing how much a piece of exactly that size can be sold for. You may repeatedly cut the board along full rows or columns, producing smaller rectangles, and you can sell any number of pieces that match the listed dimensions (orientation cannot be swapped). Your task is to decide where to cut, if at all, so that the total selling price of the resulting pieces is as large as possible. Return that maximum achievable amount of money.

title: Longest Binary Subsequence Less Than or Equal to K
explanation_short:
You are given a binary string `s` and a positive integer `k`.  
From `s` you may pick any characters in order (forming a subsequence) and interpret the resulting bits as a binary number.  
Your task is to determine the maximum possible length of such a subsequence whose binary value does not exceed `k`.  
Return that length as an integer.

title: Greatest English Letter in Upper and Lower Case
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` that consists only of English letters. Find every letter that shows up in the string both as a lowercase character and as its matching uppercase character. From those letters pick the one that comes latest in the alphabet. Output that letter in uppercase, or return an empty string if no such letter exists.

title: Sum of Numbers With Units Digit K
explanation_short:
You are given two integers `num` and `k`.  
You must form a collection of positive numbers, each ending with the digit `k`, whose total sum equals `num`.  
Determine the smallest possible number of elements in such a collection, or output `-1` if no collection can achieve the required sum.

title: Naming a Company
explanation_short: You are given an array of lowercase strings called ideas. For any two different strings, you may swap their first letters to form two new names; a swap is considered valid only if both new names are not already present in the original array. Count how many distinct valid company names can be created by such swaps, treating the two resulting names as an unordered pair. Return that count as an integer.

title: Count Unreachable Pairs of Nodes in an Undirected Graph
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of edges, where each edge connects two distinct nodes numbered from 0 to n‑1 in an undirected graph. The graph may consist of several separate components. Your task is to determine how many unordered pairs of different nodes cannot reach each other by any path. Return that number as a single integer.

title: Number of Distinct Roll Sequences
explanation_short: You are given an integer n, representing how many times a fair six‑sided die is rolled. A sequence of n results is valid only if any two equal faces occur at positions that differ by exactly one, and every pair of adjacent faces in the sequence are coprime (their greatest common divisor equals 1). Your task is to count how many different length‑n sequences satisfy those rules. Return the count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Count Asterisks
explanation_short:
You receive a single string `s`.  
The vertical bar character ‘|’ appears in the string in pairs: the first and second ‘|’ form one pair, the third and fourth form the next, and so on.  
Your task is to count how many ‘*’ characters are present in `s` but are **outside** every such paired segment (i.e., ignore any ‘*’ that lies between a matching pair of ‘|’).  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Maximum XOR After Operations
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly choose any non‑negative integer `x` and an index `i`, then replace `nums[i]` with `nums[i] AND (nums[i] XOR x)`. After performing any number of these operations, you need to obtain the greatest possible value of the bitwise XOR of all elements in the array. Return that maximum XOR as a single integer.

title: Check if Matrix Is X-Matrix
explanation_short:
You are given a square grid of integers, represented as an n × n 2‑D array.  
An X‑Matrix requires every element on both the main diagonal and the anti‑diagonal to be non‑zero, while every other (off‑diagonal) element must be exactly zero.  
Your task is to examine the grid and decide whether it satisfies these two conditions.  
Return true if the grid is an X‑Matrix; otherwise return false.

title: Count Number of Ways to Place Houses
explanation_short: You are given a single integer n, representing two parallel rows of n plots (one row on each side of the street). You must count all possible ways to decide for each plot whether to leave it empty or place a house, with the restriction that on each side no two houses may occupy neighboring plots. A house on plot i on one side does not affect the other side, so both sides can have houses at the same index. Return the total number of valid arrangements modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Spiral Matrix IV
explanation_short: You receive two integers m and n that define the size of a matrix, plus the head of a singly‑linked list of integers. Fill an m × n grid by placing the list’s values one by one while moving clockwise in a spiral starting at the top‑left corner; any cells that remain after the list is exhausted should contain -1. Return the completed matrix.

title: Number of People Aware of a Secret
explanation_short: You are given three integers n, delay and forget. Starting with one person on day 1, each person begins spreading the secret to one new person every day after delay days of knowing it, and stops spreading (and is no longer counted) forget days after they first learned it. Your task is to determine how many people still know the secret at the close of day n. Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Maximum Score Of Spliced Array
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of equal length. You may pick any segment `[left, right]` and exchange the elements of the two arrays within that segment. After the swap, compute the sum of each array and take the larger of the two sums as the score. Your task is to choose the segment that makes this score as large as possible and output that maximum score.

title: Minimum Score After Removals on a Tree
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` where `nums[i]` is the value of node i, and a list `edges` describing an undirected tree on the nodes 0 … n‑1. You must choose two different edges to delete, which breaks the tree into exactly three connected components. For each component compute the XOR of the values of its nodes, then take the difference between the largest and smallest of those three XOR results. Return the smallest possible difference achievable by any pair of edge deletions.

title: Decode the Message
explanation_short: You receive two strings: `key`, a sentence that defines a substitution alphabet, and `message`, the text to decode. From the key you build a one‑to‑one mapping where each distinct letter, taken in order of first appearance, corresponds to the usual English alphabet (a‑z). Apply that mapping to every letter of the message, leaving spaces unchanged. The result is the decoded plain‑English sentence.

title: The Latest Time to Catch a Bus
explanation_short: You are given an array of distinct bus departure times, an array of distinct passenger arrival times, and the maximum number of passengers each bus can hold. Passengers line up in order of arrival and board the earliest bus that departs no earlier than their arrival time, filling each bus up to its capacity. You must choose an arrival time (different from any other passenger’s time) that still allows you to get on a bus after all earlier‑arriving passengers have taken their seats. Return the greatest possible integer time you can arrive and still catch a bus.

title: Number of Increasing Paths in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of integers. From any cell you may move to its up, down, left, or right neighbor, and a path is valid only if each step goes to a strictly larger value. Count every possible strictly increasing path, allowing any start and any end, and treat two paths as different when their sequences of visited cells differ. Output the total number of such paths modulo 10⁹ + 7.

title: Evaluate Boolean Binary Tree
explanation_short: You receive a full binary tree whose nodes either hold a logical operator (AND or OR) or a Boolean value (true/false) if they are leaves. Starting from the leaves, each internal node computes the result of applying its operator to the results of its two children. Your task is to determine the Boolean value produced at the root after this evaluation. The program should output the final result as either `true` or `false`.

title: Minimum Amount of Time to Fill Cups
explanation_short: You receive an array of three integers where each entry tells how many cold, warm, and hot cups must be filled. Each second you may fill either one cup of any type or two cups simultaneously, but the two must be of different types. Compute and return the smallest number of seconds required to finish all the cups.

title: Move Pieces to Obtain a String
explanation_short:
You are given two equal‑length strings, `start` and `target`, each made up of the characters `L`, `R`, and `_`.  
You may repeatedly slide an `L` one position to the left or an `R` one position to the right, but a piece cannot jump over another piece or move past the string’s ends.  
Determine whether a sequence of such moves can turn `start` into exactly `target`.  
Return **true** if it is possible, otherwise return **false**.

title: Smallest Number in Infinite Set
explanation_short: You start with an infinite collection that contains every positive integer. The class must support two actions: one that removes and returns the current smallest number, and another that can re‑insert a previously removed number back into the collection. Each operation is given as a method call with an optional integer argument. The output consists of the numbers returned by the removal actions, in the order they occur.

title: Count the Number of Ideal Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integers n and maxValue. An ideal array is a length‑n integer sequence where each element is between 1 and maxValue and the values can only stay the same or increase by a factor that divides the next value. Your task is to determine how many different arrays satisfy these conditions. Return that count modulo 10⁹ + 7.

title: Subarray With Elements Greater Than Varying Threshold
explanation_short: You are given an integer array and a single integer called threshold. You need to find a contiguous subarray of length k such that every element inside it is greater than threshold divided by k. Return the length of any subarray that satisfies this condition. If no such subarray exists, output -1.

title: Minimum Sum of Squared Difference
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, and two non‑negative integers `k1` and `k2`. You may perform at most `k1` unit‑changes (increase or decrease by 1) on any elements of `nums1` and at most `k2` such changes on any elements of `nums2`. After applying those changes, compute the sum of the squared differences \((nums1[i] - nums2[i])^2\) for all positions `i`. The required output is the smallest possible value of that sum.

title: Query Kth Smallest Trimmed Number
explanation_short: You are given an array of equal‑length strings that contain only digits, and a list of queries where each query provides a rank k and a trim length t. For every query you virtually keep only the last t characters of each string, treat those trimmed strings as numbers, and determine which original index holds the k‑th smallest value (breaking ties by the smaller original index). The answer for a query is that original index. Return an array containing the answers for all queries in the order they were asked.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make Array Divisible
explanation_short: You receive two positive‑integer arrays, nums and numsDivide. You may delete any elements from nums. The task is to make the smallest element that remains in nums divide every element of numsDivide, while using the fewest deletions possible. Return that minimum number of deletions, or -1 if no amount of deletions can satisfy the condition.

title: Max Sum of a Pair With Equal Sum of Digits
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers. Choose two different indices whose numbers have identical sums of their decimal digits, and add those two numbers together. Return the greatest such sum among all possible pairs, or –1 if no pair shares the same digit‑sum. The input is the array, and the output is a single integer.

title: Maximum Number of Pairs in Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. Repeatedly pick any two equal values, treat them as a pair, and delete both from the array until no such pair exists. Return a two‑element array where the first entry is the total number of pairs removed and the second entry is the count of numbers that remain.

title: Number of Zero-Filled Subarrays
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. Your task is to count every contiguous, non‑empty subarray whose elements are all zero. Subarrays can be of any length, from a single zero up to the longest run of consecutive zeros. Output the total number of such zero‑filled subarrays as a single integer.

title: Shortest Impossible Sequence of Rolls
explanation_short: You are given an array `rolls` of length n, where each element is a result of rolling a k‑sided die, and the integer k itself. Consider every possible sequence of die results of a certain length; we need to determine the smallest length L for which at least one such sequence cannot be found as a subsequence inside `rolls`. In other words, all sequences of length L‑1 must appear somewhere in the given array, but some sequence of length L is missing. Return that minimal L as an integer.

title: Design a Number Container System
explanation_short: You receive a series of commands, each either adding a number to a specific index, removing the entry at an index, or asking for the smallest index that currently holds a given number. Adding a number overwrites any previous value at that index, while removing clears it. For every query command you must report the minimal index that contains the requested number, or ‑1 if the number is absent. The output is the list of results for all query commands in the order they appear.

title: Best Poker Hand
explanation_short: You receive two length‑5 arrays: `ranks`, containing the numeric values of each card, and `suits`, containing the suit symbol of each card. From these five cards you must decide which poker hand category (e.g., “Flush”, “Three of a Kind”, etc.) can be formed that is highest in the standard ranking order. Consider all possible subsets of the cards when evaluating each hand type. Return the name of that best hand as a case‑sensitive string.

title: Number of Excellent Pairs
explanation_short:
You are given a list of positive integers `nums` and another positive integer `k`.  
For every ordered pair of elements `(a, b)` taken from the list (including the case `a = b` when the value appears at least once), compute the number of 1‑bits in `a AND b` and in `a OR b`, add those two counts together, and check whether the sum is at least `k`.  
Count how many distinct ordered pairs satisfy this condition.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: First Letter to Appear Twice
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` made up of lowercase English letters. Scan the characters in order and identify the first letter whose second appearance occurs at the smallest index among all letters that appear at least twice. Return that letter as a single‑character string.

title: Equal Row and Column Pairs
explanation_short: You are given an n × n integer matrix grid. For each row index ri and column index cj, check whether the sequence of numbers in row ri matches exactly the sequence in column cj (in the same order). Count all such row‑column pairs. Output the total count as an integer.

title: Design a Food Rating System
explanation_short: You are given three parallel lists: food names, their cuisine types, and initial integer ratings. The system must support two operations-updating the rating of a specific food, and asking for the highest‑rated food within a given cuisine (breaking ties by the alphabetically smallest name). Each operation is supplied as a command with its required arguments, and you must return the name of the food only for the query commands. The output is a sequence of food names corresponding to those queries, in the order they appear.

title: Make Array Zero by Subtracting Equal Amounts
explanation_short: You receive an array of non‑negative integers. In each step you may choose a positive value x and subtract x from every element that is at least x, turning those elements closer to zero. Your task is to determine the smallest number of steps required to make every array entry equal to 0, and output that minimum count.

title: Find Closest Node to Given Two Nodes
explanation_short:
You are given a directed graph represented by an array edges, where edges[i] is the node reached from i or -1 if there is no outgoing edge, together with two start nodes node1 and node2.  
Find a node that can be reached from both start nodes.  
Among all such common reachable nodes, choose the one that makes the larger of the two distances (from node1 and from node2) as small as possible; if several nodes tie, pick the smallest index.  
Return that node’s index, or -1 if no node is reachable from both.

title: Maximum Number of Groups Entering a Competition
explanation_short: You receive an array of positive integers representing student grades. You must partition the array into a sequence of non‑empty groups, keeping the original order, so that each group contains more students than the one before it and also has a larger total grade sum than the previous group. The task is to determine the greatest possible number of such groups. The answer you return is a single integer – that maximum count.

title: Task Scheduler II
explanation_short: You are given a list `tasks` where each element denotes the type of the next job to finish, and an integer `space` that specifies how many days must separate two executions of the same type. Each day you may either complete the next pending task (in order) or take a break, but you cannot perform a task of type X until at least `space` days have passed since the last X was done. Your goal is to arrange these days so that all tasks are completed while respecting the spacing rule. Return the smallest possible number of days needed to finish the entire sequence.

title: Longest Cycle in a Graph
explanation_short: You are given an array `edges` of length `n`; for each index `i`, `edges[i]` is the node that node `i` points to, and a value of `-1` means node `i` has no outgoing edge. Your task is to identify the longest directed cycle- a sequence of distinct nodes that eventually returns to its starting node. If at least one cycle exists, output the number of nodes in the longest such cycle; otherwise output `-1`. Because each node has at most one outgoing edge, any cycle that appears will be simple and non‑branching.

title: Minimum Replacements to Sort the Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly pick any element and replace it by two new numbers whose sum equals the original value, thereby increasing the length of the array. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of these replacements that results in the entire array being sorted in non‑decreasing order, and output that minimum count.

title: Check if There is a Valid Partition For The Array
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums`.  
You must decide whether the array can be broken into one or more consecutive pieces so that every piece satisfies one of the allowed patterns (for example, all equal numbers or a strictly increasing sequence of length three).  
If such a partition exists, the answer is `true`; otherwise it is `false`.  
Return the Boolean result.

title: Number of Arithmetic Triplets
explanation_short: You receive a strictly increasing integer array `nums` and a positive integer `diff`. You must count how many index triples `(i, j, k)` with `i < j < k` satisfy `nums[j] - nums[i] = diff` and `nums[k] - nums[j] = diff`. The answer is a single integer representing the total number of such arithmetic triplets.

title: Count Number of Bad Pairs
explanation_short:
You receive a zero‑based integer array `nums`.  
For every pair of indices `i < j` you check whether the difference of the indices equals the difference of the corresponding array values; if they are not equal, the pair is considered “bad”.  
Your task is to count how many such bad pairs exist in the whole array.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Merge Similar Items
explanation_short: You receive two 2‑D integer arrays, each containing pairs [value, weight]. For every distinct value that appears in either array, you must add together all of its weights from both arrays. Return a new 2‑D array of [value, totalWeight] pairs sorted in increasing order of the value.

title: Largest Local Values in a Matrix
explanation_short: You receive a square matrix `grid` of size `n × n` containing integers. For every possible 3 × 3 sub‑matrix that can be placed inside `grid`, you must determine the greatest number that appears in that sub‑matrix. Collect those maximum values into a new matrix whose dimensions are `(n‑2) × (n‑2)`, preserving the relative positions of the sub‑matrices. The program should output this resulting matrix.

title: Reachable Nodes With Restrictions
explanation_short: You are given the number of nodes n, a list of n − 1 undirected edges that form a tree, and an array of nodes that are forbidden (restricted). Starting from node 0, you may travel along the edges but you cannot step onto any restricted node. Your task is to determine how many distinct nodes can be visited while never entering a restricted node. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Node With Highest Edge Score
explanation_short: You are given an array `edges` where the element at position `i` tells which node the directed edge from node `i` points to. For each node, calculate its edge score by adding up the indices of all nodes that have an edge leading into it. Return the index of the node with the largest edge score; if several nodes share the maximum score, choose the smallest index among them.

title: Longest Ideal Subsequence
explanation_short:
You are given a lowercase string `s` and an integer `k`.  
From `s` you may delete any characters, but the remaining characters must stay in their original order.  
We need the maximum possible length of a subsequence where every pair of adjacent letters differs by at most `k` positions in the alphabet (the alphabet is not circular).  
Return that length as a single integer.

title: Count Special Integers
explanation_short: You are given a positive integer n. A “special” integer is any positive number whose decimal digits are all different from each other. Your task is to determine how many integers between 1 and n (including both ends) are special. The result should be returned as a single integer representing that count.

title: Shifting Letters II
explanation_short: You receive a lowercase string s and a list of operations, each given as [start, end, direction] where direction is 1 to move letters forward or 0 to move them backward. For every operation you must adjust every character between start and end (inclusive), shifting each one one step in the alphabet and wrapping around from z to a or a to z as needed. After performing all the operations in order, return the final version of s.

title: Construct Smallest Number From DI String
explanation_short:
You are given a string `pattern` of length `n` made up of the characters ‘I’ (increase) and ‘D’ (decrease).  
Create another string `num` of length `n + 1` that uses each digit 1‑9 at most once, such that for every index `i`:
- if `pattern[i]` is ‘I’, then `num[i]` must be smaller than `num[i+1]`;
- if `pattern[i]` is ‘D’, then `num[i]` must be larger than `num[i+1]`.  
Among all strings that satisfy these rules, return the lexicographically smallest one.  
The output is that minimal `num` string.

title: Largest Palindromic Number
explanation_short: You are given a string that contains only decimal digits. From the available digits you may pick any subset (respecting their frequencies) and reorder them to build a palindrome – a number that reads the same forward and backward. The resulting palindrome must be the largest possible numeric value and cannot have leading zeros (except when the answer is exactly “0”). Return this maximal palindrome as a string.

title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
explanation_short: You are given a string `blocks` consisting only of the characters ‘W’ (white) and ‘B’ (black) and an integer `k`. In one move you may change any ‘W’ into a ‘B’. You need to make the string contain at least one run of `k` consecutive ‘B’s while using as few moves as possible. Return the smallest number of moves required.

title: Find the K-Sum of an Array
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`.  
From the array you can form any subsequence (keeping the original order) and compute its sum, with the empty subsequence contributing a sum of 0.  
The K‑Sum is the k‑th largest sum when all these subsequence sums are listed in descending order, counting repeated values separately.  
Your task is to output that k‑th largest sum.

title: Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree whose node values are all distinct, together with an integer `start` that identifies the node where an infection begins at minute 0. Each minute the infection spreads from every infected node to its immediate neighbors – its left child, right child, and parent – if they exist. Return the number of minutes required until every node in the tree becomes infected.

title: Removing Stars From a String
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s` that may contain lowercase letters and the character `*`. Each `*` removes itself and the closest character to its left, and this process is applied from left to right until no stars remain. Return the final string after all such deletions (it may be empty).

title: Longest Subsequence With Limited Sum
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and another array `queries`. For each value in `queries` you must determine the greatest possible number of elements you can pick from `nums` (keeping their original order) so that the total of the chosen elements does not exceed that query value. Return an array where each position holds the maximum subsequence size for the corresponding query.

title: Build a Matrix With Conditions
explanation_short:
You receive an integer k and two lists of ordered pairs rowConditions and colConditions, where each pair [a, b] means “a must appear before b” in rows or columns respectively.  
You must put every number from 1 to k once into a k × k grid, leaving all other cells as 0.  
The chosen positions must make the row index of a smaller than that of b for all row conditions, and the column index of a smaller than that of b for all column conditions.  
Return any matrix that meets these rules, or an empty matrix if no such arrangement exists.

title: Find Subarrays With Equal Sum
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. You must decide whether there are two distinct subarrays of length 2 (starting at different positions) whose elements add up to the same total. Return **true** if such a pair exists, otherwise return **false**.

title: Strictly Palindromic Number
explanation_short:
You are given a single integer n.  
For each base b from 2 up to n − 2, you must check whether the representation of n in that base reads the same forward and backward.  
If every one of those base‑b strings is a palindrome, the answer is true; otherwise it is false.  
Return the Boolean result.

title: Maximum Rows Covered by Columns
explanation_short: You are given a binary matrix with m rows and n columns and an integer numSelect. You must choose exactly numSelect different columns. A row counts as covered when all columns that contain a 1 in that row are among the chosen columns (rows that contain only 0’s are automatically covered). Return the maximum possible number of rows that can be covered by such a selection.

title: Maximum Number of Robots Within Budget
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length arrays, chargeTimes and runningCosts, plus an integer budget. For any consecutive block of k robots, the cost to run them equals the largest value in chargeTimes within that block plus k times the sum of the corresponding runningCosts. Your task is to determine the greatest k for which at least one such consecutive block has a total cost not exceeding budget. Return that maximum k (0 if no block satisfies the budget).

title: Number of Ways to Reach a Position After Exactly k Steps
explanation_short: You receive three integers: `startPos`, `endPos` and a positive integer `k`. You must count how many different sequences of exactly `k` moves-each move being one step left or one step right-begin at `startPos` and finish at `endPos`. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Longest Nice Subarray
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` of positive integers. A subarray is “nice” when every pair of different elements inside it has a bitwise AND equal to 0. Your task is to determine the maximum possible length of such a contiguous subarray (single‑element subarrays always count). Return that length as an integer.

title: Meeting Rooms III
explanation_short: You receive an integer n and a list of meetings, each given by a start time and an end time (all start times are distinct). Meetings are assigned to rooms in chronological order: a meeting begins at its start time if any room is free, otherwise it waits until the earliest‑finishing occupied room becomes free, and then uses the smallest‑numbered available room. While processing, keep track of how many meetings each room hosts. Return the index of the room that hosted the most meetings, breaking ties by choosing the lower index.

title: Check If It Is a Good Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to select a subset of these numbers, multiply each by any integer, and add them up to get a sum of 1. The output will be True if this is achievable and False otherwise. We need to consider all possible subsets and integer multipliers to make this determination.

title: Remove Sub-Folders from the Filesystem
explanation_short: We are given a list of folders as input, and we need to identify and remove any sub-folders within these folders. A sub-folder is defined as a folder that starts with another folder's path followed by a "/". Our goal is to return the remaining folders after removing all sub-folders. The output will be a list of folders with no sub-folders.

title: Minimum Swaps to Make Strings Equal
explanation_short: We are given two strings, each containing only the letters "x" and "y", and they are the same length. Our goal is to make these two strings identical by swapping characters between them. We need to find the minimum number of swaps required to achieve this, or determine if it's impossible. The result will be the minimum number of swaps needed, or -1 if it can't be done.

title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
explanation_short: We are given a string containing parentheses and lowercase English characters. Our goal is to find the minimum number of parentheses that need to be removed to make the string valid. The output will be any valid string that results from removing the minimum number of parentheses. The input string can contain a mix of valid and invalid parentheses sequences. We need to determine which parentheses to remove to achieve a valid string.

title: Cells with Odd Values in a Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a matrix with all zeros and a list of locations to increment. For each location, we need to apply some operations that will change the values in the matrix. Our goal is to find out how many cells in the matrix will have odd values after all the increments have been applied. The input includes the size of the matrix and the list of locations, and the output is the count of odd-valued cells.

title: Tiling a Rectangle with the Fewest Squares
explanation_short: We are given a rectangle with dimensions n by m. Our goal is to determine the minimum number of squares, with integer side lengths, needed to completely cover this rectangle. The input consists of the rectangle's dimensions, and we need to find the smallest set of squares that can fit together to form the rectangle. The output will be the total count of these squares.

title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
explanation_short: We are given three lists of job information: start times, end times, and profits. Our goal is to select a subset of these jobs such that no two jobs overlap in time, and we want to maximize the total profit from the chosen jobs. The input consists of these three lists, and the output will be the maximum achievable profit. We need to find the optimal combination of jobs that yields the highest profit without any time conflicts.

title: Number of Closed Islands
explanation_short: We are given a 2D grid of 0s and 1s, where 0s represent land and 1s represent water. Our task is to find the number of "closed islands", which are groups of land cells completely surrounded by water cells. The input is this 2D grid, and the output will be the count of these closed islands. We need to identify and count all such islands in the given grid.

title: Queens That Can Attack the King
explanation_short: We are given the positions of multiple black queens and one white king on a chessboard. Our task is to find the coordinates of the black queens that can directly attack the white king. The input includes the positions of the queens and the king, and the output will be the coordinates of the queens that can attack the king. We need to consider the possible moves of a queen in a chess game to determine which queens can attack the king. The goal is to return the coordinates of these attacking queens.

title: Reconstruct a 2-Row Binary Matrix
explanation_short: We are given information about a 2-row matrix, including the total number of 1s in the top row, the total number of 1s in the bottom row, and the sum of 1s in each column. Our task is to use this information to recreate the matrix. The output should be a 2D array representing the reconstructed matrix, or an empty array if no valid solution exists. We need to find a combination of 1s and 0s that satisfies all the given conditions.

title: Maximum Score Words Formed by Letters
explanation_short: We are given a list of words, a set of letters, and a score for each letter of the alphabet. Our task is to find the maximum score that can be achieved by forming a set of words using the given letters, with each letter used only once and each word used only once. The output will be the maximum total score of the words that can be formed.

title: Smallest Even Multiple
explanation_short: We are given a number as input and need to find the smallest number that is both a multiple of the input number and even. The goal is to determine this smallest even multiple. The input is a single number, and the output will be the smallest even multiple of that number. We need to find a way to calculate this output based on the given input.

title: Length of the Longest Alphabetical Continuous Substring
explanation_short: We are given a string of lowercase letters as input. Our task is to find the longest substring where the letters are consecutive in the alphabet. The output will be the length of this longest alphabetical continuous substring. We need to examine the input string to identify all possible alphabetical continuous substrings and determine which one is the longest.

title: Most Frequent Even Element
explanation_short: We are given a list of integers as input and need to find the most frequent even number in this list. If multiple even numbers appear the same number of times, we should find the smallest one. The output will be this most frequent even number, or -1 if no even numbers are found in the list. We need to examine each number in the list to determine the most frequent even element.

title: Smallest Subarrays With Maximum Bitwise OR
explanation_short: We are given an array of non-negative integers and need to find the size of the smallest subarray starting at each index that has the maximum possible bitwise OR. The input is this array of integers, and the output will be another array where each element represents the length of the smallest subarray with the maximum bitwise OR starting at the corresponding index. We need to determine this length for each index in the array. The goal is to return an array of these lengths.

title: Maximum Matching of Players With Trainers
explanation_short: We are given two lists: one for players with their abilities and one for trainers with their training capacities. We need to find the maximum number of pairs that can be formed between players and trainers, where each player's ability is less than or equal to a trainer's capacity, and each player and trainer can only be in one pair. The output will be the maximum number of these pairs that can be formed.

title: Reverse Odd Levels of Binary Tree
explanation_short: We are given the root of a perfect binary tree, where every parent node has two children and all leaves are at the same level. Our task is to reverse the node values at each odd level of the tree. The input is the root of the binary tree, and we need to return the root of the modified tree with the odd levels reversed. The output will be the root of the resulting tree after reversing the node values at odd levels.

title: Count Days Spent Together
explanation_short: We are given four dates representing when Alice and Bob arrive and leave Rome. We need to find the total number of days that both Alice and Bob are in Rome at the same time. The input dates are in the format "MM-DD" and we should return the total number of overlapping days.

title: Optimal Partition of String
explanation_short: We're given a string of characters, and we need to divide it into smaller groups, or substrings, where each substring contains only unique characters. Our goal is to find the smallest number of substrings that can be created from the given string. The input is the original string, and the output will be the minimum number of substrings required to meet the condition. We're looking for the most efficient way to partition the string while ensuring each substring has no repeating characters.

title: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
explanation_short: We are given a collection of time intervals, each with a start and end point. Our task is to group these intervals in a way that no two intervals in the same group overlap. We need to find the smallest number of groups required to achieve this. The output will be the minimum number of groups needed to divide the intervals without any overlaps.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence II
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a number k. Our task is to find the longest subsequence in the array where the difference between any two consecutive elements does not exceed k. The output will be the length of this longest subsequence. We need to analyze the array and identify the longest sequence that meets this condition.

title: Sum of Prefix Scores of Strings
explanation_short: We are given a list of strings and need to find the sum of scores for each string. The score of a string is determined by how many other strings it is a prefix of. For each string, we will calculate the sum of scores of all its prefixes, including itself. The output will be a list of these sums, one for each input string.

title: Minimum Money Required Before Transactions
explanation_short: We are given a list of transactions, each with a cost and a cashback amount. Our goal is to find the minimum amount of money we need to have before starting any transactions, so that we can complete all of them in any order. The amount of money we have changes after each transaction, based on its cost and cashback. We need to determine the smallest initial amount of money that allows us to complete all transactions successfully. The output will be this minimum amount of money required.

title: Minimum Hours of Training to Win a Competition
explanation_short: You are given two positive integers initialEnergy and initialExperience, plus two same‑length arrays energy and experience that describe the n opponents you must face in order. To defeat opponent i you need strictly more energy and experience than energy[i] and experience[i]; after the win your energy decreases by energy[i] and your experience increases by experience[i]. Before the contest you may spend training hours, each hour raising either your initial energy or your initial experience by one. Return the minimum number of training hours required to be able to beat all opponents.

title: Minimum Amount of Time to Collect Garbage
explanation_short: You receive a list where each element describes the pieces of metal (M), paper (P) and glass (G) left at a house, and another list giving the travel time between consecutive houses. Three trucks, each dedicated to one type of garbage, start at house 0 and may move forward only, but only one truck can work (drive or collect) at any moment. You must determine how long it will take, in minutes, for all three trucks together to pick up every piece of garbage. Return that total time as a single integer.

title: Maximum Segment Sum After Removals
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and another array `removeQueries`, both of length `n`. For each index in `removeQueries` you delete the element at that position in `nums`, which may break the array into several contiguous blocks of positive numbers, and you must determine the largest sum of any such block after the deletion. Collect these maximum sums in order, producing an output array `answer` of length `n`.

title: Time Needed to Rearrange a Binary String
explanation_short: You are given a binary string s. In each second, every occurrence of the pattern “01” flips to “10” at the same time. The flipping repeats until the string contains no more “01” substrings. Return the total number of seconds required for this process to finish.

title: Sort the People
explanation_short: We are given two lists: one containing people's names and the other containing their corresponding heights. We need to sort these people based on their heights in descending order. The input consists of these two lists, and the output will be a list of names sorted by their heights, with the tallest person first. Our goal is to match each name with its correct height and arrange them accordingly. The result will be a list of names in the order of their heights, from tallest to shortest.

title: Number of Common Factors
explanation_short: We are given two positive integers, and we need to find the number of integers that divide both of them. These integers are called common factors, and they must divide both numbers without leaving a remainder. Our task is to count how many such common factors exist for the given pair of integers. The output will be the total count of these common factors.

title: Longest Uploaded Prefix
explanation_short: We are given a stream of video uploads, each identified by a unique number. Our task is to track the upload process and find the length of the longest sequence of videos that have been uploaded in order, starting from the first video. The input is a series of video uploads, and the output is the length of the longest uploaded prefix at various points. We need to design a data structure that can efficiently calculate this length as the upload process progresses. The goal is to determine the maximum sequence of videos that have been uploaded in the correct order.

title: Maximum Sum of an Hourglass
explanation_short: We're given a matrix of integers with a certain number of rows and columns. Our task is to find the maximum sum of elements that form an hourglass shape within this matrix. The hourglass shape consists of a specific arrangement of cells that must be entirely contained within the matrix. We need to calculate the sum of elements for all possible hourglass shapes and determine the maximum sum. The output will be the maximum sum found.

title: Number of Pairs Satisfying Inequality
explanation_short: We are given two integer arrays and a difference value. Our task is to find the number of pairs of elements, one from each array, that satisfy a specific inequality condition. The input arrays and difference value are used to determine these pairs, and the output will be the total count of pairs that meet the given conditions.

title: Longest Subarray With Maximum Bitwise AND
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to find the length of the longest subarray where the bitwise AND of all its elements is maximum. The input is this array of integers, and the output will be the length of the longest subarray that meets this condition. Our goal is to identify the maximum possible bitwise AND value and then determine the longest contiguous sequence of elements that yields this value. We will return the length of this longest subarray as the result.

title: Find All Good Indices
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a positive integer k. Our task is to find all indices in the array that satisfy a specific condition, where the subarray to the left of the index is in non-increasing order and the subarray to the right of the index is in non-decreasing order. The input consists of the array and the integer k, and the output will be a list of indices that meet this condition. We need to examine each index in the array and determine whether it meets the specified criteria. The result will be a list of indices that are considered "good" based on these conditions.

title: Remove Letter To Equalize Frequency
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase English letters and need to determine if removing one letter can make the frequency of all remaining letters equal. The input is this string, and we're looking to find out if it's possible to achieve equal letter frequencies by deleting just one character. Our output will be a simple true or false, indicating whether this is possible or not. We need to consider the counts of each letter in the string to make this determination.

title: Number of Good Paths
explanation_short: We are given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and their corresponding values, as well as the connections between these nodes. Our task is to find the number of distinct "good paths" in this tree, where a good path is a simple path that meets certain conditions. The input consists of the node values and the connections between them, and the output is the total count of these distinct good paths. We need to consider all possible paths and determine which ones satisfy the given conditions.

title: Bitwise XOR of All Pairings
explanation_short: We are given two arrays of non-negative integers, nums1 and nums2. Our task is to find the bitwise XOR of all possible pairings between these two arrays. To do this, we need to calculate the bitwise XOR of each pair of numbers, one from nums1 and one from nums2, and then find the bitwise XOR of all these results. The final output will be a single number that is the result of this operation.

title: Minimize XOR
explanation_short: We are given two positive integers, num1 and num2, and we need to find a positive integer x. The goal is to minimize the result of the bitwise XOR operation between x and num1. The output will be the integer x that achieves this minimization, with the additional condition that x has the same number of set bits as num2.

title: Maximum Deletions on a String
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase English letters and need to find the maximum number of operations required to delete the entire string. In each operation, we can delete a sequence of letters if the same sequence appears immediately after it. The goal is to determine the highest number of such operations that can be performed to delete all the letters in the string. The output will be the maximum number of operations needed.

title: Number of Valid Clock Times
explanation_short: We're given a string representing time in "hh:mm" format, but some digits are unknown and represented by a "?". We need to find the number of valid clock times that can be created by replacing these unknown digits with any digit from 0 to 9. The output will be the total count of valid times, considering the constraints of a 24-hour clock. The input string will have a fixed length of 5 characters, including the colon.

title: Largest Positive Integer That Exists With Its Negative
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers, and we need to find the largest positive integer that has its negative counterpart in the array. The input is this array of integers, and our task is to identify this specific positive integer. The output will be the largest positive integer that meets this condition, or -1 if no such integer exists. We're looking for a positive integer k such that -k is also present in the array.

title: Count Number of Distinct Integers After Reverse Operations
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our task is to reverse each integer in the array, add the reversed integers to the end of the array, and then find the total number of unique integers in the resulting array. The output will be the count of distinct integers in the final array. We need to consider that reversing an integer like 10 results in 01, which simplifies to 1.

title: Sum of Number and Its Reverse
explanation_short: We are given a non-negative integer as input and need to determine if it can be expressed as the sum of any non-negative integer and its reverse. The reverse of a number is obtained by reversing its digits. Our goal is to find out if such a combination exists for the given number. The output will be true if we can find such a combination, and false otherwise.

title: Range Product Queries of Powers
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer n and a set of queries, where each query specifies a range within an array of powers of 2 that sum to n. Our task is to find the product of all the powers of 2 within the specified range for each query. The output will be a list of these products, one for each query.

title: Count Subarrays With Fixed Bounds
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers and two specific integers, minK and maxK. Our task is to find the number of subarrays within the given array where all elements fall within the range defined by minK and maxK. The output will be the count of such subarrays, which are contiguous parts of the array that satisfy the given conditions. We need to consider all possible subarrays and determine how many meet the specified criteria.

title: Determine if Two Events Have Conflict
explanation_short: We are given two events, each represented by a start and end time in 24-hour format. Our task is to determine if these two events overlap or have any common time. To do this, we need to compare the start and end times of both events. The output will be true if the events conflict, meaning they have some time in common, and false if they do not.

title: Number of Subarrays With GCD Equal to K
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a target number k. Our task is to find the number of subarrays within the given array where the greatest common divisor of all the elements in the subarray is equal to k. The output will be the count of such subarrays. We need to consider all possible subarrays and determine which ones meet the specified condition.

title: Create Components With Same Value
explanation_short: We are given a tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, each having a specific value, and edges connecting these nodes. Our goal is to delete some edges to split the tree into multiple connected components, where the sum of node values in each component is the same. The input consists of the node values and the edges, and we need to find the maximum number of edges that can be deleted to achieve this. The output will be the maximum number of edges that can be deleted.

title: Minimize Maximum of Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of non-negative integers and need to find the minimum possible maximum value in the array after performing any number of operations. The input is the array of integers, and the output is the minimum maximum value that can be achieved. Our goal is to determine this minimum maximum value by considering the possible operations that can be performed on the array. The result will be the smallest maximum value that can be obtained.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Arrays Similar
explanation_short: We are given two arrays of the same length, one called nums and the other called target, and we need to find the minimum number of operations required to make the nums array similar to the target array. In each operation, we can choose two distinct indices and adjust the values accordingly. Our goal is to determine the fewest number of operations needed to achieve this similarity. The output will be the minimum number of operations required. We need to compare the input arrays and figure out the most efficient way to transform one into the other.

title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equal
explanation_short: We are given two arrays, one containing numbers and the other containing the costs of changing those numbers. Our task is to find the minimum total cost required to make all the numbers in the first array equal. The output will be the smallest possible total cost to achieve this. We need to consider the costs of increasing or decreasing each number to find the optimal solution.

title: Paths in Matrix Whose Sum Is Divisible by K
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of integers and an integer k. Starting at cell (0, 0) you may only move right or down until you reach cell (m‑1, n‑1). For every such path compute the sum of the cells visited and count how many of those sums are multiples of k. Output that count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Using a Robot to Print the Lexicographically Smallest String
explanation_short: You are given a single string `s`. A robot starts with an empty auxiliary string `t` and can repeatedly either move the first character of `s` onto the end of `t` or move the last character of `t` onto the paper. By choosing the order of these moves, you must produce the lexicographically smallest possible string that ends up on the paper. The program should output that minimal string.

title: Check Distances Between Same Letters
explanation_short: You receive a lowercase string s in which every letter that shows up does so exactly twice, and an integer array distance of length 26 mapping each alphabet letter to a required gap. For each letter present in s, count how many characters lie between its two occurrences and compare that count to the corresponding entry in distance. Return true if all present letters meet their required gaps; otherwise return false.

title: Odd String Difference
explanation_short: We are given an array of strings, all of the same length. Our task is to find the string that is different from the others based on the pattern of differences between consecutive characters in each string. The output will be the string that has a unique pattern of character differences. We need to compare the patterns of character differences among all the strings to identify the odd one out.

title: Average Value of Even Numbers That Are Divisible by Three
explanation_short: We are given a list of positive integers as input. Our task is to find the average value of the even numbers in this list that are also divisible by 3. To do this, we need to identify the numbers that meet these conditions, calculate their sum, and then divide by the count of such numbers. The result will be the output, which is the average value rounded down to the nearest integer. If no such numbers exist, the output will be 0.

title: Minimum Addition to Make Integer Beautiful
explanation_short: We are given two positive integers, n and a target value. Our goal is to find the smallest non-negative integer that we can add to n, so that the sum of the digits of the resulting number is less than or equal to the target. The output will be this minimum integer value that makes n "beautiful" according to the given condition. We need to determine this minimum value based on the given input.

title: Most Popular Video Creator
explanation_short: We are given three lists: video creators, video ids, and the number of views for each video. We need to find the creator with the most views across all their videos and identify the id of their most viewed video. The output will be a list of creators with the highest popularity along with the id of their most popular video. The goal is to handle cases where multiple creators have the same highest popularity and where a creator has multiple videos with the same highest view count.

title: Next Greater Element IV
explanation_short: We are given an array of non-negative integers and need to find the second greater integer for each number in the array. This means we are looking for an integer to the right of the current number that is greater than it, and then finding the next integer after that which is also greater. The output will be an array where each element is the second greater integer for the corresponding input number, or -1 if no such integer exists.

title: Words Within Two Edits of Dictionary
explanation_short: We are given two lists of words, called queries and dictionary, where each word has the same length and only contains lowercase letters. Our task is to find the words from the queries list that can be changed to match a word from the dictionary list by replacing one or two letters. The output will be a list of words from the queries list that can be matched to a dictionary word with two or fewer changes, in the same order they appear in the queries list.

title: Maximum Sum of Distinct Subarrays With Length K
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a length, and we need to find the maximum sum of all subarrays with the given length that have distinct elements. The input includes the array and the length, and the output will be the maximum sum of the subarrays that meet the conditions. If no subarray meets the conditions, the output will be 0. We need to consider all possible subarrays of the given length and check if their elements are distinct to determine the maximum sum.

title: Apply Operations to an Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of non-negative integers and need to apply a series of operations to it. In each operation, we compare an element with the next one and perform a specific action if they are equal. After all operations are completed, we rearrange the array to move all zeros to the end. The resulting array is our output.

title: Destroy Sequential Targets
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers representing targets and an integer space. Our goal is to find the minimum target value that, when used to seed a machine, allows it to destroy the maximum number of targets. The machine can destroy targets with values that are the seeded value plus any non-negative multiple of the space. The output will be the minimum target value that achieves this maximum destruction.

title: Height of Binary Tree After Subtree Removal Queries
explanation_short: We are given a binary tree with unique node values and a list of queries. For each query, we need to remove the subtree rooted at a specific node value and find the new height of the resulting tree. The input includes the tree and the list of queries, and the output will be an array of tree heights after each query is performed. Our goal is to calculate the height of the tree after each independent query.

title: Minimum Total Distance Traveled
explanation_short: We are given the positions of robots and factories on the X-axis, along with the capacity of each factory to repair robots. Our goal is to determine the initial direction of movement for each robot to minimize the total distance traveled by all robots when they reach a factory for repair. The output will be the minimum total distance traveled by all the robots. We need to consider how to optimize the movement of each robot to achieve this minimum distance.

title: Convert the Temperature
explanation_short: We are given a temperature in Celsius, which is a non-negative number with two decimal places. Our task is to convert this temperature into Kelvin and Fahrenheit. We need to perform the necessary calculations to find the equivalent temperatures in Kelvin and Fahrenheit. The result will be an array containing the temperature in Kelvin and Fahrenheit. The output should be accurate to five decimal places.

title: Find The Original Array of Prefix Xor
explanation_short: You receive an integer array pref of length n. Each element pref[i] represents the cumulative bitwise‑xor of the first i + 1 numbers of an unknown array arr. Your task is to reconstruct that original array arr, which is guaranteed to exist and be unique. Return arr as an array of n integers.

title: The Employee That Worked on the Longest Task
explanation_short: You are given the number of employees `n` and a list `logs`, where each entry contains an employee’s id and the time they finish their current task. The first task begins at time 0, and each subsequent task starts right after the previous one ends, so the duration of a task is the difference between its finish time and the finish time of the task before it. Your goal is to identify which employee handled the task with the greatest duration, breaking ties by choosing the smallest employee id. Return that employee’s id as a single integer.

title: Find the Pivot Integer
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer as input and need to find a special integer, called the pivot integer. The pivot integer is a number where the sum of all numbers before it equals the sum of all numbers after it, including itself. Our task is to find this pivot integer. If such an integer exists, we return it; otherwise, we return -1 as the output.

title: Most Profitable Path in a Tree
explanation_short: You are given an undirected tree described by edges, the index bob where Bob starts, and an array amount where amount[i] is the value of the gate at node i. Alice begins at the root (node 0) and both players move one step per turn toward each other’s start positions, opening gates they reach; if they arrive at the same node at the same time they split its value. Your task is to choose the leaf Alice will head for so that her total collected value (adding full amounts, half amounts when shared, and ignoring already‑opened gates) is as large as possible. Return that maximum net income as a single integer.

title: Count Subarrays With Median K
explanation_short: We're given an array of distinct integers and a target number k. Our task is to find the number of subarrays within this array that have a median equal to k. The input consists of the array and the target number, and the output will be the count of such subarrays. We need to consider all possible non-empty subarrays and determine which ones meet the median condition. The result will be the total count of these subarrays.

title: Remove Nodes From Linked List
explanation_short:
You receive the head of a singly‑linked list whose node values are given in order.  
For each node, if there exists any node later in the list with a greater value, that node must be removed.  
After all such deletions, the list should be re‑linked so that only the surviving nodes remain.  
Return the head of this modified list, which will be represented by the sequence of its remaining values.

title: Append Characters to String to Make Subsequence
explanation_short: You are given two lowercase strings `s` and `t`. You must determine the smallest number of characters that can be added to the end of `s` so that `t` appears as a subsequence of the extended string. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Count Ways To Build Good Strings
explanation_short: You are given four integers zero, one, low and high. Starting from an empty string, you may repeatedly append either a block of zero ‘0’ characters or a block of one ‘1’ characters. A “good” string is any resulting string whose total length lies between low and high (inclusive). Return the number of different good strings possible, modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Number of Subarrays With LCM Equal to K
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a target number k. Our task is to find the number of subarrays within the given array where the least common multiple of the subarray's elements equals k. The input includes the array and the target number, and the output will be the count of such subarrays. We need to consider all possible subarrays and determine their least common multiple to find the desired count.

title: Number of Distinct Averages
explanation_short: You receive an even‑length array of integers. While the array still has elements, you repeatedly take one minimum and one maximum value, compute their average \((a+b)/2\), and discard those two numbers. Your task is to determine how many unique average values are produced throughout this process, and output that count.

title: Minimum Cuts to Divide a Circle
explanation_short:
You are given a single integer n.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of straight cuts through the circle that will produce exactly n identical slices.  
Each cut must be a line segment that goes from one point on the circumference to another (or through the center), and the resulting pieces must all have the same shape and size.  
Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Minimum Penalty for a Shop
explanation_short: We are given a string representing the customer visit log of a shop, where 'Y' indicates a customer arrived and 'N' indicates no customer arrived at a particular hour. We need to find the minimum penalty the shop can incur by closing at a certain hour, considering the number of customers who would be turned away. The penalty is calculated based on the number of customers who arrive after the shop closes. Our goal is to determine the minimum possible penalty. The output will be the minimum penalty the shop can incur.

title: Divide Nodes Into the Maximum Number of Groups
explanation_short:
You are given the number of nodes n and a list of undirected edges connecting pairs of those nodes.  
Each node must be placed into one of the groups numbered 1, 2, …, m, and every edge must join two nodes that belong to different groups.  
Your task is to choose the grouping that allows the largest possible value of m; if no assignment can satisfy all edges, you must report that it is impossible.  
Return that maximum m, or ‑1 when a valid grouping does not exist.

title: Divide Players Into Teams of Equal Skill
explanation_short: You receive an even‑length array of positive integers, where each value is a player’s skill. You must pair the players into n⁄2 teams of two so that every team’s skill sum is identical. For each valid pair, compute its chemistry as the product of the two skills and add all these products together. Output the resulting total, or ‑1 if it’s impossible to form teams with equal skill sums.

title: Longest Square Streak in an Array
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums`.  
A subsequence of this array is a “square streak” if, after sorting the chosen elements, every number equals the square of the one before it.  
Your task is to determine the maximum possible length of such a subsequence.  
Return that length, or `-1` if no square streak exists.

title: Total Cost to Hire K Workers
explanation_short: We are given a list of worker costs, and two integers representing the number of workers to hire and the number of candidates to consider. Our goal is to find the total cost of hiring exactly the specified number of workers, following specific rules to select the workers. The output will be the total cost of hiring these workers. We need to determine how to select the workers to minimize the total cost.

title: Minimum Score of a Path Between Two Cities
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of roads, each described by two city numbers and the distance of the road connecting them. A path’s score is the smallest distance among all roads that appear on that path. Your task is to consider every possible path that starts at city 1 and ends at city n, and determine the lowest score that can be achieved among those paths. Return that minimum score as a single integer.
