title: Minimum Total Cost to Make Arrays Unequal
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of the same length, nums1 and nums2. You may repeatedly swap any two positions inside nums1, and each swap costs the sum of the two indices involved. The goal is to rearrange nums1 so that for every index i, the element at nums1[i] is different from nums2[i]. You must compute the smallest possible total cost that achieves this condition. The answer is that minimum cost (or an indication that it’s impossible, if no such rearrangement exists).

title: Frog Jump II
explanation_short: You are given a strictly increasing array of integers, each representing the position of a stone in a river. A frog starts on the first stone, must reach the last stone and then return to the first, and it may step on any stone at most once. The length of each jump equals the distance between the two stones involved, and the cost of a complete path is the maximum jump length used in that path. Return the minimum possible cost among all such feasible round‑trip paths.

title: Delete Greatest Value in Each Row
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of positive integers. In each step you delete one element from every row – specifically the largest remaining value in that row – and then add the biggest of those deleted numbers to a running total. After each step the grid loses one column, so you repeat the process until no columns remain. The required output is the final sum accumulated over all steps.

title: Maximum Value of a String in an Array
explanation_short: You are given an array of strings that may contain letters, digits, or both. For each string, its value is its length unless the string is made up solely of digits, in which case its value is the integer represented by those digits. Return the largest value found among all strings in the array.

title: Design Memory Allocator
explanation_short: You are given an integer n that defines the length of a zero‑indexed memory array, initially all free. A series of operations-such as requests to allocate a contiguous block of a given size and commands to free previously allocated blocks-are provided as input. Your task is to simulate these operations, keeping track of which portions of the array are occupied or available. For each allocation request you must output the starting index of the allocated block (or -1 if no suitable space exists), while free operations produce no output.

title: Add Edges to Make Degrees of All Nodes Even
explanation_short: You are given the number of nodes n and a list of existing undirected edges between them. You may insert zero, one, or two new edges-provided they are not duplicates or self‑loops-and you must decide whether it’s possible to end up with every node having an even degree. Return **true** if such a construction exists, otherwise return **false**.

title: Count Pairs Of Similar Strings
explanation_short: You receive a list of lowercase strings. Two strings are considered similar when the set of distinct letters appearing in each is identical, regardless of order or repetitions. Count how many unordered index pairs (i, j) with i < j have similar strings, and return that total.

title: Smallest Value After Replacing With Sum of Prime Factors
explanation_short:
You receive a single positive integer n.  
Repeatedly break the current value into its prime factors (counting repeated factors) and replace the number with the sum of those primes.  
During this process the numbers may go up or down, but eventually they stop changing or enter a cycle; the task is to determine the smallest value that ever appears.  
Return that minimum value as the answer.

title: Maximum Enemy Forts That Can Be Captured
explanation_short: You receive an array where each element is 1 (your fort), -1 (enemy fort), or 0 (empty ground. You may pick a 1 and move its army to a 0 that lies to its left or right, but the move is only allowed if every position between them is -1. All enemy forts encountered on that path are considered captured. Your task is to determine the greatest possible number of enemy forts that can be captured with a single such move. If no valid move exists, return 0.

title: Reward Top K Students
explanation_short: You receive two word lists – one of positive feedback and one of negative feedback – plus a list of feedback strings, a matching list of student IDs, and an integer k. For each feedback string, the student at the same index gains 3 points for every positive word it contains and loses 1 point for every negative word it contains. After processing all reports, students are ranked by total points in descending order, with lower IDs breaking ties. The output is the IDs of the top k students in that ranking.

title: Maximum Tastiness of Candy Basket
explanation_short: You are given a list of candy prices and an integer k. From the list you must pick exactly k different candies so that the smallest absolute price difference between any two chosen candies is as large as possible. Return that largest achievable minimum difference.

title: Take K of Each Character From Left and Right
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` made only of the letters a, b, and c, and a non‑negative integer `k`.  
Each minute you may remove the leftmost or the rightmost character of the current string, and you keep all characters you have taken.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of minutes required to have collected at least `k` a’s, `k` b’s, and `k` c’s; if this is impossible, you must report `-1`.  
Return that minimum minute count (or `-1` when the goal cannot be reached).

title: Count Anagrams
explanation_short:
You receive a single string `s` that consists of one or more words, with each pair of consecutive words separated by exactly one space.  
For each word, any rearrangement of its letters is allowed, but the order of the words themselves must stay the same.  
Your task is to determine how many different overall strings can be formed this way, counting each distinct arrangement only once.  
Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Distinct Prime Factors of Product of Array
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` containing positive integers. First form the product of all elements in the array, then look at the prime numbers that divide this product. Count how many different primes appear as factors, ignoring their multiplicities. Return that count as the answer.

title: Count the Digits That Divide a Number
explanation_short: You are given a single integer `num`. Look at each digit that appears in its decimal representation, ignoring any zeros because division by zero is undefined. Count how many of those digits are exact divisors of `num` (i.e., `num` modulo the digit equals zero). Output that count as an integer.

title: Shortest Distance to Target String in a Circular Array
explanation_short: You receive a circular array of words, a target word, and a starting index. From the start you may step one position forward or backward, wrapping around the ends, and you must determine the fewest steps required to land on any occurrence of the target. Return that minimum distance, or -1 if the target never appears in the array.

title: Partition String Into Substrings With Values at Most K
explanation_short:
You are given a string `s` made of digits 1‑9 and an integer `k`.  
You must cut the string into consecutive pieces so that each piece, when read as a decimal number, does not exceed `k`.  
Among all such possible cuts, find the one that uses the fewest pieces.  
Return that minimum number of pieces, or `-1` if no way to satisfy the condition exists.

title: Minimize the Maximum of Two Arrays
explanation_short:
You are given four integers `divisor1`, `divisor2`, `uniqueCnt1` and `uniqueCnt2`.  
Pick distinct positive integers and divide them into two arrays `arr1` and `arr2` so that exactly `uniqueCnt1` numbers in `arr1` are not divisible by `divisor1`, and exactly `uniqueCnt2` numbers in `arr2` are not divisible by `divisor2`.  
All other chosen numbers may be any values (including multiples of the divisors).  
Return the smallest possible value of the largest integer that appears in either array.

title: Number of Great Partitions
explanation_short:
You receive an array `nums` of positive integers and a threshold `k`.  
Each element must belong to exactly one of two ordered groups, forming a partition of the whole array.  
A partition is “great” when the sum of the numbers in each group is at least `k`.  
Return how many distinct great partitions exist, giving the answer modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Find Xor-Beauty of Array
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For every ordered triple of indices (i, j, k) you compute the value `((nums[i] | nums[j]) & nums[k])`, where `|` is bitwise OR and `&` is bitwise AND. The task is to XOR together all those values from every possible triple. The result of that XOR operation is the required output.

title: Maximize the Minimum Powered City
explanation_short: You are given an array stations where stations[i] is the number of power stations already in city i, an integer r that defines how far each station’s power reaches, and an integer k that tells how many additional stations you may place anywhere. Each city’s total power equals the sum of stations in all cities whose distance to it is at most r. Your task is to decide where to add the k new stations so that the smallest total power among all cities becomes as large as possible. Return that maximum achievable minimum power value.

title: Find Consecutive Integers from a Data Stream
explanation_short: You receive a sequence of integer values one by one, together with a fixed window size k and a target value. After each new integer arrives, you must determine whether the most recent k numbers in the stream are all exactly equal to the target value. The data structure should return a true/false answer for each incoming integer, indicating if the condition holds at that point. The input consists of the initial parameters (k and the target) followed by the stream of integers, and the output is the series of boolean results.

title: Closest Prime Numbers in Range
explanation_short: You are given two positive integers `left` and `right`. Consider every prime number that lies between them, inclusive. Find a pair of different primes whose gap is the smallest possible; if several pairs share that gap, choose the one whose lower prime is the smallest. Return the two numbers as `[num1, num2]`, or `[-1, -1]` if fewer than two primes exist in the range.

title: Categorize Box According to Criteria
explanation_short: You are given four integers - length, width, height, and mass - that describe a box’s dimensions and weight. First determine whether the box is “Bulky” by checking if any dimension is at least 10⁴ or if its volume (length × width × height) exceeds 10⁹. Then check if the mass is at least 100 to decide if it is “Heavy”. Based on these two tests, return the string “Bulky”, “Heavy”, “Both”, or “Neither” as appropriate. The output is a single word enclosed in quotes.

title: Maximum Count of Positive Integer and Negative Integer
explanation_short: You are given a list of integers that is already sorted from smallest to largest. Count how many elements are greater than zero and how many are less than zero, ignoring any zeros. Compare the two counts and keep the larger one. Output that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Maximal Score After Applying K Operations
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a number `k`. In each of the `k` steps you choose an index `i`, add the current value of `nums[i]` to your total score, and then replace `nums[i]` with `ceil(nums[i] / 3)`. Your task is to decide which indices to pick in order to make the accumulated score as large as possible after exactly `k` operations. Return that maximum achievable score.

title: Make Number of Distinct Characters Equal
explanation_short: You receive two strings, word1 and word2. A single move lets you pick one character from each string and swap them. You must decide whether there is a swap that makes the count of different letters in the two resulting strings exactly the same. Return true if such a swap exists, otherwise return false.

title: Time to Cross a Bridge
explanation_short: You are given two integers n (the number of boxes) and k (the number of workers), plus a k × 4 array where each row [i] contains the times for worker i to cross to the right side, pick up a box, cross back to the left side, and put the box down. All workers start on the left bank of the bridge, and they must repeatedly move boxes from the right warehouse to the left one, obeying the specified ordering rules that compare workers’ efficiencies. Your task is to determine how many minutes will have elapsed when the nᵗʰ (and final) box is placed on the left side. The answer is a single integer representing that total time.

title: Difference Between Element Sum and Digit Sum of an Array
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` containing positive integers. First, add up all the numbers in the array to get the element sum. Then, break each number into its decimal digits, add those digits together to obtain the digit sum. Return the absolute value of the difference between the element sum and the digit sum.

title: Count the Number of Good Subarrays
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`.  
A subarray is considered “good” when it contains at least `k` distinct pairs of positions `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `nums[i] = nums[j]`.  
Your task is to count how many different subarrays of `nums` satisfy this condition.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Circular Sentence
explanation_short: We are given a sentence, which is a list of words separated by spaces. Our task is to determine if the sentence is circular, meaning the last character of each word matches the first character of the next word, and the last character of the last word matches the first character of the first word. The output will be true if the sentence is circular and false otherwise. We need to examine the words in the sentence and compare the characters to make this determination.

title: Closest Nodes Queries in a Binary Search Tree
explanation_short: We're given the root of a binary search tree and a list of positive integers called queries. For each query, we need to find the largest number in the tree that is less than or equal to the query, and the smallest number in the tree that is greater than or equal to the query. The output will be a 2D array where each sub-array contains these two values for each query, or -1 if no such value exists.

title: Number of Unequal Triplets in Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our task is to find the number of unique triplets in the array where the elements at three different positions are all different from each other. The output will be the total count of such triplets that meet the given conditions.

title: Maximum Number of Non-overlapping Palindrome Substrings
explanation_short: We are given a string and a minimum length requirement. Our task is to find the maximum number of non-overlapping substrings within the string that are palindromes and meet the minimum length requirement. The output will be the count of these substrings. We need to select substrings that do not overlap with each other and are palindromes, meaning they read the same forwards and backwards.

title: Minimum Fuel Cost to Report to the Capital
explanation_short: We are given a network of cities connected by roads and a capital city where all representatives need to meet. Each city has a car with a limited number of seats, and representatives can travel together to reduce fuel costs. We need to find the minimum amount of fuel required for all representatives to reach the capital city. The input includes the road connections between cities and the number of seats in each car, and the output is the minimum number of liters of fuel needed.

title: Count Palindromic Subsequences
explanation_short: We're given a string of digits as input and we need to find the number of subsequences of length 5 within this string that are palindromes. A palindrome is a sequence that reads the same backward as forward. Our task is to count how many such palindromic subsequences exist in the given string. The output will be the total count of these palindromic subsequences, adjusted to fit within a large numerical range by taking the result modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Split Message Based on Limit
explanation_short: We are given a string message and a positive integer limit. Our task is to split the message into parts, with each part having a specific suffix and a maximum length of limit, while ensuring the total message can be reconstructed from these parts. The goal is to find the fewest number of parts possible that meet these conditions and return them as an array of strings. If it's impossible to split the message as required, we should return an empty array. The output should be an array of strings, where each string is a part of the original message with its corresponding suffix.

title: Maximum Number of Points From Grid Queries
explanation_short: We are given a grid of integers and a list of queries. For each query, we start at the top left of the grid and need to find the maximum number of points we can get by following a certain process. The output will be a list of maximum points we can get for each query. We need to determine how to navigate the grid to maximize points without exceeding the query value. The result is an array of maximum points for each query.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Sort a Binary Tree by Level
explanation_short: We are given the root of a binary tree with unique values. Our goal is to determine the minimum number of operations required to sort the values at each level in a strictly increasing order. To achieve this, we can swap the values of any two nodes at the same level in one operation. The output will be the minimum number of such operations needed to sort the tree level by level.

title: Number of Beautiful Partitions
explanation_short: We are given a string of digits and two integers, k and minLength. Our task is to find the number of ways to divide the string into k parts, where each part meets certain conditions. The output will be the total count of these divisions, and since the count can be very large, we need to provide the result modulo 10^9 + 7. We need to consider all possible combinations of the string to achieve this.

title: Cycle Length Queries in a Tree
explanation_short: We are given a complete binary tree with a specific number of nodes and a set of queries, where each query consists of two node values. For each query, we need to find the length of a cycle that forms when an edge is added between the two nodes. The output will be an array containing the cycle lengths for each query. Our task is to determine the size of the cycle that is created after adding the edge between the specified nodes.

title: Maximum Star Sum of a Graph
explanation_short: We are given a graph with nodes having certain values and edges connecting these nodes. Our task is to find the maximum sum of node values that can be achieved by selecting a subset of edges, such that all selected edges are connected to a common node, and the total number of selected edges does not exceed a given limit. The output will be the maximum sum of node values that can be obtained under these conditions. The input includes the node values, the edges, and the maximum number of edges that can be selected.

title: Minimum Common Value
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays that are already sorted in non‑decreasing order. Your task is to identify the smallest number that occurs in both arrays at least once. If the two arrays share no common value, you should output -1.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal II
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of the same length `n` and an integer `k`. In one operation you may pick two positions `i` and `j` in `nums1`, decrease `nums1[i]` by `k` and increase `nums1[j]` by `k`. The task is to determine the smallest number of such operations needed to make `nums1` identical to `nums2`, or report that it cannot be done. Output that minimum count, or `-1` if no sequence of operations can achieve equality.

title: Difference Between Maximum and Minimum Price Sum
explanation_short: You are given the number of nodes n, a list of n − 1 undirected edges that form a tree, and an array price where price[i] is the cost of node i. For any node you pick as the root, look at every possible path that begins at that root and compute the sum of the node prices along each path; the cost for that root is the difference between the largest and smallest of those sums. Your task is to choose the root that makes this difference as large as possible. Return that maximum difference as a single integer.

title: Sort the Students by Their Kth Score
explanation_short: We are given a table of student scores for different exams and a specific exam number, k. Our task is to rearrange the students in the table based on their scores in the kth exam. The students with the highest scores in that exam should be at the top, and those with the lowest scores should be at the bottom. The output will be the rearranged table of student scores.

title: Check if Point Is Reachable
explanation_short: We are given the coordinates of a target point on an infinitely large grid, represented by two integers targetX and targetY. Our goal is to determine if it's possible to reach this target point from the starting point (1, 1) by taking a series of steps. The output will be true if we can reach the target point and false otherwise. We need to figure out if there's a valid sequence of moves that allows us to arrive at the target point.

title: Count Increasing Quadruplets
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers from 1 to n, and we need to find the number of increasing quadruplets in this array. A quadruplet is considered increasing if the first element is less than the third, the third is less than the second, and the second is less than the fourth. Our task is to count how many such quadruplets exist in the given array. The output will be the total count of these increasing quadruplets.

title: Alternating Digit Sum
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer as input, and we need to calculate the sum of its digits, where the sign of each digit alternates between positive and negative. The first digit is always positive, the second is negative, the third is positive, and so on. Our goal is to find this alternating sum of the digits. The output will be the result of this calculation.

title: Count Distinct Numbers on Board
explanation_short: We're given a positive integer that's initially placed on a board. Every day, certain numbers are added to the board based on specific conditions. Our task is to find the total number of distinct integers present on the board after a large number of days have passed. The input is the initial integer, and the output is the count of unique numbers on the board after the specified time period. We need to determine how many different numbers will be on the board after this process.

title: Separate the Digits in an Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our task is to take each integer in the array, break it down into its individual digits, and then combine these digits into a new array. The output will be an array containing all the digits from the original integers, in the same order they appeared. The resulting array will have each digit separated and ordered as they were in the original array of integers.

title: Count Collisions of Monkeys on a Polygon
explanation_short: We are given a regular convex polygon with a certain number of vertices, each having a monkey that moves to a neighboring vertex. Our task is to find the number of ways these monkeys can move so that at least one collision occurs, either by landing on the same vertex or intersecting on an edge. The input is the number of vertices in the polygon, and the output is the number of ways collisions can happen, calculated modulo a large number to avoid very large results. We need to consider all possible movements of the monkeys to determine the total number of collisions.

title: Maximum Subsequence Score
explanation_short:
You are given two integer arrays of the same size and a positive integer k.  
Select exactly k different positions; the score of a selection equals the sum of the chosen nums1 values multiplied by the smallest nums2 value among those positions.  
Your task is to determine the greatest possible score achievable by any such selection.  
Return that maximum score as a single integer.

title: Increment Submatrices by One
explanation_short: You are given an integer n that defines an n × n matrix initially filled with zeros, and a list of queries where each query provides the coordinates (row1, col1) of the top‑left corner and (row2, col2) of the bottom‑right corner of a submatrix. For every query you must add 1 to every element inside the specified submatrix. After processing all queries, the matrix reflects all the accumulated increments. Return the resulting n × n matrix.

title: Disconnect Path in a Binary Matrix by at Most One Flip
explanation_short: You receive an m × n binary matrix where you can move only down or right through cells that contain 1, starting at (0, 0) and aiming for (m‑1, n‑1). You may flip the value of at most one cell, but the two corner cells cannot be changed. After the optional flip, determine whether there is no possible path from the start to the finish using the allowed moves. Return true if the matrix can be made disconnected, otherwise return false.

title: Minimum Impossible OR
explanation_short:
You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
An integer `x` is considered “expressible” if you can pick any subset of the array’s elements and obtain `x` by applying the bitwise OR operation to them.  
Your task is to determine the smallest positive integer that cannot be produced in this way.  
Return that integer as the answer.

title: Take Gifts From the Richest Pile
explanation_short: You are given an integer array gifts representing the number of gifts in each pile and an integer k the number of seconds. Each second you must pick the pile that currently holds the most gifts and reduce its count to the integer part of one‑tenth of its original size (the rest are taken away). After performing this operation exactly k times, add up the numbers left in all piles. The required output is this total sum.

title: Handling Sum Queries After Update
explanation_short:
You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2` and a list of queries, each query being a triple `[type, left, right]`.  
For each query you must update the arrays according to its type: type 1 toggles the bits of `nums1` between `left` and `right`; type 2 adds the current sum of `nums1` in that interval to every element of `nums2` in the same interval; type 3 asks for the sum of `nums2` between `left` and `right`.  
While processing the queries, collect the results of all type 3 queries.  
Return an array containing those collected sums in the order they were asked.

title: Minimum Operations to Reduce an Integer to 0
explanation_short: You are given a single positive integer n. You may repeatedly add or subtract any power of two (2ⁱ for i ≥ 0) from the current value, and you want to reach exactly zero using as few operations as possible. Return the smallest number of additions or subtractions required.

title: Minimum Score by Changing Two Elements
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. You may pick any two positions in the array and change their values to any integers you like. After those two modifications, consider the difference between the largest and the smallest element in the resulting array; the task is to make this difference as small as possible. Return that smallest achievable difference as the answer.

title: Left and Right Sum Differences
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For each position `i`, consider the sum of all elements to its left (excluding `i`) and the sum of all elements to its right (excluding `i`). The task is to compute the absolute difference between these two sums for every index. Return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` holds that absolute difference. The output array has the same length as the input array.

title: Count the Number of Square-Free Subsets
explanation_short: You are given a positive‑integer array `nums`. A subset is square‑free when the product of all its chosen elements has no divisor that is a perfect square larger than 1. Count all non‑empty subsets that satisfy this condition and return the total modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Merge Two 2D Arrays by Summing Values
explanation_short: You receive two 2‑D integer arrays, each containing pairs [id, value] that are sorted by id and have no duplicate ids within the same array. Combine the arrays so that each distinct id appears once, adding the two values together when an id is present in both arrays. The merged list must stay sorted in ascending order by id. Return the resulting list of [id, summed value] pairs.

title: Find the Divisibility Array of a String
explanation_short:
You receive a string `word` made of digit characters and an integer `m`.  
For each position `i` (0‑based) you consider the prefix formed by the first `i+1` characters of `word`.  
You must decide whether that numeric prefix is divisible by `m` and record `1` if it is, otherwise `0`.  
The result is an array of length `n` containing those 0/1 values for all prefixes.

title: Find the Maximum Number of Marked Indices
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` where every index starts unmarked. You may repeatedly choose two different unmarked positions `i` and `j` such that `2 × nums[i] ≤ nums[j]`, and then mark both of those indices. The task is to determine the largest possible total of indices that can become marked after applying the operation any number of times. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Minimum Time to Visit a Cell In a Grid
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid where each entry tells the earliest second at which that cell may be entered. Starting from the top‑left corner at time 0, you may move up, down, left or right, each step consuming one second, but you can only step into a cell when the current time is at least its value. Compute the smallest possible time at which you can reach the bottom‑right cell, or return ‑1 if no such route exists.

title: Count Total Number of Colored Cells
explanation_short: You are given a single positive integer n. Starting with an empty infinite grid, a fixed coloring routine is performed once per minute for n minutes, expanding outward from the origin. After the n‑th minute you must determine how many unit cells have been colored in total. Return that count as an integer.

title: Difference Between Ones and Zeros in Row and Column
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix as input, where each cell contains either 0 or 1. Our task is to create a new matrix where each cell represents the difference between the number of ones and zeros in the corresponding row and column of the original matrix. The output will be this new difference matrix, where each cell contains the calculated difference value.

title: Count Ways to Group Overlapping Ranges
explanation_short: You receive a list of integer pairs, each pair [startᵢ, endᵢ] describing a closed interval. You must divide the intervals into two (possibly empty) groups, but any intervals that overlap-share at least one integer-must stay together in the same group. Return how many different divisions are possible, giving the answer modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Find the String with LCP
explanation_short: You are given an n × n integer matrix lcp, where lcp[i][j] represents the length of the longest common prefix of the suffixes starting at positions i and j in an unknown string of length n. Your task is to construct a lowercase‑letter string of length n that matches all these prefix lengths. If more than one string satisfies the matrix, you must return the alphabetically smallest one; if no string can produce the given matrix, return an empty string. The output is that resulting string (or an empty string).

title: Count Number of Possible Root Nodes
explanation_short: You are given an undirected tree described by a list of n‑1 edges, a list of guessed parent‑child pairs, and an integer k. For each node you imagine it as the root, direct all edges away from it, and count how many guesses correctly describe a parent‑to‑child relationship in that orientation. Return how many nodes yield at least k correct guesses (or 0 if none do).

title: Number of Ways to Earn Points
explanation_short: You are given an integer target and a list types where each element [countᵢ, marksᵢ] tells how many questions of that type exist and how many points each one is worth. You must count how many different selections of questions (using at most the given count for each type) produce a total score exactly equal to target. Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Split With Minimum Sum
explanation_short: You receive a single positive integer `num`. Its decimal digits must be divided into two groups, each group forming a non‑negative integer (leading zeros are allowed). Your task is to choose the grouping that makes the sum of the two resulting numbers as small as possible. Return that minimum sum as an integer.

title: Minimum Time to Complete All Tasks
explanation_short: You receive a list of tasks, each described by three integers - the earliest second it may start, the latest second it may finish, and how many seconds it must run (the running time can be split into separate moments). Your goal is to choose moments inside the allowed ranges for all tasks so that the computer is turned on for as few total seconds as possible, turning it off whenever no chosen moment occurs. Return that minimum total number of seconds the computer needs to be on.

title: Count the Number of Vowel Strings in Range
explanation_short: You receive a list of words and two indices `left` and `right`. A word is a vowel string if its first and last characters are one of `a, e, i, o, u`. Count how many words from position `left` through `right` (including both ends) are vowel strings. Output that count as a single integer.

title: Count the Number of Beautiful Subarrays
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
A subarray is called beautiful if, by repeatedly picking any contiguous segment inside it and subtracting a power of two ( 2^k ) from every element that has the k‑th bit set, you can eventually turn every element of that subarray into 0.  
Your task is to count how many non‑empty contiguous subarrays of `nums` satisfy this condition.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Rearrange Array to Maximize Prefix Score
explanation_short: You are given an integer array nums. You may permute its elements in any order, then compute the running sums from the first element up to each position. The task is to choose an ordering that makes as many of those running sums positive as possible. Return the largest possible count of positive prefix sums.

title: Distribute Money to Maximum Children
explanation_short: You are given two integers: `money`, the total dollars you have, and `children`, the number of kids you must give money to. You must assign each child a positive integer amount so that the sum of all amounts equals `money`. Among all possible assignments, you need to find the greatest possible number of children who receive exactly 8 dollars. Output that maximum count, or -1 if no distribution meeting the rules exists.

title: Minimum Time to Repair Cars
explanation_short: You receive an array `ranks` where each element is the speed rating of a mechanic, and an integer `cars` indicating how many cars must be fixed. A mechanic with rank `r` can finish `n` cars in `r × n²` minutes, and all mechanics work at the same time. Your task is to determine the smallest amount of time after which the combined work of all mechanics is enough to repair at least `cars` vehicles. Return that minimum time as a single integer.

title: Number of Even and Odd Bits
explanation_short: You receive a single positive integer n. Count how many 1‑bits occur at even‑indexed positions (0, 2, 4, …) and how many occur at odd‑indexed positions (1, 3, 5, …) when the binary form of n is read from right to left. Output the two counts as an array [even, odd].

title: Find Score of an Array After Marking All Elements
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` of positive integers. Starting with a score of 0, repeatedly choose the smallest element that hasn’t been marked yet, add its value to the score, and then mark that element together with its immediate left and right neighbors (if they exist). Continue this marking process until every position in the array is marked, and output the final accumulated score.

title: Maximize Greatness of an Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. You may rearrange its elements in any order to form a new array `perm`. The task is to make as many positions as possible where the element in `perm` is strictly larger than the element originally at the same index in `nums`. Return the greatest possible number of such positions.

title: The Number of Beautiful Subsets
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` of positive integers and a positive integer `k`.  
Consider any non‑empty subset formed by deleting some (or none) of the elements, keeping the original order of the remaining indices.  
A subset is “beautiful” if no two numbers inside it have an absolute difference exactly equal to `k`.  
Return how many different beautiful subsets exist for the given `nums` and `k`.

title: Smallest Missing Non-negative Integer After Operations
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array nums and an integer value. You may repeatedly add or subtract value to any element of nums. After performing any number of these operations, consider the MEX-the smallest non‑negative integer not present in the array-and aim to make this MEX as large as possible. Return the maximum achievable MEX as the answer.

title: Pass the Pillow
explanation_short: You receive two positive integers n and time. Imagine n people standing in order, with a pillow that moves to the next person each second and reverses direction when it reaches either end of the line. Your task is to determine which person’s index is holding the pillow after exactly time seconds, and output that index.

title: Kth Largest Sum in a Binary Tree
explanation_short:
You receive a binary tree (accessed via its root node) and a positive integer k.  
For every depth‑level of the tree, compute the sum of the node values that lie on that level.  
Find the k‑th largest value among those level sums, counting equal sums separately.  
If the tree contains fewer than k levels, return -1; otherwise return the identified sum.

title: Prime Subtraction Operation
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly pick any index `i` and any prime number `p`, then subtract `p` from `nums[i]`. The task is to decide whether, after any number of these subtractions, the entire array can be transformed into a strictly increasing sequence (each element larger than its predecessor). Output `true` if this is achievable, otherwise output `false`.

title: Check Knight Tour Configuration
explanation_short: You receive an n × n grid where each cell contains a unique number from 0 to n·n – 1, representing the step at which a knight visited that square. Starting from the cell marked 0, you must check that every successive step (1, 2, …, n·n – 1) is reachable from the previous one by a legal knight move (two squares in one direction and one in the perpendicular direction). If all consecutive moves satisfy this rule, the configuration is valid; otherwise it is not. Return true when the whole tour is valid and false when any step breaks the knight‑move condition.

title: Form Smallest Number From Two Digit Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two arrays, each containing digits from 0 to 9. You must form the smallest possible positive integer that uses at least one digit from the first array and at least one digit from the second array. If a digit appears in both arrays, that single digit itself is a valid answer. Return the integer you obtain as the result.

title: Minimum Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal
explanation_short: You are given a list `nums` of positive integers and another list `queries`. For each value `q` in `queries`, you must determine the smallest total number of +1 or ‑1 steps needed to turn every element of `nums` into `q`, assuming the original array is restored before handling the next query. Return an array where the i‑th entry is that minimum count for `queries[i]`.

title: Find the Substring With Maximum Cost
explanation_short: You receive three inputs: a string s, a string chars containing distinct letters, and an integer array vals of the same length as chars. Each letter listed in chars gets the corresponding value from vals, while every other letter is considered to have value 1. The cost of a substring is the sum of the values of its characters, and the empty substring has cost 0. Your task is to determine the maximum possible cost among all substrings of s and output that number.

title: Collect Coins in a Tree
explanation_short: You are given the number of nodes n, a list of n − 1 undirected edges connecting those nodes, and an array coins where coins[i] is 1 if node i holds a coin and 0 otherwise. You may begin at any node and move along edges, counting each time you traverse an edge (even if you use the same edge multiple times). The task is to determine the smallest total number of edge traversals needed to visit every coin‑bearing node and finally return to the starting node. Output that minimum number as a single integer.

title: Convert an Array Into a 2D Array With Conditions
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums`.  
Your task is to reorganize all its elements into a list of rows, where each row contains only distinct numbers.  
Every element of `nums` must appear exactly once, and rows may have different lengths.  
Return the resulting 2‑D array; any arrangement that satisfies the distinct‑in‑row condition is accepted.

title: Make K-Subarray Sums Equal
explanation_short:
You are given a circular integer array arr and an integer k.  
You may change the value of any element, counting each unit of change as one operation, and you may repeat this as many times as you like.  
Your task is to make the sum of every contiguous subarray of length k (wrapping around the end of the array) identical.  
Return the smallest possible total number of operations required to achieve this.

title: Find the Longest Balanced Substring of a Binary String
explanation_short:
You receive a string `s` that contains only the characters ‘0’ and ‘1’.  
A balanced substring is any contiguous part of `s` where every ‘0’ appears before any ‘1’ and the counts of ‘0’s and ‘1’s are the same (the empty substring also counts).  
Your task is to determine the maximum possible length of such a balanced substring within `s`.  
Return that length as an integer.

title: Minimum Reverse Operations
explanation_short: You are given the length n of an array, a starting index p where the only 1 is placed, a list banned of positions that can never contain the 1, and a parameter k that defines the allowed reverse operation. For each index i from 0 to n‑1 you must determine the smallest number of those operations required to move the 1 from p to i without ever landing on a banned position; if it cannot be reached, the answer for that index is -1. The result is an array of n integers, where the i‑th entry is the minimum operation count (or -1) for position i.

title: Shortest Cycle in a Graph
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of unordered pairs edges, each pair describing an undirected edge between two distinct vertices numbered 0 to n‑1. Your task is to determine the smallest number of edges that form a closed walk (a cycle) where no edge is repeated, and report that length. If the graph contains no such cycle, output -1.

title: K Items With the Maximum Sum
explanation_short: You are given four non‑negative integers: the counts of 1’s, 0’s, –1’s in a bag, and a number k. From the bag you must select exactly k items, aiming for the largest possible total of the numbers written on the chosen items. Return that maximum sum as an integer.

title: Minimum Number of Visited Cells in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n integer matrix grid, and you start in the top‑left cell (0, 0). From any cell (i, j) you may move to other cells according to the rules defined by the value stored in that cell. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of distinct cells that must be visited in order to reach the bottom‑right cell (m‑1, n‑1); if no sequence of moves can reach that cell, you should report –1. The output is a single integer representing this minimum count (or –1 when unreachable).

title: Mice and Cheese
explanation_short: You are given two equal‑length arrays reward1 and reward2, each describing the points a cheese type yields when eaten by mouse 1 or mouse 2, plus an integer k. Every cheese type (indexed 0…n‑1) must be assigned to exactly one mouse, and mouse 1 must eat precisely k types while mouse 2 eats the remaining n‑k types. The total score is the sum of the appropriate rewards for the chosen assignments. Return the largest possible total score.

title: Prime In Diagonal
explanation_short: You receive a rectangular grid of integers (a 0‑indexed 2‑D array). Look at every element that appears on either of the two diagonals that run from corner to corner; among those numbers identify the prime ones and pick the greatest value. Return that largest prime, or return 0 if none of the diagonal elements are prime.

title: Minimize the Maximum Difference of Pairs
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `p`. Choose `p` pairs of distinct indices from the array, compute the absolute difference for each pair, and consider the largest difference among the selected pairs. Return the smallest possible value of that largest difference (if no pairs are chosen, the answer is 0).

title: Check if Object Instance of Class
explanation_short: You are given two arguments: a value and a class (or constructor) to test against. Your task is to determine whether the value behaves as an instance of that class, meaning it can access the class’s methods either directly or through inheritance. The function should return a Boolean-`true` if the value is an instance of the specified class or any of its ancestors, and `false` otherwise. Edge cases such as `undefined` or non‑object values must also be handled.

title: Cache With Time Limit
explanation_short: The input is a list of actions (construction, set, get, count) together with the times they are invoked. `set(key, value, duration)` stores a key‑value pair that expires after the given number of milliseconds, returning true if an un‑expired entry for that key already existed and false otherwise (the stored value and timer are replaced). `get(key)` should return the value only while the key’s timer has not elapsed, otherwise it returns -1. `count()` reports how many keys are still un‑expired at the moment it is called.

title: Sum of Distances
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For each index `i`, you must add up the absolute differences `|i ‑ j|` for every other index `j` where `nums[j]` equals `nums[i]`. If no such `j` exists, the sum for that position is 0. Output the array `arr` containing these sums for all indices.

title: Counter
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list describing how many times a special function is invoked. The function should start by returning n the first time it is called, and each later call must return a value that is exactly one larger than the value returned previously. Your task is to simulate those calls and collect the results in order. The output is the sequence of numbers produced by the successive calls.

title: Memoize
explanation_short:
You are given the name of a known function (sum, fib, or factorial) and two parallel lists: one describing actions (“call” or “getCallCount”) and the other providing the arguments for each call action.  
A “call” action should invoke the memoized version of the chosen function with the supplied arguments and record the returned value; repeated calls with identical arguments must use the cached result instead of invoking the original function again.  
A “getCallCount” action must report how many times the original function has actually been executed so far.  
Return an array containing the result of each action in order – the computed value for “call” actions and the current call count for “getCallCount” actions.

title: Snail Traversal
explanation_short:
You receive a one‑dimensional array `nums` together with two integers `rowsCount` and `colsCount`.  
First check that the product `rowsCount * colsCount` equals the length of `nums`; otherwise the result is an empty array.  
If the sizes match, you must place the numbers into a matrix of the given dimensions so that reading the matrix column by column, alternating top‑to‑bottom and bottom‑to‑top, reproduces the original order.  
The output is that resulting two‑dimensional array.

title: Debounce
explanation_short: You are given a delay t (in milliseconds) and an ordered list of calls, each described by the time it is invoked and the arguments it receives. Simulate a debounced version of the original function: after a call, wait t milliseconds before executing it, but cancel that pending execution if another call arrives within the waiting window; the later call then starts its own waiting period. Return the sequence of calls that finally run, each represented by its actual execution time and the arguments it was called with.

title: Flatten Deeply Nested Array
explanation_short: You receive a multi‑dimensional array `arr` and an integer `n`. Starting from depth 0, you must replace each sub‑array whose current nesting depth is strictly less than `n` with its contained elements, leaving deeper levels untouched. The result is a single‑level array that reflects this selective flattening.

title: Sleep
explanation_short: You receive a single positive integer `millis` that tells how many milliseconds to pause. Your task is to implement an asynchronous function that waits for roughly that amount of time before finishing. The function should return a promise that resolves after the delay; the resolved value can be any value.

title: Array Prototype Last
explanation_short:
You receive an array that has already been parsed from JSON.  
Your task is to make a method called `last()` available on every array, which when invoked returns the array’s final element.  
If the array is empty, the method must return `-1` instead.  
The output is simply the value produced by calling `array.last()`.

title: Array Reduce Transformation
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`, a binary function `fn`, and an initial value `init`. Starting with `init`, you repeatedly call `fn` using the current result and the next element of `nums`, feeding the returned value back into the next call. After processing every element (or none, if the array is empty), you output the final value obtained.

title: Group By
explanation_short: You receive an array and a callback function that, when given an element, returns a string key. Your task is to create a method so that calling array.groupBy(fn) produces an object whose properties are those keys. Each property’s value must be an array containing all original elements that generate the same key, preserving their original order. The resulting object is the output; the order of the keys themselves does not matter.

title: Memoize II
explanation_short: You receive a function `fn` that may accept any number of arguments of any type. Your task is to produce a new function that forwards calls to `fn` but remembers each result, using strict (`===`) equality on the argument values to decide whether a call is new or a repeat. When the wrapper is invoked with arguments it has seen before, it must return the cached result without calling `fn` again; otherwise it should call `fn`, store the outcome, and return it. The output is this memoized version of `fn`, which behaves identically to the original while minimizing the number of actual executions.

title: Function Composition
explanation_short: You are given a list of functions, each taking an integer and returning an integer, and a single integer x. First you must build a new function that applies the given functions one after another, starting with the last function in the list and working toward the first. Then you evaluate this composed function at the value x. The program should output the resulting integer.

title: Promise Time Limit
explanation_short: You are given an asynchronous function `fn`, a time limit `t` in milliseconds, and the arguments that will be passed to `fn`. Create a new version of `fn` that starts the original function and monitors its execution time. If the original function finishes before `t` milliseconds, the wrapper should resolve with the function’s return value; otherwise it must reject with the error message “Time Limit Exceeded”. The result you return should indicate whether the call was resolved or rejected and the elapsed time in milliseconds.

title: Filter Elements from Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `arr` and a function `fn` that, when called with an element (and optionally its index), returns a truthy or falsy value. Build a new array that keeps only those elements for which `fn` evaluates to truthy. The result you output is this filtered array.

title: Apply Transform Over Each Element in Array
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers and a function that takes a value and its index. Create a new array where each position i contains the result of calling the function with the original element arr[i] and the index i. Return this newly built array.

title: Design Graph With Shortest Path Calculator
explanation_short: You are given a directed weighted graph with n vertices numbered 0 to n‑1 and an initial list of edges, each described by a source node, a destination node, and a cost. Your task is to build a Graph object that can store this structure and later answer shortest‑path queries between any two vertices. The class must support adding new edges and, when asked, return the minimum total cost to travel from a specified start node to a specified end node (or indicate that no path exists). The output consists of the results of those shortest‑path queries, one value per query.

title: Find the Width of Columns of a Grid
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed m × n integer matrix grid. For each column, determine the largest “length” among its numbers, where the length of a non‑negative integer equals its digit count and a negative integer’s length is its digit count plus one for the minus sign. Collect these maximum lengths in order, forming an array of size n. Return that array as the answer.

title: Cousins in Binary Tree II
explanation_short: You are given the root of a binary tree. For every node, compute the sum of the values of all nodes that share its depth but have a different parent (its cousins) and replace the node’s value with that sum. If a node has no cousins, its new value becomes 0. Return the root of the tree after all values have been updated.

title: Find the Maximum Divisibility Score
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays, `nums` and `divisors`. For each element in `divisors` you count how many numbers in `nums` are divisible by it; this count is its divisibility score. Find the divisor with the largest score, and if several divisors tie, choose the smallest among them. Output that divisor as a single integer.

title: Minimize the Total Price of the Trips
explanation_short: You are given a tree with n nodes, its edges, and a price for each node. A list of trips specifies start and end nodes, and each trip’s cost is the sum of the prices of the nodes on the chosen path between those two nodes. Before any trip you may select any set of nodes that are not directly connected and halve their prices. Return the smallest possible total cost of all trips after the optimal choice of nodes to discount.

title: Find the Array Concatenation Value
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers as input. Our task is to find the concatenation value of this array by repeatedly picking the first and last elements, concatenating them, and adding the result to a running total, until the array is empty. The output will be the final concatenation value. We need to determine the correct sequence of operations to achieve this.

title: Maximum Number of Integers to Choose From a Range I
explanation_short: We are given a list of banned integers, a range of integers from 1 to n, and a maximum allowed sum. Our task is to find the maximum number of integers we can choose from the range that are not banned and whose sum does not exceed the maximum allowed sum. The output will be the count of these chosen integers.

title: House Robber IV
explanation_short: We are given a list of houses with money in each one and a minimum number of houses to rob. The goal is to find the minimum amount of money that must be stolen from any one house in order to rob at least the specified number of houses, without stealing from adjacent homes. The input includes the list of money in each house and the minimum number of houses to rob. The output will be the minimum capability, or maximum amount stolen from any one house, out of all possible ways to meet the minimum number of houses requirement.

title: Split the Array to Make Coprime Products
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers and we need to find a way to split this array into two parts such that the products of the numbers in each part have no common factors other than 1. Our goal is to determine if such a split is possible and if so, find the minimum number of splits required. The input is the array of integers, and the output will be the minimum number of splits, or a special value if no such split exists.

title: Subsequence With the Minimum Score
explanation_short: We are given two strings, s and t, and we need to find the minimum possible score to make t a subsequence of s by removing characters from t. The input consists of these two strings, and the output will be the minimum score achieved. To get this score, we have to figure out the optimal way to remove characters from t so that the remaining characters form a subsequence of s. The goal is to minimize the score, which is calculated based on the positions of the removed characters in t.

title: Maximum Difference by Remapping a Digit
explanation_short: We are given an integer as input and need to find the difference between the maximum and minimum values that can be obtained by replacing exactly one digit with another. The goal is to determine the largest and smallest possible numbers that can be formed by remapping one digit. The output will be the difference between these two extreme values. We need to consider all possible remappings of a single digit to achieve this.

title: Substring XOR Queries
explanation_short: We are given a binary string and a set of queries, where each query contains two integers. Our task is to find the shortest substring of the binary string that, when converted to decimal and XORed with the first integer, equals the second integer. We need to return the start and end positions of this substring, or indicate if no such substring exists. The output will be a list of these positions for each query.

title: Rearranging Fruits
explanation_short: We are given two baskets, each containing a set of fruits with different costs. Our goal is to make the two baskets equal by possibly swapping fruits between them, and we need to find the minimum cost to do this. The baskets are considered equal if they contain the same fruits in the same quantities, regardless of order. The output will be the minimum cost to achieve this, or -1 if it's impossible to make the baskets equal.

title: Maximize Win From Two Segments
explanation_short: We are given a sorted list of prize positions on the X-axis and an integer k. Our goal is to find the maximum number of prizes we can collect by selecting two segments of length k. The output will be the total number of prizes we can win with the optimal selection of these two segments. We need to consider all possible combinations of segments to achieve this maximum.

title: Count the Number of Fair Pairs
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and two target numbers, lower and upper. Our task is to find the number of pairs in the array where the sum of the pair falls within the range defined by lower and upper. The input includes the array and the two target numbers, and the output will be the total count of such pairs that meet this condition.

title: Minimum Cost to Split an Array
explanation_short: We are given an integer array and a value k. Our task is to split the array into subarrays and calculate the minimum possible cost of the split, where the cost is determined by the sum of the importance value of each subarray. The importance value of a subarray is calculated by removing numbers that appear only once, then adding k to the length of the resulting subarray. The output will be the minimum cost of splitting the array.

title: Count Vowel Strings in Ranges
explanation_short: We are given a list of words and a set of queries, where each query specifies a range of indices in the list. Our task is to count the number of words within each specified range that start and end with a vowel. The output will be a list of counts, one for each query, representing the number of vowel strings found in the corresponding range.

title: Put Marbles in Bags
explanation_short: We are given a set of marbles with different weights and a certain number of bags. Our task is to divide these marbles into the bags in such a way that we can find the maximum and minimum possible total scores, where the score is calculated by summing the costs of all the bags. The output will be the difference between the maximum and minimum scores that can be achieved by distributing the marbles into the bags. We need to consider all possible distributions of marbles into the bags to find these scores.

title: Apply Bitwise Operations to Make Strings Equal
explanation_short: We are given two binary strings, s and target, of the same length. Our goal is to determine if we can make string s equal to target by performing a specific operation that involves replacing characters in s using bitwise operations. The input consists of these two binary strings, and the output is a boolean value indicating whether it's possible to make s equal to target. We need to find out if there's a sequence of operations that can transform s into target.

title: Maximum Sum With Exactly K Elements
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a number k. Our goal is to choose exactly k elements from the array in a way that maximizes their sum. The input consists of the array and the value of k, and the output will be the maximum sum that can be achieved by selecting k elements. We need to find the optimal selection of k elements to get the highest possible sum.

title: Calculate Delayed Arrival Time
explanation_short: We are given two times: the original arrival time of a train and the amount of time it has been delayed. We need to calculate the new arrival time by adding the delay to the original time. The input consists of two positive integers representing these times in 24-hour format. Our task is to find the new arrival time, also in 24-hour format, and return it as the output.

title: Sum Multiples
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer n, and we need to find the sum of all integers between 1 and n that are divisible by 3, 5, or 7. The input is the integer n, and the output is the sum of the numbers in the range [1, n] that meet this condition. Our task is to calculate this sum for a given value of n. The result will be an integer representing the total sum of the numbers that satisfy the divisibility condition.

title: Make Array Empty
explanation_short: We are given an array of distinct integers and can perform certain operations to empty it. Our goal is to determine the minimum number of operations required to make the array empty. The input is the array of integers, and the output is the number of operations it takes to empty the array. We need to find the most efficient way to remove all elements from the array. The result will be an integer representing the minimum number of operations needed.

title: Find the Prefix Common Array of Two Arrays
explanation_short: We are given two arrays of integers, A and B, which are permutations of numbers from 1 to n. We need to find a new array where each element at index i represents the count of numbers that appear at or before index i in both A and B. The output will be an array of these counts, giving us the prefix common array of A and B. The goal is to calculate this prefix common array based on the given input arrays A and B.

title: Maximum Number of Fish in a Grid
explanation_short: We are given a 2D grid representing water cells where a fisher can start and move to adjacent cells. The goal is to find the maximum number of fish that can be caught by choosing the optimal starting cell. The input is a 2D matrix, and the output is the maximum number of fish that can be caught, or 0 if no water cell exists. We need to determine the best starting point to achieve the highest catch.

title: First Completely Painted Row or Column
explanation_short: We are given a list of numbers and a matrix filled with the same numbers. Our task is to go through the list one by one and mark the corresponding cell in the matrix. We need to find the point at which either a full row or a full column in the matrix is completely marked. The output will be the position in the list where this happens.

title: Sliding Subarray Beauty
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and two parameters, the size of the subarray and the position of the negative integer to find. Our task is to calculate the "beauty" of each subarray, which is the xth smallest negative integer if it exists, or 0 if there are fewer than x negative integers. We need to find the beauty of all subarrays of a given size and return these values in an array. The output will contain the beauty of each subarray in order from the first index in the array.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to 1
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers and need to find the minimum number of operations to make all elements equal to 1. The operation involves replacing an element with the greatest common divisor of itself and another element in the array. Our goal is to determine the minimum number of these operations required to achieve an array of all 1s, or return -1 if it's impossible. The input is the array of positive integers, and the output is the minimum number of operations or -1 if not possible.

title: Design Cancellable Function
explanation_short: We are given a generator object that yields promises and we need to create a function that can handle these promises and also allow for cancellation of the task. The function should return a cancel function and a promise, where the cancel function can be used to stop the task and the promise will resolve or reject based on the outcome of the task. The input to our function is the generator object, and the output will be an array containing the cancel function and the promise. The promise will resolve with the final value returned by the generator or reject with any error that occurs during the task.

title: Determine the Winner of a Bowling Game
explanation_short: We are given two arrays representing the number of pins hit by two players in a bowling game. Our task is to determine which player wins the game by calculating their scores based on the number of pins hit in each turn. The output will be the number of the player who wins, either 1 or 2. We need to consider the scoring rules of bowling to calculate the total score for each player. The player with the higher score wins the game.

title: Minimum Cost of a Path With Special Roads
explanation_short: We are given a starting position and a target position in a 2D space, along with some special one-way roads that connect certain positions. Our goal is to find the minimum cost required to travel from the starting position to the target position, considering both normal movement and the use of special roads. The cost of movement is calculated as the sum of the absolute differences in x and y coordinates. We need to determine the most cost-effective path to reach the target position. The output will be the minimum cost required to make this journey.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
explanation_short: We are given a string and a positive integer, and we need to find the lexicographically smallest string that is larger than the given string and meets certain conditions. The input string is considered "beautiful" based on certain rules, and we need to find a new string that is also beautiful. The output will be the lexicographically smallest beautiful string that is larger than the input string, or an empty string if no such string exists. We need to compare strings character by character to determine which one is lexicographically larger.

title: Find the Score of All Prefixes of an Array
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array nums. For each prefix ending at index i, consider a conversion array where every element of the prefix is multiplied by 2, and the score of that prefix is the sum of those doubled values. Return an array ans of the same length where ans[i] holds the score of the prefix nums[0..i].

title: Minimum Additions to Make Valid String
explanation_short: You are given a string `word` that may contain the letters a, b, and c in any order. You may insert additional a, b, or c characters anywhere in the string. Your task is to determine the smallest number of insertions required so that the entire resulting string can be split into one or more consecutive copies of the exact pattern “abc”. Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Create Hello World Function
explanation_short: We are given no specific input, but rather a task to create a function. Our goal is to design this function so that it always returns the same message, regardless of any arguments it might receive. The output should be a simple greeting, and it should remain the same no matter what inputs are provided to the function. The function should be able to handle any number and type of arguments, but still produce the same consistent output.

title: Allow One Function Call
explanation_short: We are given a function and we need to create a new function that behaves the same way, but only allows the original function to be called once. The input is the original function and the new function will be called with various sets of arguments. Our goal is to ensure the original function is only executed once, and we need to return the result of that single function call. The output will be the result of the original function call, or nothing if the function has already been called.

title: Counter II
explanation_short: We're given an initial integer value and need to create an object with three functions that can modify this value. The goal is to return this object, which will allow us to increment, decrement, or reset the initial value. The input is the initial integer, and the output will be the modified values after a series of function calls. We need to find a way to implement these functions to produce the correct output values. The output will be a list of integers representing the modified values after each function call.

title: Find the Distinct Difference Array
explanation_short: We are given an array of numbers as input. Our task is to find the distinct difference array, where each element represents the difference between the number of distinct elements in the prefix and the number of distinct elements in the suffix of the array. The output will be an array of the same length as the input array, containing these distinct differences.

title: Make Costs of Paths Equal in a Binary Tree
explanation_short: We are given a perfect binary tree with nodes numbered from 1 to n, and each node has a cost associated with it. Our goal is to find the minimum number of increments needed to make the total cost of paths from the root to each leaf node equal. The input includes the number of nodes and an array of costs for each node, and the output will be the minimum number of increments required. We need to determine how to adjust the costs of the nodes to achieve equal path costs.

title: Number of Adjacent Elements With the Same Color
explanation_short: We're given an array of uncolored elements and a list of queries, where each query specifies an index and a color to paint that index. Our task is to process each query and determine the number of adjacent elements that have the same color after painting. The input consists of the array size and the list of queries, and the output will be an array where each element represents the count of adjacent elements with the same color after each query. We need to find this count for each query and return the results in an array.

title: Frequency Tracker
explanation_short: We are given a stream of values and need to design a system that can track how often each value appears. Our task is to create a data structure that can efficiently add, remove, and query the frequency of these values. The input will be a series of values and queries, and we need to output the frequency of specific values or confirm if a value has a certain frequency. The goal is to design a system that can handle these operations accurately and efficiently.

title: Chunk Array
explanation_short: We are given an array and a chunk size as input. Our task is to divide the array into smaller subarrays, each of a specified length, while keeping the original elements in order. The output will be a new array containing these subarrays, with the last one possibly being shorter than the specified size if the array length is not evenly divisible. We need to find a way to split the array into these chunks without using any external functions. The resulting array of subarrays is our desired output.

title: Generate Fibonacci Sequence
explanation_short:
You are given an integer `callCount` that tells how many times the generator will be asked for the next value.  
Your task is to provide a generator that produces the Fibonacci numbers in order, starting with 0 and 1.  
When the generator’s `next()` method is called `callCount` times, collect each returned value into a list.  
The output should be that list; if `callCount` is 0 the list is empty.

title: Nested Array Generator
explanation_short: You receive a nested array that may contain integers or other arrays, possibly many levels deep. Your task is to create a generator that walks through the structure from left to right, yielding every integer it meets in the same sequence as an inorder traversal would visit them. When the generator is exhausted, it should indicate completion, and the sequence of yielded values represents the required output.

title: Row With Maximum Ones
explanation_short: You are given a binary matrix `mat` with `m` rows and `n` columns. For each row you must count how many 1’s it contains and identify the row that has the largest such count. If several rows share the maximum count, choose the one with the smallest index. Return a two‑element array: the chosen row’s index followed by its number of 1’s.

title: Maximum OR
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a limit on the number of operations we can perform, where each operation involves doubling a number in the array. Our goal is to find the maximum possible result of performing a bitwise OR operation on all the numbers in the array after applying the operations. The input consists of the array and the operation limit, and the output is the maximum bitwise OR value that can be achieved. We need to determine how to strategically apply the operations to maximize this result.

title: Power of Heroes
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers representing the strength of heroes. Our goal is to find the sum of the power of all possible non-empty groups of heroes, where the power of a group is calculated based on the strength of its heroes. The power of each group is then added together and the result is returned modulo 10^9 + 7. The input array contains the strengths of the heroes, and the output will be the total sum of the powers of all groups.

title: Neighboring Bitwise XOR
explanation_short: We are given an array called "derived" which is formed by taking the bitwise XOR of adjacent values in another array called "original". Our task is to figure out if it's possible for such an "original" array to exist. We need to determine whether the given "derived" array could have been formed from a valid binary array. The output will be true if a valid "original" array exists, and false otherwise.

title: Count the Number of Complete Components
explanation_short: We are given a number of vertices and a list of connections between them. Our task is to find the number of groups of connected vertices where every vertex in the group is directly connected to every other vertex. The output will be the count of these fully connected groups.

title: Find the Losers of the Circular Game
explanation_short: We are given a number of friends sitting in a circle and a specific step size. The friends pass a ball to each other, moving a certain number of steps clockwise each time. We need to determine which friends will lose the game, meaning they will not be the last ones holding the ball when the game ends. The output will be a list of the losers, identified by their numbers in the circle.

title: Maximum Number of Moves in a Grid
explanation_short: We are given a grid of positive integers and can start at any cell in the first column. Our goal is to find the maximum number of moves we can make by traversing the grid. The output will be the highest number of moves possible. We need to determine the best starting point and path to achieve this maximum number of moves. The result will be an integer representing the maximum number of moves that can be performed.

title: Call Function with Custom Context
