explanation_short: We are given a function and an object, and we need to find a way to call the function with the object as its context. The function will receive the object and any additional arguments passed to it. Our goal is to return the result of the function call with the correct context set. The output will be the result of the function execution with the provided context and arguments.

title: Number of Senior Citizens
explanation_short: You receive an array where each element is a 15‑character string that encodes a passenger’s information, including their age. Your task is to determine how many of those passengers are strictly older than 60 years. Extract the age from each string, compare it with 60, and keep a tally of the qualifying passengers. The program should output that total count as an integer.

title: Return Length of Arguments Passed
explanation_short: We are given a function with a variable number of inputs, which can be of any type. Our task is to determine the total number of inputs passed to this function. The output will be the count of these inputs. For example, if we pass one value, the output should be 1, and if we pass multiple values, the output should be the total count of those values.

title: To Be Or Not To Be
explanation_short: We are given a value and need to create a function that tests if this value matches an expected result. The input is any type of value, and we need to find a way to compare it to another value. Our goal is to return an object that indicates whether the comparison was successful or not, with the output being either a confirmation of equality or an error message. The function should help developers verify if their code is working as intended.

title: Buy Two Chocolates
explanation_short: We are given a list of chocolate prices and an amount of money. Our goal is to buy two chocolates in a way that leaves us with some remaining money, and we want to minimize the cost of the chocolates we buy. The input includes the list of prices and the initial amount of money, and the output will be the amount of money we have left after making the purchase, or the initial amount if we can't afford to buy two chocolates without going into debt.

title: Compact Object
explanation_short: We are given an object or array that may contain falsy values, such as null, 0, or false. Our task is to remove any keys that have these falsy values, and do this for any nested objects or arrays as well. The output will be a new object or array that is the same as the original, but with all falsy values removed. We need to identify which values are falsy and remove their corresponding keys to create the compact object. The result should be a cleaned-up version of the input object or array.

title: Find the Punishment Number of an Integer
explanation_short: We are given a positive integer n as input. Our task is to find a specific value, known as the punishment number of n, by considering all integers from 1 to n and checking if they satisfy certain conditions. The output will be the sum of the squares of these integers that meet the specified criteria. We need to identify the relevant integers and calculate this sum to obtain the punishment number of n.

title: Extra Characters in a String
explanation_short: We're given a string and a list of words, and we need to break the string into substrings that match the words in the list. The goal is to find the minimum number of characters in the string that don't fit into any of these substrings. Our input is the string and the list of words, and our output will be the count of these extra characters. We want to find the optimal way to break the string to minimize this count.

title: Remove Trailing Zeros From a String
explanation_short: We are given a string that represents a positive integer. Our task is to remove any zeros that appear at the end of this string. The output will be the resulting string after removing the trailing zeros. We need to find a way to identify and remove these extra zeros to get the desired output.

title: Maximum Strength of a Group
explanation_short: We are given a list of student exam scores. Our goal is to find the maximum strength of a group that can be formed by selecting some or all of these students, where the strength is calculated by multiplying the scores of the selected students. The output will be the maximum possible strength of a group. We need to consider all possible combinations of students to determine the optimal group. The input list can contain both positive and negative scores, which will affect the overall strength of the group.

title: Modify Graph Edge Weights
explanation_short: We are given a weighted graph with some edges having unknown weights, represented by -1. Our goal is to assign positive integer values to these unknown weights so that the shortest distance between two specific nodes, the source and destination, equals a given target value. The input includes the graph's structure, the source and destination nodes, and the target distance. We need to find a way to modify the unknown weights to achieve the target distance and return the updated graph, or determine that it's impossible to do so. The output will be the modified graph or an empty array if no solution exists.

title: Greatest Common Divisor Traversal
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to find if it's possible to traverse between any two indices in the array. The condition for traversal between two indices is that the greatest common divisor of the numbers at those indices must be greater than 1. Our task is to determine if we can traverse between every pair of indices, and the output will be a boolean value indicating whether this is possible or not.

title: Difference of Number of Distinct Values on Diagonals
explanation_short: We are given a 2D grid of size m x n as input. Our task is to create a new matrix of the same size where each cell contains the difference between the number of distinct values on its main diagonal and anti-diagonal. The output will be this new matrix, calculated based on the diagonal values of each cell in the original grid. We need to find a way to efficiently calculate these diagonal values and their distinct counts.

title: Event Emitter
explanation_short: You are given two parallel arrays: one lists method names to call on an EventEmitter instance (e.g., “subscribe”, “emit”), and the other provides the arguments for each call. Your task is to mimic the behavior of the EventEmitter-record callbacks when “subscribe” is invoked and, when “emit” is called, execute all callbacks for that event (optionally passing an argument array) and collect their return values. For each method call you must produce a result entry: “subscribed” for a successful subscription and “emitted” together with the list of callback results for an emit. The final output is the sequence of these result entries matching the order of the input actions.

title: Sum in a Matrix
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed rectangular grid of integers. In each round you delete one element from every row – the element that is currently the largest in that row – and then add the biggest value among the deleted elements to your total score. The process repeats until all rows become empty. Return the accumulated score after the matrix is completely emptied.

title: Minimize String Length
explanation_short: We are given a string as input and need to minimize its length by performing certain operations. The goal is to find the shortest possible length of the string after these operations. Our task is to determine this minimum length. The output will be an integer representing the length of the minimized string. We need to figure out how to reduce the string length effectively.

title: Timeout Cancellation
explanation_short: We are given a function, an array of arguments, and a timeout in milliseconds. Our task is to return a cancel function that can be used to cancel the execution of the given function if invoked before the timeout. The goal is to either execute the function with the provided arguments after the specified delay or cancel its execution if the cancel function is invoked beforehand. The output will indicate whether the function was executed or cancelled.

title: Semi-Ordered Permutation
explanation_short: We are given a sequence of numbers from 1 to n. Our goal is to transform this sequence into a semi-ordered permutation, where the first number is 1 and the last number is n, by swapping numbers in the sequence. We need to find the minimum number of swaps required to achieve this. The output will be the minimum number of operations needed to make the sequence semi-ordered.

title: Maximum Strictly Increasing Cells in a Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a matrix with integer values, and we need to find the maximum number of cells that can be visited. The input is this matrix, and the task is to determine the longest path of strictly increasing cell values that can be traversed. The output will be the maximum number of cells that can be visited, starting from any cell in the matrix. We need to consider all possible starting cells and movement options to find this maximum.

title: Add Two Promises
explanation_short: We are given two promises that resolve with certain values after a specific amount of time. Our task is to create a function that takes these promises as input and returns a new promise that resolves with the sum of the values from the input promises. The output will be a promise that resolves with the total sum of the two input values.

title: Sum of Matrix After Queries
explanation_short: We are given a size 'n' and a list of queries where each query has a type, index, and value. We need to apply these queries to an 'n x n' matrix filled with zeros and find the total sum of integers in the matrix after all queries are applied. The queries can either add a value to a row or column in the matrix or replace all values in a row or column with a given value. Our goal is to calculate the sum of all integers in the matrix after these operations are performed.

title: Count of Integers
explanation_short: We are given two numeric strings and two integers representing minimum and maximum sums. Our task is to find the count of integers whose digit sum falls within the given range. The input includes the numeric strings and the sum limits, and we need to output the total count of such integers, adjusted to fit within a specific large number range. The goal is to determine how many integers meet this digit sum condition.

title: Sort By
explanation_short: We are given an array and a function that returns a number for each item in the array. Our task is to sort the array based on the numbers returned by this function. The sorted array should be in ascending order, meaning the items with the smallest returned numbers come first. The output will be a new array with the items sorted according to these rules.

title: Execute Asynchronous Functions in Parallel
explanation_short: We're given an array of asynchronous functions, each returning a promise. Our task is to execute all these functions in parallel and return a new promise that resolves or rejects based on the outcome of the individual promises. The input is the array of functions, and the output is a promise that provides information about the resolution or rejection of the promises, including the time it took and the values or error messages. We need to find a way to manage the execution of these functions and handle the resulting promises. The goal is to return a promise that reflects the overall outcome of the parallel execution.

title: Calculator with Method Chaining
explanation_short: We are given a sequence of mathematical operations and initial values. Our task is to design a class that can perform these operations in a chained manner, allowing us to add, subtract, multiply, divide, and exponentiate the initial value consecutively. The input includes the initial number and a series of operations with their corresponding values. We need to find the final result after all operations have been applied. The output will be the result of these consecutive operations.

title: Check if The Number is Fascinating
explanation_short: We are given a 3-digit integer as input. Our task is to determine if this number is fascinating by checking if the concatenation of the number and its multiples contains all digits from 1 to 9 exactly once, without any zeros. The output will be true if the number is fascinating and false otherwise. We need to find a way to verify this condition based on the given input number.

title: Neither Minimum nor Maximum
explanation_short: We are given an array of distinct positive integers as input. Our task is to find a number in the array that is neither the smallest nor the largest value, and return that number. If no such number exists, we need to return -1 as the output. The goal is to identify a middle-ground value, if it exists, and return it as the result.

title: Movement of Robots
explanation_short: We are given the initial positions of robots on a number line and their directions of movement. We need to find the sum of distances between all pairs of robots after a certain number of seconds, considering that they change direction when they collide. The input includes the initial positions and directions, as well as the time elapsed. The output is the total distance between all pairs of robots at that time, calculated modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Find the Longest Semi-Repetitive Substring
explanation_short: We're given a string of digits, and we need to find the longest substring where no more than one pair of adjacent digits are the same. The input is this digit string, and our goal is to determine the length of the longest substring that meets this condition. The output will be the length of this longest semi-repetitive substring. We'll be working with strings that only contain digits from 0 to 9.

title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Substring Operation
explanation_short: We are given a string of lowercase English letters as input. Our task is to perform a specific operation on a substring within this string to transform it into the lexicographically smallest possible string. The output will be this transformed string, which is the smallest alphabetically. We need to determine the optimal substring to operate on to achieve this result.

title: Collecting Chocolates
explanation_short: We are given an array of costs to collect different chocolates and a cost to perform an operation. Our goal is to find the minimum cost to collect all types of chocolates, considering we can perform the operation as many times as needed. The input includes the array of costs and the operation cost, and the output is the minimum total cost to collect all chocolates. We need to determine the optimal way to collect the chocolates, either by paying the initial cost or by performing operations to change the chocolate types.

title: Maximum Sum Queries
explanation_short: We are given two integer arrays and a set of queries, where each query has a target value for the first array and a minimum value for the second array. We need to find the maximum sum of corresponding elements from the two arrays that meet the query's conditions. The output will be an array of maximum sums, one for each query, or -1 if no such sum exists.

title: Total Distance Traveled
explanation_short: We are given the amount of fuel in a truck's main and additional tanks. We need to calculate the maximum distance the truck can travel, considering that fuel is transferred from the additional tank to the main tank under certain conditions. The truck's mileage is 10 km per liter, and fuel transfer occurs when 5 liters are used from the main tank. Our goal is to find the total distance traveled by the truck.

title: Find the Value of the Partition
explanation_short: We're given a list of positive integers and need to divide it into two separate lists. Our goal is to find the smallest possible difference between the largest number in the first list and the smallest number in the second list. The input is the list of integers, and the output will be the minimum difference achieved by partitioning the list in this way.

title: Special Permutations
explanation_short: We are given an array of distinct positive integers and need to find the total number of special permutations of these integers. A special permutation is defined by a specific condition that we must identify and apply to all possible arrangements of the integers. The input is the array of integers, and the output is the total count of special permutations, which will be returned modulo 10^9 + 7 to handle large results.

title: Painting the Walls
explanation_short: We are given two lists of numbers representing the costs and time taken to paint different walls. Our task is to find the minimum amount of money needed to paint all the walls using two painters, one paid and one free. The output will be the minimum total cost, considering the time taken by each painter to paint the walls. We need to determine how to assign the walls to the painters to achieve this minimum cost.

title: Minimum String Length After Removing Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a string s made up of only capital letters.  
You may repeatedly delete any occurrence of the two‑character patterns “AB” or “CD”; after each deletion the remaining parts of the string join together, possibly creating new deletable patterns.  
Your task is to keep applying such deletions until no more are possible and determine the smallest length the string can reach.  
Return that minimum possible length as an integer.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Palindrome
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s` made of lowercase letters. You may change any characters, but you must first achieve a palindrome using the fewest possible changes, and if several palindromes require that minimum number, you must pick the one that comes earliest in alphabetical order. Output the palindrome that satisfies these conditions.

title: Minimum Cost to Make All Characters Equal
explanation_short: The input is a binary string s of length n. You may repeatedly apply two kinds of operations-flipping a single character or flipping a prefix-each costing an amount that depends on the index used. The task is to find a sequence of operations that turns the entire string into all ‘0’s or all ‘1’s with the smallest possible total cost. Output that minimum cost as a single integer.

title: Array Wrapper
explanation_short:
You are given one or more integer arrays and a string indicating the operation to perform.  
Your task is to model each array with an object that behaves specially when combined or converted: adding two objects should yield the total of all numbers they contain, and converting an object to a string should produce a bracketed list of its elements.  
The program must return the value that results from applying the requested operation to the provided objects.  
The output is either a numeric sum or a quoted string representation, depending on the operation.

title: Is Object Empty
explanation_short: You receive a value that is either an object or an array, already parsed from JSON. Your task is to check whether that value contains any keys (for an object) or any items (for an array). Return the Boolean `true` if it has no keys or items, and `false` otherwise. The result tells you if the given structure is empty.

title: Longest Even Odd Subarray With Threshold
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a value `threshold`. From the array you must pick a contiguous segment that begins with an even number, then strictly alternates between odd and even, and where every element in the segment is ≤ `threshold`. Among all segments that satisfy these rules, you need to report the maximum possible length. If no such segment exists, the answer is 0.

title: Relocate Marbles
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` with the starting positions of the marbles, and two equal‑length arrays `moveFrom` and `moveTo`. For each index i, every marble that is currently at position `moveFrom[i]` is moved to position `moveTo[i]`. After all moves are applied, determine which positions contain at least one marble. Output those occupied positions as a sorted list.

title: Continuous Subarrays
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. A subarray is any non‑empty contiguous slice of this array, and it is considered *continuous* when it meets the specific condition described in the statement. Your task is to determine how many of these subarrays are continuous. Output that total as a single integer.

title: Longest Alternating Subarray
explanation_short: You’re given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. A subarray is alternating if each pair of neighboring elements differs by exactly 1 and the sign of the difference flips at every step (e.g., +1, ‑1, +1,…). Find the length of the longest such contiguous segment in `nums`, and output that length-or ‑1 if no alternating subarray exists.

title: Find the Maximum Achievable Number
explanation_short:
You are given two integers, num and t.  
A starting value x is called achievable if, by applying a certain operation no more than t times, you can turn x into num.  
Your task is to determine the greatest possible integer x that satisfies this condition.  
Print that maximum x as the answer.

title: Prime Pairs With Target Sum
explanation_short:
You receive a single integer n.  
You must find every unordered pair of prime numbers x and y such that x + y equals n.  
Return the collection of these pairs as a list of two‑element arrays, sorted by the first element of each pair in ascending order.  
If no such pairs exist, the result should be an empty list.

title: Decremental String Concatenation
explanation_short: We are given an array of strings and need to perform a series of join operations between them. The goal is to minimize the length of the final string after all operations are completed. The input is an array of strings, and the output is the minimum possible length of the final string. We need to find the optimal way to concatenate these strings while considering the rules of the join operation.

title: Partition String Into Minimum Beautiful Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a binary string `s`.  
You must split it into one or more contiguous pieces so that each piece, without leading zeros, is the binary representation of a power of 5.  
The task is to determine the smallest possible number of pieces that achieve this.  
If no such splitting exists, return ‑1.

title: Maximum Number of Jumps to Reach the Last Index
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` and an integer `target`. Starting at index 0, you may move to any later index `j` whose value differs from the current value by at most `target` (i.e., `|nums[j]‑nums[i]| ≤ target`). Your task is to determine the greatest possible number of such jumps that still lets you finish exactly at the last index `n‑1`. Return that maximum count, or `-1` if reaching the end is impossible.

title: Sum of Imbalance Numbers of All Subarrays
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. For each contiguous subarray, sort its elements and count how many adjacent positions in the sorted list have a gap larger than 1; this count is the subarray’s imbalance number. The task is to sum the imbalance numbers of all possible subarrays and return that total.

title: Apply Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to Zero
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`.  
You may repeatedly pick any contiguous segment of exactly `k` elements and reduce each of those `k` values by 1.  
Your task is to decide whether a sequence of such operations can turn every entry of `nums` into 0.  
Return **true** if it is possible and **false** otherwise.

title: Number of Black Blocks
explanation_short: You are given the dimensions m and n of a grid and a list of coordinates that mark black cells; every other cell is white. A block is any 2 × 2 sub‑grid, identified by its top‑left corner, and you must count how many black cells each block contains. For each possible count k (from 0 to 4) you need to determine how many blocks have exactly k black cells. Return these five counts in an array where the k‑th element corresponds to blocks with k black cells.

title: Longest Non-decreasing Subarray From Two Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of equal length. For each index you may choose either value from the first or the second array to form a new array, and you want that new array to contain the longest possible contiguous segment that never decreases. Return the length of that longest non‑decreasing subarray you can achieve.

title: Maximum Beauty of an Array After Applying Operation
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`.  
For each position you may change its value at most once to any number inside the interval `[nums[i]‑k, nums[i]+k]`.  
After performing any number of these changes, consider the longest subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) whose elements are all equal; its length is called the array’s beauty.  
Return the greatest possible beauty you can achieve.

title: Sum of Squares of Special Elements
explanation_short: You receive an integer array nums of length n, indexed starting at 1. An element nums[i] is “special” when the index i is a divisor of n (i.e., n % i == 0). Your task is to add together the squares of every special element. The output is a single integer equal to that total sum.

title: Check if Array is Good
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. First identify the largest value `n` in the array; the array would be “good” only if its length equals `n + 1`, every integer from 1 to `n‑1` appears exactly once, and the value `n` appears twice. Check whether these frequency conditions hold for the given `nums`. Return **true** if they do, otherwise return **false**.

title: Minimum Index of a Valid Split
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` that contains exactly one element occurring in more than half of the positions. You may cut the array after any index `i`, producing a left part `nums[0…i]` and a right part `nums[i+1…n‑1]`. A split is valid only when the same dominant element appears in both parts, each still holding a majority in its own subarray. Return the smallest index `i` that yields a valid split (or `-1` if none exists).

title: Length of the Longest Valid Substring
explanation_short: You receive a single string `word` and an array `forbidden` containing several short strings. A substring of `word` is considered valid when none of the strings in `forbidden` occur anywhere inside that substring. Your task is to find the greatest possible length of such a valid substring. Output that length as an integer.

title: Visit Array Positions to Maximize Score
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `x`. Starting at index 0, you may travel to other indices, collecting the value at each visited position; however, whenever you move from a number of one parity to a number of the opposite parity you lose `x` points. Your task is to choose a sequence of visits that yields the greatest possible total score, counting the initial value at index 0. Return that maximum achievable score as a single integer.

title: Largest Element in an Array after Merge Operations
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed array `nums` of positive integers. You may repeatedly pick an index `i` and replace the two adjacent elements `nums[i]` and `nums[i+1]` with their sum, shrinking the array by one each time. After performing any number of such merges, you want to know the greatest value that can appear as an element of the final array. The output is that maximum possible value.

title: Split Strings by Separator
explanation_short: You receive an array of strings `words` and a single character `separator`. Each string must be divided at every occurrence of the separator character. All resulting fragments that are not empty are gathered together. The function should return one flat array containing those fragments in their original order.

title: Sort Vowels in a String
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Identify all the vowel characters (a, e, i, o, u, in either case) that appear in `s`.  
Reorder only those vowels so that they appear in ascending ASCII order, while every consonant stays at its original position.  
Return the new string after this vowel‑only sorting is applied.

title: Count Paths That Can Form a Palindrome in a Tree
explanation_short: You are given a rooted tree described by a parent array (node 0 is the root) and a string s where s[i] is the label on the edge between node i and its parent. For every unordered pair of distinct nodes (u, v) consider the sequence of edge labels encountered on the unique path connecting them. You must count how many pairs produce a label multiset that can be rearranged into a palindrome (i.e., at most one character appears an odd number of times). The answer is a single integer – the total number of such node pairs.

title: Ways to Express an Integer as Sum of Powers
explanation_short:
You are given two positive integers n and x.  
You must count how many different sets of distinct positive integers exist such that the sum of each element raised to the x‑th power equals n.  
Each integer may appear at most once in a set, and the order of the numbers does not matter.  
Return that count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Maximum Number of Groups With Increasing Length
explanation_short: You are given an array usageLimits where usageLimits[i] tells how many times the integer i may appear in total. You must partition some of these integers into several groups, each group containing distinct numbers and the groups’ sizes strictly increasing from one to the next. The task is to determine the greatest possible number of such groups that can be formed without exceeding any usage limit. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Count Complete Subarrays in an Array
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` of positive integers. First identify the set of distinct values that appear anywhere in the whole array. A subarray (any contiguous, non‑empty segment) is considered “complete” if it contains every one of those distinct values at least once. Return the total number of such complete subarrays.

title: Number of Employees Who Met the Target
explanation_short: You receive an array `hours` where each element records how many hours a particular employee has worked, and a non‑negative integer `target` representing the minimum required hours. Your task is to determine how many entries in the array are greater than or equal to `target`. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Shortest String That Contains Three Strings
explanation_short: You are given three strings a, b and c. Your task is to construct the shortest possible string that has each of the three given strings appearing somewhere as a contiguous substring; if several strings achieve the minimal length, you must return the one that comes first in lexicographic order. Output that resulting string.

title: Insert Greatest Common Divisors in Linked List
explanation_short: You are given the head of a singly‑linked list where each node stores an integer. For every pair of consecutive nodes, a new node must be placed between them whose value is the greatest common divisor of the two original values. Return the head of the list after all such insertions have been performed.

title: Count Stepping Numbers in Range
explanation_short: You are given two positive integers `low` and `high`, each provided as a string. A stepping number is an integer whose every pair of neighboring digits differs by exactly 1, and it cannot start with a zero. Your task is to determine how many stepping numbers lie in the inclusive interval [`low`, `high`]. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Account Balance After Rounded Purchase
explanation_short: You receive a single integer `purchaseAmount` that tells how many dollars the item costs. First, round that amount to the nearest multiple of 10, then subtract the rounded value from the initial $100 balance. The result of this subtraction is the final account balance you must output as an integer.

title: Minimum Time to Make Array Sum At Most x
explanation_short:
You are given two equal‑length integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2` and an integer `x`.  
Each second you may pick an index `i`, set `nums1[i]` to 0, and add `nums2[j]` to every other position `j ≠ i`.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of seconds required so that the total sum of the updated `nums1` does not exceed `x`; if it is impossible, return ‑1.  
The output is a single integer representing that minimum time (or ‑1).

title: Maximum Elegance of a K-Length Subsequence
explanation_short:
You receive an array `items` where each element contains a profit and a category, plus an integer `k`.  
Select exactly `k` items in their original order to form a subsequence, then compute its elegance as the sum of the chosen profits plus the square of how many different categories appear in that subsequence.  
Return the largest possible elegance value among all such length‑`k` subsequences.

title: Minimum Seconds to Equalize a Circular Array
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed array `nums` of length `n`.  
Each second all positions are updated at once according to the rule described in the statement (each element can be replaced by a value taken from a neighboring index).  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of seconds required until every entry of the array holds the same value.  
Return that minimum number as an integer.

title: Check if it is Possible to Split Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a value `m`. Starting with the whole array, you may repeatedly pick any sub‑array of length at least two and cut it into two smaller sub‑arrays, but a cut is allowed only if both pieces satisfy the “good” condition defined by the problem. The task is to decide whether a sequence of such cuts can eventually break the original array down into exactly `n` single‑element arrays. Return **true** if this is possible, otherwise return **false**.

title: Faulty Keyboard
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s`. Imagine typing its characters one by one: each non‑`i` character is added to the end of the current text, while every time an `i` is typed the whole text built so far is reversed. After processing the entire string, the text that remains on the screen is the answer. Return that final string.

title: Double a Number Represented as a Linked List
explanation_short: You are given the head of a singly linked list where each node stores one digit of a non‑negative integer, with the most significant digit first and no leading zeroes. Your task is to compute the value of that integer multiplied by two. Return a linked list that represents the doubled number, preserving the same digit order and without extra leading zeros. The output is the head node of this resulting list.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `x`.  
Choose two positions `i` and `j` such that the distance between the indices satisfies `|i‑j| ≥ x`.  
Among all such pairs, look at the absolute difference of their values, `|nums[i]‑nums[j]|`, and find the smallest possible value.  
Return that minimum absolute difference as a single integer.

title: Apply Operations to Maximize Score
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` of `n` positive integers and an integer `k`. Starting from a score of 1, you may perform up to `k` operations; each operation selects a subarray, identifies the element with the highest number of distinct prime factors (breaking ties by the smallest index), and multiplies the current score by that element’s value. Your task is to choose the operations so that the final score is as large as possible. Return the maximum achievable score modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Max Pair Sum in an Array
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers `nums`. From this list you must pick a pair of numbers whose greatest digit (the largest digit appearing in each number) is identical, and among all such pairs choose the one with the highest possible sum. Return that maximum sum, or `-1` if no pair shares the same largest digit.

title: Find the Safest Path in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an n × n grid where cells containing 1 represent thieves and cells containing 0 are empty. Starting from the top‑left corner (0, 0) you may move up, down, left or right until you reach the bottom‑right corner (n‑1, n‑1). For any chosen path, its safeness factor is the smallest Manhattan distance between any cell on the path and any thief cell; you must find the greatest possible safeness factor among all such paths and output that integer.

title: Make String a Subsequence Using Cyclic Increments
explanation_short: You are given two lowercase strings, str1 and str2. You may pick any subset of positions in str1 and, at most once, shift each chosen character forward by one step in the alphabet (with z wrapping around to a). After performing this single operation, you need to check whether str2 appears as a subsequence of the modified str1. Return true if it is possible and false otherwise.

title: Sorting Three Groups
explanation_short:
You receive an array `nums` whose entries are only the values 1, 2, or 3.  
You may delete any number of elements, and the goal is to remove as few as possible so that the remaining sequence never decreases when read from left to right.  
In other words, after the deletions the array must be sorted in non‑decreasing order.  
Return the smallest count of deletions required to achieve this.

title: Check if a String Is an Acronym of Words
explanation_short:
You receive a list of words and a separate string s.  
You must decide whether s exactly matches the sequence you get by taking the first character of each word in the list, in order.  
Return true if it matches and false otherwise.

title: Maximize the Profit as the Salesman
explanation_short: You receive an integer n (the number of houses indexed 0 … n‑1) and a list of offers, each described by a start house, an end house, and a gold amount the buyer will pay for that whole interval. Your task is to pick a subset of these offers so that no two chosen intervals share any house and the sum of their gold values is as large as possible. Return that maximum total gold.

title: Count Pairs Whose Sum is Less than Target
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a target integer `target`.  
Count how many pairs of indices `(i, j)` with `i < j` satisfy `nums[i] + nums[j]` being strictly less than `target`.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Determine the Minimum Sum of a k-avoiding Array
explanation_short:
You are given two integers n and k.  
You must choose n different positive numbers so that no two of them add up to k.  
Among all such selections, find the one whose total sum is as small as possible.  
Return that minimum sum as the answer.

title: Number of Beautiful Integers in the Range
explanation_short: You receive three positive integers low, high, and k. For every integer between low and high (inclusive) you must check two things: the count of odd digits equals the count of even digits, and the number is divisible by k. Count how many numbers satisfy both conditions. Output that count as a single integer.

title: Find the Longest Equal Subarray
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`. You may remove up to `k` elements from the array, and after those deletions you want the longest possible contiguous segment whose remaining elements are all the same value. Return the length of that longest equal subarray.

title: Furthest Point From Origin
explanation_short: You receive a string `moves` of length n, where each character is either ‘L’, ‘R’, or ‘_’. Starting at position 0 on a number line, you must follow the moves in order, but for every ‘_’ you may choose to move left or right as you wish. After performing all n steps, determine the greatest possible distance from the origin that can be achieved. Output that maximum distance as an integer.

title: Find the Minimum Possible Sum of a Beautiful Array
explanation_short:
You are given two positive integers n and target.  
You must choose n different positive numbers so that no two of them add up to target.  
Among all such selections, find the one whose total sum is as small as possible.  
Return that minimum sum, taken modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Maximize Value of Function in a Ball Passing Game
explanation_short: You are given an array `receiver` of length `n` and an integer `k`. Choose any starting player `i` (0 ≤ i < n) and follow the chain i → receiver[i] → receiver[receiver[i]] … for exactly `k` passes, adding each visited index to a running total (indices may appear multiple times). Return the largest total that can be achieved by an optimal choice of the starting player.

title: Check if Strings Can be Made Equal With Operations II
explanation_short:
You are given two lowercase strings `s1` and `s2` that have the same length `n`.  
You may repeatedly perform the described operation on either string, swapping characters at chosen positions.  
Your task is to decide whether, after any number of such swaps, the two strings can become identical.  
Return **true** if it is possible and **false** otherwise.

title: Maximum Sum of Almost Unique Subarray
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` together with two positive integers `m` and `k`.  
Look at every contiguous subarray whose length is exactly `k`.  
A subarray qualifies as “almost unique” when it contains at least `m` distinct values, and among all qualifying subarrays you must find the one with the greatest total sum.  
Output that maximum sum, or 0 if no length‑`k` subarray satisfies the distinct‑element condition.

title: Minimum Operations to Form Subsequence With Target Sum
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` where each element is a non‑negative power of 2, and an integer `target`. In one operation you may replace a chosen element `x` by two copies of `x/2` (if `x` > 0). Your task is to find the smallest number of such operations that makes it possible to pick a subsequence of the resulting array whose sum equals `target`. Return that minimum count, or ‑1 if no sequence of operations can achieve the required sum.

title: Check if Strings Can be Made Equal With Operations I
explanation_short: You are given two lowercase strings `s1` and `s2`, each exactly four characters long. You may repeatedly pick any two positions in either string and swap the characters at those positions. Determine whether, after any number of such swaps, the two strings can become identical. Output “true” if it is possible and “false” otherwise.

title: Minimum Operations to Make a Special Number
explanation_short: You are given a string `num` that encodes a non‑negative integer. You may repeatedly delete any single digit from the string; deleting all digits leaves the number 0. Your task is to remove as few digits as possible so that the remaining number is divisible by 25. Return that minimum count of deletions.

title: Minimum Edge Weight Equilibrium Queries in a Tree
explanation_short:
You are given the number of nodes n, a list of n − 1 triples describing each tree edge (its two endpoints and its weight), and a list of queries where each query contains two nodes aᵢ and bᵢ.  
For every query you must determine the smallest number of edge‑weight modifications required so that all edges lying on the unique path between aᵢ and bᵢ end up having the same weight; one modification can change any edge’s weight to any value.  
The answer for each query is independent of the others, and you should return all of them in order.  
The output is an array of length m where the i‑th element is the minimum number of operations needed for the i‑th query.

title: Count Symmetric Integers
explanation_short: You are given two positive integers low and high. An integer with an even number of digits is called symmetric when the sum of its first half of digits equals the sum of its second half; numbers with an odd number of digits never qualify. Your task is to count how many symmetric integers lie within the inclusive interval [low, high]. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Determine if a Cell Is Reachable at a Given Time
explanation_short: You are given the starting cell (sx, sy), the target cell (fx, fy) and a non‑negative integer t. Each second you must move to one of the eight neighboring cells (including diagonals), and you may revisit cells any number of times. Return “true” if it is possible to be exactly at (fx, fy) after t seconds, otherwise return “false”.

title: Count K-Subsequences of a String With Maximum Beauty
explanation_short:
You receive a string s and an integer k.  
Consider every subsequence of s that is exactly k characters long and contains no repeated character; for each such subsequence, its “beauty” is the sum of how many times each of its characters appears in the original string.  
First determine the largest possible beauty among all these k‑subsequences, then count how many distinct subsequences attain that value.  
Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid
explanation_short: You receive a 3 × 3 integer matrix where each entry tells how many stones sit in that cell, and the total number of stones is exactly nine. In one move you may pick a single stone and shift it to a neighboring cell that shares a side. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of such moves needed so that every cell ends up containing exactly one stone. Return that minimum move count as an integer.

title: String Transformation
explanation_short: You are given two strings `s` and `t` of the same length `n` and an integer `k`. One operation is defined in the statement (you may choose a suffix of `s` and rearrange it in a specific way). Your task is to count how many different sequences of exactly `k` such operations turn the initial string `s` into the target string `t`. Return that count modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Points That Intersect With Cars
explanation_short: You are given a list of pairs, each pair describing the start and end positions of a car on a number line. Look at every integer coordinate that lies inside at least one of those intervals. Count how many distinct integer points are covered by any car and return that number.

title: Minimum Right Shifts to Sort the Array
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed array `nums` containing distinct positive integers. Your task is to determine the smallest count of right‑cyclic shifts (moving each element one position forward, with the last element wrapping to the front) that makes the array sorted in increasing order, or report ‑1 if no amount of shifting can achieve a sorted array. Output that minimum number of shifts (or ‑1).

title: Count Pairs of Points With Distance k
explanation_short: You receive an array where each element is a pair of integers representing a point’s x‑ and y‑coordinates, and an integer k. For every unordered pair of distinct points, compute the “distance” as the XOR of their x‑coordinates plus the XOR of their y‑coordinates. Count how many of those pairs have a distance exactly equal to k. Return that count as an integer.

title: Count of Interesting Subarrays
explanation_short: You are given an integer array nums and two integers modulo and k. For each contiguous non‑empty segment of the array, count the positions i inside it where nums[i] mod modulo equals k; call this count cnt. A segment is “interesting” when cnt mod modulo also equals k. Your task is to find how many interesting subarrays there are. Return that total as an integer.

title: Minimum Array Length After Pair Removals
explanation_short: You are given a non‑decreasing integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly apply a specific pair‑removal operation (details of the operation are defined in the statement) as many times as you like, possibly zero. Your task is to determine the smallest possible size the array can have after performing the operation optimally. Return that minimum length as an integer.

title: Sum of Values at Indices With K Set Bits
explanation_short: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. For each index of nums, write the index in binary and count its 1 bits. Add the array element to a running total whenever the index’s bit count equals k. The final sum is the required output.

title: Maximum Element-Sum of a Complete Subset of Indices
explanation_short: You are given a 1‑indexed array of integers. You must pick a set of positions so that the product of any two chosen indices is a perfect square. Among all such “complete” subsets, find the one whose selected numbers add up to the greatest total. Output that maximum sum.

title: Maximum Number of Alloys
explanation_short: You are given the number of metal types n, the number of machines k, a budget amount, a matrix composition where composition[i][j] tells how many units of metal j a single alloy from machine i requires, plus arrays stock (available units of each metal) and cost (price per unit of each metal). You may pick any one machine and, if needed, buy additional metal so that the total spending does not exceed the budget. The task is to determine the greatest integer x such that you can produce x alloys with the chosen machine using the initial stock and at most the given budget for purchases. Output that maximum x.

title: Happy Students
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` that encodes a property of each student. A group is any subset of the indices (including the empty set), and a student is happy if at least one of the two conditions given in the statement holds for that subset. Your task is to determine how many different groups make every student happy. Output that number as a single integer.

title: Maximum Odd Binary Number
explanation_short:
You receive a binary string `s` that contains at least one ‘1’.  
Your task is to reorder its characters so that the resulting binary number is odd (its last digit must be ‘1’) and as large as possible among all such reorderings.  
The output should be the reordered string, which may include leading zeros.  
In other words, place the bits to maximize the value while ensuring the final bit is ‘1’.

title: Beautiful Towers II
explanation_short: You are given an array maxHeights of length n, where each element is the highest allowed height for a tower placed at its index. Choose a height for every tower so that every height lies between 1 and its corresponding maxHeights value and the whole sequence forms a mountain – it can rise (or stay flat) up to a single peak and then fall (or stay flat) afterwards. Among all such “beautiful” configurations, compute the largest possible total of the chosen heights. Return that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Empty
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed array of positive integers. In each operation you may pick a single value and remove either two or three occurrences of that value from the array. Determine the smallest possible number of operations that empties the whole array, or return ‑1 if any value appears only once and thus cannot be removed. The output is a single integer representing that minimum count (or ‑1 when impossible).

title: Beautiful Towers I
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers where each value is the number of bricks in a consecutive tower. You may lower any tower by removing bricks, but you cannot add bricks. Adjust the heights so they never go down before a highest point (the peak may span several towers) and never go up after it, forming a mountain shape. Return the greatest possible sum of the tower heights after these removals.

title: Count Valid Paths in a Tree
explanation_short: You are given an integer n and a list of n‑1 edges that form an undirected tree whose nodes are labeled 1 to n. For any two distinct nodes a and b, consider the unique simple path connecting them. Count all unordered pairs (a, b) for which the nodes on their path contain exactly one prime‑numbered label. Return this count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Number of K-Divisible Components
explanation_short:
You are given a tree with n nodes numbered 0 to n‑1, described by the list edges, and each node i has an integer value values[i].  
A split is created by deleting any subset of edges, producing several connected components; the value of a component is the sum of the values of its nodes.  
Your task is to choose deletions so that every component’s total value is divisible by k and the number of resulting components is as large as possible.  
Return that maximum possible number of components.

title: Maximum Value of an Ordered Triplet I
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
For every triple of indices `i < j < k` you calculate the value `(nums[i] – nums[j]) × nums[k]`.  
Return the largest value obtained among all such ordered triplets.

title: Minimum Operations to Collect Elements
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers `nums` and an integer `k`. In each step you may take the last element of the array and place it into your collection. You must keep doing this until the collection holds all numbers 1, 2, …, `k`. Return the fewest steps needed to reach that condition.

title: Split Array Into Maximum Number of Subarrays
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` of non‑negative integers. For any contiguous segment of the array, its “score” is the bitwise AND of all numbers inside that segment. You must cut the whole array into several contiguous subarrays so that the sum of their scores is as small as possible, and among all such optimal partitions return the greatest possible number of subarrays. The output is a single integer – that maximum count.

title: Maximum Value of an Ordered Triplet II
explanation_short:
You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
Consider every triple of positions `i < j < k` and compute the value `(nums[i] − nums[j]) × nums[k]`.  
Your task is to determine the largest such value among all possible ordered triplets.  
Return that maximum value as the answer.

title: Count Visited Nodes in a Directed Graph
explanation_short: You are given an array edges where edges[i] specifies the single outgoing edge from node i in a directed graph of n nodes numbered 0 to n‑1. For each starting node i, you must follow the edges repeatedly until you encounter a node you have already visited, counting every distinct node visited along the way. The task is to compute, for every node i, how many different nodes are reached during this process. Return the results as an array answer where answer[i] holds the count for the start node i. The output array has length n and contains only non‑negative integers.

title: Minimum Size Subarray in Infinite Array
explanation_short: You receive a finite array `nums` and an integer `target`. Imagine an infinite sequence created by repeatedly concatenating `nums` to itself. Your task is to determine the smallest possible length of a contiguous sub‑segment in this infinite sequence whose elements add up exactly to `target`. Output that minimal length, or `-1` if no such subarray exists.

title: Minimum Edge Reversals So Every Node Is Reachable
explanation_short: We have a directed tree (a tree if we ignore edge directions) with n nodes, and for each node we must find the smallest number of edge flips that would make it possible to travel from that node to every other node following the directed edges. Think of every edge as having a “cost”: 0 if it already points away from the current node and 1 if it points toward it, because flipping it would be required. First compute the total cost when node 0 is the root by a simple DFS that sums these costs, then reuse that information in a second DFS that “re‑roots” the tree: moving the root from a parent to a child changes the answer by +1 if the edge was originally outward (now needs a flip) or –1 if it was inward (the flip is no longer needed). This rerooting DP gives the answer for every node in linear time.

title: Divisible and Non-divisible Sums Difference
explanation_short: You receive two positive integers n and m. Consider all numbers from 1 through n and separate them into two groups: those that are not divisible by m and those that are divisible by m. Compute the sum of each group, call them num1 and num2 respectively, and then find the difference num1 minus num2. Output that single integer result.

title: Apply Operations to Make Two Strings Equal
explanation_short:
You are given two binary strings s1 and s2 of the same length n and an integer x.  
You may repeatedly change s1 by either flipping a single position (cost 1) or flipping two positions i and j simultaneously (cost x).  
Your task is to determine the smallest total cost that makes s1 identical to s2, or report -1 if no sequence of operations can achieve equality.  
The answer is a single integer representing that minimum cost (or -1).

title: Apply Operations on Array to Maximize Sum of Squares
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`. You may repeatedly pick two positions `i` and `j`, replace `nums[i]` with the bitwise AND of the two values and `nums[j]` with their bitwise OR. After any number of such operations, you must select exactly `k` elements from the resulting array and compute the sum of their squares. Return the largest possible sum, taken modulo 10⁹ + 7.

title: Last Visited Integers
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` that contains positive integers and some entries equal to `-1`. For every `-1` you must identify the most recent positive integer that appeared earlier in the array, following the described simulation of “seen” values. The answer is an array listing those identified integers in the order the `-1` positions occur.

title: Minimum Processing Time
explanation_short:
You are given two arrays: `processorTime`, where each element tells when a processor becomes free, and `tasks`, whose length is exactly four times the number of processors, each element being the duration of a task.  
Each processor has four cores, so you must assign every task to a distinct core of some processor, and a core can be used only once.  
For any assignment, a processor finishes when the latest of its four tasks (its start time plus the task’s duration) is done; the overall completion time is the maximum finish time among all processors.  
Return the smallest possible overall completion time achievable by an optimal assignment.

title: Shortest and Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
explanation_short: You are given a binary string `s` and a positive integer `k`. A substring of `s` is called beautiful when it contains exactly `k` characters `'1'`. First find the smallest length of any beautiful substring, then among all beautiful substrings of that length choose the one that is lexicographically smallest. Return that substring, or an empty string if no beautiful substring exists.

title: Longest Unequal Adjacent Groups Subsequence II
explanation_short: You’re given two parallel arrays of length n: `words`, a list of strings, and `groups`, a list of integers. You must pick a subsequence of the index list 0…n‑1 so that every pair of consecutive chosen indices satisfies the required constraints (their group values are different, and when the two strings have equal length their Hamming distance meets the condition). The objective is to make this subsequence as long as possible. Return the strings from `words` that correspond to the selected indices, in the same order. Any longest valid subsequence is acceptable.

title: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference II
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and two integers `indexDifference` and `valueDifference`. Find any two positions `i` and `j` (they may be equal) such that the distance between the indices is at least `indexDifference` and the distance between the values `nums[i]` and `nums[j]` is at least `valueDifference`. Return the pair as a two‑element array `[i, j]`; if no such pair exists, return `[-1, -1]`. Any valid pair is acceptable.

title: Longest Unequal Adjacent Groups Subsequence I
explanation_short: You are given two parallel arrays of equal length - `words`, a list of distinct strings, and `groups`, a binary list. Choose a subsequence of `words` so that the corresponding entries in `groups` never repeat consecutively (adjacent values must differ). The subsequence should be as long as possible. Return any one of the longest valid subsequences as an array of strings.

title: Minimum Sum of Mountain Triplets I
explanation_short: You are given an array nums of integers. A mountain triplet is a choice of three indices i < j < k such that nums[j] is greater than both nums[i] and nums[k]. Your task is to determine the smallest possible sum nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] among all mountain triplets, or output -1 if no such triple exists. The result is a single integer representing that minimum sum (or -1).

title: Construct Product Matrix
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer matrix grid with n rows and m columns. For each position (i, j) you must compute the product of every element in grid that does **not** lie in row i or column j. Place each of those products into a new matrix p that has the same dimensions as grid. The result p is returned as the output.

title: Minimum Changes to Make K Semi-palindromes
explanation_short: You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`. You must split the string into exactly `k` consecutive pieces and, for each piece, count how many letters would need to be altered so that the piece becomes a semi‑palindrome (a string that can be turned into a palindrome by following its repeating pattern). The goal is to choose the partition that makes the total number of required changes as small as possible. Return that minimum total number of changes.

title: Minimum Number of Changes to Make Binary String Beautiful
explanation_short: You are given a binary string `s` whose length is even. You may change any character of `s` from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0. The goal is to make the string “beautiful,” meaning it can be split into consecutive substrings where each piece satisfies the required pattern (as in the examples). Return the smallest possible number of character changes needed to achieve this.

title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares I
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. For every non‑empty contiguous subarray, count how many different numbers appear, square that count, and add the result to a running total. The final answer is the sum of those squared distinct‑element counts for all subarrays.

title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares II
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`.  
For every non‑empty contiguous subarray, count how many unique values it contains.  
Take the square of each subarray’s distinct‑value count and sum all those squares.  
Output the resulting sum modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Find Maximum Number of String Pairs
explanation_short: We are given an array of distinct strings. Our task is to find the maximum number of pairs that can be formed from these strings, where a pair consists of two strings that are reverses of each other. The output will be the largest possible number of such pairs that can be created from the given array of strings.

title: Construct the Longest New String
explanation_short: We are given three types of strings: "AA", "BB", and "AB", with x, y, and z quantities of each. Our goal is to select and arrange these strings to form a new string that does not contain "AAA" or "BBB" as a substring. The task is to find the maximum possible length of this new string. The output will be the length of the longest string that can be constructed under these conditions.

title: Interval Cancellation
explanation_short: We are given a function, its arguments, and an interval time. We need to call this function immediately with the given arguments and then repeatedly at the specified interval until a cancellation function is invoked after a certain delay. The output will be a record of each function call, including the time it was made and the result. The goal is to create this cancellation function that stops the repeated calls after the specified delay.

title: Join Two Arrays by ID
explanation_short: We are given two arrays, each containing objects with an id field. We need to merge these arrays into a new array, combining objects with the same id and sorting the result by id in ascending order. The output will be a new array with unique id values, where objects with matching ids have their properties merged. If an id only appears in one array, its object will be included in the result without modification.

title: Ways to Split Array Into Good Subarrays
explanation_short: We're given a binary array as input, and we need to find the number of ways to split it into subarrays that each contain exactly one element with the value 1. The goal is to count all possible splits that meet this condition. The output will be the total count of such splits, and since the number can be large, we'll return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Count Zero Request Servers
explanation_short: We are given the total number of servers, a list of server requests with their corresponding times, a time interval length, and a list of query times. We need to find the number of servers that did not receive any requests during a specific time interval for each query time. The output will be a list of server counts, where each count represents the number of servers with no requests during the specified time interval.

title: Find a Good Subset of the Matrix
explanation_short: We are given a binary matrix with rows and columns, and we need to find a subset of rows where the sum of each column is at most half of the total number of rows in the subset. The input is this binary matrix, and the output will be a list of row indices that form a "good" subset, sorted in ascending order. If no such subset exists, the output will be an empty list. Our goal is to identify a subset of rows that meets this condition and return the corresponding row indices.

title: Number of Beautiful Pairs
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to find the number of pairs of indices where the first digit of the number at the first index and the last digit of the number at the second index are coprime, meaning they have no common factors other than 1. The input is the array of integers, and the output is the count of such pairs. We need to examine each possible pair of indices in the array to determine if they meet this condition.

title: Robot Collisions
explanation_short: We are given information about multiple robots, including their positions, health, and movement directions on a line. Our task is to determine the health of the robots that survive after all possible collisions have occurred. The input includes the initial positions, health, and directions of the robots, and the output will be an array containing the health of the remaining robots in their original order. We need to consider how the robots interact with each other when they collide and how their health changes as a result.

title: Minimum Operations to Make the Integer Zero
explanation_short: We are given two integers, num1 and num2, and we need to find the minimum number of operations required to make num1 equal to 0. In each operation, we can subtract a value calculated using num2 and a chosen integer i from num1. Our goal is to determine the smallest number of these operations needed to reach 0, or conclude that it's impossible to do so, in which case we return -1. The result will be the minimum number of operations or -1 if it's not possible.

title: Length of the Longest Subsequence That Sums to Target
explanation_short:
You receive an array `nums` and an integer `target`.  
Your task is to determine the maximum possible length of a subsequence (elements kept in their original order, possibly skipping some) whose elements add up exactly to `target`.  
Return that length, or `-1` if no subsequence with sum `target` exists.

title: Find the K-or of an Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. For each binary digit position, count how many numbers in `nums` have a 1 there. The result’s bit is set to 1 exactly when that count is at least `k`; otherwise it stays 0. Return the integer represented by those resulting bits.

title: Count of Sub-Multisets With Bounded Sum
explanation_short:
You are given a 0‑indexed array `nums` of non‑negative integers and two integers `l` and `r`.  
Consider every possible sub‑multiset of `nums`-any collection where each value may be taken from 0 up to its total occurrences in the array-and count those whose element sum lies in the inclusive interval [l, r].  
Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference I
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums` and two integers `indexDifference` and `valueDifference`. Find any two indices `i` and `j` (they may be the same) such that the absolute distance between the indices is at least `indexDifference` and the absolute difference between `nums[i]` and `nums[j]` is at least `valueDifference`. Return the pair as a two‑element array `[i, j]`. If no such pair exists, output `[-1, -1]`.

title: Minimum Sum of Mountain Triplets II
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums`.  
Choose three positions `i < j < k` so that the middle element is larger than both the left and right elements (`nums[i] < nums[j]` and `nums[k] < nums[j]`).  
Among all such “mountain” triples, find the one whose three numbers add up to the smallest possible total.  
Return that minimum sum, or `-1` if no qualifying triple exists.

title: Minimum Number of Groups to Create a Valid Assignment
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers, each representing the number printed on a ball. Your task is to divide all the balls into some number of boxes so that every box holds balls of only one number and the counts of balls in any two boxes differ by no more than one. The goal is to use as few boxes as possible while respecting those two rules. Return that minimum number of boxes.

title: Find Champion II
explanation_short: We are given a number of teams and a list of directed edges representing which teams are stronger than others. Our task is to find the team that has no other team stronger than it, which will be the champion. If there is only one such team, we return its number, otherwise, we return -1 as the champion is not unique. The input includes the number of teams and the edges between them, and the output is the champion team's number or -1.

title: Find Champion I
explanation_short: We are given a tournament with multiple teams and a matrix showing which teams are stronger than others. Our task is to determine the champion team, which is the team that is stronger than all other teams. The input is a 2D boolean matrix representing the tournament results, and the output is the number of the champion team. We need to analyze the matrix to find the team that has no other team stronger than it.

title: Minimum Increment Operations to Make Array Beautiful
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a target value k. Our goal is to find the minimum number of operations needed to make the array "beautiful", where an array is considered beautiful if its maximum element in any subarray of size 3 or more is greater than or equal to k. The output will be the minimum number of increment operations required to achieve this.

title: Minimum Equal Sum of Two Arrays After Replacing Zeros
explanation_short: We are given two arrays of positive integers, some of which may be zeros. Our task is to replace the zeros with positive integers so that the total sum of both arrays is equal. We need to find the smallest possible sum that can be achieved in this way. The output will be this minimum equal sum, or -1 if it's impossible to make the sums equal.

title: Maximum Score After Applying Operations on a Tree
explanation_short: We are given a tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and their corresponding values. Our goal is to find the maximum score we can obtain by choosing nodes to include in our score, while ensuring the tree remains healthy, meaning the sum of values on the path from the root to any leaf node is not zero. The input consists of the tree's edges and node values, and the output is the maximum achievable score.

title: Maximum Points After Collecting Coins From All Nodes
explanation_short: We are given a tree with nodes containing coins and an integer k. Our goal is to find the maximum points we can get by collecting all the coins from the tree nodes, following certain rules for collecting coins from each node. The input includes the tree structure, the number of coins at each node, and the value of k. We need to determine the optimal way to collect coins to maximize the points. The output will be the maximum points that can be achieved after collecting all the coins.

title: Distribute Candies Among Children II
explanation_short: We are given two positive integers, the total number of candies and the maximum number of candies each child can get. Our task is to find the total number of ways to distribute the candies among 3 children without exceeding the limit for each child. The output will be the total count of these possible distributions. We need to consider all combinations that satisfy the given conditions.

title: Distribute Candies Among Children I
explanation_short: We are given two numbers, the total number of candies and a limit on how many candies each child can get. Our task is to find the total number of ways to distribute the candies among 3 children without exceeding the limit for any child. The output will be the total count of these possible distributions. We need to consider all combinations that satisfy the given conditions.

title: Maximum Balanced Subsequence Sum
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to find a subsequence with a certain balance property. The balance property is related to the difference in indices of consecutive elements in the subsequence. Our goal is to find the subsequence that satisfies this balance property and has the maximum sum. The output will be the maximum sum of such a balanced subsequence.

title: Number of Strings Which Can Be Rearranged to Contain Substring
explanation_short: We are given a length, and we need to find the total number of strings of that length that can be rearranged to contain a specific substring "leet". The input is an integer representing the length of the strings, and the output is the total count of such strings, adjusted to fit within a certain range by taking the result modulo 109 + 7. The goal is to calculate this count for a given length.

title: Maximum Spending After Buying Items
explanation_short: We are given a matrix representing the values of different items in various shops, with each shop having items sorted in non-increasing order of value. Our goal is to find the maximum amount of money that can be spent by buying all items from the shops. The input is the matrix of item values, and the output is the total maximum spending. We need to determine the optimal order of buying items to achieve this maximum spending.

title: High-Access Employees
explanation_short: You are given a list of records, each containing an employee’s name and a timestamp in “HHMM” format. For each employee we need to check whether there exists any one‑hour interval that contains at least three of their access times. All employees that satisfy this condition should be collected. Return their names sorted in alphabetical order.

title: Minimum Operations to Maximize Last Elements in Arrays
explanation_short: You are given two integer arrays of the same length. You may repeatedly choose an index i and swap the values at position i in the two arrays. The task is to make the last element of each array the greatest value that appears in its own array, using the fewest possible swaps. Return that minimum number of swaps, or -1 if the goal cannot be achieved.

title: Find Words Containing Character
explanation_short: We are given a list of words and a specific character. Our task is to identify the words that contain this character and return their corresponding indices. The input includes the list of words and the character to search for, and the output will be a list of indices where the character is found. The order of the indices in the output does not matter.

title: Maximum Strong Pair XOR II
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. From this array you must consider every pair of elements `(x, y)` that satisfies the strong‑pair condition described in the statement (a pair may consist of the same element twice). For each allowed pair compute the bitwise XOR of `x` and `y`. The answer is the maximum XOR value among all such strong pairs.

title: Maximum Strong Pair XOR I
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed integer array `nums`. A pair `(x, y)` taken from the array is called strong if it satisfies the condition described in the statement. Choose any two elements (the same element may be used twice) that form a strong pair and compute their bitwise XOR. Return the largest XOR value achievable among all strong pairs.

title: Minimum Number of Coins for Fruits
explanation_short: We are given a list of prices for different fruits, where each price represents the number of coins needed to buy that fruit. Our goal is to find the minimum number of coins required to acquire all the fruits, considering that buying certain fruits can give rewards. The input is the list of prices, and the output is the minimum number of coins needed. We need to determine the optimal way to buy the fruits to minimize the total cost.

title: Maximum Xor Product
explanation_short: We are given three integers, a, b, and n, and we need to find the maximum value of the product of two expressions, (a XOR x) and (b XOR x), where x is a number between 0 and 2^n. Our goal is to determine the value of x that results in the largest product. The output will be the maximum product value. We have to consider all possible values of x within the given range to find the optimal solution.

title: Separate Black and White Balls
explanation_short: We are given a string of 0s and 1s, representing white and black balls. Our task is to find the minimum number of swaps needed to move all the black balls to the right and all the white balls to the left.
