The input is this string of 0s and 1s, and the output will be the minimum number of swaps required to achieve this separation. We need to determine the fewest swaps to group the balls by color.

title: Count Beautiful Substrings I
explanation_short: We are given a string and a positive integer. Our task is to find the number of non-empty substrings in the string that meet certain conditions, specifically related to the count of vowels and consonants. The output will be the total count of these substrings, which are referred to as "beautiful substrings". We need to consider the relationship between vowels, consonants, and the given integer to determine which substrings are beautiful.

title: Maximize Area of Square Hole in Grid
explanation_short: We are given a grid with horizontal and vertical bars, and two lists of removable bars. Our task is to find the maximum area of a square-shaped hole that can be created by removing some of these bars. The input includes the grid size and the lists of removable horizontal and vertical bars. We need to determine the largest possible square area that can be formed after removing bars. The output will be the maximum area of this square-shaped hole.

title: Find Building Where Alice and Bob Can Meet
explanation_short: We are given an array of building heights and a list of queries, where each query represents the current locations of Alice and Bob. We need to find the leftmost building where Alice and Bob can meet, considering they can only move to a building that is taller than their current one. The output will be an array of building indices where Alice and Bob can meet, or -1 if no such building exists.

title: Find Maximum Non-decreasing Array Length
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and can perform operations to replace any subarray with its sum. Our goal is to find the maximum length of a non-decreasing array that can be achieved after applying these operations. The input is the integer array, and the output is the maximum length of a non-decreasing array that can be made. We need to determine the optimal way to apply the operations to achieve the longest non-decreasing array.

title: Matrix Similarity After Cyclic Shifts
explanation_short: We are given a matrix with integer values and a number of steps, k. The task is to determine if the matrix remains the same after applying a specific shifting process k times. The input is the original matrix and the number of steps, and the output is a boolean value indicating whether the final modified matrix is identical to the original one. We need to find out if the matrix returns to its original state after the specified number of shifts.

title: Make Three Strings Equal
explanation_short: You receive three non‑empty strings s1, s2 and s3. In each move you may delete the last character of any one of the strings, but you cannot delete all characters from a string. Your task is to determine the smallest number of such deletions needed so that all three strings become identical, or report -1 if no sequence of deletions can achieve equality. The answer you return is that minimum count (or -1).

title: Make Lexicographically Smallest Array by Swapping Elements
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers and a limit value. Our goal is to make the array as small as possible in lexicographical order by swapping elements, but only if the difference between the two elements being swapped is within the given limit. The output will be the rearranged array that is lexicographically smallest. We need to determine the sequence of swaps that achieves this.

title: Find the Peaks
explanation_short: We are given an array representing a mountain, and we need to find the indices of the peaks in this array. A peak is an element that is strictly greater than its neighboring elements. Our task is to identify these peaks and return their indices in any order. The output will be an array of indices where the peaks are located in the input array.

title: Count Beautiful Substrings II
explanation_short: We are given a string and a positive integer. Our task is to find the number of non-empty substrings in the string that meet certain conditions, specifically having an equal number of vowels and consonants, and a specific mathematical relationship with the given integer. The output will be the total count of these "beautiful" substrings. We need to examine each possible substring and determine whether it meets the required conditions.

title: Remove Adjacent Almost-Equal Characters
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase English letters and need to find the minimum number of changes required to remove all instances of adjacent characters that are either identical or next to each other in the alphabet. The input is this string, and the output will be the minimum number of operations needed. Our goal is to transform the string so that no two adjacent characters are almost-equal, and we can achieve this by changing individual characters to any lowercase letter. The result will be the smallest number of changes required to meet this condition.

title: Count the Number of Infection Sequences
explanation_short: We are given a line of people with some already infected, represented by their positions in the array. Our task is to determine the number of different orders in which the uninfected people can become infected, considering that infection spreads from an infected person to an adjacent uninfected person. The input includes the total number of people and the positions of the initially infected individuals. We need to find the total count of these unique infection sequences, and the result should be provided modulo 10^9+7. The output will be the number of different infection sequences possible.

title: Length of Longest Subarray With at Most K Frequency
explanation_short: We're given an array of integers and a limit, k, on how many times each number can appear. Our task is to find the longest subarray, which is a contiguous sequence of numbers, where each number appears no more than k times. The output will be the length of this longest subarray. We need to examine all possible subarrays to determine which one meets the condition and is the longest.

title: Find Missing and Repeated Values
explanation_short: We are given a 2D matrix with numbers ranging from 1 to n squared, where n is the size of the matrix. Our task is to identify a number that appears twice and another number that is missing from the matrix. The input is this 2D matrix, and we need to find the repeating and missing numbers. The output will be an array of two numbers, where the first number is the one that appears twice and the second number is the one that is missing.

title: Double Modular Exponentiation
explanation_short: We are given a 2D array of variables and a target number. Each variable is a set of four numbers that are used in a specific mathematical formula to calculate a result. We need to find the indices of the variables where this formula equals the target number. The output will be an array of these indices, which can be in any order.

title: Count Tested Devices After Test Operations
explanation_short: We are given a list of devices with their battery percentages. Our task is to simulate testing each device in order, following specific rules, and determine how many devices will be tested. The input is the list of battery percentages, and the output is the total number of devices that can be tested after going through the list. We need to keep track of the devices that have enough battery to be tested.

title: Count Subarrays Where Max Element Appears at Least K Times
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a positive integer k. Our task is to find the number of subarrays, which are contiguous sequences of elements, where the maximum element appears at least k times. The output will be the count of such subarrays. We need to consider all possible subarrays and determine which ones meet the specified condition. The result will be the total number of subarrays that satisfy this requirement.

title: Count the Number of Good Partitions
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our task is to find the total number of ways to divide this array into one or more contiguous subarrays such that no two subarrays contain the same number. The output will be the total count of these divisions, and since the count can be large, we need to return it modulo 1 billion plus 7.

title: Number of Possible Sets of Closing Branches
explanation_short: We are given a company with multiple branches connected by roads of varying lengths. Our task is to find the number of possible sets of branches that can be closed while ensuring the remaining branches are within a certain maximum distance from each other. The input includes the number of branches, the maximum allowed distance, and the road connections between branches. The output will be the total count of such possible sets of closing branches.

title: Count the Number of Incremovable Subarrays I
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our task is to find the total number of subarrays that can be removed to make the remaining array strictly increasing. The output will be the count of such subarrays, considering all possible contiguous sequences of elements within the array.

title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equalindromic
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and need to find the minimum cost to make all elements in the array equal to the same palindromic number. The cost is calculated as the sum of the absolute differences between each element and the target palindromic number. Our goal is to determine this minimum cost. The output will be an integer representing the minimum possible total cost.

title: Apply Operations to Maximize Frequency Score
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and a limit on the number of operations we can perform, where each operation involves changing a number in the array. Our goal is to maximize the frequency of the most common element in the array by performing these operations. The input consists of the array and the operation limit, and the output is the highest frequency we can achieve. We need to find the optimal way to modify the array to get the best possible score.

title: Find Polygon With the Largest Perimeter
explanation_short: We are given a list of positive integers representing potential side lengths of a polygon. Our task is to find the largest possible perimeter of a polygon that can be formed using these side lengths, ensuring that the longest side is smaller than the sum of the other sides. The output will be the largest possible perimeter, or -1 if it's not possible to create a polygon. We need to determine which combination of side lengths will yield the largest perimeter while meeting the conditions for a valid polygon.

title: Minimum Number Game
explanation_short: We are given an array of integers and an empty array. Alice and Bob take turns removing numbers from the given array and appending them to the empty array, following specific rules. We need to determine the final state of the empty array after all numbers have been moved. The input is the array of integers, and the output is the resulting array after the game is played. The goal is to find the arrangement of numbers in the resulting array.

title: Find Number of Coins to Place in Tree Nodes
explanation_short: We are given a tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and the cost assigned to each node. Our task is to determine the number of coins to be placed at each node based on the size of its subtree. The input includes the tree structure and node costs, and we need to find an array where each element represents the number of coins to be placed at the corresponding node. The output will be an array of size n, where each element is the number of coins placed at the respective node.

title: Count the Number of Incremovable Subarrays II
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers as input. Our task is to find the total number of subarrays that can be removed to make the remaining array strictly increasing. The output will be the count of such subarrays, considering all possible contiguous sequences of elements within the array.

title: Maximum Square Area by Removing Fences From a Field
explanation_short: We are given a rectangular field with horizontal and vertical fences, represented by the arrays hFences and vFences. Our goal is to find the maximum area of a square field that can be formed by removing some of these fences. The input includes the field's dimensions (m and n) and the locations of the fences, and we need to output the maximum square area that can be achieved, or -1 if it's impossible to form a square field. The result should be returned modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Minimum Cost to Convert String II
explanation_short: We are given two strings, source and target, as well as lists of original and changed substrings with their corresponding conversion costs. Our goal is to find the minimum cost to transform the source string into the target string by replacing substrings with their changed versions. The output will be the minimum total cost of these transformations, or -1 if it's impossible to achieve the target string.

title: Minimum Cost to Convert String I
explanation_short: We are given two strings, source and target, and some rules to change characters in the source string. Our goal is to find the minimum cost to transform the source string into the target string by applying these character change rules. The input includes the source and target strings, as well as the character change rules with their associated costs. The output will be the minimum total cost to achieve this transformation, or -1 if it's impossible.

title: Find Longest Special Substring That Occurs Thrice II
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase English letters, and we need to find the length of the longest substring that consists of only one character and appears at least three times in the string. The input string can contain various characters, and we're looking for a repeated pattern of the same character. Our goal is to determine the length of this longest repeated pattern, or return -1 if no such pattern exists. The output will be the length of the longest special substring that meets these conditions.

title: Find Longest Special Substring That Occurs Thrice I
explanation_short: We're given a string of lowercase English letters and need to find the longest substring that consists of only one character and appears at least three times. The input string can contain various characters, and we must identify the longest special substring that meets the occurrence criteria. Our goal is to determine the length of this longest special substring, and if no such substring exists, we'll output -1 as the result.

title: Palindrome Rearrangement Queries
explanation_short: We are given a string and a set of queries, where each query specifies two substrings that can be rearranged. Our task is to determine whether it's possible to make the entire string a palindrome by rearranging these substrings. The input includes the string and the queries, and the output will be an array of boolean values indicating whether a palindrome can be formed for each query.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make X and Y Equal
explanation_short: We are given two positive integers, x and y. Our goal is to find the minimum number of operations needed to make x equal to y, where we can increment or decrement x by 1, or divide x by a certain number. The output will be the smallest number of operations required to achieve this equality. We need to determine the most efficient sequence of operations to transform x into y.

title: Maximum Area of Longest Diagonal Rectangle
explanation_short: We are given a 2D array where each sub-array represents the dimensions of a rectangle. Our task is to find the rectangle with the longest diagonal and calculate its area. The input array contains pairs of length and width for each rectangle, and we need to determine which rectangle has the longest diagonal. The output will be the area of the rectangle with the longest diagonal.

title: Minimum Moves to Capture The Queen
explanation_short: We are given the positions of three chess pieces on an 8x8 board, including a black queen and two white pieces. Our goal is to determine the minimum number of moves required to capture the black queen using the white pieces. The input consists of six integers representing the positions of these pieces, and we need to find the shortest sequence of moves to achieve the capture. The output will be the minimum number of moves needed to capture the queen.

title: Maximize the Number of Partitions After Operations
explanation_short: We are given a string and an integer, and we can change one character in the string if needed. Our goal is to divide the string into the maximum number of partitions, with each partition having a limited number of unique characters. The output will be the maximum number of partitions we can achieve after making at most one change to the string.

title: Count Elements With Maximum Frequency
explanation_short: We're given an array of positive integers and need to find the total count of elements that appear with the highest frequency. The frequency of an element is how many times it appears in the array. Our task is to identify the elements with the maximum frequency and return their total count. The output will be the sum of the counts of these elements.

title: Minimum Number of Coins to be Added
explanation_short: You are given a list of coin values and an integer target. A value x is considered obtainable if some subsequence of the list adds up exactly to x. Your task is to find the smallest number of additional coins (you may choose any values) that must be inserted so that every integer from 1 through target becomes obtainable. Return that minimum count.

title: Maximum Number That Sum of the Prices Is Less Than or Equal to K
explanation_short: We are given two integers, k and x, and we need to find the largest number whose accumulated price is less than or equal to k. The price of a number is determined by the count of set bits at specific positions in its binary representation. Our task is to determine this largest number, known as the greatest cheap number. The output will be the greatest cheap number that meets the given condition.

title: Find Common Elements Between Two Arrays
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays, nums1 of length n and nums2 of length m. For each element in nums1, check whether that value appears anywhere in nums2 and count how many positions satisfy this condition; call this count answer1. Do the same in reverse: count the positions in nums2 whose values exist in nums1 to get answer2. Return the two counts as a two‑element list [answer1, answer2].

title: Divide Array Into Arrays With Max Difference
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` whose length is a multiple of 3 and a positive integer `k`.  
Your task is to split all the elements of `nums` into groups of exactly three numbers each, such that in every group the difference between the largest and smallest element does not exceed `k`.  
If you can form such groups, output a two‑dimensional array containing any valid grouping; otherwise output an empty array.

title: Count Complete Substrings
explanation_short:
You are given a string `word` and an integer `k`.  
A substring is counted if every character that appears inside it occurs exactly `k` times, and the distinct letters in the substring form a consecutive block in the alphabet (the alphabetical gap between any two neighboring letters is at most 2).  
Your task is to determine how many such substrings exist in `word`.  
Return that number as a single integer.

title: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word II
explanation_short: We are given a string of lowercase English letters as input. Our task is to find the minimum number of times keys on a telephone keypad need to be pushed to type this string, considering that the keys can be remapped to different collections of letters. The output will be the total minimum number of pushes required to type the entire string. We need to determine the optimal mapping of letters to keys to achieve this minimum number of pushes.

title: Check if Bitwise OR Has Trailing Zeros
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` containing positive integers. Your task is to decide whether you can pick two or more of those numbers so that, after applying the bitwise OR operation to the chosen elements, the resulting binary number ends with at least one zero bit. Return **true** if such a selection exists; otherwise return **false**.

title: Count the Number of Houses at a Certain Distance II
explanation_short: You are given three positive integers n, x and y. The city has houses numbered 1 to n and streets that connect each house i to i+1 as well as additional streets defined by the distances x and y. For every ordered pair of distinct houses you must determine the length of the shortest possible route between them, then count how many pairs have each possible distance k (1 ≤ k ≤ n). Return an array of length n where the k‑th entry is the number of ordered pairs whose shortest distance equals k.

title: Number of Changing Keys
explanation_short:
You receive a single string `s` that represents the sequence of characters a user typed.  
A “key change” occurs whenever two adjacent characters come from different letters, ignoring case (so ‘a’ followed by ‘A’ does not count).  
Your task is to count how many such changes happen throughout the whole string.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Alice and Bob Playing Flower Game
explanation_short: You are given two integers n and m. Consider all ordered pairs (x, y) where x is the number of flowers clockwise from Alice to Bob (1 ≤ x ≤ n) and y is the number anticlockwise (1 ≤ y ≤ m). Count how many of these pairs make the total number of flowers between them (x + y) odd. Output that count as a single integer.

title: Minimize OR of Remaining Elements Using Operations
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a limit `k` on how many operations you may perform. In one operation you choose two neighboring positions, remove those two numbers, and insert a single value equal to the bitwise AND of the chosen pair. After doing at most `k` such operations, the array will be shorter; you must make the bitwise OR of all remaining elements as small as possible. The answer to output is that minimum achievable OR value.

title: Find the Maximum Number of Elements in Subset
explanation_short: You are given an array of positive integers `nums`. From these numbers you must choose as many elements as possible and reorder them so that for every three consecutive elements `a, b, c` in the new order the relation `a × c = b` holds. The task is to determine the greatest possible size of such a subset. Return that maximum count as a single integer.

title: Type of Triangle
explanation_short: You receive an array of three integers representing potential side lengths. First, you must decide whether those lengths satisfy the triangle inequality; if they do not, the answer is “none”. If they do form a triangle, compare the lengths: all equal means “equilateral”, exactly two equal means “isosceles”, and all different means “scalene”. The result should be returned as a single string.

title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People I
explanation_short: You are given a list of n points, each described by its integer x and y coordinates. For every ordered pair of distinct points (A, B), check whether A lies strictly to the left of B (i.e., x_A < x_B) and also strictly above B (i.e., y_A > y_B). Count how many such pairs satisfy both conditions. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Ant on the Boundary
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` of non‑zero integers that represent the ant’s moves: a positive value moves it right, a negative value moves it left. Starting at the boundary (position 0), the ant processes the elements in order, updating its position after each step. Your task is to determine how many times, after completing a step, the ant’s position is exactly back at the boundary. Return that count as an integer.

title: Find the Grid of Region Average
explanation_short: You receive an m × n grid of grayscale values (0‑255) and a non‑negative threshold. A region is any 3 × 3 subgrid whose adjacent pixels differ by at most the threshold; its average intensity is the floor of the mean of its nine values. For each pixel, you collect the floor‑averaged values of all regions that contain it, compute their floor‑average, and use that as the pixel’s new value (or keep the original value if the pixel belongs to no region). The output is the resulting m × n grid of these new intensities.

title: Minimum Time to Revert Word to Initial State I
explanation_short: You receive a string `word` and an integer `k`. Every second you must delete the first `k` characters of the current string and then append `k` characters of your choice to its end; the string evolves after each step. Find the smallest positive number of seconds after which the string is exactly the same as the original `word`, and output that minimum time.

title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People II
explanation_short: You are given a list of n distinct integer points on a plane. Choose two of them to be Alice’s and Bob’s positions, with Alice required to be the upper‑left corner (higher y and lower x) and Bob the lower‑right corner (lower y and higher x) of an axis‑aligned rectangle. The rectangle-including its border-must contain no other given points. Count how many ordered pairs of points satisfy this condition and return that number.

title: Minimum Time to Revert Word to Initial State II
explanation_short: You are given a string `word` and an integer `k`. Each second you must delete the first `k` characters of the current string and then append exactly `k` characters of your choice to its end. You need to find the smallest positive number of seconds after which the string returns to its original form. Output that minimum time as an integer.

title: Number of Subarrays That Match a Pattern I
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a second array `pattern` whose elements are only –1, 0, or 1.  
A subarray of `nums` whose length is one more than `pattern` matches when, for every position k, the relationship between the k‑th and (k+1)‑th numbers in the subarray is decreasing if `pattern[k] = -1`, equal if `pattern[k] = 0`, and increasing if `pattern[k] = 1`.  
Your task is to count how many such subarrays exist in `nums`.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Palindromes After Operations
explanation_short: You receive an array `words` containing `n` lowercase strings. You may repeatedly pick any two positions-possibly in the same string-and swap the characters located there. After performing any number of such swaps, you want as many strings as possible to read the same forward and backward. The task is to compute the greatest possible number of palindrome strings you can obtain. Return that maximum count as an integer.

title: Number of Subarrays That Match a Pattern II
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a shorter array `pattern` whose elements are only ‑1, 0, or 1.  
A subarray of `nums` whose length is one more than the length of `pattern` matches when, for every position k, the relation between the k‑th and (k+1)‑st elements of the subarray follows the sign indicated by `pattern[k]` (‑1 means “greater than”, 0 means “equal to”, 1 means “less than”).  
Your task is to count how many such subarrays exist in `nums`.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Modify the Matrix
explanation_short:
You are given an m × n integer matrix indexed from 0.  
Create a copy of this matrix, then look at every cell that contains -1.  
For each such cell, find the largest number that appears anywhere in the same column of the original matrix and put that number in the copy instead of -1.  
Return the modified copy as the answer matrix.

title: Maximum Number of Operations With the Same Score I
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. You may repeatedly pick two elements, remove them, and record a “score” for that operation; every operation you perform must produce exactly the same score. The task is to determine the greatest possible number of such pair‑removals you can carry out before fewer than two elements remain. Return that maximum count as an integer.

title: Apply Operations to Make String Empty
explanation_short: You are given a single string `s`. Repeatedly apply the prescribed operation (as illustrated in the statement) until the string becomes empty. Your task is to report what the string looks like just before the final operation that clears it. The output should be that intermediate string, enclosed in quotes.

title: Maximize Consecutive Elements in an Array After Modification
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed array of positive integers. First you may raise the value of any element by at most one, then you pick one or more elements whose values become consecutive when sorted (e.g., 3, 4, 5). The task is to make this chosen group as large as possible. Output the greatest possible number of elements in such a consecutive set.

title: Maximum Number of Operations With the Same Score II
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums`. You may repeatedly remove any two elements, and each removal has a score equal to the sum of the two deleted numbers. Your goal is to choose deletions so that every operation you perform yields the same score, and to maximize how many such operations you can carry out before the array becomes too short. Return the largest possible number of operations that satisfy this equal‑score condition.

title: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs I
explanation_short: You receive a list of strings indexed from 0. For each pair of indices (i, j) with i < j, check whether the string at i appears both at the very beginning and at the very end of the string at j. Count how many such pairs satisfy this condition. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
explanation_short: You are given two arrays of positive integers, arr1 and arr2. For every pair formed by taking one number from arr1 and one from arr2, look at the decimal representation of the two numbers and find the longest sequence of leading digits they share. Return the greatest length of such a common prefix among all pairs, or 0 if no pair shares any leading digit.

title: Most Frequent Prime
explanation_short: You are given a 0‑indexed m × n matrix of single‑digit numbers. From every cell you may travel in a straight line (any of the eight directions) and concatenate the visited digits to form numbers, stopping only when you leave the matrix. Among all numbers larger than 10 that are prime, you must identify the one that occurs most frequently; if several primes share the highest frequency, return the largest of them. Output that prime, or -1 if no prime greater than 10 can be formed.

title: Find the Largest Area of Square Inside Two Rectangles
explanation_short: You are given two integer matrices, each of length n; the i‑th row of the first matrix gives the bottom‑left corner (aᵢ, bᵢ) and the i‑th row of the second gives the top‑right corner (cᵢ, dᵢ) of a rectangle whose sides are parallel to the axes. From all regions where at least two of these rectangles overlap, determine the side length of the biggest square that can be placed completely inside such a region. Return the square’s area, or 0 if no overlapping region can contain a square at all.

title: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs II
explanation_short: You receive a list of strings called words. For every pair of indices i < j, you need to check whether the string at i is simultaneously a prefix and a suffix of the string at j. Count all pairs that satisfy this condition, and output the total number as an integer.

title: Split the Array
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` whose length is even. You must decide whether the elements can be divided into two groups of exactly half the size each, with the requirement that no number appears more than once inside either group. If such a division exists, the answer is `true`; otherwise it is `false`. The output is a single Boolean value.

title: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array II
explanation_short: We are given a string and two specific substrings, along with a maximum distance. Our task is to find all indices in the string where the first substring appears and there is also an occurrence of the second substring within the specified distance. The output will be a sorted list of these indices, known as beautiful indices.

title: Minimize Length of Array Using Operations
explanation_short: We are given an array of positive integers and need to minimize its length by performing a specific operation any number of times. The operation involves selecting two elements, inserting their remainder at the end, and then deleting the selected elements. Our goal is to find the minimum possible length of the array after performing this operation. The output will be an integer representing this minimum length.

title: Earliest Second to Mark Indices I
explanation_short: You are given two 1‑indexed integer arrays, nums (length n) and changeIndices (length m). Initially none of the n positions are marked, and at each second s (1 ≤ s ≤ m) you may either decrement any element of nums by one or, if the element at the index changeIndices[s] is already zero, mark that index. Your task is to pick actions so that all positions become marked as early as possible. Return the smallest second in [1, m] when this can be achieved, or –1 if it is impossible.

title: Earliest Second to Mark Indices II
explanation_short: You’re given an integer array `nums` of length n and another array `changeIndices` of length m. Initially every position in `nums` is unmarked, and at each second s (1 ≤ s ≤ m) you may either apply the allowed change to the element at index `changeIndices[s]` (such as setting it to zero or decreasing it) or, if that element is already zero, mark that index. Choose the operations so that all indices become marked as early as possible. Return the smallest second in [1, m] when this can be achieved, or –1 if it is impossible.

title: Minimum Operations to Exceed Threshold Value I
explanation_short: You are given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `k`. In each step you may delete one occurrence of the current smallest value in the list. You must keep deleting until every remaining element is at least `k`. Return the smallest number of deletions needed to achieve this condition.

title: Minimum Operations to Exceed Threshold Value II
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a threshold value `k`. In each operation you may modify the array according to the rule described in the statement (which can only be applied while the array has at least two elements). Your task is to determine the smallest number of such operations required so that every element remaining in `nums` is at least `k`. The answer is a single integer representing that minimum count. If the array already satisfies the condition, the answer is 0.

title: Count Pairs of Connectable Servers in a Weighted Tree Network
explanation_short: You are given a weighted tree described by an array edges, where each entry contains two server indices and the length of the edge between them, plus an integer signalSpeed. For every server c, we must count how many unordered pairs of distinct servers (a, b) have a path that goes through c and satisfies the connectability rule that depends on the edge weights and signalSpeed. The result is an integer array count of size n, where count[i] stores the number of such pairs for server i. The array is returned as the final output.

title: Find the Maximum Sum of Node Values
explanation_short: You are given an undirected tree with n nodes, described by the list edges, and an array nums where nums[i] is the value of node i. A single operation lets you pick any edge [u, v] and replace both nums[u] and nums[v] with their XOR with the given integer k; you may apply this operation repeatedly on any edges. Your task is to determine the largest possible total sum of all node values after any sequence of such operations. Output that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Count Submatrices with Top-Left Element and Sum Less Than k
explanation_short: You receive a 0‑indexed integer matrix `grid` and an integer `k`. Your task is to count how many submatrices that include the cell at the top‑left corner of the grid have a total sum that does not exceed `k`. Return that count as an integer.

title: Minimum Operations to Write the Letter Y on a Grid
explanation_short: You receive an odd‑sized n × n grid whose entries are 0, 1, or 2. A “Y” consists of the two diagonal arms that meet at the middle column and the vertical stem that continues down from the intersection. You may change any cell to any of the three values, and you must make every cell that belongs to the Y share one common value while every other cell shares a different common value. Return the smallest number of such cell‑changes required.

title: Distribute Elements Into Two Arrays I
explanation_short: You receive a list of distinct integers called `nums`. The first element goes into `arr1`, the second into `arr2`, and for each subsequent element you compare the current last values of `arr1` and `arr2`; you append the element to the array whose last value is larger (if `arr1`’s last is larger, put it in `arr1`, otherwise in `arr2`). After all `n` operations, you form the final output by writing the contents of `arr1` followed by the contents of `arr2`. The output is a single array representing this concatenated order.

title: Distribute Elements Into Two Arrays II
explanation_short: You are given a 1‑indexed integer array `nums`. Starting with the first element placed in `arr1` and the second in `arr2`, you then process each subsequent element in order, deciding whether to append it to `arr1` or `arr2` based on the number of existing elements that are strictly greater than the current value in each array and, if those counts tie, on which array is shorter. After all `n` elements have been distributed, you form the final array by writing all elements of `arr1` followed by all elements of `arr2`. Return this concatenated array as the result.

title: Apple Redistribution into Boxes
explanation_short: You are given an array apple where each element tells how many apples are in a pack, and another array capacity where each element is the maximum number of apples a box can hold. You may split the apples from any pack across multiple boxes. Your task is to choose as few boxes as possible so that the sum of their capacities is at least the total number of apples in all packs. Output that minimum number of boxes; if all boxes are needed, the answer equals the length of capacity.

title: Maximize Happiness of Selected Children
explanation_short: You are given an array happiness of length n and a positive integer k. You must choose k children one after another; after each selection, every unchosen child’s happiness decreases by 1 but never becomes negative. The task is to arrange the selections so that the sum of the happiness values of the k chosen children is as large as possible. Return that maximum possible sum.

title: Find the Sum of Encrypted Integers
explanation_short: You receive an array of positive integers. For each integer, look at its digits, find the biggest digit, and rewrite the number so that every position contains that biggest digit. Add up all of those rewritten numbers and output the total sum.

title: Maximum Strength of K Disjoint Subarrays
explanation_short: You are given an integer n, an odd positive integer k, and an array nums of length n. You must choose exactly k subarrays that do not overlap, respecting the order of the original array (the end of each chosen subarray must come before the start of the next one). The goal is to make the sum of all elements inside the selected subarrays as large as possible. Output that maximum achievable total sum.

title: Shortest Uncommon Substring in an Array
explanation_short: You receive an array arr of n non‑empty strings. For each string you must find the shortest substring that does not occur in any of the other strings in the array. If multiple substrings have the same minimal length, you choose the lexicographically smallest one; if no such substring exists, you output an empty string for that position. The result is an array of these substrings, ordered correspondingly to the original input.

title: Replace Question Marks in String to Minimize Its Value
explanation_short: You are given a string s that consists of lowercase letters and ‘?’ characters. Each ‘?’ must be replaced by any lowercase letter so that the total “cost” – defined as, for every position, the number of earlier identical letters – is as small as possible. Return the fully‑filled string; if several fillings achieve the minimum cost, output the lexicographically smallest one.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make String K-Special
explanation_short: You receive a lowercase string `word` and an integer `k`. You may delete any characters; the goal is to make the remaining string “k‑special,” meaning the frequency of every pair of distinct letters differs by no more than `k`. Return the smallest possible number of deletions required to achieve this.

title: Find the Sum of the Power of All Subsequences
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`.  
For each possible subsequence of `nums`, count how many of its own subsequences have a sum exactly equal to `k`; this count is the subsequence’s “power”.  
Add together the powers of all subsequences of `nums`.  
Return the total modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Count Substrings Starting and Ending with Given Character
explanation_short:
You receive a string `s` and a single character `c`.  
Consider every possible contiguous piece of `s` (a substring) and check whether its first and last characters are both `c`.  
Count how many such substrings exist.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Existence of a Substring in a String and Its Reverse
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
You must check whether there exists any two‑character substring of `s` that also appears somewhere in the reversed version of `s`.  
If such a substring can be found, the answer is `true`; otherwise the answer is `false`.

title: Mark Elements on Array by Performing Queries
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` of positive integers and a list of queries, each query containing an index `i` and a number `k`. Starting with every element unmarked, for each query you first mark the element at position `i` and then additionally mark the `k` smallest values among the still‑unmarked elements. After performing these markings, you compute the sum of all elements that remain unmarked. The required output is an array where the `j`‑th entry is the sum after the `j`‑th query has been applied.

title: Minimum Moves to Pick K Ones
explanation_short: You are given a binary array nums, an integer k indicating how many ones must be collected, and a non‑negative integer maxChanges that caps how many modifications you may make to the array. Alice can start at any index, instantly pick up a one if it’s there, and then repeatedly perform one allowed action per move to eventually gather exactly k ones. Your job is to find the smallest possible number of moves required to do this while respecting the maxChanges limit. Output that minimum move count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Length Substring With Two Occurrences
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Your task is to determine the greatest possible length of a contiguous piece of that string which occurs at least twice somewhere within `s` (the two occurrences may overlap).  
Report that maximum length as an integer.  
If no substring appears twice, the answer is 0.

title: Apply Operations to Make Sum of Array Greater Than or Equal to k
explanation_short: You receive a single integer k. Starting from an array that contains only the number 1, you may apply the allowed operations any number of times, and you must achieve a total sum of the array that is at least k. Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of operations needed to reach that sum, and output that minimum count.

title: Longest Common Suffix Queries
explanation_short: You receive two lists of strings: `wordsContainer` and `wordsQuery`. For each string in `wordsQuery` you must pick the element of `wordsContainer` that shares the longest suffix with it; if several candidates tie, choose the one with the smallest length, and if a tie still remains, pick the earliest occurrence in `wordsContainer`. Return an array where the i‑th entry is the index of the selected string for `wordsQuery[i]`.

title: Most Frequent IDs
explanation_short:
You are given two integer arrays `nums` and `freq` of the same length `n`.  
At step `i` you insert `freq[i]` copies of the ID `nums[i]` (if `freq[i]` is positive) or remove that many copies (if `freq[i]` is negative) from the collection.  
After each step you must report how many copies the most frequent ID currently has, using 0 when the collection is empty.  
Return an array `ans` of length `n` where `ans[i]` holds this count for step `i`.

title: Minimum Levels to Gain More Points
explanation_short: You receive a binary array `possible` where each entry tells whether a level can be cleared (1) or is impossible (0). Alice plays a contiguous prefix of the levels and Bob plays the remaining suffix, and both try to maximize their own scores (gaining +1 for a clearable level and ‑1 for an impossible one). You must determine the smallest number of levels Alice can take so that, under optimal play, her total points exceed Bob’s; if no such split exists, return ‑1. The answer is the length of that prefix (at least 1) or ‑1.

title: Shortest Subarray With OR at Least K II
explanation_short:
You receive an array `nums` of non‑negative integers and an integer `k`.  
Your task is to locate the smallest‑length contiguous subarray whose bitwise OR of all its elements is at least `k`.  
Return that length, or `-1` if no such subarray exists.

title: Shortest Subarray With OR at Least K I
explanation_short:
You receive an array `nums` of non‑negative integers and an integer `k`.  
A subarray is “special” when the bitwise OR of all its elements is at least `k`.  
Your task is to determine the smallest length of any non‑empty special subarray.  
Return that length, or `-1` if no such subarray exists.

title: Water Bottles II
explanation_short: You are given two integers: `numBottles`, the count of full water bottles you start with, and `numExchange`, the number of empty bottles required to obtain one new full bottle. Each time you drink a bottle you keep its empty container, and whenever you have at least `numExchange` empties you may trade exactly `numExchange` of them for one additional full bottle (you cannot split a batch into multiple trades). Your task is to figure out the greatest total number of bottles you can drink by repeatedly drinking and exchanging under these rules. Return that maximum as a single integer.

title: Count Alternating Subarrays
explanation_short:
You receive a binary array `nums`.  
A subarray is considered alternating when each pair of neighboring elements inside it are different.  
Your task is to count how many subarrays of `nums` satisfy this alternating condition.  
Return that count as a single integer.

title: Find the Sum of Subsequence Powers
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`.  
For every subsequence of `nums` that contains exactly `k` elements, find its power – the smallest absolute difference between any two numbers in that subsequence – and add all those powers together.  
Return the total sum modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Minimize Manhattan Distances
explanation_short: You are given a list of points, each described by its integer x and y coordinates. For any two points the distance is measured with the Manhattan metric (|x₁‑x₂| + |y₁‑y₂|). You must choose exactly one point to delete so that, after its removal, the largest Manhattan distance among all remaining pairs of points is as small as possible. The required output is that minimal possible value of the maximum distance.

title: Longest Strictly Increasing or Strictly Decreasing Subarray
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers called nums.  
Your task is to look at every contiguous segment of the array and consider only those segments where the numbers strictly go up or strictly go down.  
Among all such segments, determine the maximum length that any of them can have.  
Return that length as a single integer.

title: Harshad Number
explanation_short: You receive a single integer x. First, find the sum of all its decimal digits. If x can be divided evenly by that digit‑sum, the required result is the digit‑sum itself; otherwise the result is –1. The output is just this single integer.

title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Operations With Constraint
explanation_short: You are given a lowercase string `s` and an integer `k`. You may replace any characters of `s` with any other lowercase letters, and each replacement contributes a “distance” equal to the forward cyclic difference between the original and new letters (e.g., `a`→`z` costs 1). Your task is to produce the lexicographically smallest possible string `t` whose total distance from `s` is exactly `k`. The answer should be printed as a single string.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Median of Array Equal to K
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`. In one operation you may add 1 or subtract 1 from any element of the array. Your task is to determine the smallest total number of such operations required so that, after sorting the array, its median (the middle element, or the larger of the two middle elements when the length is even) becomes exactly `k`. Return that minimum count as the answer.

title: Find the Number of Subarrays Where Boundary Elements Are Maximum
explanation_short:
You receive an array `nums` of positive integers.  
For every possible contiguous segment of the array, check whether the first and last numbers of that segment are both equal to the maximum value inside the segment.  
Count all segments that satisfy this condition.  
Return the total count as an integer.

title: Minimum Cost Walk in Weighted Graph
explanation_short:
You are given the number of vertices n, a list of undirected edges where each entry contains two endpoints and a weight, and a list of queries [si, ti].  
For each query you must consider all possible walks from si to ti (and walks may repeat vertices or edges) and determine the smallest value obtainable by taking the bitwise AND of the weights of the edges traversed; if no walk exists the answer is -1.  
Return an array whose i‑th element is the minimum cost for the i‑th query.

title: Minimum Time to Visit Disappearing Nodes
explanation_short: You are given the number of nodes n, a list of undirected edges where each edge specifies its two endpoints and the time needed to travel it, and an array disappear where disappear[i] is the moment node i vanishes. Starting from node 0, you must determine the earliest possible arrival time at every node that occurs strictly before that node disappears; if a node cannot be reached in time (or is disconnected), its result is -1. Return an array answer with answer[i] equal to this minimum feasible travel time for node i.

title: Latest Time You Can Obtain After Replacing Characters
explanation_short: You receive a string s that looks like a 12‑hour clock reading “HH:MM”, but some positions may be the character “?”. Each “?” must be turned into a digit so that the whole string becomes a legal time, where the hour part ranges from 00 to 11 and the minute part from 00 to 59. Your task is to choose digits that make the resulting time as late as possible. Return the completed string that represents this latest valid time.

title: Kth Smallest Amount With Single Denomination Combination
explanation_short: You receive an integer array coins, where each value is a coin denomination available in unlimited quantity, and an integer k. Consider every positive amount that can be formed by using only one denomination at a time (i.e., the multiples of each coin). Your task is to determine the k‑th smallest distinct amount among all those multiples, and return that amount as the answer.

title: Score of a String
explanation_short: You receive a single string `s`. For each pair of neighboring characters in `s`, take the absolute difference of their ASCII codes and add all those differences together. The required output is the total sum, presented as an integer.

title: Minimum Rectangles to Cover Points
explanation_short: You receive a list of points (xᵢ, yᵢ) on the plane and an integer w. Each rectangle you may place must have its left side on the line x = 0, its right side at some x₂, and its height up to a y‑coordinate y₂, with the width x₂ − 0 not exceeding w. Your goal is to choose as few of these rectangles as possible so that every given point lies inside at least one rectangle. Output the smallest number of rectangles needed to achieve this coverage.

title: Count the Number of Special Characters I
explanation_short:
You receive a single string `word`.  
A letter is “special” when the same alphabetic character shows up at least once in lowercase **and** at least once in uppercase somewhere in the string.  
Your task is to determine how many distinct letters satisfy this condition.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Count the Number of Special Characters II
explanation_short: You receive a single string `word`. You must count how many distinct letters appear in both lowercase and uppercase forms, with every lowercase occurrence of a letter coming before its first uppercase occurrence in the string. Return that count as an integer.

title: Maximum Prime Difference
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers called nums. Identify which elements of the array are prime numbers, then look at the positions (indices) of those prime elements. Compute the largest absolute difference between any two of those indices; if there is only one prime, the difference is zero. Return that maximum distance as a single integer.

title: Minimum Sum of Values by Dividing Array
explanation_short:
You are given an array `nums` of length `n` and another array `andValues` of length `m`.  
You must cut `nums` into exactly `m` non‑overlapping contiguous pieces so that for the i‑th piece the bitwise AND of all its elements equals `andValues[i]`.  
Each piece contributes its last element to a total sum, and you need the smallest possible sum among all valid partitions.  
Print that minimum sum (or indicate impossibility if no partition satisfies the conditions).

title: Make a Square with the Same Color
explanation_short: You receive a 3 × 3 grid where each cell is marked either ‘B’ (black) or ‘W’ (white). You may recolor at most one cell to the opposite color. Determine whether it is possible, after that single change, to have any 2 × 2 block in the grid whose four cells are all the same color. Return **true** if such a block can be created, otherwise return **false**.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Satisfy Conditions
explanation_short: You’re given an m × n matrix of non‑negative integers. In one operation you may change the value of any single cell to any other non‑negative integer. The goal is to modify as few cells as possible so that every entry grid[i][j] satisfies the condition described in the statement. The output is the minimum number of operations required. The sample cases show the initial grid and the smallest number of changes needed.

title: Find All Possible Stable Binary Arrays I
explanation_short:
You are given three integers: zero (the exact number of 0’s), one (the exact number of 1’s), and limit (the maximum allowed length of any consecutive block of identical bits).  
Your task is to count how many binary arrays contain exactly zero zeros and one ones while never having a run of the same value longer than limit.  
Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Find Edges in Shortest Paths
explanation_short:
You receive an integer n and a list of m undirected weighted edges, each given as (ai, bi, wi).  
Consider every shortest‑weight route that starts at node 0 and ends at node n‑1.  
For each edge in the original list, decide whether that edge appears in at least one of those optimal routes.  
Return a Boolean array answer where answer[i] is true if edge i is used in some shortest path, otherwise false.

title: Find the Integer Added to Array I
explanation_short:
You receive two arrays `nums1` and `nums2` that have the same number of elements.  
Every element of `nums1` has been shifted by the same unknown integer `x` (the shift can be positive or negative).  
Your task is to determine the value of `x` that makes the multiset of values in `nums1` match exactly the multiset in `nums2`.  
Return that integer `x` as the answer.

title: Minimum Array End
explanation_short: You are given two integers n and x. Your task is to imagine a strictly increasing list of n positive numbers such that the bitwise AND of every neighboring pair equals x. Among all possible lists that satisfy this condition, you must determine the smallest value that the final (nth) element can take. Print that minimum possible last element.

title: Right Triangles
explanation_short:
You receive a rectangular grid of 0s and 1s.  
A right‑triangle consists of three cells that all contain 1, where one cell shares its row with a second cell and its column with a third cell (the right angle is at the first cell).  
Count how many distinct triples of 1‑cells satisfy this condition.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Find All Possible Stable Binary Arrays II
explanation_short:
You are given three integers zero, one and limit that tell how many 0’s and 1’s must appear in a binary array and a parameter that restricts how the bits can be arranged.  
A binary array is called stable when it satisfies the rule that involves the limit value (the exact rule is defined in the statement).  
Your task is to count how many different binary arrays of length zero + one fulfil this stability condition.  
Return that count modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Word K-Periodic
explanation_short:
You are given a string `word` of length `n` and an integer `k` that evenly divides `n`.  
In one move you may copy any length‑`k` block of characters to another block that also starts at a position divisible by `k`.  
Your task is to determine the smallest number of such moves needed so that the whole string becomes a repetition of a single length‑`k` pattern (i.e., becomes `k`‑periodic).  
Return that minimum count as an integer.

title: Minimum Length of Anagram Concatenation
explanation_short:
You receive a single string `s`.  
The string is known to be formed by joining several pieces, each of which is a rearrangement of the same unknown string `t`.  
Your task is to determine the smallest possible length that such a string `t` could have.  
Return that minimum length as an integer.

title: Find the Integer Added to Array II
explanation_short:
You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`.  
`nums2` is formed by deleting exactly two elements from `nums1` and then adding the same integer `x` to every remaining element (the addition may be negative).  
Your task is to determine the smallest possible value of `x` that could make the transformed `nums1` contain exactly the same numbers, with the same frequencies, as `nums2`.  
Return that minimum integer `x` as the answer.

title: Find the Median of the Uniqueness Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums`. For every possible contiguous subarray of `nums`, count how many different values appear in that subarray, and gather all those counts into one list. After sorting this list, the task is to return the middle element (the median) of the sorted collection. The output is a single integer representing that median value.

title: Check if Grid Satisfies Conditions
explanation_short: You receive a rectangular matrix `grid` containing integers, with `m` rows and `n` columns. For every position `(i, j)` you must check whether the value stored there fulfills the given condition for that cell. If every cell meets its respective requirement, the answer is `true`; if any cell violates the rule, the answer is `false`. The result is a single Boolean value indicating whether the whole grid satisfies the conditions.

title: Valid Word
explanation_short:
You receive a single string called word.  
Your task is to check whether the word satisfies the given validity rules (for example, it must be at least three characters long and contain at least one vowel, among any other stated conditions).  
Return the Boolean value true if the word meets all the requirements; otherwise return false.

title: Find Products of Elements of Big Array
explanation_short:
You receive a list `queries`, where each entry contains three integers `fromi`, `toi`, and `modi`.  
First imagine an infinite sequence `big_nums` built by writing, for every positive integer x, the smallest sorted list of powers of two that sum to x, and then concatenating those lists one after another.  
For each query you must multiply the elements of `big_nums` whose positions run from `fromi` to `toi` (inclusive) and then take the remainder when divided by `modi`.  
Return an array whose i‑th entry is the remainder computed for the i‑th query.

title: Permutation Difference between Two Strings
explanation_short: You receive two strings `s` and `t`, each containing distinct characters and `t` being a rearrangement of `s`. For every character, look at the position it occupies in `s` and the position it occupies in `t`, compute the absolute difference of those two indices, and add up all those differences. The required result is this total sum. Output the sum as a single integer.

title: Minimum Cost to Equalize Array
explanation_short:
You receive an integer array `nums` and two cost values `cost1` and `cost2`.  
You may apply the given operations any number of times, each incurring either `cost1` or `cost2` depending on the operation chosen.  
Your task is to determine the smallest possible total cost that makes every element of `nums` identical.  
Return that minimum cost, reduced modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Taking Maximum Energy From the Mystic Dungeon
explanation_short: You are given an array energy of length n and an integer k. Choose any starting position i, then repeatedly add the energy at positions i, i + k, i + 2k, … until the index exceeds the array bounds, taking every value even if it is negative. Among all possible starting points, find the largest total energy you can collect. Output that maximum sum (it may be negative).

title: Find the Minimum Cost Array Permutation
explanation_short: You are given an array `nums` that contains each integer from 0 to n‑1 exactly once. You must choose a permutation `perm` of the same numbers that makes the sum |perm[0] − nums[perm[1]]| + |perm[1] − nums[perm[2]]| + … + |perm[n‑1] − nums[perm[0]]| as small as possible. If several permutations achieve that minimum sum, return the one that comes first in lexicographic order. The output is the selected permutation written as a list of integers.

title: Maximum Points Inside the Square
explanation_short:
You are given a list of points (x, y) and a string where the i‑th character is the tag of the i‑th point.  
A square is considered valid if it is centered at (0, 0), its sides are parallel to the axes, and no two points inside it share the same tag.  
Choose a side length for such a square so that the number of points it contains is as large as possible while keeping the square valid.  
Output the greatest possible number of points that can be included.

title: Sum of Digit Differences of All Pairs
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` of positive integers, all having the same number of digits. For every unordered pair of numbers, compare their digits at each position and count how many positions contain different digits; add these counts together for all pairs. Return the resulting total sum of digit differences.

title: Minimum Substring Partition of Equal Character Frequency
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
A substring is considered balanced when every distinct character inside it appears the same number of times.  
Your task is to cut the original string into one or more consecutive pieces, each of which must be balanced, while using as few pieces as possible.  
Return the smallest possible count of such substrings.

title: Maximum Difference Score in a Grid
explanation_short: You are given an m × n grid of positive integers. Starting from any cell, you may jump to any other cell that lies strictly below or strictly to the right of it, and each jump adds (value at the new cell − value at the current cell) to your total score. You must make at least one such move and want the sum of all move scores to be as large as possible. Output the greatest achievable total score (which may be negative).

title: Special Array I
explanation_short: You receive an array `nums` containing integers. You must examine every pair of neighboring elements and verify that one is even while the other is odd. Return **true** if this condition holds for all adjacent pairs; otherwise return **false**.

title: Special Array II
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums` and a list of queries, each query giving two indices `from` and `to` that define a subarray. A subarray is “special” if every pair of adjacent elements inside it consists of one even and one odd number. For every query you must determine whether the specified subarray meets this parity condition. Return an array of booleans where each entry is true if the corresponding subarray is special and false otherwise.

title: Find Number of Ways to Reach the K-th Stair
explanation_short: You are given a single non‑negative integer k. Alice starts on stair 1 with a jump value of 0 and may apply any sequence of the allowed operations, each of which changes her current stair and possibly her jump value. Your task is to count how many different operation sequences eventually place her on stair k (re‑visiting k later is also allowed). Output that count as a single integer.

title: Find the Number of Good Pairs I
explanation_short: You receive two integer arrays, nums1 of length n and nums2 of length m, together with a positive integer k. A pair (i, j) is considered good when the value at nums1[i] is exactly divisible by nums2[j] multiplied by k. Your task is to count how many such good pairs exist and output that total number.

title: Block Placement Queries
explanation_short: You are given a list of queries on an infinite line that starts at 0 and extends to the right. Each query is either “1 x”, which permanently puts an obstacle at coordinate x, or “2 x l”, which asks whether a block of length l can be placed somewhere strictly before x without touching any existing obstacles. Process the queries in order, remembering all obstacles added by type‑1 queries, and answer each type‑2 query with true if such a placement is possible and false otherwise. Return the answers to the type‑2 queries in the same order they appear.

title: String Compression III
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `word`.  
Repeatedly pick the longest prefix that consists of the same character, count how many times that character appears in the prefix, and append the count followed by the character to a new string.  
Continue this process until the entire original string has been consumed.  
The final string you built is the required output.

title: Find Occurrences of an Element in an Array
explanation_short: You receive three pieces of data: an integer array `nums`, an integer array `queries`, and a single integer `x`. For each value `k` in `queries`, you must determine the position (0‑based index) of the k‑th time `x` appears in `nums`, returning `-1` if `x` occurs fewer than k times. Collect these results in order into a new integer array and output it.

title: Find the XOR of Numbers Which Appear Twice
explanation_short: You receive an integer array where each element appears either once or exactly twice. Your task is to identify every value that occurs twice and combine those values using the bitwise XOR operation. Output the resulting XOR, or 0 if no element appears twice.

title: Find the Number of Distinct Colors Among the Balls
explanation_short: You receive an integer limit and a list of queries, each containing two numbers [x, y]. For every query you recolor ball x with color y, overwriting any previous color on that ball, and then you must determine how many different colors are currently present on all balls (uncolored balls are ignored). Return an array where the i‑th element is the count of distinct colors after processing the i‑th query.

title: Minimum Number of Chairs in a Waiting Room
explanation_short: You receive a string s where each character represents one second of time: ‘E’ means a new person arrives at the waiting room, and ‘L’ means one person departs. The room starts empty, and you must determine the smallest number of chairs that guarantees a free seat for every person present at any moment. Count how many people are inside after each event and track the largest simultaneous occupancy. That maximum is the required minimum number of chairs, which you output as a single integer.

title: Count Days Without Meetings
explanation_short: You receive an integer `days` indicating the total consecutive work days numbered from 1, and a list of pairs where each pair `[start, end]` marks a meeting that occupies every day from `start` through `end` inclusive. Your task is to determine how many of the days from 1 to `days` are not covered by any of the given meeting intervals, even if the intervals overlap. Return that count as a single integer.

title: Maximum Sum of Subsequence With Non-adjacent Elements
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a list of queries, each query containing a position `pos` and a new value `x`. For every query you first replace `nums[pos]` with `x`, then compute the greatest possible sum of a subsequence of the updated array where no two selected elements are adjacent (choosing nothing is allowed). The answer for the query is that maximum sum. Sum the answers for all queries and output the total modulo \(10^9+7\).

title: Find the Number of Good Pairs II
explanation_short:
You receive two integer arrays, nums1 of length n and nums2 of length m, together with a positive integer k.  
A pair (i, j) is considered good when the value at nums1[i] is divisible by the product nums2[j] × k.  
Your task is to count how many good pairs exist across all possible indices i (0 ≤ i < n) and j (0 ≤ j < m).  
Return that count as the output.

title: Clear Digits
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s`.  
Repeatedly delete any digit together with the character that is directly to its left, but only when such a left character exists.  
Continue this process until no digit has a non‑digit character before it.  
Return the string that remains after all possible deletions.

title: Find the Maximum Length of a Good Subsequence II
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`. A subsequence is formed by removing some elements while keeping the original order. The subsequence is “good” if, among its consecutive elements, there are at most `k` positions where the values are different. Your task is to find the greatest possible length of a good subsequence of `nums`. Output that maximum length as a single integer.

title: Lexicographically Minimum String After Removing Stars
explanation_short:
You are given a single string `s` that may contain zero or more ‘*’ symbols.  
Each ‘*’ must be used to delete exactly one character of the string (the character can be any letter, including the one immediately before the ‘*’).  
After all ‘*’ have been applied, you must produce the lexicographically smallest possible string that contains no ‘*’.  
The output is that final string.

title: Find Subarray With Bitwise OR Closest to K
explanation_short: You receive an array of integers and a single integer k. Choose any non‑empty contiguous segment of the array and compute the bitwise OR of all elements in that segment. Your task is to make the absolute difference between k and this OR value as small as possible. Output the minimum achievable absolute difference.

title: Find the N-th Value After K Seconds
explanation_short: You receive two integers n and k. Start with an array of length n where every entry equals 1. Each second you replace the array by its prefix sums – each position becomes the sum of all elements up to that index. After performing this transformation k times, output the value that ends up at the n‑th (last) position. The result is a single integer.

title: Find The First Player to win K Games in a Row
explanation_short: You are given an array `skills` where each element is the unique skill level of player i (players are numbered from 0 to n‑1) and a positive integer k. Players start in the order of their indices, and they repeatedly play matches where the higher‑skill player wins and stays in the front of the queue. The competition ends as soon as some player wins k games consecutively. Return the index of that player. If no one reaches k wins before the process naturally terminates, the answer is the player who eventually becomes unbeatable.

title: Maximum Total Reward Using Operations I
explanation_short: You are given an integer array rewardValues of length n. Starting with a total reward of 0, you may repeatedly pick an unmarked index, mark it, and add the appropriate amount to your total according to the operation rules. Your task is to choose the order of markings that yields the largest possible sum. Return that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Find the Maximum Length of a Good Subsequence I
explanation_short:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a non‑negative integer `k`.  
A subsequence of `nums` is considered “good” if, when you look at its consecutive elements, there are at most `k` positions where the value changes from one element to the next.  
Your task is to choose a subsequence that satisfies this condition and has the greatest possible number of elements.  
Return the length of that longest good subsequence.

title: Find the Child Who Has the Ball After K Seconds
explanation_short: You are given two positive integers n and k. There are n children numbered 0 to n − 1 standing in a line, with child 0 initially holding a ball and the passing direction set to the right. Each second the ball moves to the adjacent child; when it reaches either end of the line the direction flips. After k seconds, output the number of the child who currently has the ball.

title: Maximum Total Damage With Spell Casting
explanation_short:
You are given a list of integers where each number represents the damage of a spell, and the same damage may appear many times.  
You must choose some spells to cast, but after picking a spell with damage x you cannot pick any spell whose damage is x‑2, x‑1, x+1, or x+2, and each spell can be used at most once.  
The goal is to obtain the largest possible total damage from the chosen spells.  
Return that maximum sum as a single integer.

title: Maximum Total Reward Using Operations II
explanation_short: You are given an integer array rewardValues of length n. Starting with a total reward of 0 and all positions unmarked, you may repeatedly pick an unmarked index, mark it, and increase the total reward according to the operation’s rule. Your goal is to choose the order of markings that makes the final total reward as large as possible. Output the maximum achievable total reward as a single integer.

title: Peaks in Array
explanation_short: You are given an integer array `nums` and a list of queries. Each query is either type 2, which changes the value at a specified index of `nums`, or type 1, which asks for the number of “peaks” (elements larger than both their immediate neighbors) inside a given sub‑range of the current array. Process the queries in order, applying updates as they appear, and record the result of every type 1 query. Return an array containing those recorded counts in the same order they were asked.

title: Count Pairs That Form a Complete Day II
explanation_short:
You are given an array of integers where each element represents a number of hours.  
Your task is to count how many unordered pairs of distinct indices (i, j) have a sum that is exactly divisible by 24, meaning the two times together make a whole number of days.  
Only the total number of such pairs is required.  
Return that count as an integer.

title: Count Pairs That Form a Complete Day I
explanation_short: You are given an array of integers where each value represents a number of hours. Your task is to count how many distinct pairs of positions (i, j) (i < j) have a combined total that equals a whole number of days (i.e., the sum is divisible by 24). Return that count as a single integer.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Binary Array Elements Equal to One II
explanation_short:
You are given an array consisting only of 0s and 1s.  
You may repeatedly change any element’s value from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0.  
Your task is to determine the smallest possible number of such flips that will turn every entry of the array into a 1.  
Return that minimum count as the answer.

title: Minimum Average of Smallest and Largest Elements
explanation_short: You are given an even‑length array of integers. After sorting the array, pair the smallest element with the largest, the second smallest with the second largest, and so on, computing the average of each pair. Among all these averages, identify the smallest one. Output that minimum average as a floating‑point number.

title: Find Minimum Operations to Make All Elements Divisible by Three
explanation_short: You receive an integer array `nums`. In one move you may add 1 or subtract 1 from any element. The task is to find the smallest total number of moves needed so that every element becomes divisible by 3. Output that minimum number as an integer.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Binary Array Elements Equal to One I
explanation_short: You are given a binary array `nums` where each element is either 0 or 1.
